ITID-61111.def: An incident in which data belonging to, or processed on behalf of, the organization is exposed through misconfigured or compromised cloud storage operated by a third-party vendor, and the exposure has not yet been further classified.
ITID-61111.purpose: Provides an intake classification for vendor cloud-storage exposure incidents (misconfigured buckets, exposed object stores, leaky SaaS repositories) that have not yet been triaged into a more specific sibling leaf.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported vendor cloud-storage exposures pending triage
Cases where the specific exposure mechanism (misconfiguration vs. compromise vs. insider) is not yet known
Exposures discovered via external researcher or bug-bounty notification
scopeExcludes: Exposures already reclassified to a more specific data-breach or network-compromise leaf
Exposure of the organization's own cloud storage not managed by a vendor (an internal cloud-security ITID)
ITID-61111.severity: Medium-High pending scope confirmation; escalate immediately if exposed data includes customer PII, credentials, or regulated data classes.
ITID-61111.priority: P2 at intake, re-evaluate to P1 once data sensitivity and exposure duration are confirmed.
ITID-61111.escalation: Escalate to third-party risk management and legal/privacy within 24 hours of confirmation; escalate to the vendor's security contact immediately to request access logs and remediation.
indicators: Vendor or researcher notification of an open/misconfigured bucket or object store
Data belonging to the organization found indexed by search engines or scanning tools
Vendor breach notification citing cloud storage as the exposure vector
vectors: Publicly readable/writable cloud storage buckets
Misconfigured access-control lists on vendor-managed object storage
Exposed backup or export files left in accessible storage
rootCauses: Vendor default-permissive storage configuration
Lack of contractual security requirements for vendor cloud storage
No independent verification of vendor storage security posture
controls: Vendor security assessment requiring cloud storage configuration review
Contractual data-handling and encryption-at-rest requirements
Continuous external attack-surface monitoring for organization-tagged assets
ITID-61111.detection: Detection is largely external and reactive (researcher/vendor notification, attack-surface scanning); the organization has no direct telemetry into vendor-operated storage.
ITID-61111.response: Confirm scope and sensitivity of exposed data with the vendor, initiate breach-notification assessment, and reclassify to a specific sibling leaf once the exposure mechanism is known.
metrics: Count of vendor cloud-storage exposures reported per quarter
Mean time to reclassify from intake to specific leaf
Mean time to vendor remediation confirmation
detections: External attack-surface monitoring alerts for organization-branded assets
ITID-61111.notes: This is the intake bucket for the Vendor Cloud Storage Exposure group; incidents should be reclassified promptly once the exposure mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Vendor Cloud Storage Exposure
playbook.description: A vendor-managed cloud storage bucket or container holding the organization's data is discovered publicly accessible or misconfigured.

steps.title: Confirm exposure report source and scope
steps.desc: Capture how the exposure was discovered (vendor notification, security researcher, internal scanning, media report) and the specific storage resource(s) named.
steps.guidance: Record discovery channel, exact bucket/container names or URLs, and any evidence (screenshots, cached search results) before they disappear.
steps.outcome: Documented exposure report with resource identifiers and discovery timeline.

steps.title: Determine what organizational data resided in the exposed resource
steps.desc: Work with the vendor's incident contact to inventory what data types and record volumes were stored in the exposed location.
steps.guidance: Request the vendor's own access logs for the bucket if available; do not assume vendor claims are complete without corroboration.
steps.outcome: Preliminary data-type and volume inventory for the exposed resource.

steps.title: Assess public accessibility window and access evidence
steps.desc: Determine how long the resource was exposed and whether third parties accessed it, using vendor logs, web archive snapshots, or search engine cache history.
steps.guidance: Check services like Wayback Machine or search cache for indexing evidence; ask vendor for CloudTrail/access logs covering the exposure window.
steps.outcome: Estimated exposure window and evidence of unauthorized access, if any.

steps.title: Confirm vendor has restricted public access
steps.desc: Obtain vendor confirmation and, where possible, independent verification (e.g., attempting the previously-exposed URL) that the storage resource is no longer publicly accessible.
steps.guidance: Do not rely solely on vendor's verbal assurance; request a screenshot of updated bucket policy or ACL.
steps.outcome: Storage resource confirmed no longer publicly reachable.
steps.abort: If vendor cannot confirm within agreed SLA, escalate to vendor relationship manager and Legal.

steps.title: Revoke or rotate the organization's credentials tied to the vendor integration
steps.desc: Rotate API keys, service account credentials, or shared secrets used by the organization to interact with the affected vendor system, independent of vendor action.
steps.guidance: Prioritize any credentials that could have been harvested from the exposed storage itself.
steps.outcome: All organization-side credentials associated with the exposed resource rotated.

steps.title: Notify internal stakeholders and activate vendor incident clause
steps.desc: Notify vendor relationship manager, Legal, and Privacy teams; invoke breach-notification and cooperation clauses in the vendor contract.
steps.guidance: Reference the specific contract clause requiring vendor cooperation and timely disclosure.
steps.outcome: Vendor formally engaged under contractual incident-response obligations.

steps.title: Verify vendor's remediation of underlying misconfiguration
steps.desc: Request and review vendor's evidence that the root-cause misconfiguration (e.g., default-public bucket policy) has been corrected across all similar resources, not just the one exposed.
steps.guidance: Ask specifically whether the vendor audited sibling buckets/containers for the same misconfiguration class.
steps.outcome: Vendor-provided evidence of systemic fix confirmed adequate.
steps.abort: If vendor cannot demonstrate systemic remediation, escalate to Procurement for contractual remedy discussion.

steps.title: Scan for downstream use of exposed data
steps.desc: Search for evidence of exposed data appearing on paste sites, dark web forums, or being used in follow-on phishing/fraud attempts against the organization or its customers.
steps.guidance: Engage threat intelligence resources or a monitoring vendor for this sweep.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of whether exposed data has surfaced elsewhere.

steps.title: Determine and execute notification obligations
steps.desc: Work with Legal/Privacy to determine whether affected individuals, regulators, or customers must be notified based on data types and jurisdictions involved.
steps.guidance: Use the organization's breach-notification decision matrix; factor in vendor's own regulatory obligations separately.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and, if required, executed within statutory timelines.

steps.title: Restore or re-establish the vendor integration under hardened terms
steps.desc: Reconnect the integration only after confirming new access controls, and update the vendor risk register with revised risk rating.
steps.guidance: Consider requiring encryption-at-rest attestation or private endpoint configuration as a condition of resumption.
steps.outcome: Integration resumed under documented, improved security terms.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review and update vendor risk profile
steps.desc: Document root cause, timeline, organizational impact, and vendor's remediation adequacy; update the vendor's risk tier and audit cadence accordingly.
steps.guidance: Include recommendation on whether continued vendor relationship requires enhanced monitoring or contract amendment.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report filed and vendor risk register updated.

ITID-61121.def: An incident in which credentials used by a third-party vendor to access, process, or store organizational data or systems have been compromised, and the full scope and downstream impact are not yet determined.
ITID-61121.purpose: Provides an intake classification for incidents involving compromise of credentials belonging to or issued by a third-party vendor, before the downstream impact is fully understood.
scopeIncludes: Vendor employee or service-account credentials found in a credential dump or stealer log
Vendor-reported credential compromise pending impact assessment
Compromised API keys or tokens issued to a vendor integration
scopeExcludes: Credential compromise already confirmed to have enabled network intrusion (see Third-Party Network Compromise)
Compromise of the organization's own employee credentials (an internal identity-security ITID)
ITID-61121.severity: Medium-High; escalate to High if the credential grants access to production systems or sensitive data stores.
ITID-61121.priority: P2 at intake, escalating to P1 if active misuse is confirmed.
ITID-61121.escalation: Escalate to the vendor's security team for immediate credential rotation, and to internal identity/access management to review and constrain the vendor's granted access.
indicators: Vendor credentials appearing in dark-web credential-dump monitoring
Anomalous authentication attempts using vendor-issued API keys
Vendor notification of a credential-stuffing or phishing incident affecting staff
vectors: Phishing of vendor employees
Credential reuse across vendor systems
Exposed API keys in vendor source-code repositories
rootCauses: Lack of MFA enforcement on vendor accounts with access to organizational systems
No credential-rotation policy for vendor-issued API keys
Insufficient least-privilege scoping of vendor access
controls: MFA requirement for all vendor access to organizational systems
Vendor credential-rotation and API key lifecycle policy
Dark-web/credential-dump monitoring covering vendor-issued identifiers
ITID-61121.detection: Detection relies on external credential monitoring and vendor self-reporting; internal telemetry is limited to monitoring the organization's own systems for anomalous vendor-credential use.
ITID-61121.response: Coordinate immediate credential rotation with the vendor, audit access logs for misuse, and reclassify once the scope of misuse is confirmed.
metrics: Count of vendor credential compromise reports per quarter
Mean time to credential rotation after notification
Percentage of vendor accounts with MFA enforced
detections: Anomalous vendor API key usage alerts
ITID-61121.notes: This is the intake bucket for Third-Party Credential Compromise; reclassify to a network-compromise leaf if the credential is confirmed to have enabled system access.

playbook.name: Third-Party Credential Compromise
playbook.description: Credentials used by or belonging to a third-party vendor to access organizational systems or data are compromised.

steps.title: Validate the credential compromise report
steps.desc: Confirm details of which vendor credentials were compromised (vendor employee account, service account, API key) and the notification source.
steps.guidance: Request incident details in writing from the vendor including scope of compromised credentials.

steps.title: Identify all organizational systems accessible via the compromised credentials
steps.desc: Map every organizational system, application, or data store the vendor credential set had access to.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference vendor access provisioning records and IAM logs.
steps.outcome: Complete access map for the compromised credential.

steps.title: Review access logs for anomalous activity using the compromised credentials
steps.desc: Search authentication and activity logs for the affected accounts/keys for unusual login times, locations, or data access volumes.
steps.guidance: Extend log review window to cover the full suspected compromise period, not just since notification.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether the compromised credentials were actually misused against organizational systems.

steps.title: Disable or revoke the compromised credentials immediately
steps.desc: Revoke the vendor's access tokens, API keys, or account sessions on the organization's side, independent of vendor-side revocation.
steps.guidance: Do not wait for vendor confirmation before revoking on the org side if immediate risk exists.
steps.outcome: Compromised credentials disabled for organizational access.

steps.title: Force re-authentication and issue new credentials under stronger controls
steps.desc: Issue replacement credentials to the vendor with MFA enforcement and scoped least-privilege permissions.
steps.guidance: Consider requiring IP allowlisting or short-lived tokens as a condition of reinstatement.
steps.outcome: New, hardened credentials issued and old ones fully retired.

steps.title: Notify vendor relationship manager and Security leadership
steps.desc: Escalate incident details to the vendor relationship manager and CISO/Security leadership for visibility and coordination.

steps.title: Confirm vendor's remediation of the compromise root cause
steps.desc: Obtain vendor's account of how the credentials were compromised (phishing, infostealer, credential stuffing) and evidence the underlying vendor-side weakness is fixed.
steps.outcome: Root cause confirmed and vendor remediation validated.
steps.abort: If vendor cannot substantiate remediation, escalate to Procurement/Legal for contractual review.

steps.title: Rotate any organizational secrets exposed via the compromised access
steps.desc: Rotate any internal credentials, tokens, or keys that were reachable or visible to someone using the compromised vendor credentials.
steps.outcome: All potentially exposed organizational secrets rotated.

steps.title: Assess and communicate impact to affected data subjects if applicable
steps.desc: Determine with Legal/Privacy whether the misuse of vendor credentials resulted in exposure requiring notification.
steps.outcome: Notification requirement determined and actioned if needed.

steps.title: Resume normal vendor access under monitoring
steps.desc: Restore full vendor operations once hardened credentials are validated, with a defined monitoring period.
steps.outcome: Vendor access normalized with enhanced monitoring in place.

steps.title: Document incident and update vendor access policy
steps.desc: Record the full incident timeline and update vendor credential-issuance standards (MFA, rotation cadence, scoping) based on findings.
steps.outcome: Lessons-learned report filed and policy updates proposed.

ITID-61131.def: An incident in which customer or business-partner data entrusted to a third-party vendor for processing or storage has been disclosed without authorization, and the leak's root cause has not yet been classified.
ITID-61131.purpose: Provides an intake classification for incidents where customer or partner data held by a third party has leaked, before the specific cause is determined.
scopeIncludes: Data-sharing partner or reseller reporting an unexplained leak of shared customer data
Leak discovered via customer complaint or external notification pending vendor confirmation
Data found for sale or posted publicly with unconfirmed source
scopeExcludes: Leaks already confirmed to originate from a specific cloud-storage misconfiguration (see ITID-61111 group)
Leaks caused by the organization's own systems rather than a third party
ITID-61131.severity: Medium-High; escalate to High if regulated data classes (PII, financial, health) are involved.
ITID-61131.priority: P2 at intake, escalating to P1 upon confirmation of scale or regulated data exposure.
ITID-61131.escalation: Escalate to legal/privacy for breach-notification obligations and to the vendor/partner's designated security contact within 24 hours.
indicators: Customer data appearing on a leak forum or paste site
Partner notification of an unexplained data exposure
Regulatory or media inquiry referencing a shared dataset
vectors: Unauthorized access to partner-shared data repositories
Insider misuse at a data-sharing partner
Insecure data-transfer mechanisms between organization and partner
rootCauses: Absence of data-sharing agreements specifying security controls
No encryption requirement for data in transit or at rest with partners
Lack of visibility into how shared data is stored downstream
controls: Data-sharing agreements with defined security and audit requirements
Data classification and minimization prior to sharing with partners
Leak-site and paste-site monitoring for organization-related data
ITID-61131.detection: Detection is primarily external (leak-site monitoring, customer/partner reports); internal telemetry into partner systems is generally unavailable.
ITID-61131.response: Confirm the source and scope with the partner, initiate breach-notification assessment, and reclassify to a specific leaf once the cause is known.
metrics: Count of partner data leak reports per quarter
Mean time to source confirmation
Number of records affected per incident
detections: Leak-site and dark-web monitoring for customer data
ITID-61131.notes: This is the intake bucket for Customer and Partner Data Leak; reclassify once the leak mechanism and responsible party are confirmed.

playbook.name: Customer and Partner Data Leak (Supply Chain Context)
playbook.description: Organizational customer or partner data held by a third party is leaked or disclosed without authorization.

steps.title: Confirm the leak report and identify the responsible party
steps.desc: Establish whether the leak originated at a vendor, partner, or downstream sub-processor and capture the notification details.
steps.outcome: Confirmed leak source and initial scope.

steps.title: Inventory the specific customer/partner data records involved
steps.desc: Work with the vendor/partner to determine exact records, fields, and individuals affected.
steps.guidance: Request a data dictionary and record count, not just a general description.

steps.title: Determine leak vector and whether it is ongoing
steps.desc: Establish how the leak occurred (misconfigured share, insider action, breach) and whether exposure is continuing.
steps.outcome: Leak vector identified and current exposure status confirmed.

steps.title: Request immediate takedown or access restriction from the responsible party
steps.desc: Formally request the vendor/partner restrict further access or take down the exposed data source.
steps.guidance: Put the request in writing referencing contractual obligations and timelines.
steps.abort: If the party is unresponsive, escalate to Legal for formal demand.

steps.title: Suspend or restrict the organization's data feed to the affected party
steps.desc: Pause any ongoing data sharing to the vendor/partner pending confirmation of adequate controls.
steps.outcome: Further data flow to the affected party halted.

steps.title: Engage Legal and Privacy teams
steps.desc: Brief Legal and Privacy on scope and potential notification obligations; invoke data processing agreement breach clauses.
steps.outcome: Legal/Privacy actively engaged and contractual clauses invoked.

steps.title: Verify remediation of the leak vector
steps.desc: Obtain and validate evidence that the vendor/partner has corrected the underlying cause of the leak.

steps.title: Search for further distribution of leaked data
steps.desc: Monitor for the leaked data appearing on public forums, paste sites, or being used in fraud/phishing.
steps.outcome: Distribution scope confirmed or ruled out.

steps.title: Execute notification to affected customers/partners and regulators as required
steps.desc: Determine and carry out notification obligations based on jurisdiction and data sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Required notifications completed within statutory timeframes.

steps.title: Resume data sharing under revised safeguards
steps.desc: Reinstate the data feed only after new contractual and technical safeguards are agreed and verified.
steps.outcome: Data sharing resumed with documented improved safeguards.

steps.title: Document incident and reassess partner risk tier
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and update the partner's risk classification and audit frequency.

ITID-61141.def: A breach or unauthorized disclosure at a data broker or people-search aggregator, exposing aggregated personal records that include the organization's customers, employees, or executives, distinct from breaches at bureaus performing regulated credit-reporting functions.
ITID-61141.purpose: Classifies incidents at data brokers or people-search aggregators that expose records the organization's customers or employees are part of.
scopeIncludes: Breach of a people-search or data-broker platform exposing organization-affiliated individuals' records
Aggregated dossiers (address history, relatives, phone numbers) sold or leaked from a broker
Notification from a broker that organization-linked records were included in a breach
scopeExcludes: Breach at a regulated credit bureau or reporting agency (see ITID-61142)
Direct breach of the organization's own customer database
ITID-61141.severity: Medium; escalate to High if the exposed records enable targeted social engineering or physical-security risk to executives.
ITID-61141.priority: P3, escalating to P2 if executive or high-risk personnel data is involved.
ITID-61141.escalation: Escalate to executive protection and security awareness teams if senior leadership data is exposed; notify affected individuals per policy.
indicators: Data-broker breach notification naming organization-affiliated individuals
Aggregated personal dossiers found on criminal marketplaces referencing employees
Increase in targeted phishing or vishing following a known broker breach
vectors: Compromise of the data broker's own infrastructure
Scraping of the broker's platform via API abuse
Insider sale of aggregated records at the broker
rootCauses: Data brokers holding aggregated PII with weaker security controls than primary data holders
Lack of organizational visibility into which brokers hold employee/executive data
No opt-out or data-minimization program with brokers
controls: Executive data-broker opt-out and monitoring program
Threat intelligence monitoring for aggregator breach disclosures
Security awareness briefing following confirmed aggregator breaches
ITID-61141.detection: Detection depends almost entirely on external breach notifications and threat intelligence; no internal telemetry exists into broker platforms.
ITID-61141.response: Confirm which individuals are affected, assess targeted social-engineering risk, and brief affected personnel and executive protection as needed.
metrics: Number of data-broker breaches affecting organization-linked individuals per year
Number of employees enrolled in broker opt-out programs
detections: Threat intelligence feeds for data-broker breach disclosures
ITID-61141.notes: Differentiated from ITID-61142 by aggregator type: people-search/data-broker platforms rather than regulated credit-reporting agencies.

playbook.name: Data Broker/People-Search Site Breach Exposing Aggregated Records
playbook.description: A data broker or people-search site holding aggregated organizational or employee/customer records suffers a breach.

steps.title: Confirm the data aggregator breach and organizational exposure
steps.desc: Verify the breach report and determine whether organizational employee, customer, or executive data was aggregated by the broker.
steps.guidance: Check whether the organization or its personnel data was ever sold to or scraped by this aggregator.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether organizational-linked data was present in the breached aggregator dataset.

steps.title: Determine categories and sensitivity of aggregated records exposed
steps.desc: Identify what record types (PII, addresses, SSNs, employment history) were exposed for affected individuals.
steps.outcome: Sensitivity and category inventory of exposed records.

steps.title: Identify and flag high-risk exposed individuals (executives, security personnel)
steps.desc: Cross-reference exposed records against high-profile or high-risk personnel (executives, physical-security-sensitive staff) for targeted protective measures.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical security/executive protection if applicable.
steps.outcome: High-risk individuals identified and flagged for protective action.

steps.title: Submit opt-out/removal requests to the aggregator
steps.desc: File formal data-removal or opt-out requests with the aggregator for affected individuals' records.

steps.title: Notify Legal and Privacy of potential downstream exposure
steps.desc: Brief Legal and Privacy on the aggregator breach and the presence of organizational-linked records, given the aggregator relationship is typically indirect (data was scraped or purchased, not contractually shared).
steps.guidance: Clarify that no direct contractual relationship may exist, which affects available remedies.
steps.outcome: Legal/Privacy briefed and remedy options assessed.

steps.title: Monitor for misuse of exposed aggregated data
steps.desc: Monitor for phishing, doxxing, SIM-swap attempts, or physical-security incidents targeting individuals whose aggregated data was exposed.
steps.outcome: Monitoring in place; any misuse detected and actioned.

steps.title: Offer protective services to significantly affected individuals
steps.desc: Where warranted, offer identity-monitoring or executive-protection services to individuals with significant exposure.

steps.title: Document incident and review data-minimization practices
steps.desc: Record findings and evaluate whether organizational data-sharing practices contribute to aggregator exposure risk.
steps.outcome: Report filed with recommendations on limiting future data aggregation exposure.

ITID-61142.def: A breach or unauthorized disclosure at a credit bureau or other regulated consumer-reporting agency, exposing financial identity records (credit history, SSNs, account data) belonging to the organization's customers or employees, distinct from breaches at unregulated data brokers.
ITID-61142.purpose: Classifies incidents at credit bureaus or regulated reporting agencies that expose financial or identity records tied to the organization's customers or employees.
scopeIncludes: Breach notification from a credit bureau naming organization-affiliated individuals
Exposure of credit-report or identity-verification data used in the organization's onboarding/KYC processes
Regulatory notification tied to a reporting-agency breach affecting the organization's customer base
scopeExcludes: Breach at an unregulated people-search/data-broker platform (see ITID-61141)
Fraud arising from the organization's own credit-check process failures
ITID-61142.severity: High, given the sensitivity of financial identity data and associated fraud/identity-theft risk.
ITID-61142.priority: P1 if the organization used the breached bureau for customer verification; P2 otherwise.
ITID-61142.escalation: Escalate to legal, fraud, and customer-communications teams immediately; assess whether the organization's identity-verification workflows must be temporarily adjusted.
indicators: Bureau breach notification listing the organization as a data-sharing partner
Spike in identity-theft or synthetic-identity fraud reports among customers
Regulatory bulletin identifying the bureau as compromised
vectors: Exploitation of a vulnerability in the bureau's consumer-facing web application
Compromise of bureau employee or contractor credentials
Insecure API used for credit-data lookups
rootCauses: Concentration risk from reliance on a small number of credit bureaus
Lack of contractual security audit rights over bureau infrastructure
No fallback identity-verification process if a bureau is compromised
controls: Contractual right-to-audit clauses with credit bureaus
Fraud monitoring for customers whose data was verified via the affected bureau
Alternate identity-verification provider on standby
ITID-61142.detection: Detection is external and reliant on regulatory/bureau disclosure; the organization has no direct visibility into bureau infrastructure.
ITID-61142.response: Determine customer overlap with the breached bureau's dataset, notify affected customers, and monitor for downstream identity-fraud attempts.
metrics: Number of customers affected by bureau breaches per year
Fraud-attempt rate among affected customers post-notification
sops: Credit Bureau Breach Customer Notification SOP
detections: Fraud monitoring alerts tied to breached identity data
ITID-61142.notes: Differentiated from ITID-61141 by the regulated, financial-identity nature of the aggregator; carries higher default severity due to fraud potential.

playbook.name: Credit Bureau/Reporting Agency Data Aggregator Breach
playbook.description: A credit bureau or consumer reporting agency holding organizational customer or employee credit data suffers a breach.

steps.title: Confirm bureau breach notification and organizational relationship
steps.desc: Validate the breach disclosure from the credit bureau and confirm the organization's relationship (customer screening, employee background checks, financing).
steps.outcome: Confirmed relationship and applicability of the breach to the organization.

steps.title: Determine scope of affected employees/customers and data types
steps.desc: Obtain from the bureau which individuals tied to the organization were affected and what data types (SSN, credit history, DOB) were exposed.
steps.outcome: Affected population and data-type inventory obtained.

steps.title: Assess regulatory notification triggers
steps.desc: Determine, with Legal, whether the exposure triggers FCRA, state breach-notification, or other regulatory obligations for the organization.

steps.title: Suspend reliance on affected bureau data pending validation
steps.desc: Pause automated decisions (credit checks, background checks) relying on data confirmed or suspected compromised, until integrity is validated.
steps.outcome: Reliance on potentially compromised bureau data paused.

steps.title: Engage Legal and Compliance on notification strategy
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on notification content, timing, and coordination with the bureau's own notification campaign.
steps.outcome: Notification strategy aligned with bureau and regulators.

steps.title: Verify bureau's remediation and credit-monitoring offer adequacy
steps.desc: Confirm the bureau's remediation steps and whether credit-monitoring/identity-protection services offered meet organizational obligations to affected individuals.
steps.outcome: Remediation and monitoring offer confirmed adequate or supplemented.
steps.abort: If inadequate, escalate to Legal to require additional bureau action.

steps.title: Notify affected individuals and provide protective resources
steps.desc: Send required notifications and provide credit-monitoring enrollment instructions to affected employees/customers.

steps.title: Resume reliance on bureau data once integrity confirmed
steps.desc: Restore automated decision processes once data integrity and bureau remediation are verified.

steps.title: Document incident and reassess bureau dependency risk
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and evaluate diversification of reporting-agency dependency.

ITID-61143.def: An incident at a third-party data aggregator affecting organization-linked records, where the aggregator's type (unregulated broker vs. regulated reporting agency) has not yet been confirmed.
ITID-61143.purpose: Provides an intake classification for data-aggregator incidents that have not yet been identified as either a people-search/data-broker breach or a credit-bureau breach.
scopeIncludes: Initial reports of an aggregator breach before the aggregator type is confirmed
Ambiguous third-party notifications that do not specify the nature of the aggregator
scopeExcludes: Confirmed people-search/data-broker breaches (see ITID-61141)
Confirmed credit bureau/reporting agency breaches (see ITID-61142)
ITID-61143.severity: Medium pending classification; treat as High until the data class is ruled out as financial/regulated.
ITID-61143.escalation: Escalate to third-party risk management to confirm aggregator type and data class as quickly as possible.
indicators: Ambiguous breach notification referencing an unnamed or unfamiliar aggregator
Media reports of a data-aggregator breach with unclear scope
vectors: Not yet determined pending classification
rootCauses: Delayed or incomplete vendor breach disclosure
Lack of a maintained inventory of which aggregators hold organization-linked data
controls: Third-party data aggregator inventory and risk register
Threat intelligence monitoring for aggregator breach disclosures
ITID-61143.detection: Detection is entirely external and reliant on aggregator or media disclosure.
ITID-61143.response: Rapidly confirm the aggregator's type and data class held, then reclassify to ITID-61141 or ITID-61142 as appropriate.
metrics: Mean time to reclassify from intake to specific leaf
detections: Threat intelligence feeds for aggregator breach disclosures
ITID-61143.notes: This is the intake bucket for Incident at a Data Aggregator; reclassify promptly once the aggregator type is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Data Aggregator Incident
playbook.description: A data aggregator holding organizational or customer data experiences an incident not otherwise categorized.

steps.title: Confirm the aggregator incident and organizational exposure
steps.desc: Validate the incident report and confirm whether organizational data was held by the aggregator.

steps.title: Determine data types and volume affected
steps.desc: Establish what data categories and how many records tied to the organization were involved.

steps.title: Request formal incident details and remediation plan from aggregator
steps.desc: Formally request the aggregator's incident report and planned remediation steps.
steps.outcome: Incident report and remediation plan received.
steps.abort: If unresponsive, escalate via vendor relationship manager and Legal.

steps.title: Restrict further data submission to the aggregator pending assessment
steps.desc: Pause any ongoing data feeds to the aggregator until the incident is understood.

steps.title: Verify aggregator's remediation adequacy
steps.desc: Review evidence of the aggregator's remediation and confirm it addresses the root cause.

steps.title: Determine and execute notification obligations if applicable
steps.desc: Assess with Legal/Privacy whether notification of affected individuals or regulators is required.
steps.outcome: Notification decision made and executed if required.

steps.title: Resume data relationship under confirmed safeguards
steps.desc: Restore the data relationship with the aggregator once safeguards are verified.

steps.title: Document incident and update aggregator risk assessment
steps.desc: File the post-incident report and update the aggregator's risk profile.
steps.outcome: Report filed and risk profile updated.

ITID-61211.def: An incident in which a vendor's VPN, remote-access gateway, or remote-support tooling has been compromised, creating a potential pathway into the organization's network, and full impact has not yet been assessed.
ITID-61211.purpose: Provides an intake classification for incidents involving a compromised VPN or remote-access system operated by a vendor, before the intrusion's downstream impact is confirmed.
scopeIncludes: Vendor notification of a breached VPN concentrator or remote-access gateway used to connect to the organization
Suspicious authentication from vendor remote-access infrastructure pending investigation
Compromise of vendor remote-support tools (e.g., screen-sharing utilities) used for support access
scopeExcludes: Confirmed intrusion into organizational systems via the vendor VPN (see Supplier System Intrusion)
Compromise of the organization's own VPN infrastructure not tied to a vendor
ITID-61211.severity: High by default, given the direct network pathway risk; escalate immediately upon any sign of lateral movement.
ITID-61211.priority: P1 at intake given the potential for direct network access.
ITID-61211.escalation: Escalate immediately to network security to disable or restrict the vendor's remote-access channel pending investigation.
indicators: Vendor breach notification naming VPN/remote-access infrastructure
Anomalous authentication patterns from vendor-associated remote-access IP ranges
Unexpected remote-support sessions initiated outside of scheduled maintenance windows
vectors: Exploitation of unpatched VPN gateway vulnerabilities
Credential theft against vendor remote-access accounts
Abuse of always-on remote-support tooling left enabled
rootCauses: Standing/always-on vendor remote-access channels rather than just-in-time access
Lack of MFA on vendor remote-access accounts
Unpatched vendor-managed VPN infrastructure
controls: Just-in-time vendor remote-access provisioning
MFA enforcement on all vendor remote-access accounts
Network segmentation isolating vendor remote-access entry points
ITID-61211.detection: Moderate: authentication and network logs on the organization's side of the connection provide signal, but full visibility depends on vendor-side monitoring.
ITID-61211.response: Immediately disable or restrict the affected remote-access channel, review authentication logs for misuse, and reclassify once intrusion scope is confirmed.
metrics: Number of standing vendor remote-access channels in inventory
Mean time to disable a compromised vendor access channel
sops: Vendor Remote Access Compromise Response SOP
detections: Anomalous authentication alerting on vendor remote-access channels
ITID-61211.notes: This is the intake bucket for VPN or Remote Access Breach; reclassify to Supplier System Intrusion if lateral movement into organizational systems is confirmed.

playbook.name: Vendor VPN or Remote Access Breach
playbook.description: A vendor's VPN or remote-access mechanism used to connect into organizational systems is breached.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor VPN/remote-access breach report
steps.desc: Validate notification details and identify which remote-access channel (VPN, RDP gateway, remote-support tool) was compromised.
steps.outcome: Confirmed breach details and affected access channel.

steps.title: Review organizational logs for activity via the vendor's access channel
steps.desc: Search VPN/remote-access logs on the organization's side for connections from the vendor during the suspected compromise window.
steps.guidance: Look for anomalous session times, source IPs, or lateral movement following vendor connections.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether the breach reached organizational systems.

steps.title: Identify all systems reachable via the vendor's remote-access path
steps.desc: Map the network segments, servers, and applications accessible through the vendor's VPN/remote-access tunnel.

steps.title: Disable the vendor's VPN/remote-access account immediately
steps.desc: Suspend the vendor's remote-access credentials and firewall rules on the organization's side.
steps.guidance: Act on the org side regardless of vendor's own remediation timeline.
steps.outcome: Vendor remote access to organizational network severed.

steps.title: Hunt for lateral movement or persistence originating from the vendor connection
steps.desc: Search for indicators of compromise on systems reachable via the vendor's access path.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence or presence of lateral movement, with findings actioned.

steps.title: Notify Security leadership and vendor relationship manager
steps.desc: Escalate to Security leadership and the vendor relationship manager for coordinated response.

steps.title: Verify vendor's remediation of the breached access channel
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has closed the vulnerability or compromised credential path used to breach the VPN/remote-access system.
steps.abort: If unconfirmed, do not restore access.

steps.title: Rotate organization-side secrets exposed via the access path
steps.desc: Rotate any credentials, certificates, or keys reachable via the compromised remote-access channel.

steps.title: Reinstate vendor remote access under hardened controls
steps.desc: Restore access only with MFA, network segmentation, and session monitoring in place.

steps.title: Document incident and update remote-access vendor standards
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and revise remote-access requirements for vendors.

ITID-61221.def: A confirmed intrusion into a supplier's IT environment, where the supplier has direct network or system connectivity to the organization and the specific compromise vector has not yet been classified into a more specific sibling leaf.
ITID-61221.purpose: Provides an intake classification for confirmed intrusions into a supplier's systems that may pose a risk to the organization, before the specific compromise vector is identified.
scopeIncludes: Supplier notification of a confirmed intrusion into their environment
Threat intelligence indicating a supplier's systems are compromised prior to supplier confirmation
Intrusions where the vector (VPN, SaaS, MSP tooling) is not yet determined
scopeExcludes: Intrusions already confirmed as VPN/remote-access breaches (see ITID-61211)
Intrusions already confirmed as SaaS vendor compromise (see ITID-61231) or MSP breach (see ITID-61241)
ITID-61221.severity: High by default given direct connectivity risk to organizational systems.
ITID-61221.priority: P1 at intake pending vector confirmation.
ITID-61221.escalation: Escalate immediately to network security and third-party risk management to assess exposure and consider temporary connectivity isolation.
indicators: Supplier breach notification without specified vector
Threat intelligence reporting compromise of a known supplier
Unusual network traffic originating from supplier-connected network segments
vectors: Not yet determined pending classification
rootCauses: Insufficient network segmentation between supplier connections and core systems
Lack of continuous monitoring of supplier-facing network segments
controls: Network segmentation for all supplier connectivity
Continuous monitoring of supplier-facing network segments
Supplier security assessment program
ITID-61221.detection: Moderate: network monitoring at the organization's perimeter with supplier connections provides some signal; full picture depends on supplier disclosure.
ITID-61221.response: Isolate or restrict supplier connectivity pending investigation, and reclassify to a specific leaf once the compromise vector is confirmed.
metrics: Mean time to reclassify from intake to specific leaf
Number of supplier intrusions requiring connectivity isolation per year
ITID-61221.notes: This is the intake bucket for Supplier System Intrusion; reclassify once the specific vector (VPN, SaaS, MSP) is confirmed.

playbook.name: Supplier System Intrusion
playbook.description: A supplier's internal systems are intruded upon, creating risk to the organization through shared connectivity or data.

steps.title: Confirm supplier intrusion notification and scope
steps.desc: Validate the supplier's intrusion report and determine what systems and data at the supplier were affected.
steps.outcome: Confirmed intrusion scope at the supplier.

steps.title: Identify organizational touchpoints with the supplier
steps.desc: Inventory all integrations, shared credentials, data exchanges, and network connections between the organization and the supplier.
steps.outcome: Complete inventory of organizational exposure via the supplier.

steps.title: Review organizational logs for signs of compromise via supplier touchpoints
steps.desc: Examine logs for anomalous activity originating from or destined to supplier-connected systems.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether the intrusion has reached organizational systems.

steps.title: Isolate or restrict supplier connectivity to organizational systems
steps.desc: Disable or heavily restrict network connections, data feeds, and shared credentials with the supplier pending assessment.

steps.title: Rotate organization-side credentials shared with the supplier
steps.desc: Rotate any API keys, certificates, or account credentials used in the organization-supplier integration.

steps.title: Escalate to vendor relationship manager and Legal
steps.desc: Notify vendor relationship manager and Legal to invoke contractual incident-cooperation clauses.

steps.title: Verify supplier's eradication of the intrusion
steps.desc: Obtain evidence the supplier has removed attacker persistence and closed the intrusion vector.
steps.abort: If unconfirmed, maintain containment and consider alternate supplier.

steps.title: Conduct joint forensic review of shared systems if warranted
steps.desc: If organizational systems show compromise indicators, coordinate joint forensics with the supplier and internal IR team.
steps.outcome: Joint forensic findings documented and remediated.

steps.title: Restore supplier connectivity under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Reinstate integrations only once remediation is verified, with enhanced monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Connectivity restored with monitoring in place.

steps.title: Document incident and update supplier risk tier
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and adjust the supplier's risk classification and audit cadence.
steps.outcome: Report filed and risk tier updated.

ITID-61231.def: An incident in which a cloud-based SaaS vendor used by the organization has been compromised at the platform or tenant level, and the specific impact to the organization's data or operations has not yet been classified.
ITID-61231.purpose: Provides an intake classification for compromise of a cloud SaaS vendor whose platform the organization relies on, before downstream impact is fully assessed.
scopeIncludes: SaaS vendor notification of a platform-wide security incident
Compromise of the organization's tenant within a multi-tenant SaaS platform
Suspicious activity originating from a SaaS integration pending vendor confirmation
scopeExcludes: Compromise already attributed to a stolen credential (see ITID-61121) without platform-level compromise
Compromise of an on-premises or self-hosted vendor system (see Supplier System Intrusion)
ITID-61231.severity: High if the SaaS platform holds sensitive organizational data or has privileged integration access; Medium otherwise.
ITID-61231.priority: P1 if production data or integrations are affected; P2 otherwise.
ITID-61231.escalation: Escalate to the application/integration owner and third-party risk management immediately; consider suspending API integrations pending vendor confirmation.
indicators: SaaS vendor status page or security bulletin reporting an incident
Anomalous API activity from a SaaS integration
Unexpected data changes or exports within the organization's SaaS tenant
vectors: Compromise of the SaaS vendor's underlying infrastructure
Exploitation of a vulnerability in the SaaS application
Compromise of OAuth tokens or API keys used for SaaS integration
rootCauses: Overly broad OAuth/API scopes granted to SaaS integrations
Lack of tenant-level activity monitoring
Vendor's multi-tenant architecture lacking sufficient isolation
controls: Least-privilege OAuth/API scoping for SaaS integrations
SaaS tenant activity logging and monitoring (SSPM)
Vendor incident notification clauses in SaaS contracts
ITID-61231.detection: Moderate: SaaS Security Posture Management (SSPM) and API activity logs provide organization-side signal; full scope depends on vendor disclosure.
ITID-61231.response: Suspend or restrict affected integrations, review tenant activity logs for unauthorized access, and reclassify once impact is confirmed.
metrics: Number of SaaS vendor incidents affecting the organization's tenant per year
Mean time to suspend affected integrations
ITID-61231.notes: This is the intake bucket for Cloud SaaS Vendor Compromise; reclassify once the specific impact and mechanism are confirmed.

playbook.name: Cloud SaaS Vendor Compromise
playbook.description: A SaaS vendor used by the organization suffers a security compromise affecting the shared platform or tenant environment.

steps.title: Confirm SaaS vendor compromise notification
steps.desc: Validate the vendor's disclosure and determine whether the compromise is platform-wide or tenant-specific.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of the SaaS compromise.

steps.title: Determine organizational tenant exposure
steps.desc: Establish whether the organization's tenant/instance was affected and what data or configurations were exposed.
steps.guidance: Request vendor's tenant-specific impact assessment, not just the general disclosure.

steps.title: Review organizational admin and access logs within the SaaS platform
steps.desc: Examine the organization's own admin console logs for the SaaS platform for anomalous configuration changes or data access.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of anomalous activity within the tenant.

steps.title: Revoke and rotate organizational API keys and SSO tokens for the SaaS platform
steps.desc: Rotate all integration credentials, API tokens, and force re-authentication of SSO sessions for the affected SaaS platform.

steps.title: Restrict or disable non-essential integrations to the SaaS platform
steps.desc: Temporarily disable third-party app integrations and data exports connected to the SaaS platform pending assessment.

steps.title: Escalate to vendor relationship manager and Security leadership
steps.desc: Notify relevant stakeholders and request the vendor's incident response team engage directly.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders engaged and vendor IR team responding.

steps.title: Verify vendor's platform-wide remediation
steps.desc: Obtain evidence the vendor has closed the vulnerability/attack vector across the shared platform.
steps.abort: If not confirmed, maintain restricted integration state.

steps.title: Review and reset tenant configuration settings
steps.desc: Audit and reset tenant security configurations (SSO settings, admin roles, API scopes) to known-good baselines.

steps.title: Restore integrations and normal SaaS operations
steps.desc: Re-enable integrations and full functionality once remediation and configuration integrity are confirmed.

steps.title: Document incident and reassess SaaS vendor risk tier
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and update the vendor's risk rating and monitoring requirements.
steps.outcome: Report filed and risk tier updated.

ITID-61241.def: An incident in which an MSP providing IT or security services to the organization is compromised, viewed and classified through the lens of the trust relationship and network access the MSP holds into the organization's environment, rather than through the multi-client pivot/blast-radius lens.
ITID-61241.purpose: Classifies a breach at a Managed Service Provider (MSP) through the third-party-trust and network-compromise angle specific to supply-chain classification, distinct from the pivot-based multi-client compromise already tracked under ITID-54921.
scopeIncludes: Compromise of MSP-managed remote monitoring and management (RMM) tooling with access into the organization's network
MSP breach notification requiring review of the organization's specific trust and access grants to the MSP
Compromise of MSP-held administrative credentials scoped to the organization's environment
scopeExcludes: Cross-client pivot analysis and blast-radius assessment across multiple downstream victims of the same MSP breach — see ITID-54921 (MSP Breach Used as Pivot Point into Multiple Downstream Clients), which is the authoritative leaf for that multi-tenant angle
General SaaS vendor compromise not involving privileged remote-management access (see ITID-61231)
ITID-61241.severity: High by default, given the privileged administrative access MSPs typically hold.
ITID-61241.priority: P1, given the potential for direct administrative-level access into organizational systems.
ITID-61241.escalation: Escalate immediately to IT operations to review and, if warranted, revoke the MSP's administrative access pending investigation; cross-reference with ITID-54921 if multiple clients of the same MSP are known to be affected.
indicators: MSP notification of a security incident affecting their RMM platform
Unexpected administrative actions performed via MSP-held credentials
Threat intelligence naming the specific MSP as compromised
vectors: Compromise of MSP-managed RMM or PSA (professional services automation) tooling
Compromise of MSP administrative credentials
Supply-chain compromise of MSP-deployed software agents
rootCauses: Standing, overly broad administrative access granted to the MSP
Lack of independent monitoring of MSP-initiated administrative actions
No contractual requirement for the MSP to segregate per-client access
controls: Least-privilege, time-bound MSP administrative access
Independent monitoring/alerting on MSP-initiated administrative actions
Contractual requirement for per-client access segregation at the MSP
ITID-61241.detection: Moderate: privileged-access monitoring and administrative-action logging on the organization's side provide meaningful signal; full scope depends on MSP disclosure.
ITID-61241.response: Revoke or restrict MSP administrative access, audit all administrative actions taken via MSP accounts, and coordinate with ITID-54921 owners if this is part of a known multi-client MSP breach.
metrics: Number of MSP relationships with standing administrative access
Mean time to revoke MSP access upon breach notification
detections: Privileged-access monitoring on MSP administrative accounts
ITID-61241.notes: This is the intake/trust-angle bucket for MSP breaches under supply-chain classification. Cross-reference ITID-54921 for the multi-client pivot/blast-radius analysis rather than duplicating it here.

playbook.name: MSP Breach (Third-Party Network Compromise Context)
playbook.description: A managed service provider with administrative access to organizational systems is breached.

steps.title: Confirm MSP breach notification and urgency triage
steps.desc: Validate the MSP's breach disclosure and immediately triage as high-urgency given the MSP's typically broad administrative access.
steps.guidance: MSP breaches warrant faster escalation than typical vendor incidents due to privileged access scope.
steps.outcome: Breach confirmed and triaged as high priority.

steps.title: Inventory every organizational system and account the MSP can access
steps.desc: Compile a complete list of systems, admin accounts, RMM tools, and privileged credentials the MSP uses to manage the organization's environment.
steps.guidance: Include remote monitoring and management (RMM) tool access, domain admin accounts, and any backdoor/support accounts.

steps.title: Review logs across all MSP-managed systems for compromise indicators
steps.desc: Search authentication and administrative-action logs across every system the MSP touches for signs of unauthorized activity.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether the breach has propagated into organizational systems.

steps.title: Disable all MSP administrative access immediately
steps.desc: Suspend the MSP's domain admin accounts, RMM tool access, and any remote-management channels into organizational systems.
steps.guidance: Do not wait for MSP confirmation given the scope of typical MSP privilege.
steps.outcome: All MSP administrative access to organizational systems severed.

steps.title: Hunt for MSP-tool-based persistence or lateral movement
steps.desc: Search for malicious use of the RMM tool or other MSP-installed agents as an attacker foothold.
steps.outcome: Confirmed absence or presence of persistence mechanisms, with findings remediated.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership, Legal, and all affected business units
steps.desc: Given broad potential impact, escalate immediately to executive leadership and notify all business units relying on MSP-managed systems.
steps.outcome: Full organizational awareness and coordinated response.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials and certificates known or reachable by the MSP
steps.desc: Rotate domain admin credentials, service account passwords, and certificates the MSP had access to or could have exposed.

steps.title: Verify MSP's remediation and independently validate organizational systems are clean
steps.desc: Obtain MSP remediation evidence and conduct independent internal verification (not solely relying on MSP self-report) that organizational systems show no residual compromise.
steps.outcome: Independent verification of clean systems obtained.
steps.abort: If independent verification fails, escalate to full incident response and consider MSP replacement.

steps.title: Reinstate MSP access under revised, least-privilege terms
steps.desc: Restore only necessary MSP access with tightened scoping, MFA, and session recording, or transition to an alternate MSP.
steps.outcome: Access restored under hardened terms or contingency MSP activated.

steps.title: Document incident and reassess MSP dependency and access model
steps.desc: File a post-incident report evaluating the broader risk of centralized MSP administrative access and recommend architectural changes.
steps.outcome: Report filed with recommendations on limiting future MSP blast radius.

ITID-61311.def: The compromise of a software vendor's distribution artifact (installer, update package, container image, firmware bundle) such that malicious code reaches the organization through a channel it has already whitelisted, resulting in a critical, wide-blast-radius disruption once the tainted release is installed.
ITID-61311.purpose: Captures the moment a vendor's own build, packaging, or release pipeline is used to distribute malicious code inside a product the organization already trusts and has deployed at scale.
scopeIncludes: A signed vendor update or installer found to contain injected malicious code after release
A vendor's auto-update mechanism pushing a tainted build to production systems
Discovery that a previously-trusted vendor binary was tampered with between the vendor's build and its distribution to customers
scopeExcludes: Malicious code introduced via a compromised individual developer workstation prior to build (ITID-61312)
Exploitation of a known vulnerability in otherwise-legitimate vendor software (tracked under Third-Party Software Exploitation)
A newly published malicious open-source package masquerading as a legitimate one (ITID-61321)
ITID-61311.severity: Critical. This ITID exists specifically to capture events where a trusted distribution channel becomes an attack vector against many systems simultaneously, so severity defaults high even before scope is confirmed.
ITID-61311.priority: P1 immediately upon any credible indication that a currently-deployed vendor package is compromised, regardless of whether exploitation has yet been observed internally.
ITID-61311.escalation: Escalate to incident command, the vendor's security contact, and change/patch management simultaneously; treat as a potential mass-compromise event until the scope of affected internal systems is bounded.
indicators: Vendor security advisory disclosing a compromised release
Unexpected outbound network activity immediately following a vendor update
File hash mismatch between the vendor's published checksum and the installed binary
Threat intelligence reporting naming the vendor's supply chain as compromised
vectors: Compromise of the vendor's build server or release-signing infrastructure
Injection into a shared library the vendor statically links into its product
Tampering with an update package in transit or at a compromised CDN/mirror
rootCauses: Vendor lacking reproducible or verifiable builds
No internal verification of vendor package integrity (signature/hash checking) prior to deployment
Overly broad trust of vendor auto-update channels with no staged rollout
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Vendor binary/package integrity verification (signature and hash checking) prior to deployment
Staged/canary rollout of vendor updates before fleet-wide deployment
Vendor security advisory monitoring and rapid patch-triage process
ITID-61311.detection: Limited at the point of compromise since the artifact arrives through a trusted channel; detection typically relies on post-install behavioral anomalies or external advisory notification rather than pre-install controls.
ITID-61311.response: Immediately isolate systems running the affected version, halt further rollout of the update, and coordinate with the vendor on a validated remediation build before resuming deployment.
metrics: Time from vendor advisory to internal containment
Number of systems running an affected vendor build at time of disclosure
Mean time to validate a vendor-issued remediation
detections: File integrity monitoring on vendor-managed binaries
Outbound network anomaly detection following software updates
ITID-61311.notes: Distinguish this leaf from the parallel Third-Party Software Exploitation domain's dependency-confusion/typosquatting leaves: this ITID captures the critical-outage/business-impact consequence of a compromised vendor distribution, not the technical mechanism of the compromise itself, which is documented separately.

playbook.name: Malicious Code Injected into Vendor's Distributed Software Package
playbook.description: A vendor's distributed software package or update is found to contain maliciously injected code affecting downstream customers, including the organization.

steps.title: Confirm the malicious code report and affected package/version
steps.desc: Validate the vendor advisory or independent research identifying the malicious code, including exact package name, version, and injection point.
steps.guidance: Cross-check against vendor advisories, CVE databases, and security researcher publications.

steps.title: Determine where the affected package is deployed internally
steps.desc: Search internal software inventory, SBOMs, and package manifests to identify every system running the affected package/version.
steps.guidance: Use SBOM tooling or dependency scanning across all environments including build servers.
steps.outcome: Complete internal deployment inventory of the affected package.

steps.title: Analyze the malicious code behavior and indicators of compromise
steps.desc: Review vendor/researcher analysis of what the injected code does (data exfiltration, backdoor, C2 beaconing) and gather associated IOCs.
steps.outcome: IOC list and behavior profile obtained for detection use.

steps.title: Isolate or disable systems running the affected package
steps.desc: Network-isolate or take offline systems confirmed to run the compromised package version pending remediation.
steps.abort: If isolation would cause critical outage, apply compensating network controls (block C2 IOCs) instead.

steps.title: Block known indicators of compromise at network and endpoint layers
steps.desc: Deploy IOC blocks (C2 domains/IPs, file hashes) across firewalls, proxies, and EDR.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and secrets accessible to affected systems
steps.desc: Rotate any secrets, tokens, or credentials that were reachable by processes running the malicious code.

steps.title: Remove the malicious package and revert to a verified clean version
steps.desc: Uninstall the compromised package version and reinstall a vendor-verified clean version or apply the vendor's patched release.
steps.guidance: Verify package integrity via checksums/signatures before reinstalling.
steps.outcome: All instances of the malicious package removed and replaced.

steps.title: Forensically sweep affected systems for secondary persistence
steps.desc: Scan systems that ran the malicious package for dropped payloads, scheduled tasks, or other persistence mechanisms left behind.
steps.outcome: Systems confirmed free of secondary persistence.

steps.title: Restore affected systems to production with verification
steps.desc: Return isolated systems to production only after clean-version verification and persistence sweep pass.

steps.title: Assess and communicate downstream impact if applicable
steps.desc: Determine whether the injected code resulted in data exfiltration requiring customer or regulator notification.
steps.outcome: Notification decision documented and executed if required.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen software supply chain controls
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and recommend improvements such as package pinning, checksum verification, and SBOM monitoring.
steps.outcome: Report filed with control improvement recommendations.

ITID-61312.def: The introduction of malicious code into a vendor's codebase via a compromised developer workstation, IDE, source-control credential, or local build environment, such that the code is committed and later shipped as part of a legitimate release, producing a critical downstream disruption for organizations that consume that release.
ITID-61312.purpose: Captures malicious code that entered a vendor's software before it was ever built or packaged, because the attacker compromised a developer's environment or credentials upstream in the pipeline.
scopeIncludes: Malicious commits traced to a developer's stolen source-control credentials
A compromised developer laptop used to inject code prior to code review
A malicious local build tool or IDE plugin altering source before compilation
scopeExcludes: Tampering with an already-built release artifact after it leaves development (ITID-61311)
Compromise of the automated CI/CD orchestration system itself rather than an individual developer's environment (ITID-61341)
ITID-61312.severity: Critical, because code that passes through legitimate developer workflows is difficult to distinguish from genuine feature work and can persist through code review undetected.
ITID-61312.priority: P1 upon confirmation that a developer environment with commit access to a shipped product has been compromised.
ITID-61312.escalation: Escalate to the vendor's engineering security team and internal risk management the moment a developer-environment compromise is confirmed, even before malicious commits are identified.
indicators: Anomalous commit activity outside a developer's normal working pattern
Vendor disclosure of a compromised engineer account or workstation
Unexplained changes to build scripts or dependency manifests attributed to a known developer identity
vectors: Phishing or credential theft against a vendor's software engineers
Malware on a developer workstation with source-control access
Exposed developer API tokens enabling unauthorized commits
rootCauses: Vendor lacking mandatory code review for all commits
No hardware-token or phishing-resistant MFA on developer source-control accounts
Developer workstations not isolated from general-purpose internet browsing
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
controls: Mandatory peer code review on all commits reaching a release branch
Phishing-resistant MFA for source-control and build-system access
Endpoint detection on developer workstations with elevated monitoring
ITID-61312.detection: Weak from the customer side; detection realistically depends on the vendor's own internal controls and subsequent public disclosure rather than anything observable in the customer environment before impact.
ITID-61312.response: Treat as a supplier-side incident requiring vendor coordination; internally, focus on identifying and isolating all systems running code committed during the compromised window.
metrics: Number of vendor-disclosed developer-environment compromises per year
Time to identify internally-deployed versions affected by a disclosed compromise window
detections: Source-control anomalous-commit alerting (vendor-side, referenced via advisory)
ITID-61312.notes: Differentiated from ITID-61311 by injection point: this leaf is upstream of the build (developer environment), while 61311 is at or after packaging/distribution.

playbook.name: Malicious Code Injected via Compromised Developer Environment
playbook.description: A vendor's developer environment or build system is compromised, resulting in malicious code being injected into software delivered to the organization.

steps.title: Confirm vendor disclosure of compromised developer environment
steps.desc: Validate the vendor's advisory describing the compromised developer workstation, build environment, or signing process.
steps.outcome: Confirmed nature and scope of the developer-environment compromise.

steps.title: Determine which software versions/builds are potentially affected
steps.desc: Establish the build/release window during which the compromised environment could have injected malicious code.

steps.title: Inventory internal deployments within the affected build window
steps.desc: Identify all internal installations matching the affected build/version range.

steps.title: Isolate systems running potentially affected builds
steps.desc: Network-isolate or restrict systems running software from the suspect build window.

steps.title: Block indicators of compromise associated with the injected code
steps.desc: Deploy any available IOCs (hashes, C2 infrastructure) from the vendor advisory across security tooling.

steps.title: Verify vendor's re-signed/clean release and code-signing integrity restoration
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has re-established trusted code-signing and issued a verified clean release.
steps.guidance: Check signing certificate validity and any revocation of compromised signing keys.
steps.outcome: Vendor's clean release and signing integrity confirmed.
steps.abort: If unconfirmed, do not deploy vendor updates.

steps.title: Deploy the verified clean version and remove suspect builds
steps.desc: Replace all instances of the potentially affected build with the vendor-verified clean release.

steps.title: Sweep affected systems for persistence or secondary compromise
steps.desc: Conduct forensic sweeps on systems that ran the suspect build to detect any resulting compromise.

steps.title: Restore normal operations with the verified release
steps.desc: Return systems to production on the confirmed clean version.

steps.title: Document incident and evaluate build-provenance verification requirements
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and recommend requiring vendors to provide build provenance attestation (e.g., SLSA) going forward.
steps.outcome: Report filed with vendor requirement recommendations.

ITID-61313.def: A catch-all classification for malicious code discovered to have entered a vendor's product through the supply chain, used during initial triage before the specific injection point (distributed package vs. developer environment) has been determined.
ITID-61313.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for a confirmed malicious-code-injection event in the supply chain context that does not yet have enough information to classify as a distribution-artifact or developer-environment compromise.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported vendor code-injection incidents pending root-cause determination
Cases where available evidence does not yet distinguish build-artifact tampering from developer-environment compromise
scopeExcludes: Any case where the injection point has been confirmed as the distributed package (reclassify to ITID-61311)
Any case confirmed as originating in a developer environment (reclassify to ITID-61312)
ITID-61313.severity: Critical by default until root cause narrows the classification, consistent with the sibling leaves in this group.
ITID-61313.priority: P1 pending reclassification; do not let intake ambiguity delay containment actions.
ITID-61313.escalation: Escalate immediately as with any confirmed supply-chain code injection; reclassification to a specific sibling ITID should not block escalation or containment.
indicators: Initial detection of unexpected code behavior traced to a vendor product with root cause still under investigation
vectors: Unknown/unconfirmed pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial forensic detail to determine injection point
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Incident triage workflow requiring reclassification within a defined SLA once root cause is known
ITID-61313.detection: Not applicable as a distinct detection surface; this leaf exists for classification triage, not detection engineering.
ITID-61313.response: Handle with full supply-chain-compromise response urgency while root-cause investigation proceeds; reclassify promptly once the injection point is determined.
metrics: Number of incidents held in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
Average time to reclassification
ITID-61313.notes: This is an intake/triage leaf, not a distinct attack pattern; every incident logged here should be reclassified into ITID-61311 or ITID-61312 once root cause is established.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Malicious Code Injection (Supply Chain Context)
playbook.description: Malicious code is discovered injected into vendor-supplied software through an unspecified or unclassified vector.

steps.title: Confirm the malicious code discovery and affected software
steps.desc: Validate the report and identify the specific vendor software and version affected.

steps.title: Inventory internal deployments of the affected software
steps.desc: Identify all internal systems running the affected vendor software.

steps.title: Gather available indicators of compromise
steps.desc: Collect any IOCs published by the vendor or researchers related to the injected code.

steps.title: Isolate affected systems
steps.desc: Contain systems running the affected software pending remediation.

steps.title: Deploy available IOC blocks
steps.desc: Apply IOC blocks across network and endpoint security tooling.

steps.title: Remove malicious code and deploy vendor-verified clean version
steps.desc: Replace the affected software with a verified clean version once available from the vendor.

steps.title: Sweep for secondary persistence
steps.desc: Scan affected systems for dropped payloads or persistence mechanisms.

steps.title: Restore systems to production
steps.desc: Return remediated systems to normal operation.

steps.title: Document incident and update supply chain monitoring
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and recommend software supply chain monitoring improvements.

ITID-61321.def: The ingestion of a malicious package published under a name deceptively similar to a legitimate open-source library (typosquatting) into an organization's build or dependency chain, resulting in critical system disruption when the malicious code executes.
ITID-61321.purpose: Captures the moment a build system pulls in a newly-published, deliberately malicious package that impersonates a legitimate library, causing a critical disruption once it executes in production.
scopeIncludes: A build pipeline resolving a misspelled or confusingly-similar package name to a malicious registry entry
Post-incident discovery that a typosquatted package was present in a production dependency tree and caused an outage or breach
scopeExcludes: The technical mechanics of identifying and blocking typosquatted packages generally, which is tracked under the Third-Party Software Exploitation domain
Takeover of an existing legitimate package's maintainer account (ITID-61322)
Exploitation of internal package naming/resolution precedence (ITID-61323)
ITID-61321.severity: Critical when the typosquatted package reached production and executed; Medium if caught in a pre-production dependency scan before deployment.
ITID-61321.priority: P1 if the package executed in a production environment; P2 if intercepted pre-deployment.
ITID-61321.escalation: Escalate to application security and the owning engineering team immediately upon confirmation that a typosquatted package executed outside of a sandboxed build step.
indicators: Dependency scan flags a package name closely resembling a known legitimate library
Unexpected network calls or data exfiltration originating from a build or runtime process shortly after a new dependency is added
Registry takedown notice for a malicious package matching a name in the organization's dependency manifest
vectors: Publishing a malicious package under a name one character off from a popular library
Exploiting inconsistent package-name normalization across package managers
rootCauses: No automated dependency-name verification against an approved allowlist
Developers adding dependencies without verifying publisher identity or package provenance
Lack of a private, curated package mirror for common ecosystems
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Software composition analysis (SCA) scanning on every dependency addition
Curated internal package mirror/proxy restricting resolution to vetted packages
Package-name similarity detection tooling
ITID-61321.detection: Reasonably strong at the CI/CD stage via SCA tooling; weaker once the package has already executed in a production runtime.
ITID-61321.response: Remove the malicious package from all dependency manifests, rebuild and redeploy affected artifacts, and audit for any data or credential exposure during the window the package was live.
metrics: Number of typosquat packages blocked by SCA tooling per quarter
Time from malicious-package execution to detection
detections: Anomalous outbound network activity from build agents
ITID-61321.notes: Scoped here to the critical-outage/business-impact consequence of the typosquat reaching production; the technical exploitation mechanism (registry-name-squatting itself) is documented under the parallel Third-Party Software Exploitation Tier-2 category and should be cross-referenced rather than duplicated.

playbook.name: Typosquatted Malicious Package Published to Public Registry
playbook.description: A malicious package with a name similar to a legitimate library is published to a public package registry and inadvertently installed internally.

steps.title: Confirm the typosquatted package and installation within the organization
steps.desc: Validate the malicious package name, registry, and confirm whether it was installed in any internal project via dependency scanning.
steps.guidance: Search package manifests, lockfiles, and CI logs for the exact malicious package name and any near-miss typos.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether the typosquat package was installed internally.

steps.title: Determine which systems/builds pulled the malicious package
