mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Standardized tamper-inspection checklist at hardware receipt
Quarantine procedure for any ambiguous tampering report
ITID-61433.detection: Low; dependent on manual inspection at receipt.
ITID-61433.response: Quarantine the equipment and conduct a full inspection to reclassify to a specific sibling leaf.
metrics: Mean time to reclassify from intake to specific leaf
ITID-61433.notes: This is the intake bucket for Tampered Equipment in Transit; reclassify once inspection results are known.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Tampered Equipment in Transit
playbook.description: Equipment is suspected or confirmed tampered with while in transit, through an unspecified vector.

steps.title: Document the suspected tampering evidence
steps.desc: Capture and document any physical or logical evidence suggesting tampering occurred in transit.

steps.title: Reconstruct the shipment's chain of custody
steps.desc: Review tracking and handoff records to identify potential tampering points.

steps.title: Quarantine the equipment
steps.desc: Hold the equipment in isolated storage without deploying it into production.

steps.title: Notify vendor/carrier and escalate internally
steps.desc: Report the suspected tampering and escalate to Security and Legal for guidance.

steps.title: Conduct inspection to confirm or rule out tampering
steps.desc: Inspect the equipment to determine whether tampering actually occurred.

steps.title: Decide on disposition of the equipment
steps.desc: Based on findings, decide whether to accept, return, or destroy the equipment.

steps.title: Deploy verified replacement equipment if needed
steps.desc: Obtain and deploy verified, untampered equipment to fulfill the original need.

steps.title: Document incident and improve logistics security controls
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and recommend improved shipment security and inspection procedures.

ITID-61441.def: A defensive/remediation classification capturing the organization's coordinated response when a vendor issues a formal security recall for a batch of hardware found to be compromised, encompassing inventory identification, replacement, and disposal of affected units.
ITID-61441.purpose: Tracks the organization's response to a vendor-issued security recall covering an entire batch of compromised hardware, as a remediation event rather than an attack.
scopeIncludes: Vendor-issued recall notices identifying affected model/serial ranges
Organizational inventory reconciliation against the recall scope
Coordination of replacement unit deployment and secure disposal of recalled hardware
scopeExcludes: The original attack or compromise that prompted the recall (classified under the relevant Firmware Backdoors or Rogue IoT Devices leaf)
Emergency firmware-only remediation not involving physical hardware replacement (see ITID-61442)
ITID-61441.severity: Low from a threat perspective (this is a remediation activity), but High operational priority to ensure complete recall compliance.
ITID-61441.priority: P2, tracked to completion as a remediation project rather than an active incident.
ITID-61441.escalation: Escalate to procurement and asset management leadership if recall compliance falls behind the vendor's stated timeline.
indicators: Vendor security recall notice received
Asset inventory match against recalled serial/batch ranges
vectors: Compromised or defective component embedded in a hardware batch during manufacturing, discovered only after distribution
Recalled units already deployed and network-connected before the recall notice reaches the field
rootCauses: Underlying hardware compromise identified by the vendor (tracked under the originating attack ITID)
Extended time-to-recall completion due to incomplete asset inventory
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Asset inventory management enabling rapid recall-scope reconciliation
Vendor recall compliance tracking process
Secure disposal procedure for recalled hardware
ITID-61441.detection: Not applicable — this is a remediation-tracking classification, not a detection scenario.
ITID-61441.response: Reconcile inventory against the recall scope, deploy replacements, and securely dispose of or return recalled units per vendor instructions.
metrics: Percentage of recalled units identified and remediated
Mean time to full recall compliance
ITID-61441.notes: This leaf captures the vendor's/organization's remediation response, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: Vendor-Issued Security Recall of Compromised Hardware Batch
playbook.description: A vendor issues a security recall for a batch of hardware found to be compromised, affecting units deployed by the organization.

steps.title: Confirm the recall notice and affected units
steps.desc: Validate the vendor's recall notice and cross-reference against internal asset records to identify affected serial numbers/batches.
steps.outcome: Confirmed list of internally deployed affected units.

steps.title: Understand the nature and severity of the security defect
steps.desc: Review the vendor's technical bulletin to understand the specific vulnerability or compromise driving the recall.

steps.title: Prioritize and isolate high-risk affected units
steps.desc: Based on severity and network exposure, isolate or restrict the highest-risk affected units first.

steps.title: Establish a recall remediation project plan and timeline
steps.desc: Coordinate with the vendor and internal IT/OT teams to plan the recall remediation across all affected units.

steps.title: Apply vendor-provided remediation (patch, replacement, or repair)
steps.desc: Execute the vendor's prescribed remediation across all affected units per the recall notice.
steps.outcome: All affected units remediated per vendor instructions.

steps.title: Verify remediation completeness against the full affected inventory
steps.desc: Confirm every identified affected unit has completed remediation, with no units missed.
steps.outcome: 100% remediation coverage confirmed or gaps identified and closed.

steps.title: Restore full operation of remediated units
steps.desc: Return remediated units to normal production status.

steps.title: Confirm no exploitation occurred prior to remediation
steps.desc: Review logs from affected units for signs the vulnerability was exploited before remediation was applied.

steps.title: Document recall response and update recall-management procedures
steps.desc: File a post-incident report evaluating recall response time and completeness, and update the organization's vendor-recall response procedure.

ITID-61442.def: A defensive/remediation classification capturing the organization's coordinated deployment of an emergency firmware patch issued by a vendor to remediate a discovered security defect, distinct from a full hardware recall requiring physical unit replacement.
ITID-61442.purpose: Tracks the organization's coordination of an emergency vendor-issued firmware patch remediating a security defect, without requiring physical hardware replacement.
scopeIncludes: Vendor emergency firmware patch advisories and deployment tracking
Fleet-wide firmware version reconciliation to confirm patch application
Rollback or contingency planning if the emergency patch introduces operational issues
scopeExcludes: Full hardware recall requiring physical replacement (see ITID-61441)
The original vulnerability or compromise necessitating the patch (classified under the relevant attack ITID)
ITID-61442.severity: Low from a threat perspective (this is a remediation activity), but High operational priority given the emergency nature of the patch.
ITID-61442.priority: P1 for patch deployment speed, tracked as a remediation project.
ITID-61442.escalation: Escalate to IT operations leadership if patch deployment falls behind the vendor's recommended emergency timeline.
indicators: Vendor emergency firmware patch advisory received
Fleet firmware-version scan showing incomplete patch coverage
vectors: Vendor firmware distribution channel pushing a vulnerable or tampered image ahead of the emergency remediation release
Devices left exposed in the window between public vulnerability disclosure and emergency patch deployment
rootCauses: Underlying firmware vulnerability identified by the vendor (tracked under the originating attack ITID)
Delayed patch deployment due to change-control processes not accommodating emergency timelines
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Emergency change-control process for vendor security patches
Fleet-wide firmware version tracking and compliance scanning
Rollback and contingency planning for emergency patches
ITID-61442.detection: Not applicable — this is a remediation-tracking classification, not a detection scenario.
ITID-61442.response: Deploy the emergency patch across the affected fleet within the vendor's recommended timeline and confirm compliance via version scanning.
metrics: Percentage of fleet patched within vendor's recommended timeline
Mean time to full patch compliance
ITID-61442.notes: This leaf captures the vendor's/organization's remediation response, not an adversary technique.

playbook.name: Emergency Firmware Remediation Patch Deployed by Vendor
playbook.description: A vendor releases an emergency firmware patch to remediate a critical security issue in hardware deployed by the organization.

steps.title: Confirm the emergency patch advisory and affected devices
steps.desc: Validate the vendor's emergency patch advisory and identify which internally deployed devices are affected.

steps.title: Assess the urgency and exploitation status of the underlying vulnerability
steps.desc: Determine whether the vulnerability is under active exploitation and prioritize accordingly.
steps.outcome: Urgency level and exploitation status determined.

steps.title: Apply interim compensating controls pending patch deployment
steps.desc: Deploy network-level mitigations (segmentation, access restriction) for affected devices until the patch can be applied.

steps.title: Deploy the emergency firmware patch across all affected devices
steps.desc: Roll out the vendor's emergency patch to all identified affected devices, prioritizing highest-risk assets first.
steps.outcome: Patch deployed across affected device fleet.

steps.title: Verify successful patch installation on all devices
steps.desc: Confirm patch version/checksum on each affected device to ensure full deployment success.
steps.abort: If devices fail to patch, escalate for manual remediation or replacement.

steps.title: Remove interim compensating controls once patch is verified
steps.desc: Restore normal network access/configuration for patched devices.

steps.title: Confirm no exploitation occurred prior to patch deployment
steps.desc: Review available logs from affected devices for evidence the vulnerability was exploited before the emergency patch was applied.

steps.title: Document patch response time and update emergency-patch procedures
steps.desc: File a post-incident report assessing patch response speed and update the emergency-patching runbook.

ITID-61443.def: A defensive/remediation classification capturing vendor-issued device recall or remediation activity that does not specifically fall under a full hardware batch recall or an emergency firmware patch, such as configuration-only fixes or mixed remediation programs.
ITID-61443.purpose: Provides an intake/catch-all classification for vendor device recall and remediation activities that do not fit the specific hardware-recall or firmware-patch leaves.
scopeIncludes: Vendor remediation guidance involving configuration changes rather than hardware replacement or firmware patching
Mixed remediation programs combining multiple remediation types
Remediation activity pending classification into a more specific sibling leaf
scopeExcludes: Full hardware batch recalls (see ITID-61441)
Emergency firmware-only patches (see ITID-61442)
ITID-61443.severity: Low from a threat perspective; tracked for operational completeness.
ITID-61443.priority: P3, tracked as a remediation project.
ITID-61443.escalation: Escalate to asset management if remediation guidance is ambiguous or spans multiple remediation types.
indicators: Vendor remediation advisory not matching a full recall or firmware-only patch pattern
vectors: Generic vendor hardware defect or compromise prompting a recall that does not fit a more specific sub-category
Delayed or incomplete recall notification extending the exposure window for the affected device population
rootCauses: Underlying issue identified by the vendor (tracked under the originating attack ITID, if applicable)
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Vendor remediation tracking process covering all remediation types
ITID-61443.detection: Not applicable — this is a remediation-tracking classification, not a detection scenario.
ITID-61443.response: Execute the vendor's remediation guidance and reclassify to a more specific leaf if the remediation type becomes clear.
metrics: Number of miscellaneous remediation activities tracked per year
ITID-61443.notes: This leaf captures the vendor's/organization's remediation response, not an adversary technique. This is the catch-all bucket for Vendor Device Recall and Remediation.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Vendor Device Recall and Remediation
playbook.description: A vendor initiates a device recall or remediation action through an unspecified or unclassified mechanism.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor recall/remediation notice
steps.desc: Validate the notice and identify affected internal devices.

steps.title: Assess severity and urgency of the underlying issue
steps.desc: Determine the risk level driving the recall/remediation and prioritize response accordingly.

steps.title: Apply interim risk-reduction measures for affected devices
steps.desc: Restrict or isolate affected devices pending full remediation if risk warrants.

steps.title: Establish a remediation plan with the vendor
steps.desc: Coordinate timeline and process for applying the vendor's remediation across affected devices.

steps.title: Execute the vendor's remediation across affected devices
steps.desc: Apply the recall fix, patch, or replacement per vendor instructions.

steps.title: Verify remediation completeness
steps.desc: Confirm all affected devices have completed remediation.

steps.title: Restore normal operations
steps.desc: Return remediated devices to normal production use.

steps.title: Document response and update recall-handling procedures
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and refine the organization's vendor recall-response procedure.

ITID-61511.def: An individual employed or contracted by a vendor who knowingly and intentionally misuses their authorized access to the organization's systems, data, or infrastructure to cause harm, exfiltrate data, or facilitate a critical disruption.
ITID-61511.purpose: Captures a vendor employee or contractor who deliberately abuses their legitimate access to the organization's systems or data for malicious purposes.
scopeIncludes: A vendor employee deliberately exfiltrating customer data for personal gain or on behalf of a third party
A vendor contractor intentionally sabotaging systems they were granted access to service
scopeExcludes: Unintentional data exposure by a vendor employee (ITID-61521)
A vendor employee reusing a personal or previously-breached credential without malicious intent (ITID-61531)
Legitimate vendor access used beyond its intended scope without clear malicious intent (ITID-61541)
ITID-61511.severity: Critical, since a malicious insider with legitimate vendor-granted access can bypass most perimeter and authentication controls entirely.
ITID-61511.priority: P1 upon any confirmed evidence of intentional malicious action by a vendor-affiliated individual.
ITID-61511.escalation: Escalate to legal, HR-equivalent vendor contacts, and law enforcement liaison as appropriate; treat as a criminal matter alongside the technical incident response.
indicators: Vendor access used outside of normal working hours or scope with no legitimate business justification
Bulk data export by a vendor account inconsistent with the vendor's contracted function
Vendor employee termination coinciding with suspicious access activity
vectors: Abuse of standing, overly broad vendor access credentials
Vendor employee collusion with an external threat actor
Use of legitimate vendor tooling to move or exfiltrate data outside authorized channels
rootCauses: Vendor access not scoped to least privilege or the minimum needed for the contracted function
No behavioral monitoring on vendor accounts distinct from employee baselines
Vendor's own internal insider-threat controls not contractually verified
controls: Least-privilege, task-scoped access grants for all vendor personnel
Behavioral analytics/UEBA applied to vendor accounts
Contractual insider-threat and background-check requirements for vendor personnel with privileged access
ITID-61511.detection: Moderate when vendor accounts are included in behavioral monitoring; weak when vendor activity is excluded from standard UEBA baselining.
ITID-61511.response: Immediately revoke the individual's access, preserve logs and evidence, and coordinate with the vendor and legal counsel on investigation and any contractual or legal remedy.
metrics: Number of confirmed malicious-insider events involving vendor personnel per year
Time from anomalous activity to access revocation
detections: UEBA alerting scoped to vendor accounts
ITID-61511.notes: This is the sole leaf under Malicious Insider at a Vendor and serves as both the general and specific classification for intentional vendor-side insider malice.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Malicious Insider at a Vendor
playbook.description: A malicious insider employed by a vendor abuses their access to affect the organization's data or systems.

steps.title: Confirm the malicious insider report from the vendor
steps.desc: Validate the vendor's notification or internal detection identifying a malicious insider and the systems/data they had access to affecting the organization.
steps.outcome: Confirmed insider incident details relevant to the organization.

steps.title: Determine what organizational data/systems the insider could access
steps.desc: Map the insider's role and access scope against organizational data or systems reachable through the vendor relationship.

steps.title: Review activity logs for the insider's actions affecting the organization
steps.desc: Examine available logs (vendor-provided or organization-side) for the insider's specific actions against organizational assets.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope of malicious activity affecting the organization.

steps.title: Revoke the insider's access to organizational systems immediately
steps.desc: Disable any direct organizational-side access, accounts, or credentials associated with the insider.
steps.outcome: Insider access to organizational systems revoked.

steps.title: Coordinate with vendor HR/Legal on containment actions
steps.desc: Engage the vendor's HR and Legal teams to ensure the insider's access is also revoked on the vendor side and appropriate employment action is taken.

steps.title: Rotate credentials/secrets the insider may have accessed
steps.desc: Rotate any organizational credentials, keys, or shared secrets the insider could have accessed or exfiltrated.

steps.title: Assess scope of data exfiltration or damage caused
steps.desc: Work with the vendor to determine the full extent of data exfiltrated, altered, or destroyed by the insider.

steps.title: Verify vendor's remediation of related access-control gaps
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has addressed any access-control weaknesses that enabled the insider's actions.

steps.title: Determine and execute notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess with Legal/Privacy whether affected customers, employees, or regulators require notification.
steps.outcome: Notification decision made and executed if required.

steps.title: Resume vendor relationship under enhanced access controls
steps.desc: Restore vendor access under stricter least-privilege and monitoring controls, or transition to an alternate vendor if warranted.
steps.outcome: Relationship resumed with enhanced controls or vendor replaced.

steps.title: Document incident and update vendor personnel-vetting requirements
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and consider requiring vendor background-check and access-review attestations.
steps.outcome: Report filed with vendor requirement recommendations.

ITID-61521.def: A vendor employee's or contractor's unintentional action, such as misconfiguration, accidental data disclosure, or mishandling, that causes a critical disruption or data exposure despite no intent to harm the organization.
ITID-61521.purpose: Captures unintentional exposure or disruption caused by a vendor employee's honest mistake rather than any malicious intent.
scopeIncludes: A vendor employee misconfiguring a shared system component, exposing organizational data
Accidental disclosure of organizational data to the wrong recipient by a vendor employee
A vendor employee's mistaken action triggering an outage of a shared service
scopeExcludes: Deliberate, intentional misuse of access by a vendor employee (ITID-61511)
Credential reuse leading to compromise, which is a distinct control failure rather than an operational mistake (ITID-61531)
ITID-61521.severity: Medium to High depending on the sensitivity of data exposed or the scope of disruption caused; can reach Critical if the mistake exposes regulated data at scale or disrupts a critical shared service.
ITID-61521.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the exposure involves regulated data or a critical shared service outage.
ITID-61521.escalation: Escalate to the vendor's operations team for immediate correction and to privacy/legal if regulated data was exposed, even though no malicious actor is involved.
indicators: Vendor self-reported configuration error affecting the organization's environment
Data discovered exposed due to a vendor's misconfigured storage or access control
Vendor incident report attributing an outage to human error rather than attack
vectors: Not applicable — this is a human-error event, not an adversary-driven attack
rootCauses: Vendor lacking change-management controls (peer review, staged rollout) for configuration changes
Insufficient vendor training on data-handling procedures
No automated guardrails preventing common misconfiguration patterns
controls: Contractual requirement for vendor change-management and peer-review processes
Independent configuration monitoring on vendor-managed shared resources
Data-handling training requirements written into vendor contracts
ITID-61521.detection: Depends heavily on independent monitoring of vendor-managed resources rather than vendor self-reporting, since the vendor may not immediately recognize its own error.
ITID-61521.response: Work with the vendor to correct the misconfiguration or disclosure immediately, assess the scope of exposure, and pursue breach-notification obligations if regulated data was involved.
metrics: Number of vendor-caused accidental exposure events per year
Time from vendor error to correction
detections: Independent configuration drift monitoring on vendor-managed resources
ITID-61521.notes: human error, not an adversary technique — mapped_mitre_tactics and mapped_mitre_techniques are intentionally empty for this leaf, distinguishing it from ITID-61511 (deliberate malice) and ITID-61531 (credential-reuse control failure).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Accidental Insider Breach (Vendor Context)
playbook.description: A vendor employee accidentally exposes or mishandles organizational data through error rather than malicious intent.

steps.title: Confirm the accidental exposure report and root cause
steps.desc: Validate the vendor's disclosure of the accidental exposure (misdirected email, misconfigured share, lost device) and confirm the cause.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exposure details and root cause.

steps.title: Determine the organizational data involved and its sensitivity
steps.desc: Establish what organizational data was exposed and its sensitivity classification.

steps.title: Assess whether the exposure was viewed or further disseminated
steps.desc: Determine whether the accidentally exposed data was accessed, downloaded, or forwarded by unintended recipients.

steps.title: Request recall or deletion of the exposed data where possible
steps.desc: Ask the vendor and any unintended recipients to delete or return the exposed data, and revoke any shared-link access.

steps.title: Notify vendor relationship manager and Privacy team
steps.desc: Brief the vendor relationship manager and Privacy team on the incident for coordinated handling.

steps.title: Verify vendor's corrective action on the underlying process error
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has addressed the process gap that led to the accidental exposure (e.g., added DLP controls, retrained staff).

steps.title: Determine and execute notification obligations if applicable
steps.desc: Assess with Legal/Privacy whether notification of affected individuals or regulators is required based on data sensitivity.
steps.outcome: Notification decision made and executed if required.

steps.title: Resume normal data-sharing operations with the vendor
steps.desc: Continue the vendor relationship once corrective actions are verified.

steps.title: Document incident and recommend data-handling safeguards
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and recommend contractual or technical data-handling safeguards (DLP, encryption, access reviews) for the vendor relationship.

ITID-61531.def: The use of a supplier/vendor employee's password across multiple services, such that a credential breach unrelated to the organization (e.g., a third-party website leak) is reused by an attacker to gain unauthorized access to the organization's systems through the vendor's legitimate account.
ITID-61531.purpose: Captures the specific control failure where a supplier employee reuses a compromised or previously-breached credential, giving an attacker access without any insider intent at all.
scopeIncludes: A vendor account compromised via credential-stuffing using a password previously leaked from an unrelated breach
Confirmed reuse of a vendor employee's personal password for organizational or vendor-platform access
scopeExcludes: Deliberate, malicious misuse of vendor access (ITID-61511)
Accidental misconfiguration or disclosure with no credential compromise involved (ITID-61521)
ITID-61531.severity: High, escalating to Critical if the reused credential had access to critical systems or sensitive data with no compensating control such as MFA.
ITID-61531.priority: P1 upon confirmation of unauthorized access via credential reuse; P2 if detected and blocked by MFA or anomaly detection before access was achieved.
ITID-61531.escalation: Escalate to the vendor immediately to force a credential reset and to internal security to assess the scope of access the compromised account held.
indicators: Login attempt matching a known credential-stuffing list or leaked-password database
Vendor account login from an unusual geography or device shortly after a public breach disclosure involving that individual
Vendor self-report of a personal account compromise coinciding with anomalous platform access
vectors: Credential-stuffing attacks using breached password databases
Password reuse across a vendor employee's personal and work-related accounts
rootCauses: No mandatory MFA enforced on vendor accounts
Vendor lacking a password-reuse policy or breached-password screening
No contractual requirement for vendor identity/credential hygiene standards
controls: Mandatory MFA on all vendor accounts with access to organizational systems
Breached-password screening for vendor account credentials where technically feasible
Contractual credential-hygiene requirements for vendor personnel
ITID-61531.detection: Moderate; credential-stuffing and impossible-travel detection can catch this pattern if vendor accounts are included in the same monitoring scope as employee accounts.
ITID-61531.response: Force immediate credential reset, enforce MFA if not already present, and review all activity performed under the compromised account during the exposure window.
metrics: Percentage of vendor accounts with MFA enforced
Number of credential-reuse compromises detected per year
detections: Impossible-travel / anomalous-login alerting on vendor accounts
ITID-61531.notes: This is the sole leaf under Supplier Employee Credential Reuse and serves as both the general and specific classification for this control failure, distinct from intentional insider malice (ITID-61511).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Supplier Employee Credential Reuse
playbook.description: A supplier employee's reused credentials (compromised elsewhere) are used to access organizational systems.

steps.title: Confirm credential reuse as the access vector
steps.desc: Validate that the supplier employee's credentials were compromised via reuse (e.g., from an unrelated third-party breach) and used to access organizational systems.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference credential-stuffing/breach-database indicators with the affected account.

steps.title: Review access and activity logs for the affected account
steps.desc: Examine organizational logs for the supplier account's login history and actions during the suspected compromise window.

steps.title: Identify all organizational systems accessible to the affected account
steps.desc: Map the full access scope of the supplier employee's organizational account.

steps.title: Disable the affected account and force credential reset
steps.desc: Immediately disable the compromised supplier account and require a new, unique credential with MFA before reinstatement.
steps.outcome: Account disabled and reset process initiated.

steps.title: Notify the supplier and vendor relationship manager
steps.desc: Inform the supplier of the compromised employee credential and coordinate on their internal response.

steps.title: Rotate any organizational secrets the account could access
steps.desc: Rotate credentials, tokens, or data reachable via the compromised account.

steps.title: Enforce MFA and unique-credential policy for all supplier accounts
steps.desc: Require MFA and prohibit shared/reused credentials for all supplier accounts as a condition of continued access.
steps.outcome: Enhanced authentication policy enforced for supplier accounts.

steps.title: Reinstate access under the hardened authentication policy
steps.desc: Restore the supplier employee's access only after MFA and unique credentials are confirmed in place.

steps.title: Document incident and update supplier account security requirements
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and formalize MFA/unique-credential requirements in supplier access agreements.

ITID-61541.def: The use of a vendor employee's or contractor's legitimately-granted privileged access to perform actions outside the scope of their contracted function, such as accessing data or systems not required for their role, regardless of whether clear malicious intent can be established.
ITID-61541.purpose: Captures a vendor individual using their legitimately-granted access beyond its intended scope, without necessarily rising to clear malicious intent or being a simple accident.
scopeIncludes: A vendor support engineer accessing customer data unrelated to an open support ticket
A vendor administrator using elevated access to browse systems outside their assigned engagement
scopeExcludes: Access clearly intended to cause harm or exfiltrate data for gain, which should be classified as deliberate malice (ITID-61511)
An honest configuration mistake with no scope-of-access issue involved (ITID-61521)
ITID-61541.severity: Medium-High, escalating to Critical if the out-of-scope access involved sensitive or regulated data.
ITID-61541.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if intent cannot be quickly ruled out or if sensitive data was accessed.
ITID-61541.escalation: Escalate to the vendor's account management team and internal privacy/legal function to determine scope of access and whether notification obligations apply.
indicators: Vendor account access to systems or records outside the scope of an active engagement or ticket
Access-log review revealing a pattern of vendor access inconsistent with contracted duties
vectors: Overly broad standing access grants that exceed the vendor's contracted function
Lack of ticket-scoped or just-in-time access enforcement for vendor support activity
rootCauses: Vendor access provisioned by role/team rather than by specific task or ticket
No periodic access review comparing granted vendor permissions to actual contracted scope
Vendor internal policies not contractually aligned with the customer's least-privilege expectations
controls: Just-in-time, ticket-scoped access provisioning for vendor support and administrative activity
Periodic access review comparing vendor permissions to contracted scope
Session recording/monitoring for privileged vendor access
ITID-61541.detection: Moderate when vendor access is tied to ticketing systems, enabling automated comparison of access to authorized scope; weak with standing, unscoped access grants.
ITID-61541.response: Investigate the scope and purpose of the out-of-scope access, restrict the vendor's access to the minimum needed going forward, and determine whether notification obligations apply.
metrics: Number of out-of-scope vendor access events identified per quarter
Percentage of vendor access provisioned on a just-in-time basis
ITID-61541.notes: This is the sole leaf under Vendor Privilege Abuse and is deliberately positioned between clear malicious intent (ITID-61511) and honest accident (ITID-61521) — it covers scope-of-access violations where intent is ambiguous or investigation is still needed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Vendor Privilege Abuse
playbook.description: A vendor employee or system abuses granted privileges to access data or perform actions beyond their authorized scope.

steps.title: Confirm the privilege abuse report
steps.desc: Validate the report identifying which vendor account exceeded its authorized scope and what actions were taken.

steps.title: Review the vendor account's granted permissions versus actual usage
steps.desc: Compare the account's provisioned access scope against the actions and data actually accessed.

steps.title: Determine whether the abuse was intentional or a provisioning error
steps.desc: Assess whether the excess access resulted from deliberate misuse or an overly broad access grant, to guide response severity.

steps.title: Restrict the vendor account to its intended least-privilege scope
steps.desc: Immediately reduce the account's permissions to only what is contractually authorized.

steps.title: Notify vendor relationship manager and, if intentional, escalate to Legal
steps.desc: Inform relevant stakeholders; escalate to Legal if the abuse appears intentional or contractually significant.

steps.title: Audit for downstream impact of the excess access
steps.desc: Determine whether any data was improperly accessed, exported, or modified as a result of the excess privilege.
steps.outcome: Impact of the privilege abuse documented.

steps.title: Verify vendor's corrective action on access-provisioning process
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor (or internal provisioning team) has corrected the process that allowed excess privilege to be granted or exploited.

steps.title: Resume vendor operations under corrected, least-privilege access
steps.desc: Continue the vendor relationship with verified least-privilege access and periodic access review.
steps.outcome: Vendor access normalized under corrected model.

steps.title: Document incident and implement periodic vendor access reviews
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and establish or reinforce periodic access-entitlement reviews for all vendor accounts.
steps.outcome: Report filed and review cadence established.

ITID-61611.def: A vendor's lapse or failure to renew a security certification (such as SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001) that was contractually required as a condition of the vendor relationship, constituting a compliance violation to be tracked and remediated through legal and vendor-management channels rather than as a technical security incident.
ITID-61611.purpose: Captures a vendor's failure to maintain a required security certification, creating a governed compliance gap distinct from any specific technical control failure.
scopeIncludes: A vendor's SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification lapsing without renewal during an active contract term
Discovery that a vendor never held a certification it represented as current during contracting or renewal
scopeExcludes: A vendor holding valid certification but failing to implement a specific contractually-required control (ITID-61612)
A vendor's technical security incident unrelated to certification status, tracked elsewhere in this taxonomy
ITID-61611.severity: Medium-High from a compliance-risk standpoint; the organization's actual technical risk exposure depends on the underlying controls, but the contractual/compliance violation itself is a governance failure warranting formal tracking regardless of technical impact.
ITID-61611.priority: P2 for compliance/legal tracking purposes, escalating to P1 if the lapsed certification coincides with a security incident or if a regulatory filing deadline is at risk.
ITID-61611.escalation: Escalate to legal, vendor management, and the compliance/GRC function; this is a contractual remedy and risk-acceptance matter, not a SOC technical response.
indicators: Annual vendor compliance review revealing an expired or unrenewed certification
Vendor's certification-tracking portal showing a lapsed status
Vendor unable to produce a current audit report upon request
vectors: Vendor's SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification lapsed or was never renewed while the vendor retained privileged access or data-processing responsibilities
Organization relied on an outdated audit report without independent re-verification of continued control effectiveness
rootCauses: Vendor management program lacking a systematic certification-expiry tracking process
Contract renewal not gated on current proof of certification
Vendor's own internal audit program failing to sustain certification renewal
controls: Contractual requirement to maintain and provide evidence of specified certifications throughout the contract term
Automated certification-expiry tracking in the vendor management system
Annual vendor compliance attestation review
ITID-61611.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; detection is a compliance/governance process (certification tracking and periodic review), not a SOC monitoring capability.
ITID-61611.response: Formally notify the vendor of the lapse, require a remediation timeline or interim compensating evidence, and escalate to contract enforcement or termination review if not resolved within the contractual grace period.
metrics: Percentage of vendors with current, contractually-required certifications
Average time to remediate a lapsed vendor certification
ITID-61611.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. Differentiated from ITID-61612 by axis: this leaf is about certification status/renewal, not implementation of a specific control.

playbook.name: Vendor Failed to Maintain Required Security Certification (SOC 2/ISO 27001)
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have let a contractually required security certification (SOC 2, ISO 27001) lapse or fail.

steps.title: Confirm how the certification lapse/failure was discovered
steps.desc: Document the discovery source (annual vendor review, audit, vendor self-disclosure, certifying body notice) and the certification status details.
steps.outcome: Discovery method and certification status documented.

steps.title: Review the contract for the specific certification requirement and remedy clauses
steps.desc: Pull the governing contract to confirm the exact certification obligation and any remedy, cure period, or termination clauses tied to non-compliance.

steps.title: Assess current risk exposure from the vendor given the lapsed certification
steps.desc: Evaluate what data/systems the vendor accesses and the practical risk increase from the certification gap, rather than assuming certification lapse equals compromise.

steps.title: Notify vendor relationship manager and Procurement of the compliance gap
steps.desc: Formally notify relevant internal stakeholders and initiate the vendor risk management gap-tracking process.

steps.title: Request the vendor's corrective action plan and target re-certification date
steps.desc: Formally request the vendor provide a written corrective action plan and timeline to restore certification.
steps.abort: If vendor is unresponsive, escalate to Legal for contractual remedy.

steps.title: Determine whether to continue, suspend, or terminate the vendor relationship pending recertification
steps.desc: Based on risk exposure and criticality, decide with Procurement/Legal whether to continue operations, restrict scope, or invoke contractual remedies.

steps.title: Monitor vendor's progress toward recertification
steps.desc: Track the vendor's corrective action plan milestones until recertification is achieved.

steps.title: Verify recertification and update vendor risk record
steps.desc: Obtain and validate the renewed certification documentation, then update the vendor's compliance status in the risk register.
steps.outcome: Recertification confirmed and risk register updated.

steps.title: Document the gap and strengthen certification-monitoring cadence
steps.desc: File a report on the compliance gap and recommend more frequent certification-expiration monitoring for all vendors.
steps.outcome: Report filed and monitoring cadence improved.

ITID-61612.def: A vendor's failure to implement one or more specific security controls that were explicitly required under the terms of its contract with the organization, discovered through audit, incident investigation, or vendor self-disclosure, and tracked as a contractual compliance violation.
ITID-61612.purpose: Captures a vendor's failure to actually implement a specific security control that the contract required, independent of whether the vendor otherwise holds valid certifications.
scopeIncludes: A vendor contractually required to encrypt data at rest found not to have implemented encryption
A right-to-audit finding that a contractually mandated control (e.g., MFA, logging retention) was never implemented
scopeExcludes: A vendor's certification itself lapsing or not being renewed (ITID-61611)
General vendor security gaps not tied to an explicit contractual requirement, tracked under Vendor Risk Management Failures
ITID-61612.severity: High, since a missing contractually-required control represents both a compliance violation and a concrete gap in the organization's actual risk posture.
ITID-61612.priority: P2 for tracking and remediation, escalating to P1 if the missing control is directly relevant to an active or recent security incident.
ITID-61612.escalation: Escalate to legal and vendor management for contractual remedy; loop in the SOC only if the missing control created a specific, currently-exploitable exposure requiring technical mitigation.
indicators: Right-to-audit assessment finding a contractually required control absent
Vendor unable to produce evidence of an attested control during a compliance review
A security incident investigation revealing a missing control that was contractually mandated
vectors: Vendor omitted or silently disabled a contractually mandated control (e.g., MFA, encryption at rest) without the organization's knowledge
No independent compliance-verification mechanism existed to catch the control gap before it was exploited or found in audit
rootCauses: Contract requirements not translated into an actionable, verifiable control checklist
No periodic control-verification audit distinct from certification-status checks
Vendor prioritizing cost savings over compliance with lower-visibility contractual requirements
controls: Periodic right-to-audit exercises verifying specific contractual controls, not just certification status
Contract clauses with clear, verifiable control specifications and remediation timelines
Vendor risk register tracking control-specific compliance status
ITID-61612.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; identified through audit and contractual review processes rather than SOC monitoring.
ITID-61612.response: Formally document the gap, require a remediation plan with a defined timeline, and consider compensating controls or contract remedies (penalties, termination rights) if unresolved.
metrics: Number of contractual control gaps identified per audit cycle
Average remediation time for identified control gaps
ITID-61612.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. Differentiated from ITID-61611 by axis: this leaf is about specific control implementation, not overall certification status.

playbook.name: Vendor Failed to Implement Contractually Required Security Controls
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have not implemented specific security controls required under the governing contract.

steps.title: Document how the control gap was discovered
steps.desc: Record the discovery source (audit, penetration test finding, vendor questionnaire, incident) and the specific missing control(s).
steps.outcome: Discovery method and specific gap documented.

steps.title: Confirm the contractual requirement for the missing control
steps.desc: Review the contract/security addendum to confirm the specific control was contractually mandated.

steps.title: Assess risk exposure created by the missing control
steps.desc: Evaluate the practical security risk posed by the absent control given the vendor's access and data handling.

steps.title: Notify vendor relationship manager and issue formal non-compliance notice
steps.desc: Formally notify the vendor of the contractual non-compliance and the requirement to remediate.

steps.title: Apply compensating controls on the organization's side if feasible
steps.desc: Where possible, implement compensating controls on the organizational side of the integration to reduce exposure while the vendor remediates.
steps.outcome: Interim risk reduction achieved where feasible.

steps.title: Obtain and validate the vendor's remediation plan and timeline
steps.desc: Require the vendor to submit a corrective action plan implementing the missing control, with a defined timeline.
steps.abort: If vendor refuses or delays unreasonably, escalate to Legal for contractual remedy.

steps.title: Verify the control has been implemented
steps.desc: Independently verify (via audit, evidence review, or re-assessment) that the required control is now in place and functioning.

steps.title: Update vendor risk record and remove compensating controls if applicable
steps.desc: Update the vendor's compliance status and remove any temporary compensating controls once the required control is confirmed in place.
steps.outcome: Vendor risk record updated and normal operations resumed.

steps.title: Document the gap and strengthen contract-compliance verification
steps.desc: File a report and recommend periodic control-attestation audits rather than relying solely on contract language.

ITID-61613.def: A catch-all classification for a vendor security-standards non-compliance finding used during initial triage before the specific pattern (certification lapse vs. specific control failure) is determined.
ITID-61613.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for a vendor non-compliance-with-security-standards finding that has not yet been narrowed to certification lapse or specific control failure.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported vendor compliance findings pending categorization among the sibling patterns in this group
scopeExcludes: Any case confirmed as a certification lapse (ITID-61611)
Any case confirmed as a specific contractual control failure (ITID-61612)
ITID-61613.severity: Medium-High by default, consistent with the sibling leaves, until the finding is further categorized.
ITID-61613.escalation: Escalate to compliance/legal and vendor management as with any confirmed non-compliance finding; reclassification should not delay the remediation-tracking process.
indicators: Initial compliance review finding pending categorization
vectors: Generic vendor non-compliance with an agreed security standard not captured by a more specific sub-category
Absence of a standardized compliance-scoring process allows marginal non-compliance to go undetected until escalation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine the specific non-compliance pattern
controls: Compliance triage workflow requiring reclassification within a defined SLA
ITID-61613.detection: Not applicable; this is a compliance/governance triage leaf, not a technical detection surface.
ITID-61613.response: Track through the standard vendor compliance remediation process while categorization proceeds; reclassify promptly once determined.
metrics: Number of findings held in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
ITID-61613.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. This is an intake/triage leaf; every finding logged here should be reclassified into a specific sibling ITID once determined.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Non-Compliance with Security Standards
playbook.description: A vendor is found non-compliant with a required security standard through an unspecified or unclassified mechanism.

steps.title: Document how the non-compliance was discovered
steps.desc: Record the discovery source and nature of the non-compliance.

steps.title: Confirm the applicable contractual/regulatory requirement
steps.desc: Verify the specific standard or requirement the vendor is non-compliant with.

steps.title: Assess risk exposure from the non-compliance
steps.desc: Evaluate the practical risk to the organization created by the vendor's non-compliance.

steps.title: Notify vendor relationship manager and issue formal notice
steps.desc: Formally notify the vendor and internal stakeholders of the non-compliance finding.
steps.outcome: Formal notice issued and stakeholders informed.

steps.title: Obtain the vendor's corrective action plan
steps.desc: Require the vendor to submit a plan and timeline to achieve compliance.
steps.abort: If vendor refuses, escalate to Legal/Procurement for contractual remedy.

steps.title: Verify compliance has been achieved
steps.desc: Independently verify the vendor has achieved compliance with the required standard.

steps.title: Update vendor risk record
steps.desc: Update the vendor's compliance status and risk rating based on verified findings.

steps.title: Document the gap and improve compliance-monitoring processes
steps.desc: File a report and recommend improved ongoing vendor compliance monitoring.

ITID-61621.def: A vendor's failure to comply with GDPR obligations (lawful basis for processing, data subject rights, breach notification timelines, data minimization, etc.) with respect to personal data the vendor processes on the organization's behalf, constituting a regulatory compliance violation.
ITID-61621.purpose: Captures a vendor's violation of the EU General Data Protection Regulation involving the organization's customer data, framed as a legal/privacy compliance matter.
scopeIncludes: A vendor processing EU personal data without a valid lawful basis or outside the scope of the data processing agreement
A vendor failing to honor a data subject access, deletion, or portability request within GDPR-mandated timelines
scopeExcludes: A US state privacy law violation (ITID-61622)
A cross-border data transfer mechanism failure not itself a GDPR substantive-processing violation (ITID-61623)
ITID-61621.severity: High to Critical depending on the number of data subjects affected and whether the violation involves special-category data, given GDPR's significant financial penalty exposure.
ITID-61621.priority: P1 if the violation carries a regulatory notification deadline or affects a large volume of EU data subjects; P2 otherwise pending legal assessment.
ITID-61621.escalation: Escalate immediately to Data Protection Officer/privacy counsel and vendor management; GDPR notification deadlines are short and legally binding regardless of technical severity.
indicators: Vendor audit or DPIA revealing non-compliant processing activity
Data subject complaint escalated through a supervisory authority naming the vendor
Vendor unable to demonstrate a documented lawful basis for a specific processing activity
vectors: Vendor processed or stored EU customer personal data without a lawful basis or required technical/organizational safeguards
Sub-processor engaged by the vendor without a data protection impact assessment or valid transfer mechanism
rootCauses: Data processing agreement not kept current with the vendor's actual processing activities
Vendor lacking a mature GDPR compliance program despite processing EU personal data
No periodic privacy audit of vendor processing activities
controls: Data processing agreements with explicit GDPR compliance obligations and audit rights
Periodic privacy impact assessments covering vendor processing activities
Vendor data-subject-request handling SLA tracking
ITID-61621.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; identified through privacy audits, DPIAs, and regulatory/complaint channels rather than SOC monitoring.
ITID-61621.response: Engage privacy counsel to assess notification obligations, require the vendor to remediate the processing activity, and document the response for regulatory defensibility.
metrics: Number of GDPR-related vendor findings per year
Average time to remediate a vendor GDPR compliance gap
ITID-61621.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. Differentiated from siblings by jurisdiction/regulation: this leaf is specifically GDPR (EU).

playbook.name: Vendor GDPR Violation Affecting Customer Data
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have violated GDPR requirements in its handling of the organization's customer data.

steps.title: Document how the GDPR violation was identified
steps.desc: Record the discovery source (vendor disclosure, DPA audit, regulator inquiry, data subject complaint) and nature of the violation.
steps.outcome: Discovery details and violation nature documented.

steps.title: Determine the specific GDPR obligation violated and data subjects affected
steps.desc: Identify the exact GDPR article/obligation breached (e.g., processing basis, sub-processor notification, data transfer) and the EU data subjects affected.
steps.guidance: Engage Data Protection Officer (DPO) for classification.

steps.title: Assess the organization's own downstream liability exposure
steps.desc: With Legal/DPO, determine whether the organization (as controller) bears independent notification or liability exposure from the vendor's (processor's) violation.

steps.title: Notify Legal, Privacy/DPO, and vendor relationship manager
steps.desc: Escalate the violation to Legal, the DPO, and the vendor relationship manager for coordinated response.

steps.title: Suspend the specific processing activity if ongoing violation risk exists
steps.desc: Pause the data processing activity tied to the violation if it is ongoing, pending vendor correction.
steps.outcome: Ongoing violation risk halted if applicable.

steps.title: Require vendor corrective action plan for GDPR compliance
steps.desc: Obtain a formal corrective action plan from the vendor addressing the specific violation and preventing recurrence.
steps.abort: If vendor is uncooperative, escalate to Legal for DPA enforcement or contract termination review.

steps.title: Verify the vendor's corrective actions are implemented
steps.desc: Independently verify the vendor has implemented the corrective measures.

steps.title: Determine and execute regulator/data-subject notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess with Legal/DPO whether the organization must notify the supervisory authority or affected data subjects within GDPR's 72-hour or other applicable window.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations determined and executed within required timelines.

steps.title: Resume or renegotiate processing activity under updated DPA terms
steps.desc: Resume the processing relationship once compliant, updating the Data Processing Agreement as needed.
steps.outcome: Processing resumed under updated, compliant terms.

steps.title: Document incident and update vendor GDPR compliance monitoring
steps.desc: File a report and strengthen ongoing GDPR compliance monitoring and audit rights for data-processing vendors.

ITID-61622.def: A vendor's failure to comply with an applicable US state privacy law's obligations (consumer rights to know, delete, opt out of sale/sharing, etc.) with respect to personal information the vendor processes on the organization's behalf, constituting a regulatory compliance violation.
ITID-61622.purpose: Captures a vendor's violation of a US state privacy law (such as CCPA/CPRA) involving the organization's customer data, framed as a legal/privacy compliance matter.
scopeIncludes: A vendor failing to honor a California consumer's right to delete or opt-out request within the statutory timeline
A vendor selling or sharing personal information in a manner inconsistent with the organization's posted privacy notice
scopeExcludes: A GDPR (EU) violation (ITID-61621)
A cross-border data transfer mechanism failure (ITID-61623)
ITID-61622.severity: High, given statutory penalty exposure and the reputational impact of a state-privacy-law violation attributed to the organization's own customer-facing privacy notice.
ITID-61622.priority: P1 if consumer rights requests are being systematically mishandled or a regulator inquiry is received; P2 for isolated findings pending legal assessment.
ITID-61622.escalation: Escalate to privacy counsel and vendor management immediately; state privacy laws carry statutory response deadlines for consumer rights requests.
indicators: Consumer complaint escalated regarding an unhonored rights request tied to a vendor
Vendor audit revealing sale/sharing of personal information inconsistent with contractual restrictions
State attorney general or privacy agency inquiry naming the vendor
vectors: Vendor sold or shared California consumer data without honoring opt-out / do-not-sell requests
Vendor retained consumer data beyond the retention period disclosed in its privacy notice
rootCauses: Vendor contract not updated to reflect current state privacy law service-provider restrictions
No process to relay and verify consumer rights request fulfillment through the vendor
Vendor's own data-sale practices not adequately reviewed at onboarding
controls: Service-provider/contractor clauses meeting state privacy law requirements in vendor contracts
Consumer rights request relay-and-verification process with the vendor
Periodic review of vendor data-sale/sharing practices
ITID-61622.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; identified through privacy audits, consumer complaints, or regulatory inquiries rather than SOC monitoring.
ITID-61622.response: Engage privacy counsel, require the vendor to remediate the specific handling failure, and update contractual terms or the consumer-facing privacy notice as needed.
metrics: Number of state-privacy-law-related vendor findings per year
Average time to remediate a vendor consumer-rights-request failure
ITID-61622.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. Differentiated from siblings by jurisdiction/regulation: this leaf is specifically US state privacy law.

playbook.name: Vendor CCPA/State Privacy Law Violation
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have violated CCPA or another applicable state privacy law in handling the organization's customer data.

steps.title: Document how the violation was identified
steps.desc: Record the discovery source and the specific state privacy law and provision violated.

steps.title: Determine affected California/state consumers and data categories
steps.desc: Identify the affected consumer population and data categories involved in the violation.
steps.outcome: Affected population and data categories identified.

steps.title: Assess the organization's own notification and liability exposure
steps.desc: With Legal/Privacy, determine whether the organization has independent obligations under CCPA/state law given the vendor's (service provider's) violation.

steps.title: Notify Legal, Privacy, and vendor relationship manager
steps.desc: Escalate the violation internally for coordinated response.

steps.title: Suspend the non-compliant data practice if ongoing
steps.desc: Pause the specific data-sharing or sale practice tied to the violation if it is ongoing.

steps.title: Require vendor corrective action plan
steps.desc: Obtain a formal corrective action plan from the vendor to bring the practice into compliance.
steps.abort: If vendor is uncooperative, escalate to Legal for contractual remedy.

steps.title: Verify corrective actions are implemented
steps.desc: Independently verify the vendor's corrective measures are in place.

steps.title: Determine and execute consumer/regulator notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess with Legal whether notification to affected consumers or the state Attorney General is required.
steps.outcome: Notification decision made and executed if required.

steps.title: Update the vendor contract/data-sharing agreement
steps.desc: Revise the governing service-provider agreement to reflect corrected practices and compliance commitments.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen state privacy law compliance monitoring
steps.desc: File a report and strengthen ongoing compliance monitoring for vendors handling regulated consumer data.

ITID-61623.def: A vendor's transfer of personal data across international borders without a valid legal transfer mechanism (such as Standard Contractual Clauses, an adequacy decision, or binding corporate rules) as required by applicable data protection law, constituting a regulatory compliance violation.
ITID-61623.purpose: Captures a vendor's failure to maintain a valid legal mechanism for transferring personal data across international borders, framed as a legal/privacy compliance matter.
scopeIncludes: A vendor transferring EU personal data to a non-adequate jurisdiction without executed Standard Contractual Clauses
A vendor's subprocessor chain crossing borders without the transfer mechanism required by the organization's data processing agreement
scopeExcludes: A substantive GDPR processing violation not related to cross-border transfer mechanism (ITID-61621)
A US state privacy law violation unrelated to international transfer (ITID-61622)
ITID-61623.severity: High, since an invalid transfer mechanism can invalidate the legal basis for an entire category of vendor processing, with significant regulatory penalty exposure.
ITID-61623.priority: P1 if the invalid transfer is ongoing and affects a large volume of data subjects; P2 for a contained or already-remediated finding.
ITID-61623.escalation: Escalate to privacy counsel and vendor management immediately; determine whether processing must be suspended pending execution of a valid transfer mechanism.
indicators: Vendor audit revealing data transferred to a jurisdiction without a corresponding valid transfer mechanism on file
Subprocessor disclosure revealing an undisclosed cross-border transfer
Regulatory guidance change invalidating a previously-relied-upon transfer mechanism
vectors: Vendor transferred customer data to a jurisdiction lacking an adequacy decision or a valid transfer mechanism (e.g., standard contractual clauses)
Cloud storage region misconfiguration replicated data outside the contractually permitted geography
rootCauses: Vendor's subprocessor list and data-flow mapping not kept current with actual processing locations
No periodic review of transfer mechanisms against evolving regulatory guidance
Data processing agreement silent on permissible processing locations
controls: Data processing agreements specifying permissible processing locations and required transfer mechanisms
Periodic subprocessor and data-flow mapping review
Contractual notification obligations for any change in vendor processing location
ITID-61623.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; identified through data-flow mapping audits and contractual review rather than SOC monitoring.
ITID-61623.response: Engage privacy counsel to assess exposure, require the vendor to execute a valid transfer mechanism or cease the non-compliant transfer, and document remediation for regulatory defensibility.
metrics: Number of cross-border transfer mechanism gaps identified per year
Percentage of vendor subprocessors with a documented valid transfer mechanism
ITID-61623.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. Differentiated from siblings by axis: this leaf is specifically the cross-border transfer mechanism, not substantive processing compliance within a single jurisdiction.

playbook.name: Vendor Cross-Border Data Transfer Violation
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have transferred organizational data across borders in violation of applicable data-transfer restrictions.

steps.title: Document how the transfer violation was identified
steps.desc: Record the discovery source and the specific cross-border transfer that violated applicable law or contract terms.

steps.title: Determine the data categories, volume, and destination jurisdiction involved
steps.desc: Establish what data was transferred, in what volume, and to which jurisdiction, and whether adequate transfer mechanisms (SCCs, adequacy decisions) were in place.
steps.outcome: Transfer scope and legal basis gap identified.

steps.title: Assess organizational liability exposure with Legal
steps.desc: Determine whether the organization bears independent regulatory exposure for the unauthorized transfer.

steps.title: Suspend the non-compliant cross-border transfer immediately
steps.desc: Halt the specific data transfer or processing activity causing the violation.

steps.title: Notify Legal, DPO, and vendor relationship manager
steps.desc: Escalate the violation for coordinated legal and vendor management response.

steps.title: Implement or correct the appropriate transfer mechanism
steps.desc: Work with the vendor and Legal to put in place a valid transfer mechanism (Standard Contractual Clauses, adequacy reliance, or data localization) before resuming.

steps.title: Verify the corrected transfer mechanism is properly implemented
steps.desc: Independently verify the new transfer mechanism is documented and technically enforced.

steps.title: Determine and execute regulator notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess with Legal whether the violation requires notification to a data protection authority.
steps.outcome: Notification decision made and executed if required.

steps.title: Resume data transfer under the corrected mechanism
steps.desc: Resume the cross-border data flow once the compliant mechanism is verified in place.

steps.title: Document incident and formalize cross-border transfer review process
steps.desc: File a report and establish a formal review checkpoint for all new vendor cross-border data flows.
steps.outcome: Report filed and review process established.

ITID-61624.def: A catch-all classification for a vendor's data protection law violation used during initial triage before the specific regulation and violation pattern is determined.
ITID-61624.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for a vendor data-protection-law violation that has not yet been narrowed to GDPR, US state privacy law, or cross-border transfer classification.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported vendor privacy-law findings pending jurisdictional/regulatory categorization among the sibling patterns in this group
scopeExcludes: Any case confirmed as a GDPR violation (ITID-61621)
Any case confirmed as a US state privacy law violation (ITID-61622)
Any case confirmed as a cross-border transfer violation (ITID-61623)
ITID-61624.severity: High by default, consistent with the sibling leaves, until the finding is further categorized.
ITID-61624.priority: P2 pending reclassification, escalating to P1 if a regulatory notification deadline is implicated.
ITID-61624.escalation: Escalate to privacy counsel and vendor management as with any confirmed data-protection-law finding; reclassification should not delay legal review.
indicators: Initial privacy audit or complaint finding pending regulatory categorization
vectors: Generic third-party data protection law violation not captured by a more specific sub-category
Vendor's data handling practices diverged from the organization's disclosed privacy commitments without detection
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine the applicable regulation or violation pattern
controls: Privacy compliance triage workflow requiring reclassification within a defined SLA
ITID-61624.detection: Not applicable; this is a legal/privacy triage leaf, not a technical detection surface.
ITID-61624.response: Track through standard privacy incident response while categorization proceeds; reclassify promptly once the applicable regulation is determined.
metrics: Number of findings held in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
ITID-61624.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. This is an intake/triage leaf; every finding logged here should be reclassified into a specific sibling ITID once determined.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Third-Party Data Protection Law Violation
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have violated an applicable data protection law through an unspecified or unclassified mechanism.

steps.title: Document how the violation was identified
steps.desc: Record the discovery source and the applicable law/provision violated.

steps.title: Determine data and individuals affected
steps.desc: Establish the data categories and individuals affected by the violation.

steps.title: Assess organizational liability exposure
steps.desc: With Legal, determine the organization's own notification or liability exposure.

steps.title: Notify Legal, Privacy, and vendor relationship manager
steps.desc: Escalate the violation internally.

steps.title: Suspend the non-compliant activity if ongoing
steps.desc: Pause the specific practice causing the violation if it is ongoing.

steps.title: Require and verify vendor corrective action
steps.desc: Obtain and independently verify the vendor's corrective action plan and implementation.
steps.abort: If uncooperative, escalate to Legal for contractual remedy.

steps.title: Determine and execute notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess with Legal whether notification is required and execute if so.
steps.outcome: Notification decision made and executed if required.

steps.title: Resume the relationship under corrected terms
steps.desc: Continue the vendor relationship once compliance is verified.

steps.title: Document incident and improve compliance monitoring
steps.desc: File a report and strengthen ongoing vendor data-protection compliance monitoring.

ITID-61631.def: A vendor's disclosure of the organization's customer data to a downstream sub-processor without the disclosure, consent, or contractual approval required by the data processing agreement, constituting an unauthorized data-sharing violation.
ITID-61631.purpose: Captures a vendor sharing the organization's customer data with a sub-processor that was never disclosed or approved, framed as a legal/contractual compliance matter.
scopeIncludes: A vendor engaging an undisclosed sub-processor to handle organizational customer data
A vendor's sub-processor list found to be materially out of date with actual data-sharing practices
scopeExcludes: A vendor selling or monetizing data commercially without consent (ITID-61632)
A cross-border data transfer mechanism failure with an already-approved sub-processor (ITID-61623)
ITID-61631.severity: High to Critical depending on the volume and sensitivity of data shared and the nature of the undisclosed sub-processor's own security posture.
ITID-61631.priority: P1 if the undisclosed sub-processor's security posture is unknown or the data volume is significant; P2 for a contained or already-remediated disclosure gap.
ITID-61631.escalation: Escalate to privacy counsel and vendor management immediately to assess the undisclosed sub-processor's risk and any notification obligations.
indicators: Vendor audit revealing a sub-processor not listed in the contractually required disclosure
Data flow mapping identifying an unexpected downstream data recipient
Sub-processor breach notification naming a vendor relationship not previously disclosed to the organization
vectors: Vendor forwarded customer data to an undisclosed sub-processor outside the approved processing chain
Contractual sub-processor notification/approval clause not enforced before data flowed downstream
rootCauses: Vendor's sub-processor list not kept current or contractually enforced
No periodic vendor data-flow audit to verify sub-processor disclosures
Contract lacking a requirement for prior notice/approval before engaging a new sub-processor
controls: Contractual requirement for prior notice and approval before engaging any new sub-processor
Periodic vendor data-flow and sub-processor audit
Right-to-audit clause covering sub-processor arrangements
ITID-61631.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; identified through data-flow audits and sub-processor disclosure review rather than SOC monitoring.
ITID-61631.response: Require the vendor to cease unauthorized sharing or formalize approval, assess the sub-processor's security posture, and pursue contractual remedy if the disclosure requirement was violated.
metrics: Number of undisclosed sub-processor findings per year
Percentage of vendor sub-processor lists verified as current
ITID-61631.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. Differentiated from ITID-61632 by axis: this leaf is about undisclosed third-party sharing, not commercial monetization.

playbook.name: Vendor Sharing Customer Data with Unauthorized Sub-Processor
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have shared organizational customer data with a sub-processor not disclosed or authorized under the governing agreement.

steps.title: Confirm the unauthorized sub-processor and data shared
steps.desc: Validate the discovery and identify the specific sub-processor and data categories shared without authorization.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized sub-processor and data scope.

steps.title: Review the contract's sub-processor approval requirements
steps.desc: Confirm the contractual requirement for sub-processor disclosure/approval that was violated.

steps.title: Assess the sub-processor's own security posture and data handling
steps.desc: Evaluate what is known about the unauthorized sub-processor's security controls to gauge risk.

steps.title: Demand immediate cessation of data sharing with the unauthorized sub-processor
steps.desc: Formally require the vendor to stop sharing organizational data with the unauthorized sub-processor immediately.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal and Privacy
steps.desc: Brief Legal and Privacy on the unauthorized disclosure for liability and notification assessment.

steps.title: Require the vendor to obtain data deletion confirmation from the sub-processor
steps.desc: Require the vendor to secure and provide evidence that the unauthorized sub-processor has deleted the improperly shared data.
steps.abort: If deletion cannot be confirmed, escalate to Legal for further remedy.

steps.title: Verify vendor's process fix to prevent unauthorized sub-processing
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has corrected its internal process for sub-processor vetting and disclosure.

steps.title: Determine and execute notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess with Legal/Privacy whether affected customers or regulators require notification.
steps.outcome: Notification decision made and executed if required.

steps.title: Update the contract's sub-processor terms and approval workflow
steps.desc: Revise the agreement to strengthen sub-processor approval and audit rights going forward.

steps.title: Document incident and implement sub-processor registry monitoring
steps.desc: File a report and implement ongoing monitoring of vendor-disclosed sub-processor lists for changes.

ITID-61632.def: A vendor's use of the organization's customer data for its own commercial monetization (sale, advertising, analytics-for-profit, or similar) beyond the scope of consent obtained or contractually permitted, constituting an unauthorized data-sharing violation.
ITID-61632.purpose: Captures a vendor commercially selling or monetizing the organization's customer data without the consent or contractual right to do so, framed as a legal/contractual compliance matter.
scopeIncludes: A vendor discovered selling aggregated or identifiable customer data to a third party for commercial gain
A vendor using customer data to train or improve its own products beyond what the contract or privacy notice permits
scopeExcludes: A vendor sharing data with an undisclosed sub-processor for service delivery rather than commercial monetization (ITID-61631)
ITID-61632.severity: Critical, given the direct violation of consumer trust and the organization's own privacy commitments, with significant regulatory and reputational exposure.
ITID-61632.priority: P1 upon any confirmed evidence of unauthorized commercial monetization of customer data.
ITID-61632.escalation: Escalate immediately to privacy counsel, executive leadership, and vendor management; this is a trust-and-brand issue as much as a legal one and may require customer notification.
indicators: Investigative journalism, regulator inquiry, or whistleblower report naming the vendor's data monetization practices
Contractual audit revealing data use inconsistent with the organization's privacy notice
Vendor's own public statements or marketing materials referencing use of the organization's customer data
vectors: Vendor monetized or sold customer data to third parties (e.g., advertisers, data brokers) without consent
