Data-use restrictions in the master services agreement not technically enforced or audited
rootCauses: Contract silent or ambiguous on permitted secondary uses of data
No periodic review of vendor's actual data monetization practices against contractual terms
Vendor's business model fundamentally reliant on data monetization not disclosed at onboarding
controls: Explicit contractual prohibition on unauthorized data sale/monetization with audit rights
Periodic review of vendor's data monetization practices and business model changes
Consent and privacy-notice alignment review at vendor onboarding and renewal
ITID-61632.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; typically identified through external disclosure, regulatory inquiry, or contractual audit rather than SOC monitoring.
ITID-61632.response: Immediately demand the vendor cease the unauthorized use, assess customer notification and regulatory reporting obligations, and pursue contract termination or legal remedy as warranted.
metrics: Number of confirmed unauthorized monetization findings per year
Time from discovery to vendor cessation of unauthorized use
ITID-61632.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. Differentiated from ITID-61631 by axis: this leaf is about the vendor's own commercial monetization, not third-party sub-processor sharing.

playbook.name: Vendor Selling/Monetizing Data Without Consent
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have sold or monetized organizational customer data without proper authorization or consent.

steps.title: Confirm the unauthorized sale/monetization and data involved
steps.desc: Validate the discovery and identify what data was sold/monetized and to whom.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized activity and data scope.

steps.title: Review the contract and consent basis for the data in question
steps.desc: Confirm the contractual and consent terms that the vendor's monetization activity violated.

steps.title: Assess scope and duration of the unauthorized monetization
steps.desc: Determine how long the unauthorized sale/monetization occurred and the volume of data involved.

steps.title: Demand immediate cessation of the unauthorized monetization
steps.desc: Formally require the vendor to stop selling or monetizing the data immediately.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal for breach-of-contract and regulatory assessment
steps.desc: Engage Legal to assess contractual remedies and potential regulatory violations (e.g., unauthorized 'sale' under state privacy law).

steps.title: Require the vendor to identify and notify downstream purchasers
steps.desc: Require the vendor to identify all parties who purchased or received the data and pursue deletion where possible.
steps.outcome: Downstream purchasers identified and deletion pursued.

steps.title: Verify vendor's corrected data-use practices
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has implemented controls preventing further unauthorized monetization.

steps.title: Determine and execute customer/regulator notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess with Legal/Privacy whether affected customers or regulators require notification.
steps.outcome: Notification decision made and executed if required.

steps.title: Determine whether to continue or terminate the vendor relationship
steps.desc: Based on severity, decide with Procurement/Legal whether to continue the relationship under stricter terms or terminate.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen data-use audit rights
steps.desc: File a report and strengthen contractual audit rights over vendor data monetization practices.
steps.outcome: Report filed and audit rights strengthened.

ITID-61633.def: A catch-all classification for a vendor's unauthorized data-sharing violation used during initial triage before the specific pattern is determined.
ITID-61633.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for an unauthorized data-sharing finding that has not yet been narrowed to undisclosed sub-processor sharing or commercial monetization.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported unauthorized data-sharing findings pending categorization among the sibling patterns in this group
scopeExcludes: Any case confirmed as undisclosed sub-processor sharing (ITID-61631)
Any case confirmed as commercial monetization without consent (ITID-61632)
ITID-61633.severity: High by default, consistent with the sibling leaves, until the finding is further categorized.
ITID-61633.escalation: Escalate to privacy counsel and vendor management as with any confirmed unauthorized data-sharing finding; reclassification should not delay legal review.
indicators: Initial data-sharing finding pending categorization
vectors: Generic unauthorized vendor data sharing not captured by a more specific sub-category
No data-flow mapping in place to detect data leaving the approved processing boundary
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine the specific unauthorized-sharing pattern
controls: Privacy compliance triage workflow requiring reclassification within a defined SLA
ITID-61633.detection: Not applicable; this is a legal/privacy triage leaf, not a technical detection surface.
ITID-61633.response: Track through standard privacy incident response while categorization proceeds; reclassify promptly once determined.
metrics: Number of findings held in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
ITID-61633.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. This is an intake/triage leaf; every finding logged here should be reclassified into a specific sibling ITID once determined.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Unauthorized Data Sharing
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have shared organizational data in an unauthorized manner through an unspecified or unclassified mechanism.

steps.title: Confirm the unauthorized data sharing and scope
steps.desc: Validate the discovery and identify the data shared, recipient, and circumstances.

steps.title: Review the contract terms violated
steps.desc: Confirm the specific contractual or consent terms breached.

steps.title: Assess risk and impact of the unauthorized sharing
steps.desc: Evaluate the sensitivity of shared data and potential downstream impact.

steps.title: Demand immediate cessation of the unauthorized sharing
steps.desc: Require the vendor to stop the unauthorized sharing activity immediately.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal and Privacy
steps.desc: Brief Legal and Privacy for liability and remedy assessment.

steps.title: Require vendor to pursue data deletion from unauthorized recipients
steps.desc: Require the vendor to obtain deletion confirmation from any party that received the data.
steps.outcome: Deletion pursued and confirmed where possible.

steps.title: Verify vendor's corrective process controls
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has fixed the process that allowed the unauthorized sharing.

steps.title: Determine and execute notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess with Legal/Privacy whether notification is required.
steps.outcome: Notification decision made and executed if required.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen data-sharing audit controls
steps.desc: File a report and strengthen contractual data-sharing restrictions and audit rights.

ITID-61641.def: A vendor's disclosure of a security breach affecting the organization's data or systems that occurs later than required under the contractual notification clause or applicable breach-notification law, without evidence of deliberate concealment.
ITID-61641.purpose: Captures a vendor breach that was eventually disclosed, but only after missing the contractual or legal notification deadline, framed as a legal/contractual compliance matter.
scopeIncludes: A vendor disclosing a breach 30 days after discovery when the contract required notification within 72 hours
A vendor's notification timeline found to be inconsistent with regulatory breach-notification deadlines applicable to the organization
scopeExcludes: A vendor found to have deliberately hidden a known breach rather than merely delaying notification (ITID-61642)
ITID-61641.severity: High, since a late notification compresses the organization's own downstream regulatory and customer notification timelines, increasing legal exposure independent of the underlying breach severity.
ITID-61641.priority: P1 immediately upon receipt of a late breach notification, since the organization's own notification clock may already be at risk.
ITID-61641.escalation: Escalate to legal and privacy counsel immediately to assess the organization's own downstream notification obligations and any contractual remedy for the vendor's delay.
indicators: Vendor breach notification received outside the contractually specified window
Evidence the vendor knew of the breach earlier than the notification date but attributes the delay to internal process rather than intentional concealment
vectors: Vendor became aware of a breach affecting shared data but delayed notification past the contractual or legal deadline
No breach-notification SLA built into the vendor contract to force timely disclosure
rootCauses: Vendor lacking a mature incident response and notification process
Contract notification clause not clearly specified or not actively enforced
Vendor's own breach-investigation process taking longer than the contractual notification window allows
controls: Contractual breach-notification clause with a clearly defined, enforceable timeline
Vendor incident response capability assessment at onboarding
Escalation contacts and tabletop exercises with critical vendors covering notification timelines
ITID-61641.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; this is a contractual timeline compliance matter identified upon receipt of the vendor's notification.
ITID-61641.response: Immediately assess the organization's own downstream notification obligations given the compressed timeline, and pursue contractual remedy for the vendor's delay.
metrics: Number of late vendor breach notifications per year
Average delay between vendor discovery and vendor notification
ITID-61641.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. Differentiated from ITID-61642 by axis: this leaf is timing/delay without evidence of intent to conceal, not active concealment.

playbook.name: Vendor Delayed Breach Notification Beyond Contractual/Legal Requirement
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have notified the organization of a data breach later than required by contract or law.

steps.title: Confirm the actual breach discovery date versus notification date
steps.desc: Establish the vendor's actual breach discovery timeline and compare it against the date the organization was notified.
steps.guidance: Request the vendor's internal incident timeline documentation.

steps.title: Review contractual and regulatory notification timelines violated
steps.desc: Confirm the specific contractual clause or regulatory deadline (e.g., GDPR 72 hours, state breach law) that was missed.

steps.title: Assess impact of the delay on the organization's own response and obligations
steps.desc: Determine whether the delay caused the organization to miss its own downstream notification deadlines or increased harm to affected individuals.
steps.outcome: Downstream impact of the delay assessed.

steps.title: Immediately begin the organization's own incident response for the underlying breach
steps.desc: Treat the underlying breach as newly actionable and begin the organization's standard breach response regardless of the delay.
steps.outcome: Organization's breach response initiated without further delay.

steps.title: Escalate the delayed-notification issue to Legal
steps.desc: Notify Legal of the vendor's contractual/regulatory notification failure for liability and remedy assessment.

steps.title: Require vendor's root-cause explanation and process fix for notification delay
steps.desc: Require the vendor to explain the cause of the delay and implement process changes to meet notification deadlines going forward.

steps.title: Determine and execute the organization's own regulator/customer notification, accounting for the delay
steps.desc: Assess with Legal/Privacy the organization's notification obligations, noting the delay may affect timelines and regulator communications.
steps.outcome: Notification executed, with delay context communicated to regulators if relevant.

steps.title: Update the contract's breach-notification clause and penalties
steps.desc: Strengthen the contractual notification-timeline requirement and add penalties for non-compliance.

steps.title: Document incident and reassess vendor's risk tier for notification reliability
steps.desc: File a report and adjust the vendor's risk tier and monitoring cadence given the notification failure.
steps.outcome: Report filed and risk tier updated.

ITID-61642.def: A vendor's deliberate withholding of knowledge of a security breach affecting the organization's data or systems, discovered independently of the vendor's own disclosure (e.g., via threat intelligence, a third party, or forensic investigation), constituting active concealment rather than a mere notification delay.
ITID-61642.purpose: Captures a vendor that knowingly concealed a breach from the organization rather than merely delaying its disclosure, framed as a legal/contractual compliance matter with potential fraud implications.
scopeIncludes: Evidence that a vendor knew of a breach for an extended period and made no disclosure until confronted with independent evidence
A vendor's internal communications or incident records showing deliberate suppression of a known breach
scopeExcludes: A vendor that disclosed a breach late but with no evidence of deliberate concealment (ITID-61641)
ITID-61642.severity: Critical, given the combination of an underlying security breach with a deliberate breach of trust and likely breach of contractual good-faith and notification obligations.
ITID-61642.priority: P1 immediately upon any credible evidence of vendor concealment.
ITID-61642.escalation: Escalate to legal counsel, executive leadership, and potentially regulators/law enforcement immediately; concealment materially changes both the legal exposure and the trust relationship with the vendor.
indicators: Independent threat intelligence or forensic evidence of a breach the vendor never disclosed
Discrepancy between a vendor's public statements and internal records regarding breach timing
A former vendor employee or whistleblower reporting knowledge of an undisclosed breach
vectors: Vendor knowingly withheld disclosure of a confirmed breach affecting the organization's data
Vendor's incident response process lacked a mandatory customer-notification trigger
rootCauses: Vendor incentive structures discouraging prompt breach disclosure (reputational or contractual penalty avoidance)
No independent verification mechanism to detect a vendor breach absent vendor self-disclosure
Contract lacking meaningful penalties for concealment distinct from mere delay
controls: Independent threat intelligence monitoring for indicators of a vendor breach not yet disclosed
Contractual penalties and termination rights specific to concealment, distinct from delay
Right-to-audit clauses enabling independent verification of vendor security posture
ITID-61642.detection: Weak by design, since concealment means the vendor is actively withholding the primary evidence source; detection depends on independent threat intelligence or third-party disclosure.
ITID-61642.response: Treat as a serious breach-of-trust event: engage legal counsel on contractual and potential fraud remedies, assess full scope of the concealed breach independently, and evaluate the vendor relationship for termination.
metrics: Number of confirmed vendor concealment events per year
Time from independent discovery to full scope assessment of the concealed breach
detections: Independent threat intelligence monitoring for vendor-related breach indicators
ITID-61642.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. Differentiated from ITID-61641 by axis: this leaf requires evidence of deliberate concealment, a materially more severe finding than delay alone.

playbook.name: Vendor Concealed Known Breach from Customer
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have deliberately concealed a known data breach from the organization.

steps.title: Confirm evidence of deliberate concealment
steps.desc: Gather evidence (whistleblower report, regulatory action, media disclosure) establishing the vendor knowingly withheld breach information.

steps.title: Determine when the vendor actually knew of the breach versus when it disclosed
steps.desc: Establish the vendor's actual knowledge timeline against the disclosure date to quantify the concealment period.

steps.title: Assess the underlying breach's impact on organizational data
steps.desc: Determine what organizational data was affected by the originally concealed breach.

steps.title: Immediately begin full incident response for the underlying breach
steps.desc: Treat the concealed breach as newly discovered and initiate the organization's standard incident response.

steps.title: Escalate immediately to executive leadership and Legal
steps.desc: Given the deliberate concealment, escalate to executive leadership and Legal for a decision on the vendor relationship and potential legal action.
steps.outcome: Executive/Legal engaged and decision process initiated.

steps.title: Rotate any credentials/secrets tied to the concealed breach
steps.desc: Rotate organizational secrets that may have been exposed in the originally concealed breach.

steps.title: Verify the vendor's current remediation of the underlying breach
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has, belatedly, remediated the root cause of the original breach.

steps.title: Determine and execute delayed regulator/customer notification
steps.desc: Assess with Legal the organization's notification obligations, factoring in the concealment period and increased regulatory scrutiny risk.

steps.title: Terminate or restrict the vendor relationship pending Legal review
steps.desc: Given the trust breach from concealment, decide with Legal/Procurement whether to terminate or severely restrict the vendor relationship.

steps.title: Document incident and pursue contractual/legal remedies
steps.desc: File a comprehensive report documenting the concealment and any legal remedies pursued, and update vendor contract terms requiring immediate disclosure.
steps.outcome: Report filed and contract terms strengthened.

ITID-61643.def: A catch-all classification for a vendor's failure to disclose a breach used during initial triage before the specific pattern (delay vs. concealment) is determined.
ITID-61643.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for a vendor breach-disclosure-failure finding that has not yet been narrowed to a late-notification or active-concealment classification.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported vendor breach-disclosure-failure findings pending categorization among the sibling patterns in this group
scopeExcludes: Any case confirmed as a late-but-good-faith notification (ITID-61641)
Any case confirmed as deliberate concealment (ITID-61642)
ITID-61643.severity: High to Critical by default, consistent with the sibling leaves, until the finding is further categorized.
ITID-61643.escalation: Escalate to legal and privacy counsel as with any confirmed disclosure-failure finding; reclassification should not delay assessment of the organization's own notification obligations.
indicators: Initial breach-disclosure-failure finding pending categorization
vectors: Generic vendor failure to disclose a breach not captured by a more specific sub-category
No independent monitoring channel to detect vendor breaches the vendor itself did not report
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine whether the failure was delay or concealment
controls: Compliance triage workflow requiring reclassification within a defined SLA
ITID-61643.detection: Not applicable; this is a legal/privacy triage leaf, not a technical detection surface.
ITID-61643.response: Assess the organization's own downstream notification obligations immediately regardless of categorization status; reclassify promptly once determined.
metrics: Number of findings held in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
ITID-61643.notes: regulatory/contractual compliance failure — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. This is an intake/triage leaf; every finding logged here should be reclassified into a specific sibling ITID once determined.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Failure to Disclose Vendor Breach
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have failed to disclose a data breach through an unspecified or unclassified circumstance.

steps.title: Confirm the non-disclosure and underlying breach details
steps.desc: Validate the report and gather details of the underlying breach that was not disclosed.

steps.title: Determine notification timeline requirements that were missed
steps.desc: Confirm the contractual/regulatory notification requirement that was not met.

steps.title: Assess impact on organizational data
steps.desc: Determine what organizational data was affected by the undisclosed breach.

steps.title: Begin incident response for the underlying breach
steps.desc: Initiate standard incident response for the newly disclosed breach.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal
steps.desc: Notify Legal of the disclosure failure for liability and remedy assessment.

steps.title: Verify the vendor's remediation of the underlying breach
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has remediated the root cause of the breach.

steps.title: Determine and execute notification obligations
steps.desc: Assess with Legal whether notification of affected individuals or regulators is required.
steps.outcome: Notification decision made and executed if required.

steps.title: Update contract disclosure requirements
steps.desc: Strengthen the contract's breach-disclosure clause and remedies for non-compliance.

steps.title: Document incident and reassess vendor risk tier
steps.desc: File a report and update the vendor's risk classification given the disclosure failure.
steps.outcome: Report filed and risk tier updated.

ITID-61711.def: The discovery of internal fraud (financial misstatement, embezzlement, billing fraud) at a vendor organization, where the fraud directly affects the quality, continuity, or integrity of contracted services delivered to the organization.
ITID-61711.purpose: Classifies incidents where fraud committed internally by a vendor's own staff or leadership disrupts services the vendor contractually provides to the organization.
scopeIncludes: Vendor internal fraud investigation results shared with the organization as a customer
Billing or invoicing fraud discovered in vendor financial statements affecting the organization's contract
Vendor leadership fraud triggering regulatory action that disrupts service delivery
scopeExcludes: Fraud that subsequently leads to vendor bankruptcy and service loss (see ITID-61712)
Fraud targeting the organization directly rather than occurring within the vendor's own operations (a fraud-investigation ITID under a different Tier-1 domain)
ITID-61711.severity: Medium, escalating to High if the fraud materially affects service delivery or financial exposure to the organization.
ITID-61711.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if immediate service continuity is at risk.
ITID-61711.escalation: Escalate to vendor management and finance/legal to assess contractual and financial exposure.
indicators: Vendor disclosure of an internal fraud investigation
News reporting or regulatory filings describing vendor fraud
Unexplained billing discrepancies or service-quality degradation from the vendor
vectors: Vendor employee abused legitimate access or approval authority to commit fraud affecting contracted services
Vendor's internal fraud controls (segregation of duties, transaction review) failed to detect the misconduct
rootCauses: Insufficient vendor financial health and governance due diligence
Lack of ongoing vendor financial monitoring post-contract-signing
Concentration of critical services with a single vendor lacking oversight
controls: Vendor financial health monitoring as part of third-party risk management
Contractual audit rights and service-level continuity clauses
Vendor diversification for critical services
ITID-61711.detection: Low from internal telemetry; detection relies on vendor disclosure, financial monitoring services, or media reporting.
ITID-61711.response: Assess service continuity risk, review contractual protections, and consider vendor diversification if fraud materially affects delivery.
metrics: Number of vendors under active fraud investigation
Service-level impact incidents attributed to vendor fraud
ITID-61711.notes: Vendor business-continuity impact — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk and business-continuity channels.

playbook.name: Vendor's Own Internal Fraud Discovered, Affecting Contracted Services
playbook.description: A vendor's own internal fraud is discovered, creating risk to the continuity or integrity of services contracted by the organization.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor fraud disclosure and affected services
steps.desc: Validate the disclosure (vendor announcement, media report, regulatory filing) and determine which contracted services may be affected.
steps.outcome: Confirmed fraud details and affected service scope.

steps.title: Assess financial and operational stability implications for the vendor
steps.desc: Evaluate whether the fraud threatens the vendor's ongoing financial viability or ability to deliver contracted services.
steps.guidance: Engage Finance/Procurement for vendor financial health assessment.

steps.title: Determine whether organizational data or funds were directly affected
steps.desc: Assess whether the fraud involved misuse of organizational funds, data, or resources specifically.

steps.title: Review and, if warranted, suspend payments or financial transactions with the vendor
steps.desc: Pause outgoing payments or financial commitments pending clarity on the fraud's scope, if organizational funds could be at risk.

steps.title: Activate contingency/alternate vendor planning
steps.desc: Begin evaluating and preparing contingency vendors in case service continuity is threatened.
steps.outcome: Contingency plan activated or readiness confirmed.

steps.title: Escalate to Finance, Legal, and Procurement leadership
steps.desc: Brief relevant leadership on the fraud's business continuity and financial implications.

steps.title: Verify the extent of impact through vendor and independent audit information
steps.desc: Obtain audit or investigative findings clarifying the true extent of the fraud and its effect on services provided to the organization.

steps.title: Recover any organizational funds or assets improperly diverted
steps.desc: Pursue recovery of any organizational funds or assets affected by the fraud through Legal/Finance channels.

steps.title: Determine whether to continue, restructure, or exit the vendor relationship
steps.desc: Based on findings, decide with Procurement/Legal whether to continue the relationship under enhanced oversight, or transition to an alternate vendor.

steps.title: Restore normal service operations
steps.desc: Confirm continuity of contracted services, whether through the original vendor or a transitioned alternate.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen vendor financial due diligence
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and recommend enhanced financial due diligence and monitoring for critical vendors.

ITID-61712.def: The organizational disruption resulting from a vendor entering bankruptcy or insolvency proceedings following the discovery of internal fraud, including loss of contracted services, data-access disputes during insolvency, and asset-recovery complications.
ITID-61712.purpose: Classifies incidents where a vendor's bankruptcy, triggered by discovered fraud, directly disrupts the organization's operations.
scopeIncludes: Vendor bankruptcy filing following a fraud disclosure, with direct impact to the organization's contracted services
Data or system access disputes arising from a vendor's insolvency proceedings
Loss of support/maintenance for vendor-supplied systems due to vendor closure
scopeExcludes: Vendor internal fraud not resulting in bankruptcy (see ITID-61711)
Vendor bankruptcy unrelated to fraud (e.g., ordinary business failure — track as a general vendor continuity event outside this leaf if no fraud nexus exists)
ITID-61712.severity: High, given the potential for complete loss of a contracted service or system.
ITID-61712.priority: P1 if the vendor provides a critical service with no immediate alternative.
ITID-61712.escalation: Escalate immediately to business continuity, legal, and procurement to activate contingency/exit plans.
indicators: Vendor bankruptcy filing notification
Sudden cessation of vendor support or service delivery
Legal notices regarding data or asset custody during insolvency proceedings
vectors: Vendor's financial collapse following fraud discovery abruptly terminated contracted services with no transition plan
No financial-health monitoring or contingency clause to anticipate vendor insolvency risk
rootCauses: Lack of a documented vendor exit/contingency plan for critical services
Insufficient data-portability provisions in the vendor contract
Single-vendor dependency without a fallback provider
controls: Vendor exit and business-continuity planning for critical services
Contractual data-portability and escrow provisions
Vendor concentration-risk assessment
ITID-61712.detection: Not a technical detection scenario; identified through legal/business notifications and vendor relationship monitoring.
ITID-61712.response: Activate the vendor exit/contingency plan, secure organizational data held by the vendor, and transition to an alternative provider.
metrics: Number of critical vendors with a documented exit plan
Time to service restoration after a vendor bankruptcy event
ITID-61712.notes: Vendor business-continuity impact — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk and business-continuity channels.

playbook.name: Vendor Bankruptcy Following Fraud Discovery Disrupting Organization
playbook.description: A vendor enters bankruptcy following the discovery of internal fraud, disrupting services or contractual obligations to the organization.

steps.title: Confirm the bankruptcy filing and immediate service impact
steps.desc: Validate the bankruptcy filing details and assess immediate impact on services or deliverables the vendor was providing.
steps.outcome: Confirmed bankruptcy status and immediate impact.

steps.title: Review contractual protections and organizational exposure
steps.desc: Review the contract for bankruptcy/insolvency clauses, data-return provisions, and any organizational financial exposure (prepayments, deposits).
steps.guidance: Engage Legal to assess standing in bankruptcy proceedings if applicable.

steps.title: Assess criticality and urgency of service continuity needs
steps.desc: Determine how quickly the organization needs to establish continuity given the disrupted service's criticality.

steps.title: Activate business continuity/contingency vendor plan immediately
steps.desc: Engage the pre-identified contingency vendor or interim solution to maintain service continuity.

steps.title: Secure organizational data held by the bankrupt vendor
steps.desc: Urgently request return or secure deletion of organizational data held by the vendor before administrators or creditors take control of systems.
steps.guidance: Act quickly, as data access may be lost once bankruptcy proceedings restrict vendor operations.
steps.outcome: Data retrieval or deletion request submitted urgently.
steps.abort: If vendor becomes unresponsive, escalate to Legal to pursue data recovery through the bankruptcy proceeding.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership, Legal, and Finance
steps.desc: Brief leadership on the disruption and financial exposure for coordinated organizational response.

steps.title: File claims in the bankruptcy proceeding if organizational funds are at risk
steps.desc: Work with Legal to file appropriate claims to recover prepayments, deposits, or damages through the bankruptcy process.

steps.title: Confirm secure transition or destruction of organizational data
steps.desc: Verify organizational data has been returned or securely destroyed by the vendor/bankruptcy administrator.

steps.title: Fully transition services to the alternate/contingency vendor
steps.desc: Complete the transition of all affected services to the new vendor or internal solution.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen contingency planning for critical vendors
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and ensure all critical vendors have documented, tested contingency/exit plans.
steps.outcome: Report filed and contingency planning strengthened.

ITID-61713.def: An initial report of financial fraud discovered at a vendor organization, where the ultimate impact on the organization (service disruption short of bankruptcy, or full vendor bankruptcy) has not yet been determined.
ITID-61713.purpose: Provides an intake classification for vendor financial fraud incidents before the specific impact (service disruption vs. bankruptcy) is determined.
scopeIncludes: Early-stage vendor fraud disclosures pending impact assessment
Media or regulatory reports of vendor fraud investigation without confirmed organizational impact
scopeExcludes: Confirmed service disruption without bankruptcy (see ITID-61711)
Confirmed vendor bankruptcy following fraud (see ITID-61712)
ITID-61713.escalation: Escalate to vendor management to monitor the situation and assess potential impact to service continuity.
indicators: Initial media or regulatory report of vendor fraud investigation
vectors: Generic vendor financial fraud incident not captured by a more specific sub-category
Insufficient vendor financial and integrity due diligence at onboarding or renewal
rootCauses: Insufficient ongoing vendor financial health monitoring
controls: Vendor financial health monitoring as part of third-party risk management
ITID-61713.detection: Not a technical detection scenario; identified through vendor monitoring and external reporting.
ITID-61713.response: Monitor developments closely and reclassify once the impact (service disruption or bankruptcy) becomes clear.
metrics: Mean time to reclassify from intake to specific leaf
ITID-61713.notes: This is the intake bucket for Vendor Financial Fraud Incident. Vendor business-continuity impact — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk and business-continuity channels.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Vendor Financial Fraud Incident
playbook.description: A vendor is affected by an internal financial fraud incident through an unspecified or unclassified circumstance.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor fraud disclosure and scope
steps.desc: Validate the disclosure and determine the general scope and nature of the fraud.

steps.title: Assess impact on organizational services or funds
steps.desc: Determine whether organizational services, data, or funds are affected.

steps.title: Assess vendor financial stability implications
steps.desc: Evaluate whether the fraud threatens the vendor's ability to continue delivering services.

steps.title: Review and adjust financial exposure with the vendor as needed
steps.desc: Pause or adjust payments/commitments if organizational funds are at risk.

steps.title: Prepare contingency plans for service continuity
steps.desc: Begin evaluating contingency options in case the fraud disrupts service delivery.

steps.title: Monitor vendor's remediation and stabilization efforts
steps.desc: Track the vendor's corrective actions and financial stabilization progress.

steps.title: Determine whether to continue or transition the vendor relationship
steps.desc: Decide with Procurement/Legal on the future of the vendor relationship based on findings.

steps.title: Restore normal service operations
steps.desc: Confirm service continuity through the original or alternate vendor.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen vendor financial monitoring
steps.desc: File a report and recommend ongoing financial health monitoring for critical vendors.

ITID-61721.def: A ransomware attack against a vendor's IT environment that disrupts or halts the vendor's ability to deliver a contracted service to the organization, where the primary impact is operational/service availability rather than confirmed data exposure.
ITID-61721.purpose: Classifies ransomware attacks against a vendor that disrupt the delivery of a shared service to the organization, without necessarily exposing organizational data.
scopeIncludes: Vendor ransomware attack causing an outage or degradation of a service the organization relies on
Vendor communication of service disruption timelines during ransomware recovery
Organizational business-continuity activation due to a vendor ransomware outage
scopeExcludes: Vendor ransomware attacks confirmed to have exposed the organization's data (see ITID-61722)
Ransomware attacks directly against the organization's own systems (a different Tier-1 domain)
ITID-61721.severity: High, given direct operational impact to the organization's service delivery.
ITID-61721.priority: P1 if the affected service is business-critical.
ITID-61721.escalation: Escalate immediately to business continuity and vendor management to activate contingency plans and obtain a recovery timeline from the vendor.
indicators: Vendor notification of a ransomware attack affecting service delivery
Sudden, unexplained outage of a vendor-provided service
Vendor status page or communications describing recovery efforts
vectors: Ransomware deployment against the vendor's core service infrastructure
rootCauses: Vendor's own inadequate ransomware prevention/detection controls
Lack of organizational failover or redundancy for the affected vendor service
controls: Business continuity/failover planning for critical vendor services
Vendor ransomware resilience requirements in contracts
Regular vendor incident-communication drills
ITID-61721.detection: Low from internal telemetry alone; detection relies on vendor notification and observed service outage.
ITID-61721.response: Activate business continuity plans for the affected service, maintain regular communication with the vendor on recovery timelines, and document operational impact.
metrics: Duration of service disruption per vendor ransomware event
Number of critical vendor services with documented failover plans
sops: Vendor Service Outage Business Continuity SOP
ITID-61721.notes: Differentiated from ITID-61722 by impact type: operational/service disruption here versus confirmed data exposure in the sibling leaf.

playbook.name: Vendor Ransomware Attack Disrupting Shared Service Delivery
playbook.description: A vendor suffers a ransomware attack that disrupts the delivery of a service the organization depends on.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor ransomware attack and service impact
steps.desc: Validate the vendor's disclosure and determine which specific services delivered to the organization are disrupted.

steps.title: Assess expected outage duration and criticality
steps.desc: Obtain the vendor's estimated recovery timeline and assess against the criticality of the affected service to organizational operations.

steps.title: Determine whether organizational data held by the vendor is also at risk
steps.desc: Establish whether the ransomware attack also threatens exposure or loss of organizational data held by the vendor.
steps.outcome: Data risk determined separately from service disruption.

steps.title: Activate business continuity plan for the affected service
steps.desc: Invoke the documented business continuity plan, including manual workarounds or alternate vendor activation, for the disrupted service.

steps.title: Suspend integrations with the affected vendor pending assessment
steps.desc: Disable data flows or integrations with the vendor's systems if there is risk of the ransomware propagating or affecting data integrity.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership and affected business units
steps.desc: Communicate the disruption and continuity plan to affected business units and leadership.

steps.title: Verify vendor's recovery and confirm system integrity before reconnecting
steps.desc: Obtain vendor confirmation and, where feasible, independent verification that systems are restored and free of ransomware before resuming the integration.
steps.abort: If unverified, extend continuity measures.

steps.title: Rotate organizational credentials shared with the vendor
steps.desc: Rotate any API keys, credentials, or shared secrets used in the integration as a precaution.

steps.title: Restore the vendor integration and resume normal service
steps.desc: Reconnect and resume normal service delivery once recovery is verified.

steps.title: Assess business impact of the disruption and pursue contractual remedies if applicable
steps.desc: Evaluate SLA breaches or damages from the disruption and pursue remedies per the contract.
steps.outcome: Business impact assessed and remedies pursued if applicable.

steps.title: Document incident and update business continuity plan for the vendor
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and refine the business continuity plan and alternate vendor readiness based on lessons learned.
steps.outcome: Report filed and continuity plan updated.

ITID-61722.def: A ransomware attack against a vendor's IT environment in which the organization's data, held or processed by the vendor, is confirmed or strongly suspected to have been exfiltrated (double-extortion) or otherwise exposed as part of the attack.
ITID-61722.purpose: Classifies ransomware attacks against a vendor that expose the organization's data held by that vendor, distinct from cases where the impact is purely operational.
scopeIncludes: Vendor ransomware notification confirming data exfiltration involving organizational data
Organizational data found on a ransomware group's leak site
Double-extortion ransom demands referencing organizational data specifically
scopeExcludes: Vendor ransomware attacks with purely operational/service disruption impact and no confirmed data exposure (see ITID-61721)
Data exposure from vendor breaches not involving ransomware (see Third-Party Data Breaches Tier-3)
ITID-61722.severity: High to Critical, given the combined operational and data-breach impact.
ITID-61722.priority: P1, requiring both business-continuity and breach-notification response tracks.
ITID-61722.escalation: Escalate immediately to legal/privacy for breach-notification assessment in parallel with business continuity activation.
indicators: Vendor notification confirming data exfiltration in a ransomware incident
Organizational data appearing on a ransomware leak site
Ransom note referencing specific organizational data
vectors: Double-extortion ransomware deployment against vendor infrastructure holding organizational data
rootCauses: Vendor's inadequate data segmentation exposing bulk data to a single compromise
Lack of encryption-at-rest for organizational data held by the vendor
controls: Contractual encryption-at-rest requirements for vendor-held data
Data minimization with vendors handling sensitive information
Leak-site monitoring for organizational data
ITID-61722.detection: Low from internal telemetry; relies on vendor notification and leak-site/dark-web monitoring.
ITID-61722.response: Initiate breach-notification assessment, activate business continuity for the affected service, and monitor leak sites for further data exposure.
metrics: Number of customers/records affected per vendor ransomware data-exposure event
Mean time to breach-notification determination
sops: Vendor Ransomware Data Exposure Response SOP
ITID-61722.notes: Differentiated from ITID-61721 by confirmed data exposure alongside the operational impact.

playbook.name: Vendor Ransomware Attack Exposing Organization's Data Held by Vendor
playbook.description: A vendor suffers a ransomware attack that results in exposure or exfiltration of the organization's data held by the vendor.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor ransomware attack and data exposure
steps.desc: Validate the vendor's disclosure regarding the ransomware attack and confirm whether organizational data was exposed or exfiltrated (double-extortion).

steps.title: Determine the specific organizational data types and volume affected
steps.desc: Obtain from the vendor the specific data categories and record counts exposed.

steps.title: Monitor for the organization's data appearing on leak sites
steps.desc: Monitor ransomware group leak sites and dark web forums for evidence of organizational data being published.
steps.outcome: Leak-site monitoring in place and results documented.

steps.title: Rotate organizational credentials and secrets shared with the vendor
steps.desc: Rotate all API keys, credentials, and shared secrets used with the vendor's affected systems.

steps.title: Suspend data flows to the vendor pending assessment
steps.desc: Pause any ongoing data transfers to the vendor until the scope of exposure is understood.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal and Privacy
steps.desc: Brief Legal and Privacy for notification and liability assessment.

steps.title: Verify vendor's ransomware eradication and system restoration
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has eradicated the ransomware and restored systems from clean backups.
steps.abort: If unconfirmed, keep data flows suspended.

steps.title: Assess whether ransom payment (if made by vendor) affects the organization's own obligations
steps.desc: With Legal, evaluate any implications if the vendor paid or considered paying a ransom (e.g., sanctions screening, disclosure obligations).

steps.title: Determine and execute notification obligations to affected individuals and regulators
steps.desc: Assess with Legal/Privacy the organization's notification obligations given the confirmed data exposure and execute within required timelines.

steps.title: Resume the vendor relationship under enhanced data-protection terms
steps.desc: Reinstate the relationship only after confirming enhanced encryption, backup, and access controls are in place.

steps.title: Document incident and reassess vendor risk tier and data-minimization practices
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and evaluate reducing the volume/sensitivity of data shared with this vendor going forward.

ITID-61723.def: An initial report of a ransomware attack against a vendor, where it has not yet been determined whether organizational data was exposed or whether impact is limited to service disruption.
ITID-61723.purpose: Provides an intake classification for vendor ransomware attacks before it is confirmed whether data exposure occurred alongside operational disruption.
scopeIncludes: Initial vendor ransomware notifications pending data-exposure confirmation
Threat intelligence indicating a vendor ransomware attack before vendor confirmation
scopeExcludes: Confirmed operational-only impact (see ITID-61721)
Confirmed data exposure alongside the attack (see ITID-61722)
ITID-61723.severity: High pending confirmation; treat as data-exposure-possible until ruled out.
ITID-61723.escalation: Escalate to business continuity and legal/privacy in parallel pending confirmation of scope.
indicators: Initial vendor ransomware notification lacking data-exposure detail
Threat intelligence report of a vendor ransomware attack pending vendor confirmation
vectors: Ransomware deployment against vendor infrastructure (mechanism to be confirmed)
rootCauses: To be determined pending investigation
controls: Business continuity/failover planning for critical vendor services
Leak-site monitoring for organizational data
ITID-61723.detection: Low from internal telemetry; relies on vendor notification and external monitoring.
ITID-61723.response: Activate business continuity precautions and monitor for data-exposure confirmation, reclassifying once scope is known.
metrics: Mean time to reclassify from intake to specific leaf
sops: Vendor Ransomware Data Exposure Response SOP
ITID-61723.notes: This is the intake bucket for Vendor Ransomware Attack; reclassify once data-exposure status is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Vendor Ransomware Attack
playbook.description: A vendor suffers a ransomware attack with unspecified impact on the organization.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor ransomware attack and initial impact
steps.desc: Validate the disclosure and determine the general impact on organizational services or data.

steps.title: Determine whether service disruption, data exposure, or both are involved
steps.desc: Clarify with the vendor whether the attack affects service availability, data confidentiality, or both.

steps.title: Activate contingency plan if service continuity is affected
steps.desc: Invoke business continuity measures for any disrupted service.

steps.title: Rotate credentials and suspend data flows as a precaution
steps.desc: Rotate shared credentials and pause data transfers to the vendor pending assessment.

steps.title: Escalate to Security leadership and Legal
steps.desc: Brief relevant stakeholders on the situation.

steps.title: Verify vendor's remediation and restoration
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has eradicated the ransomware and restored affected systems.

steps.title: Determine and execute notification obligations if data was exposed
steps.desc: Assess with Legal/Privacy whether notification is required based on confirmed impact.
steps.outcome: Notification decision made and executed if required.

steps.title: Resume normal operations with the vendor
steps.desc: Restore full service/integration once remediation is verified.

steps.title: Document incident and reassess vendor risk tier
steps.desc: File a report and update the vendor's risk classification and continuity plan.
steps.outcome: Report filed and risk tier updated.

ITID-61731.def: Operational downtime or degraded service experienced by the organization as a direct consequence of a security breach at a vendor, where the primary tracked impact is business/service disruption rather than the breach mechanism itself.
ITID-61731.purpose: Classifies organizational service downtime that results from a vendor security breach, regardless of the breach's specific technical cause.
scopeIncludes: Service outages attributed to a vendor breach where the root-cause attack is tracked under a different ITID
Cumulative downtime tracking across a vendor breach's recovery period
Customer-facing service degradation stemming from a vendor security incident
scopeExcludes: The technical breach itself (tracked under the relevant Third-Party Data Breach or Network Compromise leaf, or the Vendor Ransomware Attack group)
Downtime from a vendor's non-security-related outage (an availability/uptime ITID, not this taxonomy)
ITID-61731.severity: High if the affected service is business-critical or customer-facing.
ITID-61731.priority: P1 for business-critical services, P2 otherwise.
ITID-61731.escalation: Escalate to business continuity and customer communications teams to manage downstream impact.
indicators: Vendor-attributed service outage or SLA breach following a disclosed security incident
Customer complaints correlating with a known vendor breach timeline
vectors: Downstream consequence of the vendor's underlying breach (tracked separately)
rootCauses: Lack of redundancy/failover for the affected vendor service
Vendor SLA not accounting for security-incident recovery timelines
controls: Business continuity/failover planning for critical vendor services
SLA clauses addressing security-incident recovery commitments
ITID-61731.detection: Moderate: internal service-monitoring tools directly observe the downtime, though root-cause attribution depends on vendor disclosure.
ITID-61731.response: Activate business continuity measures, communicate impact to affected stakeholders, and track downtime duration against SLA commitments.
metrics: Cumulative downtime hours attributed to vendor breaches per year
SLA compliance rate during vendor security incidents
sops: Vendor Service Outage Business Continuity SOP
ITID-61731.notes: Vendor business-continuity impact — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk and business-continuity channels. This is the general leaf for Service Downtime Due to Vendor Breach; no further sibling differentiation exists.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Service Downtime Due to Vendor Breach
playbook.description: The organization experiences service downtime as a result of a security breach at a vendor.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor breach as the cause of downtime
steps.desc: Validate that the observed service downtime is attributable to a security breach at the vendor rather than an unrelated outage.

steps.title: Assess scope and expected duration of the downtime
steps.desc: Obtain the vendor's estimated recovery timeline and determine which organizational functions are affected.

steps.title: Determine whether organizational data is also at risk
steps.desc: Clarify whether the underlying breach also threatens data confidentiality/integrity beyond availability.

steps.title: Activate business continuity/workaround measures
steps.desc: Implement manual workarounds or alternate service arrangements to minimize business impact during the outage.

steps.title: Communicate downtime impact to affected internal stakeholders and customers
steps.desc: Notify affected business units and, if customer-facing, communicate status to customers.

steps.title: Monitor vendor's remediation progress
steps.desc: Track the vendor's remediation and restoration progress toward resolving the underlying breach.

steps.title: Restore normal service once vendor confirms resolution
steps.desc: Resume normal reliance on the vendor's service once restoration is confirmed.

steps.title: Assess SLA impact and pursue contractual remedies if applicable
steps.desc: Evaluate service-level agreement breaches and pursue applicable remedies or credits.
steps.outcome: SLA impact assessed and remedies pursued if applicable.

steps.title: Document incident and strengthen continuity planning
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and improve business continuity and alternate-vendor readiness plans.
steps.outcome: Report filed and continuity plans strengthened.

ITID-61741.def: A disruption to the organization's supply of goods, components, or manufacturing output resulting from a security incident (cyberattack, ransomware, system compromise) at a supplier's logistics or manufacturing operation.
ITID-61741.purpose: Classifies disruptions to the organization's operations caused by a security incident affecting a supplier's logistics or manufacturing capability.
scopeIncludes: Supplier manufacturing-line shutdown caused by a cyberattack
Logistics/freight-forwarder system compromise delaying shipments
Supplier production disruption cascading into the organization's own operations or product availability
scopeExcludes: Financial fraud or bankruptcy at the supplier not tied to a security incident (see Vendor Financial Fraud Incident group)
Physical (non-cyber) logistics disruptions such as natural disasters (outside this taxonomy)
ITID-61741.severity: High if the disruption affects critical production, delivery, or customer commitments.
ITID-61741.priority: P1 if organizational operations are materially impacted; P2 otherwise.
ITID-61741.escalation: Escalate to supply-chain/procurement leadership to activate alternative sourcing and to business continuity for operational impact management.
indicators: Supplier notification of a cyberattack affecting production or logistics systems
Unexpected delays or shortages traced to a known supplier security incident
Industry reporting of a widespread attack on logistics/manufacturing infrastructure
vectors: Ransomware or destructive attacks against supplier operational technology (OT) or logistics systems
Compromise of supplier enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems controlling production scheduling
rootCauses: Supplier's inadequate OT/IT security segmentation
Lack of alternative sourcing for critical components
No visibility into supplier operational resilience posture
controls: Supplier diversification for critical components
Supply-chain resilience/contingency planning
Supplier security assessment including OT security posture
ITID-61741.detection: Low from internal telemetry; detection relies on supplier disclosure and observed supply disruption.
ITID-61741.response: Activate alternative sourcing where available, communicate impact to affected business units and customers, and track recovery against supplier-provided timelines.
metrics: Number of supplier logistics/manufacturing disruptions per year
Time to activate alternative sourcing after disruption
sops: Supply Chain Disruption Business Continuity SOP
ITID-61741.notes: Vendor business-continuity impact — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies in the general case; ransomware-driven disruptions carry T1486 when confirmed. This is the general leaf for Supplier Logistics and Manufacturing Disruptions; no further sibling differentiation exists.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Supplier Logistics and Manufacturing Disruption
playbook.description: A security incident at a supplier disrupts logistics or manufacturing processes the organization depends on.

steps.title: Confirm the supplier incident and its cause of disruption
steps.desc: Validate the supplier's disclosure and confirm the security incident is the cause of the logistics/manufacturing disruption.

steps.title: Assess the disruption's impact on organizational supply/production
steps.desc: Determine which organizational products, orders, or operations depend on the affected supplier and the extent of impact.

steps.title: Obtain the supplier's estimated recovery timeline
steps.desc: Request the supplier's assessment of when normal logistics/manufacturing capacity will resume.

steps.title: Activate alternate supplier or logistics contingency plan
steps.desc: Engage backup suppliers or alternate logistics arrangements to mitigate the disruption's impact.

steps.title: Communicate impact to affected internal stakeholders and customers
steps.desc: Notify Operations, Sales, and customers as appropriate regarding potential delays or impacts.

steps.title: Monitor supplier's remediation and recovery progress
steps.desc: Track the supplier's progress in resolving the underlying security incident and restoring operations.

steps.title: Transition back to the primary supplier once recovery is confirmed
steps.desc: Resume normal reliance on the primary supplier once their operations and security posture are confirmed restored.

steps.title: Assess contractual remedies for the disruption
steps.desc: Evaluate SLA or contract breach implications and pursue remedies as applicable.
steps.outcome: Contractual remedies assessed and pursued if applicable.

steps.title: Document incident and diversify critical supplier dependencies
steps.desc: File a post-incident report and recommend supplier diversification or enhanced contingency planning for critical logistics/manufacturing dependencies.

ITID-61811.def: A full-lifecycle nation-state attack against a supply-chain vendor, in which a state-sponsored actor targets the vendor's infrastructure, software, or personnel specifically to gain access to the organization, its sector, or its customers.
ITID-61811.purpose: Classifies a confirmed or strongly suspected nation-state attack targeting a supply-chain vendor as a means of reaching the organization or its sector.
scopeIncludes: Government or vendor attribution of a nation-state actor targeting a shared supplier
Threat intelligence linking a supplier compromise to known APT infrastructure or TTPs
Sector-wide advisories naming a vendor as the target of state-sponsored supply-chain targeting
scopeExcludes: Financially motivated (non-state) attacks against a vendor (classified under other Third-Party Network Compromise or Vendor Ransomware leaves)
Sustained persistent APT presence already established in a vendor's network (see Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) in Vendor Networks group)
ITID-61811.severity: Critical, given nation-state capability, strategic intent, and potential for sector-wide impact.
ITID-61811.priority: P1, with immediate executive and, where applicable, government coordination.
ITID-61811.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, legal, and national cybersecurity authorities; coordinate with sector information-sharing organizations (ISACs).
indicators: Government advisory naming a nation-state actor targeting a specific vendor or sector
Threat intelligence correlating vendor compromise indicators with known APT infrastructure
Sector-wide notification of coordinated supply-chain targeting
vectors: Spear-phishing against vendor personnel with privileged access
Exploitation of vendor software build/release pipelines
Compromise of vendor infrastructure for staging follow-on attacks against customers
rootCauses: Vendor's insufficient security controls relative to nation-state threat sophistication
Lack of sector-wide threat intelligence sharing regarding vendor targeting
Strategic value of the vendor as an access point to multiple high-value targets
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Sector threat-intelligence sharing (ISAC participation)
Vendor software supply-chain integrity verification (SBOM, code signing)
Enhanced monitoring for known APT infrastructure and TTPs in vendor-originated traffic
ITID-61811.detection: Low to moderate from internal telemetry alone; strongest detection comes from sector-wide threat intelligence sharing and government advisories.
ITID-61811.response: Coordinate with government authorities and sector ISACs, isolate vendor connectivity pending investigation, and conduct a full threat-hunt for related indicators.
metrics: Number of nation-state-attributed vendor targeting events per year
Mean time to threat-hunt completion after advisory receipt
sops: Nation-State Supply Chain Attack Response SOP
detections: APT infrastructure/TTP correlation alerts on vendor-originated traffic
ITID-61811.notes: This is the general leaf for Nation-State Attack on Supply Chain Vendor; framed with full APT lifecycle tactic coverage per taxonomy guidance.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Nation-State Attack on Supply Chain Vendor
playbook.description: A nation-state actor is identified attacking a vendor in the organization's supply chain, creating downstream risk to the organization.

steps.title: Confirm nation-state attribution and affected vendor
steps.desc: Validate the intelligence source (government advisory, threat intel provider, vendor disclosure) attributing the attack to a nation-state actor and identify the specific vendor targeted.
steps.guidance: Corroborate attribution against multiple sources where possible.
steps.outcome: Confirmed nation-state attack and affected vendor.

steps.title: Determine organizational exposure through the vendor relationship
steps.desc: Map all organizational systems, data, and integrations connected to the targeted vendor.

steps.title: Hunt for related indicators of compromise within organizational systems
steps.desc: Proactively search organizational logs and endpoints for IOCs and TTPs associated with the nation-state actor, given the potential for downstream targeting.
steps.guidance: Leverage threat intelligence feeds specific to the identified threat actor.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of related compromise indicators.

steps.title: Restrict or isolate connectivity to the targeted vendor pending assessment
steps.desc: Reduce or sever network connections and data flows to the vendor until the scope of compromise is understood.
steps.outcome: Exposure to the compromised vendor contained.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials and secrets shared with the vendor
steps.desc: Rotate API keys, certificates, and any shared credentials as a precaution given the sophistication of nation-state actors.

steps.title: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, Legal, and government liaison/CISA
steps.desc: Given nation-state involvement, engage executive leadership, Legal, and relevant government cybersecurity liaison contacts for guidance and information sharing.

steps.title: Conduct full incident response as if directly targeted
steps.desc: Treat the organization's own environment with the same rigor as a direct nation-state incident, including full forensic investigation of any confirmed compromise.
steps.outcome: Full IR conducted; any compromise remediated.

steps.title: Verify vendor's remediation and threat-actor eviction before restoring integration
steps.desc: Confirm through vendor attestation and independent threat intelligence that the actor has been evicted from the vendor's environment.
steps.abort: If unconfirmed, maintain restricted connectivity indefinitely and consider alternate vendor.

steps.title: Restore vendor connectivity under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Reinstate the integration only with heightened monitoring and threat-hunting for a sustained period.

steps.title: Share threat intelligence with industry/government partners as appropriate
steps.desc: Contribute relevant, sanitized threat intelligence to industry ISACs or government partners to aid broader defense.

steps.title: Document incident and reassess vendor's nation-state risk exposure
steps.desc: File a comprehensive report and update the vendor's risk tier and geopolitical risk assessment.
steps.outcome: Report filed and risk assessment updated.

ITID-61821.def: The discovery of a sustained, persistent APT presence already established within a vendor's network — long-term access, staged infrastructure, and ongoing collection — as opposed to the initial compromise or targeting event.
ITID-61821.purpose: Classifies the discovery of an established, persistent Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) presence within a vendor's network, distinct from the initial targeting/intrusion event.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of long-dwell-time APT persistence mechanisms in vendor infrastructure
Evidence of ongoing data collection or staging within a compromised vendor environment
Vendor threat-hunt findings confirming established APT presence
scopeExcludes: The initial targeting or intrusion event before persistence is established (see Nation-State Attack on Supply Chain Vendor group)
Financially motivated persistent threats without nation-state attribution
ITID-61821.severity: Critical, given the extended access window and likely broad collection already achieved by the threat actor.
ITID-61821.priority: P1, with immediate full-scope threat-hunt and containment planning.
ITID-61821.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, legal, and national cybersecurity authorities; assume broad compromise of any data or access the vendor holds for the organization.
indicators: Discovery of long-dwell persistence mechanisms (scheduled tasks, backdoors) in vendor systems
Evidence of staged data collection over an extended period
Vendor forensic findings indicating multi-month or multi-year unauthorized access
vectors: Persistent backdoors maintained via valid credentials or trusted relationships
Living-off-the-land techniques to avoid detection over extended dwell time
Staged command-and-control infrastructure for long-term access
rootCauses: Insufficient vendor threat-hunting and long-dwell-time detection capability
Lack of periodic security reassessment of established vendor relationships
Over-reliance on point-in-time vendor security assessments rather than continuous monitoring
controls: Periodic vendor security reassessment beyond point-in-time due diligence
Vendor threat-hunting program for long-dwell-time indicators
Full data-exposure assessment upon APT discovery
ITID-61821.detection: Low; discovery typically results from a dedicated threat-hunt or forensic investigation rather than routine monitoring.
ITID-61821.response: Assume comprehensive data exposure, conduct a full forensic investigation with the vendor, and coordinate with government authorities.
metrics: Estimated dwell time upon APT discovery
Scope of data assessed as exposed per incident
ITID-61821.notes: Differentiated from ITID-61811 by lifecycle stage: established persistence and ongoing collection versus the initial targeting/intrusion event.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General APT in Vendor Networks
playbook.description: An advanced persistent threat group is discovered maintaining a foothold within a vendor's network, creating downstream risk to the organization.

steps.title: Confirm the APT presence and affected vendor
steps.desc: Validate the disclosure identifying the APT group and the specific vendor network compromised.
steps.outcome: Confirmed APT presence and affected vendor.

steps.title: Determine the APT's dwell time and scope within the vendor
steps.desc: Obtain from the vendor (or threat intel) how long the APT has had access and what systems/data were reachable.

steps.title: Hunt for the APT's known TTPs within organizational systems
steps.desc: Proactively search for the specific APT's known tools, techniques, and infrastructure within the organization's own environment.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence within organizational systems.

steps.title: Isolate or restrict connectivity to the compromised vendor
steps.desc: Sever or heavily restrict network connections and data flows to the vendor pending eviction confirmation.

steps.title: Rotate all credentials and secrets shared with the vendor
steps.desc: Rotate all shared credentials given the extended access an APT may have had.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership, Legal, and government/industry threat-sharing partners
steps.desc: Engage senior stakeholders and relevant threat-sharing bodies given the APT's typical sophistication and persistence.

steps.title: Conduct full forensic investigation of any organizational compromise found
steps.desc: If APT indicators are found within organizational systems, conduct thorough forensic investigation and eviction.

steps.title: Verify the vendor's confirmed eviction of the APT
steps.desc: Obtain independent or vendor-attested confirmation that the APT has been fully evicted, not just temporarily disrupted (APTs often maintain multiple footholds).
steps.guidance: Be skeptical of premature 'all clear' claims given APT persistence tactics.
steps.abort: If confidence is low, maintain restricted connectivity and continue monitoring.

steps.title: Restore vendor connectivity under sustained enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Reinstate the integration with an extended period of heightened monitoring given APT re-entry risk.

steps.title: Document incident and update long-term threat-hunting posture for vendor-linked risk
steps.desc: File a comprehensive report and establish ongoing threat-hunting focused on this APT group's TTPs.
steps.outcome: Report filed and threat-hunting program updated.

ITID-61831.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected effort by a foreign state or state-affiliated entity to manipulate the broader supply chain — through ownership influence, regulatory leverage, or coordinated multi-vendor targeting — to affect the integrity of products or services reaching the organization, distinct from a single-vendor intrusion or established APT presence.
ITID-61831.purpose: Classifies deliberate manipulation of the supply chain by a foreign entity to influence the integrity of products, components, or software reaching the organization, beyond a single vendor intrusion.
scopeIncludes: Foreign state ownership or influence over a critical supplier discovered post-contract
Coordinated manipulation of multiple suppliers in a product's manufacturing chain
Regulatory or export-control findings indicating foreign-state leverage over supply-chain integrity
scopeExcludes: A single-vendor intrusion event (see Nation-State Attack on Supply Chain Vendor group)
Established persistent access within one vendor's network without broader supply-chain manipulation evidence (see Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) in Vendor Networks group)
ITID-61831.severity: Critical, given the strategic, multi-vendor, and potentially long-term nature of the manipulation.
ITID-61831.priority: P1, with executive, legal, and government coordination given the strategic scope.
ITID-61831.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, legal, and national cybersecurity/export-control authorities; consider engaging government supply-chain risk management programs.
indicators: Government advisory identifying foreign-state manipulation of a supply-chain segment
Corporate ownership research revealing undisclosed foreign-state influence over a critical supplier
Coordinated anomalies across multiple suppliers in the same manufacturing chain
vectors: Foreign-state acquisition or investment leverage over a critical supplier
Coordinated compromise or influence across multiple tiers of a supply chain
Regulatory or legal coercion of suppliers operating within the foreign state's jurisdiction
rootCauses: Insufficient supply-chain ownership and beneficial-interest due diligence
Reliance on suppliers within jurisdictions subject to state coercion of private industry
Lack of multi-tier supply-chain visibility beyond direct (Tier-1) suppliers
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Multi-tier supply-chain visibility and ownership due diligence
Government supply-chain risk management program participation
Diversification away from suppliers in higher-risk jurisdictions for critical components
ITID-61831.detection: Low; typically identified through government intelligence, investigative journalism, or dedicated supply-chain risk research rather than technical monitoring.
ITID-61831.response: Engage government supply-chain risk resources, reassess supplier relationships and ownership structures, and diversify sourcing where warranted.
metrics: Number of suppliers assessed for foreign-state ownership/influence risk
Number of sourcing diversification actions taken per year
sops: Supply Chain Manipulation Risk Assessment SOP
ITID-61831.notes: This is the general leaf for Supply Chain Manipulation by Foreign Entities; framed at the strategic, multi-vendor level distinct from single-vendor APT leaves.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Supply Chain Manipulation by Foreign Entities
playbook.description: A foreign entity is discovered manipulating elements of the organization's supply chain for strategic or espionage purposes.

steps.title: Confirm the manipulation and identify the foreign entity involved
steps.desc: Validate the intelligence identifying the specific manipulation (e.g., counterfeit substitution, influence over a supplier, data diversion) and the foreign entity behind it.

steps.title: Determine which supply chain elements are affected
steps.desc: Identify the specific products, components, software, or data flows subject to the manipulation.

steps.title: Assess strategic and operational risk to the organization
steps.desc: Evaluate the potential strategic impact (espionage, sabotage, IP theft) versus operational impact of the manipulation.

steps.title: Isolate or suspend the affected supply chain element
steps.desc: Halt use of the manipulated component, software, or data flow pending further assessment.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership, Legal, and government liaison
steps.desc: Given the nation-state/foreign-entity nexus, escalate to senior leadership and relevant government contacts.

steps.title: Remove and replace the manipulated element with a trusted alternative
steps.desc: Replace the affected component, software, or supplier relationship with a vetted, trusted alternative.

steps.title: Conduct forensic/technical analysis of the manipulation
steps.desc: Analyze the manipulated element to understand its full capability and any resulting compromise.

steps.title: Validate the trusted replacement's provenance
steps.desc: Confirm the replacement element's supply chain provenance meets trusted-sourcing standards before full reliance.

steps.title: Restore normal operations with the trusted replacement
steps.desc: Return to normal operations using the verified, trusted alternative.

steps.title: Document incident and update geopolitical supply chain risk assessment
steps.desc: File a comprehensive report and update sourcing policy to account for geopolitical risk factors.
steps.outcome: Report filed and sourcing policy updated.

ITID-61841.def: A confirmed or strongly suspected nation-state or APT attack against a vendor supplying products or services to critical infrastructure sectors (energy, water, healthcare, financial services, etc.), where the targeting is motivated by the vendor's role in supporting critical infrastructure rather than general commercial espionage.
ITID-61841.purpose: Classifies nation-state or APT targeting of a vendor specifically because that vendor supports critical infrastructure the organization operates or depends on.
scopeIncludes: Government advisories identifying critical-infrastructure vendor targeting by a nation-state actor
Threat intelligence linking an attack against a critical-infrastructure vendor to known APT groups specializing in infrastructure targeting
Sector-specific ISAC alerts regarding vendor compromise affecting critical infrastructure operators
scopeExcludes: General nation-state vendor targeting without a critical-infrastructure nexus (see Nation-State Attack on Supply Chain Vendor group)
Attacks directly against the organization's own critical infrastructure systems (a different Tier-1 domain)
ITID-61841.severity: Critical, given the potential for cascading impact to essential services.
ITID-61841.escalation: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, legal, sector regulators, and national critical-infrastructure protection authorities.
indicators: Government critical-infrastructure advisory naming a targeted vendor
Threat intelligence attributing the attack to APT groups known for infrastructure targeting (e.g., ICS-focused actors)
Sector ISAC alert regarding vendor compromise with infrastructure implications
vectors: Targeting of operational technology (OT) or industrial control system (ICS) vendors
Spear-phishing against critical-infrastructure vendor engineering staff
Exploitation of remote monitoring/management tools used across infrastructure vendor customers
rootCauses: Vendor's insufficient OT/ICS-specific security controls
High strategic value of infrastructure vendors as access points to multiple critical operators
Limited sector-wide threat intelligence sharing for infrastructure-vendor targeting
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
