controls: Sector-specific ISAC participation for critical-infrastructure vendors
OT/ICS-specific vendor security assessment requirements
Enhanced monitoring for known infrastructure-targeting APT TTPs
ITID-61841.detection: Low to moderate; strongest detection comes from sector ISAC alerts and government critical-infrastructure advisories rather than internal telemetry alone.
ITID-61841.response: Coordinate with sector regulators and government critical-infrastructure protection authorities, isolate vendor connectivity, and assess cascading impact to essential services.
metrics: Number of critical-infrastructure vendors assessed for nation-state targeting risk
Time to sector-regulator notification after confirmation
sops: Critical Infrastructure Vendor Attack Response SOP
ITID-61841.notes: This is the general leaf for Targeted Attacks on Critical Infrastructure Vendors; differentiated from the general nation-state vendor leaf by the critical-infrastructure nexus.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Targeted Attack on Critical Infrastructure Vendor
playbook.description: A vendor supporting critical infrastructure functions is subject to a targeted attack, creating downstream risk to the organization.

steps.title: Confirm the targeted attack and affected critical infrastructure vendor
steps.desc: Validate the disclosure and identify the specific vendor and critical function affected.
steps.outcome: Confirmed attack details and affected vendor.

steps.title: Determine organizational dependency on the affected critical function
steps.desc: Assess how the organization's operations depend on the critical infrastructure function provided by the vendor.

steps.title: Hunt for related compromise indicators in organizational systems
steps.desc: Search for indicators of compromise associated with the attack within the organization's own environment given the critical infrastructure targeting pattern.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of related compromise.

steps.title: Activate critical infrastructure contingency/continuity plan
steps.desc: Invoke continuity plans for the affected critical function, including manual failover procedures if applicable.

steps.title: Restrict connectivity to the affected vendor pending assessment
steps.desc: Reduce or isolate network connections to the vendor to limit exposure.

steps.title: Escalate immediately to executive leadership, Legal, and government/sector ISAC
steps.desc: Given critical infrastructure implications, escalate to senior leadership and engage relevant sector-specific Information Sharing and Analysis Center (ISAC) and government contacts.

steps.title: Conduct full incident response for any organizational compromise found
steps.desc: Fully investigate and remediate any compromise indicators found within organizational systems.

steps.title: Verify the vendor's remediation and restoration of the critical function
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor has remediated the attack and safely restored the critical infrastructure function.
steps.abort: If unconfirmed, maintain continuity measures.

steps.title: Restore normal reliance on the vendor's critical function under enhanced monitoring
steps.desc: Transition back to normal operations with heightened monitoring for a sustained period.
steps.outcome: Normal operations restored with enhanced monitoring.

steps.title: Document incident and reassess critical infrastructure vendor resilience requirements
steps.desc: File a comprehensive report and update resilience/redundancy requirements for critical infrastructure-dependent vendors.
steps.outcome: Report filed and resilience requirements updated.

ITID-61911.def: A failure by the third-party risk management (TPRM) program to conduct a vendor's security assessment within the schedule defined by its risk tier, resulting in a period where the organization is operating without current insight into that vendor's security posture.
ITID-61911.purpose: Captures the governance gap where a scheduled vendor security assessment simply did not happen on time, leaving the organization without current visibility into that vendor's risk posture.
scopeIncludes: A high-risk-tier vendor whose annual reassessment is more than one review cycle overdue
A newly onboarded vendor whose required initial security assessment was never completed before go-live
scopeExcludes: An assessment that was completed but relied solely on unverified vendor self-attestation (ITID-61912)
ITID-61911.severity: Medium, escalating to High for vendors in a higher risk tier or with access to sensitive systems/data, since the core problem is a visibility gap rather than a confirmed technical compromise.
ITID-61911.priority: P2 for standard-tier vendors; P1 for high-risk-tier vendors significantly overdue for reassessment.
ITID-61911.escalation: Escalate to the TPRM program owner and vendor relationship manager to schedule the overdue assessment; escalate to risk leadership if the vendor's risk tier warrants and the assessment remains unscheduled after notice.
indicators: TPRM tracking system flagging a vendor assessment past its due date
Vendor risk register showing no completed assessment within the required cadence for its tier
Onboarding audit revealing a vendor live in production without a completed initial assessment
vectors: Scheduled vendor security assessment skipped or repeatedly delayed, leaving known-unknown risk unassessed
No escalation trigger when an assessment milestone is missed, allowing the gap to persist unnoticed
rootCauses: TPRM program lacking automated scheduling and escalation for overdue assessments
Insufficient TPRM staffing relative to vendor portfolio size
Vendor risk tiering not kept current, understating a vendor's true criticality
controls: Automated TPRM scheduling and escalation workflow tied to vendor risk tier
Mandatory completed assessment as a go-live gate for new vendors
Periodic reconciliation of vendor risk tiering against actual data/system access
ITID-61911.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; this is a program-management gap identified through TPRM tracking and audit, not SOC monitoring.
ITID-61911.response: Schedule and complete the overdue assessment as the primary remediation; apply compensating monitoring or access restriction for the vendor in the interim if the risk tier warrants it.
metrics: Percentage of vendor assessments completed within their required cadence
Average days overdue for assessments in arrears
ITID-61911.notes: vendor risk-management/governance gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk management (TPRM) program. Differentiated from ITID-61912 by axis: this leaf is about assessment scheduling/cadence, not the rigor of an assessment that was actually performed.

playbook.name: Vendor Security Assessment Skipped or Delayed Past Schedule
playbook.description: A vendor's required periodic security assessment was skipped or significantly delayed past its scheduled interval, discovered during governance review.

steps.title: Document how the gap was surfaced
steps.desc: Record the discovery source (internal audit, GRC platform alert, annual vendor review) and the specific assessment that was skipped or delayed.

steps.title: Determine the vendor's risk tier and the required assessment cadence
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor's assigned risk tier and the assessment frequency required by policy for that tier.
steps.outcome: Required cadence confirmed and compared to actual.

steps.title: Assess current risk exposure given the assessment gap
steps.desc: Evaluate what has changed in the vendor relationship (new data types, expanded access, prior incidents) since the last assessment to gauge urgency.

steps.title: Notify vendor risk management/GRC owner and Procurement
steps.desc: Flag the overdue assessment to the accountable vendor risk owner and Procurement for prioritization.

steps.title: Determine if interim restrictions are warranted pending assessment
steps.desc: Based on risk exposure, decide whether to restrict the vendor's access or data scope until the overdue assessment is completed.

steps.title: Schedule and complete the overdue security assessment
steps.desc: Coordinate with the vendor to complete the required assessment (questionnaire, on-site audit, third-party certification review) as soon as practicable.

steps.title: Review assessment findings and remediate any new gaps identified
steps.desc: Address any control gaps or risks surfaced by the completed assessment.

steps.title: Update the vendor's assessment record and schedule the next cycle
steps.desc: Record the completed assessment and set an automated reminder for the next scheduled cycle.
steps.outcome: Vendor record updated and next cycle scheduled.

steps.title: Document the gap and implement assessment-schedule tracking controls
steps.desc: File a report and implement automated tracking/alerting to prevent future assessment schedule slippage across the vendor portfolio.
steps.outcome: Report filed and tracking controls implemented.

ITID-61912.def: A failure by the third-party risk management (TPRM) program to independently verify a vendor's self-attestation of its security controls (via audit, evidence review, or third-party certification confirmation), resulting in a risk assessment that may materially overstate the vendor's actual security posture.
ITID-61912.purpose: Captures the governance gap where a vendor's self-reported security claims were accepted at face value with no independent verification, undermining the reliability of the resulting risk assessment.
scopeIncludes: A vendor questionnaire response accepted without requesting or reviewing supporting evidence (audit reports, penetration test results)
A vendor's claimed certification status accepted without direct verification with the certifying body or review of the certificate itself
scopeExcludes: A vendor assessment that was never scheduled or performed at all (ITID-61911)
ITID-61912.severity: Medium to High, since the risk here is a false sense of assurance about a vendor's posture rather than a confirmed absence of assessment activity, which can be more dangerous because it masks the underlying gap.
ITID-61912.priority: P2 for standard-tier vendors; P1 if the unverified attestation covers a vendor with access to critical systems or sensitive data.
ITID-61912.escalation: Escalate to the TPRM program owner to require independent verification retroactively; escalate to risk leadership if a pattern of unverified attestations is found across multiple vendors.
indicators: TPRM assessment records showing questionnaire responses with no corresponding evidence attachment or verification note
Post-incident review revealing a vendor's attested controls did not match its actual implementation
vectors: Vendor's self-attestation questionnaire accepted at face value without independent evidence or a third-party audit report
No sampling or spot-verification program to catch inaccurate or overstated vendor self-attestations
rootCauses: TPRM process not requiring evidence submission alongside self-attestation questionnaires
No sampling or spot-check program to independently verify a subset of vendor attestations
Insufficient TPRM analyst capacity to review evidence in depth for every vendor
controls: Mandatory evidence submission (audit reports, certifications, scan results) alongside all self-attestation questionnaires
Risk-based sampling program for independent verification of vendor attestations
Direct certifying-body verification for claimed certifications on high-risk vendors
ITID-61912.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; this is a program-quality gap identified through TPRM process audit, not SOC monitoring.
ITID-61912.response: Require the vendor to submit verifiable evidence for the specific attested controls, and independently verify before relying on the assessment for risk-acceptance decisions.
metrics: Percentage of vendor assessments with independently verified evidence versus self-attestation alone
Number of discrepancies found between attestation and verified evidence per audit cycle
ITID-61912.notes: vendor risk-management/governance gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk management (TPRM) program. Differentiated from ITID-61911 by axis: this leaf is about verification rigor of a completed assessment, not whether an assessment occurred at all.

playbook.name: Vendor Self-Attestation Accepted Without Independent Verification
playbook.description: A vendor's security self-attestation was accepted as sufficient without any independent verification, discovered during governance review.

steps.title: Document how the gap was surfaced
steps.desc: Record the discovery source (internal audit, new risk policy review) identifying that self-attestation was accepted without verification.

steps.title: Determine the vendor's risk tier and verification requirements
steps.desc: Confirm whether policy requires independent verification for vendors of this risk tier and data sensitivity.

steps.title: Assess the credibility and specificity of the existing self-attestation
steps.desc: Review the self-attestation content for specificity and plausibility as an interim risk gauge.

steps.title: Notify vendor risk management/GRC owner
steps.desc: Flag the verification gap to the accountable vendor risk owner.

steps.title: Require independent verification (audit, certification, or penetration test evidence)
steps.desc: Request the vendor provide independently verifiable evidence (SOC 2 report, ISO certificate, third-party audit) rather than self-attestation alone.
steps.abort: If the vendor cannot or will not provide independent verification, escalate to Procurement/Legal for contractual remedy or vendor replacement.

steps.title: Review verification results and remediate any discrepancies with prior attestation
steps.desc: Compare independent verification findings against the original self-attestation and address any discrepancies.

steps.title: Update the vendor's risk record with verified assessment results
steps.desc: Record the independently verified assessment and update the vendor's risk rating accordingly.

steps.title: Document the gap and update vendor assessment policy to require independent verification
steps.desc: File a report and revise policy to mandate independent verification for vendors above a defined risk threshold.

ITID-61913.def: A catch-all classification for an inadequate vendor security audit finding used during initial triage before the specific pattern (missed schedule vs. unverified attestation) is determined.
ITID-61913.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for an inadequate-vendor-security-audit finding that has not yet been narrowed to a scheduling gap or a verification-rigor gap.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported vendor audit-inadequacy findings pending categorization among the sibling patterns in this group
scopeExcludes: Any case confirmed as a missed/delayed assessment schedule (ITID-61911)
Any case confirmed as unverified self-attestation (ITID-61912)
ITID-61913.severity: Medium to High by default, consistent with the sibling leaves, until the finding is further categorized.
ITID-61913.escalation: Escalate to the TPRM program owner as with any confirmed audit-inadequacy finding; reclassification should not delay remediation planning.
indicators: Initial audit-inadequacy finding pending categorization
vectors: Generic inadequate vendor security audit not captured by a more specific sub-category
Audit scope excluded a system or process that later became the source of a vendor-related incident
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine the specific audit-inadequacy pattern
controls: TPRM triage workflow requiring reclassification within a defined SLA
ITID-61913.detection: Not applicable; this is a TPRM triage leaf, not a technical detection surface.
ITID-61913.response: Track through standard TPRM remediation process while categorization proceeds; reclassify promptly once determined.
metrics: Number of findings held in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
ITID-61913.notes: vendor risk-management/governance gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk management (TPRM) program. This is an intake/triage leaf; every finding logged here should be reclassified into a specific sibling ITID once determined.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Inadequate Vendor Security Audit
playbook.description: A vendor's security audit process is found inadequate through an unspecified or unclassified governance gap.

steps.title: Document how the inadequacy was discovered
steps.desc: Record the discovery source and specific nature of the audit inadequacy.

steps.title: Determine the required audit standard against actual practice
steps.desc: Compare the organization's vendor audit policy requirements against what was actually performed.
steps.outcome: Gap between policy and practice confirmed.

steps.title: Assess risk exposure from the audit inadequacy
steps.desc: Evaluate the practical risk the inadequate audit process has left unaddressed.

steps.title: Notify vendor risk management/GRC owner
steps.desc: Flag the inadequacy to the accountable owner for prioritized action.

steps.title: Conduct or commission a proper security audit
steps.desc: Perform or commission an audit meeting the organization's required standard.

steps.title: Remediate findings from the completed audit
steps.desc: Address any gaps or risks identified by the newly completed, adequate audit.
steps.outcome: Findings remediated or tracked to closure.

steps.title: Update the vendor's risk record
steps.desc: Record the completed audit and updated risk status.

steps.title: Document the gap and strengthen audit process standards
steps.desc: File a report and strengthen the organization's vendor audit process standards and quality checks.

ITID-61921.def: A vendor risk-management failure in which a vendor's access to internal systems is either not logged in a form usable for review, or is logged but never actually reviewed on any cadence, such that misuse or compromise of that access would go undetected.
ITID-61921.purpose: Captures the governance gap where a vendor has standing access to internal systems, but that access generates no logs or is never reviewed, leaving it effectively unmonitored.
scopeIncludes: Vendor remote-access sessions with no session logging or recording enabled
Vendor account access logs collected but never reviewed by any owner on a defined cadence
scopeExcludes: Vendor access that is logged and reviewed but lacks a time-bound expiration (ITID-61922)
ITID-61921.severity: High, since unmonitored standing access to internal systems is a persistent, exploitable blind spot regardless of whether the vendor is inherently trustworthy.
ITID-61921.priority: P2 for lower-risk-tier vendor access; P1 for privileged or broad-scope vendor access with no logging or review.
ITID-61921.escalation: Escalate to the access-owning system/application team and TPRM program to establish logging and a defined review cadence immediately.
indicators: Access audit revealing no session logs exist for a vendor's remote-access mechanism
Log review cadence records showing vendor access logs have never been reviewed since access was granted
Vendor access discovered during an unrelated audit that was unknown to the system owner
vectors: Vendor remote-access sessions into internal systems were not logged or centrally reviewed, hiding misuse
No periodic access-review cadence to catch dormant or anomalous vendor accounts
rootCauses: Vendor access provisioned outside of the organization's standard access-management and logging infrastructure
No defined ownership for reviewing vendor-specific access logs
Vendor remote-access tooling selected without a logging/monitoring requirement
controls: Mandatory session logging for all vendor remote access, routed through the organization's standard access infrastructure
Defined review cadence and named owner for vendor access log review
Periodic vendor access inventory reconciliation
ITID-61921.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense as a standalone control gap; where logging does exist but review is absent, the fix is procedural rather than technical.
ITID-61921.response: Implement logging where absent, assign a review owner and cadence, and retroactively review available historical access records for signs of misuse.
metrics: Percentage of vendor access points with logging enabled
Percentage of vendor access logs reviewed within the defined cadence
ITID-61921.notes: vendor risk-management/governance gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk management (TPRM) program. Differentiated from ITID-61922 by axis: this leaf is about logging/review of access, not its lifecycle/expiration.

playbook.name: Vendor Access Not Logged or Reviewed
playbook.description: A vendor's access to internal systems is found to have not been logged or periodically reviewed, discovered during governance review.

steps.title: Document how the logging/review gap was discovered
steps.desc: Record the discovery source (audit, access-governance review) identifying the vendor account(s) lacking logging or review.

steps.title: Identify all vendor accounts affected by the logging/review gap
steps.desc: Determine the full scope of vendor accounts lacking adequate logging or periodic access review.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected accounts identified.

steps.title: Attempt retrospective log reconstruction where possible
steps.desc: Where any partial logs exist, attempt to reconstruct historical vendor activity to identify any past anomalies.
steps.outcome: Retrospective review completed to the extent possible.

steps.title: Enable logging for all identified vendor accounts immediately
steps.desc: Turn on comprehensive access and activity logging for the affected vendor accounts.
steps.outcome: Logging enabled for all affected accounts.

steps.title: Notify vendor risk management/GRC owner and IT Security
steps.desc: Flag the gap to accountable owners for prioritized remediation and process fix.

steps.title: Establish a periodic access review process for the affected accounts
steps.desc: Implement a recurring access-entitlement review cadence for all vendor accounts identified in the gap.

steps.title: Conduct the first access review under the new process
steps.desc: Perform the initial review to validate all vendor access is still necessary and appropriately scoped.
steps.outcome: Initial review completed and any excess access removed.

steps.title: Update the vendor access governance record
steps.desc: Document the remediated logging and review controls in the vendor's governance record.

steps.title: Document the gap and extend logging/review requirements organization-wide
steps.desc: File a report and audit all other vendor accounts organization-wide for the same logging/review gap.
steps.outcome: Report filed and organization-wide audit initiated.

ITID-61922.def: A vendor risk-management failure in which access to internal systems is granted to a vendor without a defined expiration date or automatic revocation tied to the engagement's end date, resulting in stale, unnecessary access that persists after the business need has ended.
ITID-61922.purpose: Captures the governance gap where a vendor is granted access to internal systems with no expiration date, leaving standing access active indefinitely beyond the engagement's actual need.
scopeIncludes: A vendor's access credentials remaining active months or years after a project or support engagement concluded
Vendor access provisioned with no expiration field set in the identity/access management system
scopeExcludes: Vendor access that is time-bound but simply not logged or reviewed while active (ITID-61921)
ITID-61922.severity: High, since stale, unexpired vendor access represents an unnecessary and often-forgotten attack surface with no ongoing business justification.
ITID-61922.priority: P2 for identified stale access with no evidence of misuse; P1 if stale access is found to have been used after the engagement's actual end date.
ITID-61922.escalation: Escalate to the access-owning system/application team to revoke immediately and to TPRM to implement time-bound provisioning going forward.
indicators: Access review identifying vendor accounts with no expiration date set
Vendor account activity observed after the corresponding contract or statement of work has ended
Identity/access management audit finding a large population of vendor accounts with indefinite validity
vectors: Vendor account provisioned with standing access and no automatic expiration after the engagement ended
Offboarding process failed to revoke vendor credentials once the contracted work concluded
rootCauses: Access provisioning process not tied to contract/engagement end dates
No automated expiration or periodic recertification requirement for vendor accounts
Manual, ad hoc vendor access requests bypassing standard identity governance workflows
controls: Time-bound access provisioning tied to contract or engagement end date with automatic expiration
Periodic recertification requirement for all standing vendor access
Identity governance workflow requiring an expiration date as a mandatory field for vendor access requests
ITID-61922.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; this is a lifecycle/provisioning gap identified through access review and identity governance audit rather than SOC monitoring.
ITID-61922.response: Revoke stale access immediately upon identification, implement automatic expiration tied to engagement end dates, and audit for any activity that occurred after the engagement concluded.
metrics: Percentage of vendor access grants with a defined expiration date
Number of stale/expired-engagement vendor accounts identified and revoked per quarter
ITID-61922.notes: vendor risk-management/governance gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk management (TPRM) program. Differentiated from ITID-61921 by axis: this leaf is about access lifecycle/expiration, not logging and review of active access.

playbook.name: Vendor Access Granted Without Time-Bound Expiration
playbook.description: A vendor is found to have been granted standing access to internal systems without any time-bound expiration, discovered during governance review.

steps.title: Document how the gap was discovered
steps.desc: Record the discovery source (access audit, provisioning review) identifying vendor accounts with no expiration date.

steps.title: Inventory all vendor accounts lacking time-bound access
steps.desc: Identify every vendor account across systems that has standing, non-expiring access.

steps.title: Determine whether each account's access is still contractually justified
steps.desc: Cross-reference each standing account against active contracts and current engagement scope to identify stale or unjustified access.
steps.outcome: Justification status determined for each account.

steps.title: Disable or restrict access for accounts no longer justified
steps.desc: Immediately revoke access for any vendor accounts tied to expired or inactive engagements.

steps.title: Notify vendor risk management/GRC owner
steps.desc: Flag the gap to accountable owners for prioritized remediation and process fix.

steps.title: Implement time-bound expiration for all remaining justified vendor access
steps.desc: Configure expiration dates tied to contract end dates or defined engagement windows for all active vendor accounts.
steps.outcome: Time-bound expiration implemented for all vendor access.

steps.title: Establish a renewal/re-justification workflow for expiring access
steps.desc: Create a process requiring active re-justification before access expiration is extended.

steps.title: Update the vendor access governance record
steps.desc: Document the remediated time-bound access controls in the governance record.

steps.title: Document the gap and mandate time-bound access as a standing policy
steps.desc: File a report and formalize a policy requiring time-bound expiration for all new and existing vendor access grants.

ITID-61923.def: A catch-all classification for an unmonitored vendor access finding used during initial triage before the specific pattern (logging/review vs. lifecycle/expiration) is determined.
ITID-61923.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for an unmonitored-vendor-access finding that has not yet been narrowed to a logging/review gap or an expiration/lifecycle gap.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported vendor access governance findings pending categorization among the sibling patterns in this group
scopeExcludes: Any case confirmed as a logging/review gap (ITID-61921)
Any case confirmed as a lifecycle/expiration gap (ITID-61922)
ITID-61923.severity: High by default, consistent with the sibling leaves, until the finding is further categorized.
ITID-61923.escalation: Escalate to the TPRM program and access-owning team as with any confirmed unmonitored-access finding; reclassification should not delay remediation.
indicators: Initial vendor access governance finding pending categorization
vectors: Generic unmonitored vendor access not captured by a more specific sub-category
No unified visibility across all vendor access paths into internal systems
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine the specific access-governance gap
controls: TPRM triage workflow requiring reclassification within a defined SLA
ITID-61923.detection: Not applicable; this is a TPRM triage leaf, not a technical detection surface.
ITID-61923.response: Track through standard TPRM remediation process while categorization proceeds; reclassify promptly once determined.
metrics: Number of findings held in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
ITID-61923.notes: vendor risk-management/governance gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk management (TPRM) program. This is an intake/triage leaf; every finding logged here should be reclassified into a specific sibling ITID once determined.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Unmonitored Vendor Access
playbook.description: A vendor's access to internal systems is found unmonitored through an unspecified or unclassified governance gap.

steps.title: Document how the gap was discovered
steps.desc: Record the discovery source and nature of the unmonitored access.

steps.title: Identify the scope of unmonitored vendor access
steps.desc: Determine which vendor accounts and systems are affected by the lack of monitoring.

steps.title: Assess risk exposure from the lack of monitoring
steps.desc: Evaluate the practical risk posed by the monitoring gap given the account's access level.

steps.title: Enable monitoring/logging for the affected access immediately
steps.desc: Turn on activity monitoring and logging for the identified vendor access.

steps.title: Notify vendor risk management/GRC owner
steps.desc: Flag the gap to accountable owners for remediation.

steps.title: Establish ongoing monitoring and periodic review process
steps.desc: Implement a recurring monitoring and access review process for the vendor's access.

steps.title: Conduct an initial retrospective review under the new monitoring
steps.desc: Perform an initial review of available data to check for any historical anomalies.

steps.title: Update the vendor access governance record
steps.desc: Document the remediated monitoring controls.

steps.title: Document the gap and extend monitoring requirements organization-wide
steps.desc: File a report and audit other vendor accounts for similar monitoring gaps.

ITID-61931.def: A vendor risk-management failure in which a critical business function depends entirely on a single vendor with no documented contingency plan, alternative provider, or exit strategy, such that an outage or compromise at that vendor would directly and unavoidably disrupt the organization's operations.
ITID-61931.purpose: Captures the governance gap where the organization depends on a single vendor for a critical function with no contingency, fallback, or exit plan if that vendor becomes unavailable or compromised.
scopeIncludes: A single cloud provider or SaaS platform supporting a critical business process with no documented failover or alternative
A critical vendor relationship identified during business continuity planning as having no viable exit or substitution plan
scopeExcludes: A critical function outsourced to a vendor with known, specific security gaps despite having a contingency plan (ITID-61932)
ITID-61931.severity: Critical, since a single point of failure with no contingency plan means the organization has no way to limit business impact if the vendor experiences an outage, breach, or business failure.
ITID-61931.priority: P1 for any critical business function identified as having no vendor contingency plan.
ITID-61931.escalation: Escalate to business continuity planning, executive leadership, and the TPRM program to prioritize development of a contingency or exit plan.
indicators: Business impact analysis identifying a critical function with a single named vendor and no alternative
Business continuity plan review revealing no documented failover for a critical vendor dependency
Vendor concentration risk assessment flagging a single point of failure
vectors: Critical business function depends on a single vendor with no qualified alternate or exit plan
Vendor outage or compromise cascades directly into organizational disruption with no fallback capacity
rootCauses: Vendor selection driven by cost or convenience without consideration of concentration risk
No formal business continuity requirement to document vendor contingency plans for critical functions
Switching costs or technical lock-in discouraging investment in an alternative provider
controls: Business continuity planning requirement to document a contingency or exit plan for every critical vendor dependency
Vendor concentration risk assessment as part of the TPRM program
Periodic testing of vendor contingency/failover plans where feasible
ITID-61931.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; this is a business continuity and governance gap identified through impact analysis and continuity planning, not SOC monitoring.
ITID-61931.response: Prioritize development of a documented contingency plan, evaluate alternative providers or in-house fallback options, and incorporate the dependency into ongoing business continuity testing.
metrics: Number of critical functions with no documented vendor contingency plan
Percentage of critical vendor dependencies with a tested failover/exit plan
ITID-61931.notes: vendor risk-management/governance gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk management (TPRM) program. Differentiated from ITID-61932 by axis: this leaf is about continuity/resilience planning (or its absence), not the vendor's known security posture.

playbook.name: Single Point of Failure Vendor with No Contingency Plan
playbook.description: A vendor supporting a critical function is identified as a single point of failure with no documented contingency or alternate vendor plan.

steps.title: Document how the single-point-of-failure risk was identified
steps.desc: Record the discovery source (risk assessment, business impact analysis, near-miss incident) identifying the vendor as a single point of failure.

steps.title: Determine the criticality of the function the vendor supports
steps.desc: Assess the business impact if the vendor's service became unavailable, using business impact analysis criteria.

steps.title: Confirm the absence of a documented contingency plan
steps.desc: Verify no viable alternate vendor, failover, or manual workaround plan currently exists.

steps.title: Notify business continuity and Procurement leadership
steps.desc: Escalate the single-point-of-failure finding to business continuity planning and Procurement leadership given the criticality.

steps.title: Identify and vet potential alternate vendors or internal capabilities
steps.desc: Research and evaluate alternate vendors or internal solutions that could serve as contingency options.

steps.title: Develop and document a formal contingency/business continuity plan
steps.desc: Create a documented contingency plan including failover procedures, alternate vendor activation criteria, and manual workarounds.

steps.title: Test the contingency plan
steps.desc: Conduct a tabletop exercise or limited test of the contingency plan to validate its viability.

steps.title: Formalize the contingency plan into business continuity documentation
steps.desc: Incorporate the validated plan into the organization's formal business continuity/disaster recovery documentation.
steps.outcome: Plan formalized and accessible to relevant teams.

steps.title: Document the gap and establish periodic single-point-of-failure reviews
steps.desc: File a report and establish a recurring review process to identify other critical single-point-of-failure vendor dependencies.
steps.outcome: Report filed and review process established.

ITID-61932.def: A vendor risk-management failure in which a critical business function remains outsourced to a vendor with previously identified and documented security gaps, without adequate compensating controls or a remediation plan being enforced, representing a knowing acceptance of elevated risk.
ITID-61932.purpose: Captures the governance gap where the organization knowingly continues to rely on a vendor for a critical function despite documented, known security gaps in that vendor's posture.
scopeIncludes: A critical function continuing with a vendor that failed a security assessment, with no compensating controls implemented
A vendor with a known unremediated finding from a prior audit continuing to support a critical system with no risk-acceptance documentation
scopeExcludes: A single point of failure vendor with an otherwise clean security posture but no contingency plan (ITID-61931)
ITID-61932.severity: Critical, since this represents a known, documented risk being knowingly carried for a critical function rather than an undiscovered gap.
ITID-61932.priority: P1 for any critical function continuing with a vendor carrying an unremediated high-severity finding.
ITID-61932.escalation: Escalate to risk leadership for formal risk-acceptance review or forced remediation; this should not remain an informal, undocumented risk-carrying decision.
indicators: Vendor risk register showing an open, unremediated high-severity finding for a vendor supporting a critical function
No formal risk-acceptance documentation on file despite a known, aged security gap
Repeated assessment cycles identifying the same unresolved gap for the same critical vendor
vectors: Critical function outsourced to a vendor with previously identified, unresolved security gaps
Business continuity pressure overrode security risk-acceptance criteria during vendor selection
rootCauses: No formal risk-acceptance or escalation process for unremediated vendor findings tied to critical functions
Switching costs or lack of viable alternatives discouraging action on known vendor gaps
TPRM findings not weighted by the criticality of the function the vendor supports
controls: Formal risk-acceptance process requiring executive sign-off for any unremediated finding tied to a critical vendor function
Remediation-tracking with escalating consequences for aged, unresolved vendor findings
Criticality-weighted prioritization of vendor findings within the TPRM program
ITID-61932.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; this is a risk-governance gap identified through the vendor risk register and audit follow-up process, not SOC monitoring.
ITID-61932.response: Force a formal risk-acceptance decision at an appropriate leadership level, require a remediation plan with a firm deadline, or begin transition planning to an alternative vendor.
metrics: Number of critical functions supported by a vendor with an open high-severity finding
Average age of unremediated findings for critical-function vendors
ITID-61932.notes: vendor risk-management/governance gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk management (TPRM) program. Differentiated from ITID-61931 by axis: this leaf is about a known, documented security gap being knowingly carried, not the absence of a contingency plan.

playbook.name: Critical Function Outsourced to Vendor with Known Security Gaps
playbook.description: A critical business function is found to be outsourced to a vendor with known, unremediated security gaps.

steps.title: Document how the known security gaps and outsourcing arrangement were identified
steps.desc: Record the discovery source (audit, incident, risk review) and the specific critical function and vendor involved.

steps.title: Catalog the vendor's known, unremediated security gaps
steps.desc: Compile the specific security deficiencies known about the vendor from prior assessments or incidents.
steps.outcome: Complete list of known gaps compiled.

steps.title: Assess business impact if the vendor were compromised
steps.desc: Evaluate the potential business impact given the critical nature of the outsourced function combined with the known gaps.

steps.title: Escalate to executive leadership, Procurement, and Legal
steps.desc: Given the criticality, escalate the risk to senior stakeholders for an urgent decision on remediation or vendor replacement.
steps.outcome: Leadership engaged and decision process initiated.

steps.title: Apply compensating controls on the organization's side where feasible
steps.desc: Implement interim compensating controls (enhanced monitoring, restricted data sharing) to reduce risk while a longer-term decision is made.

steps.title: Require the vendor to remediate the known security gaps on a defined timeline
steps.desc: Formally require the vendor to close the identified gaps within an agreed timeline, backed by contractual consequences.
steps.abort: If the vendor is unwilling or unable, proceed to evaluate alternate vendors.

steps.title: Verify remediation or begin transition to an alternate vendor
steps.desc: Based on the vendor's remediation progress, decide whether to continue the relationship or transition the critical function elsewhere.

steps.title: Confirm the critical function operates securely going forward
steps.desc: Verify the remediated vendor or the new alternate vendor meets security requirements for the critical function.

steps.title: Document the gap and prohibit outsourcing critical functions to vendors with open critical findings
steps.desc: File a report and establish a policy preventing critical-function outsourcing to vendors with unremediated high/critical security findings.

ITID-61933.def: A catch-all classification for an over-reliance-on-a-high-risk-vendor finding used during initial triage before the specific pattern (no contingency plan vs. known security gap) is determined.
ITID-61933.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for an over-reliance-on-high-risk-vendor finding that has not yet been narrowed to a single-point-of-failure or known-security-gap classification.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported vendor over-reliance findings pending categorization among the sibling patterns in this group
scopeExcludes: Any case confirmed as a single point of failure with no contingency plan (ITID-61931)
Any case confirmed as a critical function outsourced despite known security gaps (ITID-61932)
ITID-61933.severity: Critical by default, consistent with the sibling leaves, until the finding is further categorized.
ITID-61933.escalation: Escalate to risk leadership and the TPRM program as with any confirmed over-reliance finding; reclassification should not delay risk-acceptance or remediation planning.
indicators: Initial vendor over-reliance finding pending categorization
vectors: Generic over-reliance on a high-risk vendor not captured by a more specific sub-category
Vendor risk tiering did not account for the operational criticality of the outsourced function
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine the specific over-reliance pattern
controls: TPRM triage workflow requiring reclassification within a defined SLA
ITID-61933.detection: Not applicable; this is a TPRM triage leaf, not a technical detection surface.
ITID-61933.response: Track through standard TPRM remediation and risk-acceptance process while categorization proceeds; reclassify promptly once determined.
metrics: Number of findings held in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
ITID-61933.notes: vendor risk-management/governance gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk management (TPRM) program. This is an intake/triage leaf; every finding logged here should be reclassified into a specific sibling ITID once determined.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Over-Reliance on High-Risk Vendor
playbook.description: The organization is found to be over-reliant on a high-risk vendor through an unspecified or unclassified governance gap.

steps.title: Document how the over-reliance was identified
steps.desc: Record the discovery source and nature of the over-reliance concern.

steps.title: Assess the vendor's risk profile and the organization's dependency level
steps.desc: Evaluate the vendor's current risk rating and the degree of organizational dependency on it.
steps.outcome: Risk profile and dependency level assessed.

steps.title: Determine potential business impact of continued over-reliance
steps.desc: Evaluate the potential impact should the high-risk vendor experience a disruption or compromise.

steps.title: Notify Procurement and business continuity leadership
steps.desc: Escalate the over-reliance finding for prioritized action.

steps.title: Develop a diversification or risk-reduction plan
steps.desc: Create a plan to diversify the dependency (alternate vendors, in-house capability) or reduce the vendor's risk profile.

steps.title: Begin implementing the plan
steps.desc: Execute initial steps of the diversification or risk-reduction plan.

steps.title: Update the vendor risk record with the reduced dependency status
steps.desc: Document progress toward reduced over-reliance in the vendor risk register.

steps.title: Document the gap and establish ongoing vendor concentration risk monitoring
steps.desc: File a report and establish periodic reviews of vendor concentration risk across the organization.

ITID-61941.def: A vendor risk-management failure in which the contract governing a vendor relationship lacks specific, measurable, and enforceable security requirements (such as control specifications, audit rights, notification timelines, or remedies for non-compliance), leaving the organization unable to contractually compel or enforce an adequate security posture.
ITID-61941.purpose: Captures the governance gap where a vendor contract was signed without enforceable, specific security requirements, leaving the organization with no contractual lever to compel the vendor's security posture.
scopeIncludes: A vendor contract with only vague, unenforceable language about maintaining 'reasonable security measures'
A contract missing a right-to-audit clause, breach-notification clause, or specific control requirements entirely
scopeExcludes: A contract with adequate security requirements that the vendor simply failed to meet post-signature (ITID-61942)
ITID-61941.severity: High, since a contract lacking enforceable security requirements removes the organization's primary lever for holding the vendor accountable, regardless of the vendor's actual current posture.
ITID-61941.priority: P2 for standard-tier vendors identified during a contract review; P1 for a critical or high-risk-tier vendor found to have no enforceable security requirements in its contract.
ITID-61941.escalation: Escalate to legal and vendor management to renegotiate the contract at the next available opportunity (renewal or amendment); escalate to risk leadership if renegotiation is not feasible in the near term for a critical vendor.
indicators: Contract review finding no specific security control requirements, audit rights, or breach-notification clause
Legal/procurement audit identifying a population of vendor contracts signed without standard security-terms review
Inability to enforce a remediation timeline against a vendor due to absent contractual language
vectors: Vendor contract signed without specific, measurable, enforceable security clauses (e.g., control baselines, breach notification SLAs, audit rights)
Procurement/legal review did not involve security stakeholders before contract execution
rootCauses: Vendor contracts executed without mandatory security/legal review prior to signature
Standard contract templates not including baseline security requirement language
Time pressure or business urgency bypassing the standard vendor contracting review process
controls: Mandatory security/legal review of all vendor contracts prior to signature
Standard contract template with baseline security requirement, audit-rights, and breach-notification language
Contract renewal process that flags and remediates legacy contracts lacking current security-terms standards
ITID-61941.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; this is a contracting/legal gap identified through contract review, not SOC monitoring.
ITID-61941.response: Prioritize renegotiation of the contract to include enforceable security requirements at the next opportunity, and apply compensating monitoring or access restrictions in the interim for higher-risk vendors.
metrics: Percentage of active vendor contracts with enforceable security requirement language
Number of legacy contracts remediated with updated security terms per year
ITID-61941.notes: vendor risk-management/governance gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk management (TPRM) program. Differentiated from ITID-61942 by axis: this leaf is an upstream contract-drafting gap (the requirement was never written in), not enforcement of an existing requirement.

playbook.name: Vendor Contract Lacking Enforceable Security Requirements
playbook.description: A vendor contract is found to lack enforceable, specific security requirements, discovered during governance or legal review.

steps.title: Document how the contract gap was identified
steps.desc: Record the discovery source (contract review, audit, incident revealing lack of leverage) and the specific missing or unenforceable language.

steps.title: Review the current contract against the organization's standard security addendum
steps.desc: Compare the existing contract terms to the organization's baseline required security clauses (audit rights, breach notification, control requirements).

steps.title: Assess risk exposure created by the contractual gap
steps.desc: Evaluate the practical risk the organization faces from lacking enforceable security terms with this vendor.

steps.title: Notify Legal and Procurement
steps.desc: Escalate the contractual gap to Legal and Procurement for prioritized remediation.

steps.title: Negotiate an updated security addendum with the vendor
steps.desc: Work with Legal to negotiate and add enforceable security requirements to the contract, including audit rights and breach-notification clauses.
steps.abort: If the vendor refuses reasonable security terms, escalate to Procurement leadership for a sourcing decision.

steps.title: Execute the updated contract terms
steps.desc: Finalize and execute the amended contract with the new security requirements.

steps.title: Update the vendor's contract record and risk profile
steps.desc: Document the updated contract terms in the vendor management system.

steps.title: Document the gap and audit other vendor contracts for the same deficiency
steps.desc: File a report and audit the broader vendor contract portfolio for similar missing security requirements.
steps.outcome: Report filed and portfolio audit initiated.

ITID-61942.def: A vendor risk-management failure in which a known security gap at a vendor was identified through an audit or assessment, and the organization possessed a contractual right to compel remediation, but that right was not exercised and the gap remains unresolved.
ITID-61942.purpose: Captures the governance gap where a vendor contract does include an enforceable right to audit and remediation obligations, but the organization did not act on a known finding despite having that contractual leverage.
scopeIncludes: An audit finding tracked in the vendor risk register for multiple review cycles with no remediation enforcement action taken despite an active right-to-audit clause
A vendor formally notified of a required remediation under contract, with no follow-up enforcement when the deadline passed
scopeExcludes: A vendor contract lacking the enforceable security requirements or audit rights in the first place (ITID-61941)
ITID-61942.severity: High, since the organization had the contractual tools to compel a fix and did not use them, representing a process/enforcement failure distinct from a contracting gap.
ITID-61942.priority: P1 if the unremediated finding is high-severity and affects a critical vendor relationship; P2 for lower-severity, longer-tail findings.
ITID-61942.escalation: Escalate to vendor management and legal to formally invoke the contractual remediation and audit-rights clauses; escalate to risk leadership if enforcement action does not produce vendor remediation within a defined window.
indicators: Vendor risk register showing a finding open past its committed remediation date with no formal enforcement escalation logged
Right-to-audit clause on file but never invoked despite repeated unresolved findings
Vendor relationship manager unaware that a contractual enforcement mechanism exists for the identified gap
vectors: Vendor security gap identified during an audit but never remediated despite the organization holding a contractual right to audit and require fixes
No follow-up enforcement mechanism (penalty clause, termination trigger) tied to unremediated audit findings
rootCauses: No defined escalation path from 'finding identified' to 'contractual right invoked' within the TPRM program
Vendor relationship managers lacking awareness of the specific contractual remediation and audit rights available
Reluctance to invoke contractual leverage due to relationship or business-continuity concerns
controls: Defined escalation path and SLA from finding identification to contractual enforcement action
Training for vendor relationship managers on available contractual remediation and audit-rights mechanisms
Executive-level review of vendor findings that remain unremediated past their committed deadline
ITID-61942.detection: Not applicable in the technical sense; this is a follow-through/enforcement gap identified through vendor risk register review, not SOC monitoring.
ITID-61942.response: Formally invoke the contractual right to audit and demand remediation on a firm deadline; escalate to termination or penalty clauses if the vendor does not respond.
metrics: Number of unremediated findings past their committed deadline with no enforcement action taken
Time from finding-past-due to formal contractual enforcement escalation
ITID-61942.notes: vendor risk-management/governance gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk management (TPRM) program. Differentiated from ITID-61941 by axis: this leaf is a downstream enforcement/follow-through failure where the contractual right already existed, not an upstream contract-drafting gap.

playbook.name: Known Vendor Security Gap Not Remediated Despite Contractual Right to Audit
playbook.description: A known vendor security gap remains unremediated even though the organization holds a contractual right to audit, discovered during governance review.

steps.title: Document how the unremediated gap was identified
steps.desc: Record the discovery source and details of the known, long-standing security gap.

steps.title: Confirm the contractual audit right and prior remediation commitments
steps.desc: Review the contract to confirm the audit right and any prior remediation deadlines the vendor missed.
steps.outcome: Contractual rights and missed commitments confirmed.

steps.title: Assess current risk exposure from the persistent gap
steps.desc: Evaluate the ongoing risk the unremediated gap poses given elapsed time.

steps.title: Exercise the contractual right to audit
steps.desc: Formally invoke the audit right to independently verify the gap and the vendor's lack of remediation.

steps.title: Escalate to Legal and Procurement leadership
steps.desc: Given the vendor's repeated failure to remediate, escalate for a decision on enforcement action.

steps.title: Issue a formal remediation demand with a firm deadline and consequences
steps.desc: Formally demand remediation within a defined timeline, referencing contractual remedies for continued non-compliance.

steps.title: Verify remediation or pursue contractual remedies including termination
steps.desc: Based on the vendor's response, verify remediation is complete or pursue contractual remedies up to and including termination.
steps.outcome: Gap remediated, or contractual remedy pursued.

steps.title: Update the vendor's risk record and relationship status
steps.desc: Document the outcome and update the vendor's risk tier or relationship status accordingly.

steps.title: Document the gap and establish escalation triggers for unremediated findings
steps.desc: File a report and establish automatic escalation triggers when vendor remediation deadlines are repeatedly missed.
steps.outcome: Report filed and escalation triggers established.

ITID-61943.def: A catch-all classification for a failure-to-enforce-vendor-security-policy finding used during initial triage before the specific pattern (contract lacking terms vs. terms present but not enforced) is determined.
ITID-61943.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for a failure-to-enforce-vendor-security-policy finding that has not yet been narrowed to a contract-drafting gap or a follow-through/enforcement gap.
scopeIncludes: Newly reported vendor policy-enforcement findings pending categorization among the sibling patterns in this group
scopeExcludes: Any case confirmed as a contract lacking enforceable security requirements (ITID-61941)
Any case confirmed as an unenforced existing contractual right (ITID-61942)
ITID-61943.severity: High by default, consistent with the sibling leaves, until the finding is further categorized.
ITID-61943.escalation: Escalate to vendor management and legal as with any confirmed policy-enforcement failure; reclassification should not delay remediation planning.
indicators: Initial vendor policy-enforcement finding pending categorization
vectors: Generic failure to enforce a vendor security policy not captured by a more specific sub-category
Vendor policy exceptions granted informally without a documented, time-bound risk acceptance
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail to determine the specific enforcement-failure pattern
controls: TPRM triage workflow requiring reclassification within a defined SLA
ITID-61943.detection: Not applicable; this is a TPRM triage leaf, not a technical detection surface.
ITID-61943.response: Track through standard TPRM remediation process while categorization proceeds; reclassify promptly once determined.
metrics: Number of findings held in this bucket beyond the triage SLA
ITID-61943.notes: vendor risk-management/governance gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via third-party risk management (TPRM) program. This is an intake/triage leaf; every finding logged here should be reclassified into a specific sibling ITID once determined.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Failure to Enforce Vendor Security Policy
playbook.description: The organization is found to have failed to enforce its vendor security policy through an unspecified or unclassified governance gap.

steps.title: Document how the enforcement failure was identified
steps.desc: Record the discovery source and nature of the enforcement failure.

steps.title: Determine the specific policy requirement not enforced
steps.desc: Identify the exact vendor security policy provision that was not enforced.

steps.title: Assess risk exposure from the enforcement gap
steps.desc: Evaluate the practical risk created by the lack of enforcement.

steps.title: Notify vendor risk management/GRC owner
steps.desc: Flag the enforcement gap to accountable owners for prioritized action.

steps.title: Enforce the policy requirement with the affected vendor(s)
steps.desc: Take the necessary action to bring the vendor relationship into compliance with the policy.
steps.abort: If the vendor refuses to comply, escalate to Legal/Procurement for contractual remedy.

steps.title: Verify compliance is achieved
steps.desc: Confirm the vendor now meets the policy requirement.

steps.title: Update the vendor's risk record
steps.desc: Document the resolved enforcement gap in the vendor's risk record.

steps.title: Document the gap and strengthen policy enforcement mechanisms
steps.desc: File a report and strengthen the organization's mechanisms for enforcing vendor security policy compliance.

ITID-62111.def: An incident in which a software vendor's official update mechanism (auto-updater, patch channel, or manual download from the vendor's own distribution point) delivered code that had been tampered with or replaced by an adversary, without a clearly established mechanism (injected code, forged signature, or compromised cloud build pipeline) yet confirmed.
ITID-62111.purpose: Serves as the intake leaf for a confirmed or suspected malicious software update from a legitimate third-party vendor that does not yet fit a more specific code-injection, signing-certificate, or cloud-supply-chain leaf in this Tier-3 group.
scopeIncludes: A vendor-signed or vendor-distributed update package behaving anomalously post-install and confirmed to differ from the vendor's known-good release
Reports from threat intelligence or the vendor itself of a compromised update prior to root-cause attribution
Any malicious-update case pending triage into a more specific 6212x/6213x/6214x leaf
scopeExcludes: Cases where the injection vector into the vendor's build/source is confirmed (route to ITID-62121, Third-Party Code Injection)
Cases where a forged or stolen code-signing certificate is the confirmed mechanism (route to ITID-62131)
Cases where the compromise occurred in a cloud-hosted build/distribution service specifically (route to ITID-62141)
Business-continuity/critical-disruption framing of a supply chain compromise, tracked under the parallel ITID-613xx group
ITID-62111.severity: High. A trusted update channel with a broad install base implies a potentially large blast radius even before scope is confirmed.
ITID-62111.priority: P1 on initial confirmation of any tampering in a live update channel; downgrade only once scope and mechanism are bounded.
ITID-62111.escalation: Escalate immediately to the SOC lead and vendor management; notify affected asset owners to pause auto-update ingestion pending verification.
indicators: Endpoint or EDR alerts triggered immediately following a routine vendor update
Hash mismatch between an installed update and the vendor's published checksum
Vendor security bulletin or breach notification referencing a compromised update
vectors: Compromise of vendor's update distribution infrastructure
Man-in-the-middle interception of an unsigned or weakly verified update channel
rootCauses: Organization or vendor lacking update integrity verification (signature/hash checks)
Auto-update enabled with no staged rollout or monitoring window
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Update package hash/signature verification prior to deployment
Staged/canary rollout of vendor updates before fleet-wide push
ITID-62111.detection: Detection depends heavily on EDR behavioral alerting post-update and out-of-band vendor disclosure; pure signature-based detection of a first-seen malicious update is weak.
ITID-62111.response: Freeze the affected update channel, isolate impacted hosts, and triage toward a more specific 6212x/6213x/6214x leaf as soon as mechanism is known.
metrics: Time from vendor disclosure to internal update freeze
Number of hosts exposed to a confirmed malicious update
ITID-62111.notes: Intake/unclassified leaf for this Tier-4 group; triage should move confirmed cases to a specific sibling leaf. Distinct from ITID-613xx (Critical System Disruption's own Software Supply Chain Attacks group), which tracks the same category of event from a business-continuity/operational-impact angle rather than the technical exploitation mechanism tracked here.

playbook.name: Malicious Software Update (Third-Party Vendor)
playbook.description: A trusted third-party vendor's update mechanism delivers a malicious or trojanized software update to the organization's endpoints or servers.

steps.title: Correlate anomalous behavior with recent update deployment
steps.desc: Cross-reference EDR/AV alerts, unexpected process spawns, or outbound C2-like traffic against the software update/patch deployment log for the affected vendor product.
steps.guidance: Check patch management console (SCCM/Intune/vendor auto-update logs) for the exact version and timestamp pushed to affected hosts.
steps.outcome: Confirmed correlation between a specific update package/version and onset of malicious behavior.
steps.abort: If no correlation found, treat as unrelated malware incident and redirect to standard malware IR playbook.

steps.title: Check vendor security advisories and threat intel
steps.desc: Search vendor's security bulletin, ISACs, and threat intelligence feeds for public disclosure of a compromised update or build pipeline.
steps.guidance: Search for vendor name + 'supply chain' + CVE on NVD, vendor trust center, and threat intel platforms.
steps.outcome: Determine if this is a known, publicly disclosed supply chain compromise or a novel/unreported one.

steps.title: Scope affected host population
steps.desc: Query EDR/asset inventory for all hosts that received the malicious update version.
steps.guidance: Use hash/version-based query across the fleet, not just alerting hosts, since malicious updates may be dormant on some machines.
steps.outcome: Complete list of affected/exposed hosts, including dormant ones.

steps.title: Halt further rollout of the malicious update
steps.desc: Immediately pause/block the update distribution mechanism (WSUS, vendor auto-update, package mirror) to prevent additional hosts from installing it.
steps.guidance: Block outbound access to the vendor's update CDN/domain at the firewall/proxy if pausing internally is not fast enough.
steps.outcome: No new hosts receive the compromised update.

steps.title: Network-isolate confirmed affected hosts
steps.desc: Move confirmed compromised endpoints/servers to an isolated VLAN or apply EDR network containment.
steps.guidance: Prioritize servers and privileged endpoints; preserve volatile memory before isolation if forensic capture is planned.
steps.outcome: Affected hosts cannot communicate laterally or with external C2.

steps.title: Disable or downgrade the vendor application where feasible
steps.desc: Assess whether the affected application can be safely disabled or rolled back to a last-known-good version without business disruption.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with application owner and business stakeholders on acceptable downtime.
steps.outcome: Decision recorded and, if approved, application disabled/rolled back on affected hosts.
steps.abort: If application is business-critical and cannot be disabled, apply compensating network controls instead.

steps.title: Remove malicious update and reimage where necessary
steps.desc: Uninstall the malicious update version; for hosts showing evidence of secondary payload execution, reimage from known-good baseline.
steps.guidance: Do not simply patch over a compromised host that executed the payload — reimage is required if code execution occurred.
steps.outcome: Malicious update package removed from all affected hosts; compromised hosts reimaged.

steps.title: Apply vendor-verified clean update or hotfix
steps.desc: Once the vendor issues a verified clean build/hotfix, deploy it through the standard patch pipeline after validating its signature and hash.
steps.guidance: Validate signing certificate chain and published hash against vendor's official advisory before mass deployment.
steps.outcome: All affected systems running verified clean vendor software.

steps.title: Restore and validate business operations
steps.desc: Bring reimaged/remediated systems back into production and validate application functionality and data integrity.
steps.guidance: Run integration/smoke tests before removing containment; monitor closely for 48-72 hours.
steps.outcome: Systems fully operational with no residual indicators of compromise.

steps.title: Implement update-integrity verification controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and drive adoption of update signature/hash verification and staged canary rollout for third-party software updates.
steps.guidance: Recommend canary-ring deployment, SBOM tracking for the vendor product, and update-source pinning.
steps.outcome: Post-incident report published; update verification and staged-rollout controls added to vendor management standard.

ITID-62121.def: An incident in which an adversary inserted unauthorized code into a third-party software product's source, build artifact, or distributed package, such that legitimate customers running the vendor's software unknowingly execute attacker-controlled code.
ITID-62121.purpose: Captures confirmed injection of malicious code into a third-party vendor's software prior to or during its build, packaging, or distribution process.
scopeIncludes: Malicious commits merged into a vendor's source repository and shipped in a release
Tampering with a vendor's build server or build pipeline to inject code post-compile
Backdoored binaries distributed from the vendor's own official channel
scopeExcludes: Cases where the vendor's update channel delivered altered code but the injection point is not yet confirmed (route to ITID-62111)
Cases where the injected code was made trustworthy via a forged/stolen signing certificate specifically — that mechanism is tracked separately (ITID-62131)
Injection into internal, first-party CI/CD pipelines (tracked under CI/CD Pipeline Attacks, ITID-626xx)
ITID-62121.severity: High to Critical, scaled to the vendor's customer base and the privilege level the injected code executes at.
ITID-62121.priority: P1 while the injected code remains live in any distributed version.
ITID-62121.escalation: Escalate to vendor management, legal, and executive stakeholders; coordinate takedown/patch timeline directly with the vendor.
indicators: Unexpected outbound network beaconing from a vendor application shortly after install
Static/dynamic analysis revealing code not present in the vendor's documented source
Independent researcher or vendor disclosure of a tampered build
vectors: Compromised developer credentials used to commit malicious code
Compromised build server injecting code at compile time
Insider threat within the vendor organization
rootCauses: Vendor lacking code review/commit signing requirements
Vendor build infrastructure insufficiently isolated from developer workstations
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Reproducible/verifiable builds where vendor supports them
Runtime application self-protection or integrity monitoring on high-value vendor software
ITID-62121.detection: Weak from the customer side alone; detection typically relies on vendor disclosure, threat intel, or anomalous runtime behavior of the affected software.
ITID-62121.response: Contain affected hosts, apply vendor-issued clean rebuild once available, and hunt for secondary persistence established via the injected code.
metrics: Number of hosts running a confirmed-injected version
Time to clean-rebuild deployment
ITID-62121.notes: Focused on the technical mechanism of code injection into third-party software as consumed by the organization. The parallel ITID-613xx Software Supply Chain Attacks group tracks equivalent events from a critical-system business-impact lens; cross-reference when both angles apply to the same incident.

playbook.name: Third-Party Code Injection
playbook.description: Malicious code is injected into a third-party library, script, or component that the organization consumes, executing within the organization's applications.

steps.title: Detect anomalous script/library behavior
steps.desc: Investigate alerts from CSP violation reports, RASP/WAF, or application monitoring indicating unexpected outbound calls or DOM manipulation from a third-party script/library.
steps.guidance: Review browser console CSP reports and SIEM correlation of unexpected script origins.
steps.outcome: Specific third-party script/component identified as the injection vector.

steps.title: Diff the third-party artifact against known-good baseline
steps.desc: Compare the current third-party JS/library artifact hash against a previously known-good version or SRI hash.
steps.guidance: Use subresource integrity (SRI) records or SBOM checksum history for comparison.
steps.outcome: Confirmed tampering (hash mismatch) or ruled out.
steps.abort: If hashes match, escalate as false positive and continue monitoring.

steps.title: Determine scope of exposure
steps.desc: Identify all applications/pages/services that load the compromised third-party code and the time window it was active.
steps.guidance: Check CDN/tag-manager deployment logs for injection timeframe.
steps.outcome: Full list of affected applications and exposure window documented.

steps.title: Remove or block the compromised third-party resource
steps.desc: Immediately remove the script tag/dependency reference or block the third-party domain at the CDN/WAF/CSP layer.
steps.guidance: Update Content-Security-Policy to block the offending origin as an immediate stopgap.
steps.outcome: Compromised code no longer loads in production applications.

steps.title: Revoke sessions/tokens potentially skimmed
steps.desc: If the injected code could have harvested credentials, tokens, or payment data (e.g., formjacking/Magecart-style), force session invalidation and credential reset for affected users.
steps.guidance: Prioritize payment and authentication flows for review.
steps.abort: If no credential/data-harvesting capability existed in the injected code, skip this step.

steps.title: Replace with verified clean version and pin integrity
steps.desc: Restore the third-party dependency from a verified clean source and implement SRI hashes or dependency pinning.
steps.guidance: Pin exact version numbers; avoid floating/latest tags for externally hosted scripts.
steps.outcome: Clean, integrity-verified version of the component deployed.

steps.title: Audit for backdoors in adjacent code paths
steps.desc: Review application code and build artifacts for any additional injected code introduced through the same vector.
steps.guidance: Diff full build output against last-known-clean build.

steps.title: Re-enable and monitor affected applications
steps.desc: Restore full functionality of affected applications and closely monitor CSP reports and WAF logs for recurrence.
steps.guidance: Extend monitoring window to at least 2 weeks post-incident.
steps.outcome: Applications operating normally with no recurrence of injected content.

steps.title: Formalize third-party script governance
steps.desc: Document findings and establish mandatory SRI/CSP and third-party script inventory review requirements for all externally sourced code.
steps.guidance: Include tag-manager governance and periodic third-party script re-approval in the standard.
steps.outcome: Updated third-party code governance policy published and socialized with development teams.

ITID-62131.def: An incident in which an adversary obtained or subverted a legitimate vendor's code-signing certificate (or induced installation of a rogue root certificate) so that malicious code passes operating-system and endpoint trust checks as genuine vendor software.
ITID-62131.purpose: Captures incidents where a third-party vendor's code-signing certificate or root-of-trust mechanism was stolen, forged, or otherwise abused to make malicious software appear legitimately signed.
scopeIncludes: Malware signed with a stolen vendor code-signing private key
A vendor's certificate authority relationship abused to issue a fraudulent certificate
Installation of a rogue/attacker-controlled root certificate bundled with vendor software
scopeExcludes: Injected malicious code that ships unsigned or under the attacker's own unrelated certificate (route to ITID-62121)
Certificate/PKI compromise unrelated to third-party software distribution (tracked elsewhere in the taxonomy)
ITID-62131.severity: Critical. A validly signed malicious binary defeats most allow-listing and OS trust controls.
ITID-62131.priority: P1 — signing-trust compromises require immediate certificate revocation coordination.
ITID-62131.escalation: Escalate to PKI/certificate authority, vendor, and SOC leadership immediately; request emergency certificate revocation.
indicators: Malware sample discovered signed with a known-legitimate vendor certificate
Certificate revocation list (CRL) or OCSP flag on a certificate previously trusted fleet-wide
Unexpected root certificate present in the trust store post-install
vectors: Theft of a vendor's private signing key from an insecurely stored build environment
Compromise of a certificate authority's issuance process
Social engineering of a vendor's PKI administrator
rootCauses: Vendor storing signing keys on internet-connected build systems rather than HSMs
Lack of certificate transparency monitoring for the organization's trusted vendor certificates
mitreTechniques: T1553.002 Subvert Trust Controls: Code Signing
T1553.004 Subvert Trust Controls: Install Root Certificate
controls: Certificate transparency log monitoring for vendor certificates in use
Application allow-listing that checks certificate revocation status, not presence of a signature alone
ITID-62131.detection: Moderate — CRL/OCSP checks and certificate transparency monitoring can surface abuse, but detection is often reactive to public disclosure.
ITID-62131.response: Distrust the compromised certificate fleet-wide, quarantine signed binaries pending re-verification, and coordinate vendor re-signing with a new key.
metrics: Time to fleet-wide certificate distrust after disclosure
Number of binaries quarantined pending re-signing
ITID-62131.notes: Distinct sibling axis: this leaf is defined by the trust-mechanism abuse (signing/root CA) rather than the code-injection point itself, which is ITID-62121.

playbook.name: Compromised Software Signing Certificate
playbook.description: A code-signing certificate belonging to a trusted vendor or internal build system is compromised and used to sign malicious binaries.

steps.title: Validate the suspect signing certificate
steps.desc: Investigate an alert or report of a binary signed with a trusted certificate exhibiting malicious behavior, and validate the certificate's chain and issuance history.
