steps.desc: Document the incident and implement a formal plugin approval/vetting process plus regular patch-compliance monitoring for all CMS plugins.
steps.outcome: CMS plugin governance and patch cadence policy implemented.

ITID-62422.def: An incident in which an adversary compromised a CMS plugin developer's publishing account and used it to release a tampered plugin update, affecting every site that auto-updated to the malicious version.
ITID-62422.purpose: Captures cases where a CMS plugin's own developer/publisher account was compromised and used to push a malicious update to all sites running that plugin.
scopeIncludes: A plugin marketplace account takeover resulting in a backdoored release pushed to the plugin's install base
Malicious code discovered in a plugin update traced back to the developer's compromised credentials rather than a codebase vulnerability
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a vulnerability in an otherwise-legitimate plugin release (route to ITID-62421)
An abandoned plugin exploited for its own unpatched flaws rather than a malicious push (route to ITID-62423)
ITID-62422.severity: High to Critical given the potential for simultaneous compromise across every site running the plugin.
ITID-62422.priority: P1 immediately upon marketplace or vendor confirmation of a malicious release.
ITID-62422.escalation: Escalate to web operations and CMS marketplace/vendor security team; halt auto-updates for the affected plugin fleet-wide.
indicators: Marketplace/vendor advisory naming a specific malicious plugin version
Sudden appearance of obfuscated code in a routine plugin update across multiple managed sites
Coordinated defacement or backdoor activity across sites sharing the same plugin
vectors: Supply Chain Compromise via a compromised plugin developer/publisher account pushing a malicious software update
rootCauses: Plugin marketplace lacking mandatory MFA for developer publishing accounts
Auto-update enabled fleet-wide with no staged verification window
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Staged/delayed rollout of CMS plugin auto-updates with a monitoring window
Marketplace-mandated MFA for plugin developer accounts
ITID-62422.detection: Moderate — relies on marketplace security response and post-update behavioral monitoring rather than pre-emptive detection.
ITID-62422.response: Roll back to the last known-good plugin version, audit all sites for compromise indicators, and coordinate with the marketplace on remediation timeline.
metrics: Number of sites affected by the malicious update
Time to rollback across the managed fleet
ITID-62422.notes: Sibling differentiator: the compromise originates from the plugin developer's own account being hijacked, not a vulnerability in the plugin code as shipped by a legitimate developer.

playbook.name: Malicious CMS Plugin Update Pushed by Compromised Developer Account
playbook.description: A CMS plugin developer's account is compromised and used to push a malicious update to the plugin, which is auto-updated into the organization's CMS.

steps.title: Confirm the malicious plugin update and developer account compromise
steps.desc: Investigate a vendor/community disclosure or anomalous CMS behavior following a recent plugin auto-update, and confirm reports of the developer account being compromised.
steps.guidance: Check the plugin marketplace's security advisory and community forums for corroborating reports.
steps.outcome: Confirmed the update was malicious and originated from a compromised developer account.

steps.title: Identify all sites that received the malicious update
steps.desc: Determine which CMS instances auto-updated to the malicious plugin version and the exact time window.
steps.outcome: Complete list of affected sites and update timestamps.

steps.title: Assess payload behavior and impact
steps.desc: Analyze the malicious code introduced in the update to determine its behavior (backdoor, SEO spam injection, credential theft, etc.).

steps.title: Disable auto-updates and deactivate the plugin
steps.desc: Immediately deactivate the plugin on all affected sites and disable auto-update functionality to prevent further malicious pushes.
steps.outcome: Malicious plugin deactivated; auto-update risk halted.

steps.title: Isolate sites showing signs of active compromise
steps.desc: Take severely affected sites offline or behind WAF protection pending cleanup.

steps.title: Roll back to last known-good plugin version
steps.desc: Restore the plugin to the last verified clean version once available, or remove it entirely if the vendor has not resolved the compromise.
steps.guidance: Verify the rollback version's integrity/hash against a trusted source.
steps.outcome: Malicious plugin version removed and replaced with clean version or removed entirely.

steps.title: Remove any residual backdoors introduced by the malicious update
steps.desc: Scan and clean affected sites for any persistence mechanisms installed by the malicious update.
steps.outcome: Sites confirmed clean of attacker artifacts.

steps.title: Restore normal operations with monitored auto-update policy
steps.desc: Re-enable plugin functionality with a staged/monitored update policy rather than immediate auto-update.
steps.guidance: Consider delaying auto-updates by a review window (e.g., 48-72 hours) to allow community vetting.
steps.outcome: Sites restored to normal operation with hardened update policy.

steps.title: Implement staged plugin update rollout
steps.desc: Document the incident and formalize a staged/delayed auto-update policy plus monitoring of plugin marketplace security advisories.
steps.outcome: Staged update rollout policy implemented for all CMS plugins.

ITID-62423.def: An incident in which an adversary exploited a vulnerability in a CMS plugin that is no longer actively maintained or supported, such that no vendor patch is forthcoming regardless of vulnerability severity.
ITID-62423.purpose: Captures exploitation of a CMS plugin that has been abandoned by its developer and will not receive a fix for its known vulnerabilities.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a plugin last updated years prior with no maintainer response to disclosed vulnerabilities
A plugin removed from the marketplace for abandonment but still active on production sites
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of an actively maintained plugin's own vulnerability (route to ITID-62421)
A malicious update pushed via a compromised active developer account (route to ITID-62422)
ITID-62423.severity: High. No remediation path exists short of plugin removal/replacement.
ITID-62423.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the affected site is internet-facing and handles sensitive data.
ITID-62423.escalation: Escalate to web operations with a mandatory removal/replacement requirement, not just incident closure.
indicators: Plugin flagged as 'abandoned'/'closed' in the CMS marketplace with unpatched disclosed vulnerabilities
Vulnerability scanner reporting a finding with no available fix for the installed plugin version
vectors: Exploit Public-Facing Application against a known-unpatched, unmaintained CMS plugin
rootCauses: Lack of periodic plugin inventory review for abandonment/maintenance status
Business dependency on legacy plugin functionality with no supported replacement identified
controls: Periodic CMS plugin inventory review flagging abandoned/unmaintained plugins
Mandatory removal or WAF virtual-patching for plugins with no vendor fix path
ITID-62423.detection: Strong for the specific known vulnerability once identified; the underlying risk (abandonment) itself is only caught through inventory review, not runtime detection.
ITID-62423.response: Remove or replace the abandoned plugin, apply WAF virtual patching as an interim measure, and audit for compromise indicators.
metrics: Number of abandoned plugins identified in inventory
Time to removal/replacement after flagging
ITID-62423.notes: Sibling differentiator: vendor abandonment (no future fix path) rather than a currently-fixable vulnerability (ITID-62421) or a malicious push from an active developer account (ITID-62422).

playbook.name: Abandoned/Unmaintained CMS Plugin with Unpatched Vulnerability
playbook.description: A plugin in use has been abandoned by its developer and contains a known, unpatched vulnerability that is exploited or discovered during an audit.

steps.title: Confirm plugin abandonment and vulnerability status
steps.desc: Verify the plugin has no active maintainer/updates and confirm the specific known vulnerability via CVE or vulnerability scan findings.
steps.guidance: Check plugin marketplace last-update date and any 'closed/abandoned' status flags.
steps.outcome: Confirmed abandoned status and unpatched vulnerability details.
steps.abort: If the plugin is still maintained and simply outdated, redirect to standard compromised-CMS-plugin patch workflow.

steps.title: Determine if exploitation has already occurred
steps.desc: Review web server/CMS logs for indicators of exploitation attempts or success against the vulnerable plugin.
steps.outcome: Determined whether this is a proactive audit finding or an active/past compromise.
steps.abort: If active exploitation is confirmed, escalate immediately to full IR (treat as ITID-62421-style compromise).

steps.title: Inventory all sites using the abandoned plugin
steps.desc: Identify every CMS instance using the abandoned, vulnerable plugin.

steps.title: Deactivate the abandoned plugin
steps.desc: Immediately disable the plugin on all affected sites given no vendor fix will be forthcoming.
steps.guidance: Assess functional impact and identify a replacement plugin/feature before permanent removal if needed.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable, unmaintained plugin no longer active.
steps.abort: If deactivation breaks critical site functionality, apply WAF virtual patching as an interim compensating control.

steps.title: Apply WAF virtual patch if plugin must remain active temporarily
steps.desc: Deploy a WAF rule targeting the specific known vulnerability signature if the plugin cannot be immediately deactivated.
steps.outcome: Exploit attempts blocked at the perimeter during transition.

steps.title: Permanently remove and replace the abandoned plugin
steps.desc: Fully uninstall the abandoned plugin and migrate its functionality to a maintained, actively-supported alternative.
steps.outcome: Abandoned plugin permanently removed from all sites.

steps.title: Validate site functionality post-migration
steps.desc: Confirm site functionality is preserved after removing/replacing the abandoned plugin.
steps.outcome: Sites fully functional without the vulnerable plugin.

steps.title: Add plugin maintenance-status monitoring to vetting process
steps.desc: Document the incident and add ongoing plugin maintenance-status/end-of-life monitoring to the plugin vetting and approval process.

ITID-62424.def: An incident involving compromise via a CMS plugin whose specific mechanism (unpatched vulnerability, malicious developer-account update, or vendor abandonment) has not yet been determined.
ITID-62424.purpose: Intake leaf for a CMS plugin compromise that does not yet clearly fit the direct-vulnerability, malicious-update, or abandonment leaves in this group.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered CMS plugin compromise pending root-cause triage
Ambiguous cases where multiple mechanisms may be in play
scopeExcludes: Cases where the mechanism has been confirmed as a specific vulnerability (route to ITID-62421), malicious update (ITID-62422), or abandonment (ITID-62423)
ITID-62424.severity: High pending triage, consistent with the compromised CMS plugin group generally.
ITID-62424.priority: P1 pending triage; downgrade only once mechanism and scope are confirmed.
ITID-62424.escalation: Escalate to web operations for immediate containment while root-cause triage proceeds.
indicators: Webshell, defacement, or unauthorized admin activity traced to an installed CMS plugin, mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Exploit Public-Facing Application via an as-yet-uncharacterized CMS plugin compromise mechanism
rootCauses: Incomplete plugin inventory or patch-status visibility delaying root-cause determination
controls: CMS plugin inventory and patch-status visibility tooling
ITID-62424.detection: Varies by underlying mechanism; treat detection as inherited from whichever specific leaf the case is eventually triaged to.
ITID-62424.response: Contain the affected site immediately and triage to a specific sibling leaf (ITID-62421/62422/62423) as soon as root cause is confirmed.
metrics: Time from detection to root-cause triage into a specific leaf
ITID-62424.notes: Unclassified/general intake leaf for the Compromised CMS Plugins group; cases should be re-triaged to a specific sibling leaf once mechanism is confirmed.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Compromised CMS Plugin
playbook.description: A general or unclassified compromise involving a third-party CMS plugin that does not fit a more specific scenario.

steps.title: Investigate reported CMS anomaly and identify the implicated plugin
steps.desc: Triage the alert or report of anomalous CMS behavior and identify which third-party plugin is implicated.
steps.guidance: Review recent plugin activity logs, admin change logs, and web server logs.
steps.outcome: Implicated plugin and nature of the compromise identified.
steps.abort: If a specific known scenario applies (vulnerability exploit, malicious update, abandoned plugin), redirect to that specific playbook.

steps.title: Inventory affected sites and scope of compromise
steps.desc: Determine which CMS instances are affected and the extent of any unauthorized access or content change.

steps.title: Disable the implicated plugin
steps.desc: Deactivate the plugin across all affected CMS instances.
steps.outcome: Plugin no longer active; further compromise via this vector halted.

steps.title: Isolate or restrict affected sites if actively compromised
steps.desc: Apply WAF protection or take the site offline temporarily if there is evidence of active malicious activity.

steps.title: Remove malicious artifacts and restore clean plugin state
steps.desc: Clean any backdoors/malicious content introduced and restore or replace the plugin with a verified clean/patched version.
steps.outcome: CMS instance restored to a clean, secure state.

steps.title: Restore site operations and validate
steps.desc: Bring the site back into normal operation and confirm no residual compromise indicators remain.
steps.outcome: Site fully operational and confirmed clean.

steps.title: Reinforce plugin vetting and monitoring process
steps.desc: Document findings and improve the plugin approval/vetting and ongoing anomaly-monitoring process.

steps.title: Review plugin inventory for similar risk
steps.desc: Audit remaining CMS plugins across the organization for similar risk characteristics identified in this incident.

ITID-62431.def: An incident in which an adversary exploited a malicious or vulnerable add-on/extension within an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system to gain unauthorized access to financial, supply chain, or operational data.
ITID-62431.purpose: Captures exploitation of a third-party ERP system add-on to gain unauthorized access to enterprise resource planning data.
scopeIncludes: A third-party ERP add-on with excessive data-access permissions exploited to read financial or inventory records
A vulnerable ERP marketplace extension exploited for privilege escalation within the ERP platform
scopeExcludes: Equivalent exploitation within a CRM marketplace app specifically (route to ITID-62432)
ERP data access achieved without any add-on/extension involvement (tracked elsewhere in the taxonomy under core application exploitation)
ITID-62431.severity: High given ERP systems typically hold financial and operational data central to business function.
ITID-62431.priority: P1 if financial data exposure or transaction manipulation is confirmed; P2 otherwise.
ITID-62431.escalation: Escalate to finance/ERP system owners and privacy/legal if financial or personal data exposure is confirmed.
indicators: Anomalous data export volume from the ERP system correlated with add-on activity
ERP audit log showing access outside the add-on's documented functional scope
vectors: Data from Information Repositories accessed via an over-permissioned or vulnerable ERP add-on
rootCauses: ERP add-on granted broader data-access scope than its function requires
Lack of periodic ERP marketplace add-on permission review
controls: Periodic review of ERP add-on data-access scopes
Least-privilege configuration for all ERP marketplace extensions
ITID-62431.detection: Moderate — ERP audit logging can reveal anomalous access if actively monitored, but many organizations under-instrument ERP add-on activity specifically.
ITID-62431.response: Revoke or restrict the add-on's data access, audit the scope of data accessed, and notify affected business units.
metrics: Number of ERP add-ons with excessive permission scope
Volume of data accessed during the incident
ITID-62431.notes: Sibling differentiator versus ITID-62432: this leaf is scoped to ERP-platform add-ons specifically, given the distinct financial/operational data profile relative to CRM customer data.

playbook.name: Malicious ERP System Add-On Exploited for Data Access
playbook.description: A malicious or compromised third-party add-on installed into the organization's ERP system is used to gain unauthorized access to sensitive business data.

steps.title: Identify the malicious ERP add-on and confirm unauthorized access
steps.desc: Investigate alerts of anomalous ERP data access or export activity and identify the specific third-party add-on responsible.
steps.guidance: Review ERP audit logs, add-on/extension marketplace inventory, and data-export logs.
steps.outcome: Malicious add-on identified and unauthorized data access confirmed.

steps.title: Determine scope of data accessed/exfiltrated
steps.desc: Identify which ERP modules, records, and data classifications were accessed via the malicious add-on.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference add-on permission scope with actual data-access logs.
steps.outcome: Documented scope and sensitivity of accessed/exfiltrated data.

steps.title: Identify affected business units and downstream impact
steps.desc: Determine which business processes/units rely on the affected ERP data and any downstream impact (e.g., financial, HR, supply chain data).

steps.title: Disable the malicious add-on and revoke its access
steps.desc: Immediately deactivate the add-on within the ERP system and revoke its API/service account access.
steps.outcome: Add-on no longer has access to ERP data.

steps.title: Rotate credentials associated with the add-on integration
steps.desc: Rotate any service accounts, API keys, or OAuth tokens the add-on used to access the ERP system.

steps.title: Remove the add-on and any residual backdoor configuration
steps.desc: Fully uninstall the malicious add-on and review ERP configuration for any unauthorized changes it made (e.g., new integration users, altered workflows).
steps.outcome: ERP system free of the malicious add-on and any resulting unauthorized configuration.

steps.title: Notify affected business units and, if required, regulators/customers
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance to determine and execute notification obligations based on the data exposed.
steps.outcome: Required notifications completed per data-classification and regulatory obligations.
steps.abort: If exposed data does not trigger notification thresholds, document the determination.

steps.title: Restore ERP operations with validated add-on inventory
steps.desc: Confirm ERP system operates normally with only vetted, approved add-ons active.
steps.outcome: ERP system restored to secure, fully-vetted operational state.

steps.title: Implement ERP add-on vetting and least-privilege access review
steps.desc: Document the incident and establish formal ERP add-on security review, including least-privilege scoping of add-on data access.

ITID-62432.def: An incident in which an adversary exploited a malicious or vulnerable third-party marketplace application connected to a customer relationship management (CRM) platform to exfiltrate customer personal or account data.
ITID-62432.purpose: Captures exploitation of a third-party CRM marketplace application to exfiltrate customer records.
scopeIncludes: A CRM marketplace app with excessive read scope exploited or abused to bulk-export customer records
A malicious CRM marketplace app installed via social engineering that exfiltrates contact/opportunity data to an attacker-controlled endpoint
scopeExcludes: Equivalent exploitation within an ERP add-on specifically (route to ITID-62431)
CRM data access achieved without any marketplace app involvement (tracked elsewhere in the taxonomy)
ITID-62432.severity: High given direct exposure of customer personal data with regulatory notification implications.
ITID-62432.priority: P1 if bulk customer data exfiltration is confirmed; P2 for limited-scope exposure.
ITID-62432.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal immediately given likely customer notification and regulatory reporting obligations.
indicators: Bulk CRM data export event correlated with a specific installed marketplace app
Customer complaints of unsolicited contact following a suspected CRM data leak
CRM audit log showing API calls from the app exceeding its documented functional need
vectors: Data from Information Repositories exfiltrated via an over-permissioned or malicious CRM marketplace application
rootCauses: CRM marketplace app installed without a security review of its requested data scopes
Lack of monitoring for bulk data-export events from the CRM platform
controls: Mandatory security review of CRM marketplace app data-access scopes before installation
Bulk data-export monitoring and alerting on the CRM platform
ITID-62432.detection: Moderate — CRM platforms increasingly offer audit logs for app activity and bulk export, though many organizations do not actively monitor them.
ITID-62432.response: Revoke the app's access immediately, determine the scope of customer records exposed, and initiate regulatory/customer notification processes as required.
metrics: Number of customer records exposed
Time to app access revocation
sops: CRM Marketplace App Security Review SOP
ITID-62432.notes: Sibling differentiator versus ITID-62431: this leaf is scoped to CRM marketplace apps and customer-record exposure specifically, distinct from ERP financial/operational data.

playbook.name: Compromised CRM Marketplace App Exfiltrating Customer Records
playbook.description: A third-party app installed from the CRM's app marketplace is found to be exfiltrating customer records to an external destination.

steps.title: Detect anomalous data export activity from the CRM
steps.desc: Investigate DLP/CASB alerts or CRM audit-log anomalies showing bulk record access or export tied to a specific installed marketplace app.
steps.guidance: Review CRM API activity logs filtered by connected-app client ID.
steps.outcome: Specific marketplace app confirmed as the exfiltration source.

steps.title: Determine volume and sensitivity of exfiltrated records
steps.desc: Quantify the number and classification of customer records accessed/exported by the app over the exposure window.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of exfiltrated data for breach-notification assessment.

steps.title: Review app permissions and installation history
steps.desc: Determine how the app was installed, who approved it, and what OAuth scopes/permissions it was granted.
steps.outcome: App provenance and permission scope documented.

steps.title: Revoke the app's access immediately
steps.desc: Uninstall the marketplace app and revoke its OAuth tokens/API credentials from the CRM admin console.
steps.outcome: App can no longer access CRM data.

steps.title: Block outbound destination if identifiable
steps.desc: Block network/DNS access to the external destination the app was exfiltrating to, where technically feasible.
steps.outcome: Further exfiltration to the known destination blocked.
steps.abort: If the app operates purely via CRM-vendor-hosted infrastructure with no discrete external destination, mark not applicable.

steps.title: Audit remaining marketplace apps for similar risk
steps.desc: Review all other installed CRM marketplace apps for excessive permission scopes or similar suspicious behavior.
steps.outcome: Full marketplace app inventory reviewed and any additional risky apps remediated.

steps.title: Notify affected customers and regulators as required
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance to determine and execute customer and regulatory notification obligations based on exfiltrated data classification.
steps.outcome: Required notifications completed within regulatory timelines.
steps.abort: If notification thresholds are not met, document the determination.

steps.title: Restore CRM operations with hardened app governance
steps.desc: Confirm CRM operates normally with only vetted apps installed and monitor for recurrence.
steps.outcome: CRM environment restored to a secure, monitored state.

steps.title: Implement CRM marketplace app approval and OAuth scope review process
steps.desc: Document the incident and establish mandatory security review and least-privilege OAuth scoping for all future CRM marketplace app installs.

ITID-62433.def: An incident involving exploitation of a third-party plugin/add-on within an ERP or CRM platform where the specific platform type or exploitation mechanism has not yet been determined.
ITID-62433.purpose: Intake leaf for an ERP/CRM plugin exploitation incident that does not yet clearly fit the ERP-specific or CRM-specific leaves in this group.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered ERP/CRM add-on compromise pending triage
Cases spanning both ERP and CRM systems via a shared integration add-on
scopeExcludes: Cases confirmed as ERP-specific (route to ITID-62431) or CRM-specific (route to ITID-62432)
ITID-62433.severity: High pending triage, consistent with the ERP/CRM plugin exploit group generally.
ITID-62433.priority: P1 pending triage; downgrade once scope and platform are confirmed.
ITID-62433.escalation: Escalate to the relevant business system owner for immediate containment while triage proceeds.
indicators: Anomalous data access via a business-system add-on, platform/mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Data from Information Repositories via an as-yet-uncharacterized ERP/CRM add-on compromise
rootCauses: Incomplete visibility into which business-critical system an add-on integrates with, delaying triage
controls: Unified inventory of business-system add-ons across ERP and CRM platforms
ITID-62433.detection: Varies by underlying platform; treat detection as inherited from whichever specific leaf the case is eventually triaged to.
ITID-62433.response: Contain access immediately and triage to ITID-62431 or ITID-62432 as soon as platform and mechanism are confirmed.
metrics: Time from detection to root-cause triage into a specific leaf
sops: CRM Marketplace App Security Review SOP
ITID-62433.notes: Unclassified/general intake leaf for the ERP and CRM Plugin Exploits group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General ERP/CRM Plugin Exploit
playbook.description: A general or unclassified exploit involving a third-party ERP or CRM plugin/add-on that does not fit a more specific scenario.

steps.title: Triage the reported anomaly and identify the implicated plugin
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/report and identify which ERP/CRM plugin or add-on is implicated in the anomalous activity.
steps.guidance: Review ERP/CRM audit logs and connected-app/add-on inventory.
steps.outcome: Implicated plugin and nature of the issue identified.
steps.abort: If a specific known scenario applies, redirect to that specific playbook.

steps.title: Determine scope of access or data impact
steps.desc: Assess what data or system functions the plugin accessed or affected.

steps.title: Disable the implicated plugin/add-on
steps.desc: Deactivate or uninstall the plugin from the ERP/CRM system and revoke its access credentials.

steps.title: Rotate any exposed credentials
steps.desc: Rotate service accounts/API keys/tokens associated with the plugin's integration.

steps.title: Remove residual unauthorized configuration changes
steps.desc: Review and revert any unauthorized configuration or data changes made via the plugin.
steps.outcome: ERP/CRM system restored to known-good configuration.

steps.title: Apply patched version or replace plugin
steps.desc: Apply a vendor patch if available, or replace the plugin with a secure, vetted alternative.

steps.title: Restore system operations and validate
steps.desc: Confirm the ERP/CRM system functions normally and is free of residual compromise indicators.
steps.outcome: System restored to normal, secure operation.

steps.title: Strengthen ERP/CRM plugin governance
steps.desc: Document findings and reinforce plugin vetting, least-privilege access, and periodic review processes for ERP/CRM add-ons.
steps.outcome: Updated ERP/CRM plugin governance standard published.

ITID-62441.def: An incident in which an adversary embedded persistent unauthorized access (a backdoor) into a third-party desktop, mobile, or enterprise application through an installed add-on or extension mechanism.
ITID-62441.purpose: Captures introduction of a backdoor into an organization's environment via a third-party application add-on or extension, distinct from the browser-extension and CMS-plugin cases already covered elsewhere.
scopeIncludes: A third-party desktop application add-on providing an attacker with a persistent command-and-control channel
An enterprise application extension (non-CMS, non-browser) modified or replaced to include backdoor functionality
scopeExcludes: Browser extension-based compromise (route to ITID-62411)
CMS plugin compromise (route to ITID-6242x)
Macro/script add-ins for productivity applications specifically (route to ITID-62442)
ITID-62441.severity: High — a backdoor represents standing, persistent unauthorized access rather than a one-time exploitation event.
ITID-62441.priority: P1 upon confirmation of any active backdoor channel.
ITID-62441.escalation: Escalate to incident response for full host forensics and to application owners for add-on removal fleet-wide.
indicators: Unexplained outbound command-and-control beaconing tied to a specific application add-on process
EDR detection of process injection or unusual child processes spawned from a third-party add-on
vectors: Compromise of Software Dependencies and Development Tools via a backdoored application add-on distributed through an unofficial or compromised channel
rootCauses: Add-ons sourced from unofficial or unverified distribution channels
Lack of application allow-listing covering third-party add-ons specifically
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Application add-on allow-listing restricted to vendor-verified sources
EDR monitoring for anomalous child-process activity from third-party add-ons
ITID-62441.detection: Moderate — EDR behavioral detection can surface backdoor activity, but the add-on itself often evades static signature detection.
ITID-62441.response: Remove the backdoored add-on fleet-wide, perform full host forensics on affected systems, and rotate any credentials accessible from those hosts.
metrics: Number of hosts with the backdoored add-on installed
Time to fleet-wide removal
ITID-62441.notes: Sibling differentiator versus ITID-62442: this leaf covers general application add-ons/extensions, while macro/script add-ins for productivity suites have their own leaf given their distinct delivery and execution mechanism.

playbook.name: Backdoor Introduced via Third-Party Application Add-On/Extension
playbook.description: A third-party application add-on or extension is found to contain a deliberate backdoor providing unauthorized persistent access.

steps.title: Confirm the backdoor's existence and mechanism
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/discovery (e.g., unexplained outbound connections, unauthorized authentication events) and analyze the add-on's code/behavior to confirm a deliberate backdoor.
steps.guidance: Perform static/dynamic analysis of the add-on binary or script where feasible.
steps.outcome: Confirmed backdoor mechanism and its access capability documented.
steps.abort: If analysis shows the behavior is an unintentional bug rather than a backdoor, redirect to standard vulnerability handling.

steps.title: Determine installation footprint and duration of exposure
steps.desc: Identify all hosts/applications with the backdoored add-on installed and the time since installation.
steps.outcome: Full exposure footprint and timeline documented.

steps.title: Determine whether the backdoor was exercised
steps.desc: Review logs for evidence that the backdoor access was actually used by an unauthorized party.
steps.outcome: Determined whether active exploitation occurred beyond mere presence of the backdoor.

steps.title: Remove/disable the backdoored add-on fleet-wide
steps.desc: Immediately uninstall or disable the add-on across all affected systems.

steps.title: Isolate systems with confirmed backdoor usage
steps.desc: Network-isolate any system where the backdoor was confirmed exercised, pending forensic investigation.

steps.title: Reimage confirmed-compromised systems
steps.desc: Rebuild from trusted media any system where the backdoor was actively exercised, since full extent of attacker action cannot be assured otherwise.

steps.title: Blocklist the add-on and notify the vendor/marketplace
steps.desc: Add the add-on to a permanent blocklist and report it to the relevant application marketplace/vendor for takedown.
steps.outcome: Add-on blocked from reinstallation and reported for removal from distribution.

steps.title: Restore operations and validate clean state
steps.desc: Return affected systems to production and confirm no residual backdoor access remains.
steps.outcome: Systems restored and confirmed free of backdoor access.

steps.title: Strengthen add-on/extension code review process
steps.desc: Document the incident and implement mandatory security code review or reputable-source vetting for third-party add-ons before organizational adoption.
steps.outcome: Add-on vetting and approval process strengthened.

ITID-62442.def: An incident in which an adversary distributed a malicious macro, script, or add-in through a productivity application's official or unofficial extension mechanism (e.g., Office/Excel add-ins), leading to code execution on the recipient's system.
ITID-62442.purpose: Captures malicious macro or script-based add-ins delivered through productivity application platforms such as Excel or Office add-in marketplaces.
scopeIncludes: A malicious Office/Excel add-in distributed via an app marketplace or shared file that executes attacker code on open
A macro-enabled add-in used to establish persistence or download a second-stage payload
scopeExcludes: General application add-on backdoors outside the productivity-suite macro/script context (route to ITID-62441)
Phishing emails delivering a malicious document without an add-in/marketplace distribution mechanism (tracked elsewhere in the phishing taxonomy)
ITID-62442.severity: High given the ubiquity of productivity software and the ease of lateral distribution via shared documents.
ITID-62442.priority: P1 if active code execution or lateral spread is confirmed; P2 for a contained, single-user event.
ITID-62442.escalation: Escalate to endpoint security for organization-wide macro/add-in policy enforcement and user notification.
indicators: EDR alert on a spawned process originating from a productivity application's add-in host process
Unusual macro execution activity flagged by application telemetry
User report of an unexpected add-in prompt or install
vectors: Compromise of Software Dependencies and Development Tools via a malicious productivity-suite macro/add-in
rootCauses: Macros enabled by default or insufficiently restricted via group policy
Add-in marketplace lacking rigorous vetting for publisher legitimacy
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Group policy restricting macro execution to signed/trusted sources only
Add-in marketplace allow-listing at the organizational level
ITID-62442.detection: Moderate — EDR and application telemetry can catch execution-stage indicators, though initial delivery often evades email/content filtering.
ITID-62442.response: Disable the malicious add-in organization-wide, isolate affected hosts, and review macro/add-in security policy.
metrics: Number of users who installed/executed the malicious add-in
Time to organization-wide policy enforcement
ITID-62442.notes: Sibling differentiator: this leaf is scoped specifically to the macro/script add-in mechanism within productivity applications, distinct from the general application add-on backdoor leaf (ITID-62441).

playbook.name: Malicious Macro/Script Add-In for Productivity Application (Excel/Office Add-In)
playbook.description: A malicious macro or script-based add-in for a productivity suite (e.g., Excel, Office) is distributed and executed, providing attacker code execution on end-user devices.

steps.title: Identify the malicious add-in and affected endpoints
steps.desc: Investigate EDR/AV alerts for malicious macro execution and identify the specific add-in/template responsible, plus all endpoints that opened it.
steps.guidance: Review process trees showing Office application spawning suspicious child processes.
steps.outcome: Malicious add-in identified and affected endpoint list compiled.

steps.title: Determine distribution vector
steps.desc: Determine how the malicious add-in was distributed (email attachment, shared drive, internal template repository, external download).
steps.outcome: Distribution vector documented to inform containment scope.

steps.title: Assess payload behavior and impact
steps.desc: Analyze the macro/script payload for its capability (credential theft, further malware download, data exfiltration).

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints
steps.desc: Apply EDR network isolation to all endpoints that executed the malicious add-in.

steps.title: Purge the malicious file from shared locations and quarantine copies
steps.desc: Remove the malicious add-in/template from email systems, shared drives, and any internal distribution points.
steps.outcome: Malicious file no longer accessible for further distribution.

steps.title: Remove malware and reimage affected endpoints as needed
steps.desc: Clean or reimage endpoints based on the severity of the payload's execution.

steps.title: Reinforce macro execution policy
steps.desc: Apply or tighten Group Policy/application controls to block macros from untrusted sources or the internet by default.
steps.outcome: Macro execution restricted to trusted, signed sources only.

steps.title: Restore endpoints and validate
steps.desc: Return cleaned/reimaged endpoints to service and confirm no residual malware.

steps.title: User awareness training on malicious add-ins/macros
steps.desc: Document the incident and deliver targeted user-awareness training on the risks of enabling macros/add-ins from untrusted sources.
steps.outcome: Awareness training delivered and macro-security policy reinforced.

ITID-62443.def: An incident involving a backdoor introduced via a third-party application add-on or extension whose specific delivery mechanism (general add-on versus productivity-suite macro/script) has not yet been determined.
ITID-62443.purpose: Intake leaf for an application add-on backdoor incident not yet attributed to the general add-on or macro/script-specific leaves in this group.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered application add-on backdoor pending mechanism triage
scopeExcludes: Cases confirmed as a general application add-on backdoor (route to ITID-62441) or a productivity-suite macro/script add-in (route to ITID-62442)
ITID-62443.severity: High pending triage, consistent with the Application Add-On Backdoors group generally.
ITID-62443.priority: P1 pending triage; downgrade once mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-62443.escalation: Escalate to incident response for immediate containment while mechanism triage proceeds.
indicators: Backdoor activity traced to a third-party add-on, specific delivery mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Compromise of Software Dependencies and Development Tools via an as-yet-uncharacterized add-on backdoor mechanism
rootCauses: Incomplete add-on inventory delaying mechanism determination
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Comprehensive third-party add-on inventory across desktop, mobile, and productivity platforms
ITID-62443.detection: Varies by underlying mechanism; treat detection as inherited from whichever specific leaf the case is eventually triaged to.
ITID-62443.response: Contain the affected host(s) and triage to ITID-62441 or ITID-62442 as soon as mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Time from detection to mechanism triage
ITID-62443.notes: Unclassified/general intake leaf for the Application Add-On Backdoors group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Application Add-On Backdoor
playbook.description: A general or unclassified backdoor discovered in a third-party application add-on or extension that does not fit a more specific scenario.

steps.title: Investigate and confirm the backdoor finding
steps.desc: Triage the report/alert and confirm the presence and nature of the backdoor in the third-party add-on.
steps.abort: If unconfirmed, close as false positive with documentation.

steps.title: Determine exposure footprint
steps.desc: Identify all systems/applications with the add-on installed.

steps.title: Remove or disable the add-on
steps.desc: Uninstall/disable the add-on across all affected systems.

steps.title: Isolate systems with confirmed backdoor exercise
steps.desc: Isolate any system where evidence shows the backdoor was actively used.

steps.title: Remediate affected systems
steps.desc: Clean or reimage affected systems depending on severity of backdoor use.
steps.outcome: Systems confirmed free of backdoor artifacts.

steps.title: Blocklist the add-on
steps.desc: Add the add-on to a permanent enterprise blocklist to prevent reinstallation.

steps.title: Restore and validate systems
steps.desc: Confirm affected systems are restored to normal operation and free of backdoor indicators.

steps.title: Strengthen add-on vetting process
steps.desc: Document findings and reinforce the organization's third-party add-on vetting and approval process.

ITID-62511.def: An incident in which insecure configuration settings applied by the organization within a third-party SaaS application — such as overly permissive sharing defaults, disabled security controls, or exposed public endpoints — resulted in unauthorized access or data exposure.
ITID-62511.purpose: Captures unauthorized access or data exposure resulting from an organization's own misconfiguration of a third-party SaaS application, rather than a vendor-side vulnerability.
scopeIncludes: A SaaS collaboration platform left with public-by-default sharing settings resulting in inadvertent data exposure
Security controls (MFA enforcement, IP allow-listing, audit logging) available in the SaaS platform but never enabled
scopeExcludes: OAuth/SSO token or session abuse specifically (route to ITID-62521)
Account takeover of a specific user's SaaS credentials (route to ITID-62531)
Vendor-side API vulnerability rather than organizational misconfiguration (route to ITID-62541)
ITID-62511.severity: Medium-High depending on the sensitivity of data exposed by the misconfiguration.
ITID-62511.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if sensitive or regulated data was publicly exposed.
ITID-62511.escalation: Escalate to the SaaS platform's business owner and privacy/legal if data exposure occurred.
indicators: Cloud access security broker (CASB) or SSPM alert flagging a public-sharing or disabled-control misconfiguration
External discovery (researcher, customer) of publicly accessible SaaS content
vectors: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts leveraging misconfigured public access rather than credential compromise
rootCauses: SaaS platform deployed without a security configuration baseline review
Lack of ongoing SaaS security posture management (SSPM) monitoring
controls: SaaS security posture management (SSPM) tooling with baseline configuration monitoring
Mandatory security configuration review at SaaS onboarding
ITID-62511.detection: Strong where SSPM/CASB tooling is deployed; weak otherwise, as misconfigurations produce no inherently malicious signal.
ITID-62511.response: Correct the misconfiguration immediately, assess scope of exposure, and notify affected parties as required.
metrics: Number of SaaS misconfigurations identified per SSPM scan cycle
Time to remediation after detection
ITID-62511.notes: Sibling differentiator: organizational misconfiguration of an otherwise-secure SaaS platform, as distinct from identity/session abuse (ITID-62521/62531) or vendor-side flaws (ITID-62541).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General SaaS Misconfiguration
playbook.description: A general or unclassified security misconfiguration in a third-party SaaS application exposes data or access beyond intended boundaries.

steps.title: Identify the misconfiguration via SSPM/config review
steps.desc: Investigate an SSPM (SaaS Security Posture Management) alert or manual configuration review finding indicating an unsafe SaaS setting (e.g., public sharing, overly permissive default roles).
steps.guidance: Cross-reference SSPM findings with the SaaS vendor's security configuration baseline.
steps.abort: If the setting is intentional and risk-accepted, close with documentation.

steps.title: Determine what was exposed and for how long
steps.desc: Review audit logs to determine what data/functionality was exposed and whether any unauthorized access occurred during the exposure window.
steps.outcome: Exposure scope and any confirmed unauthorized access documented.

steps.title: Correct the misconfiguration immediately
steps.desc: Apply the corrected, secure configuration setting within the SaaS admin console.

steps.title: Revoke any unauthorized access resulting from the exposure
steps.desc: Revoke sessions, shared links, or access grants that were created as a result of the misconfiguration.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized access resulting from the misconfiguration terminated.
steps.abort: If no unauthorized access occurred, mark not applicable.

steps.title: Audit for similar misconfigurations across the SaaS estate
steps.desc: Run a broader configuration audit across all SaaS applications for the same or related misconfiguration pattern.
steps.outcome: Similar misconfigurations identified and remediated organization-wide.

steps.title: Validate secure configuration and monitor
steps.desc: Confirm the corrected configuration holds and monitor for configuration drift.
steps.outcome: SaaS application confirmed securely configured with drift monitoring in place.

steps.title: Establish SaaS configuration baseline and continuous monitoring
steps.desc: Document the incident and formalize a secure-configuration baseline with continuous SSPM monitoring for all SaaS applications.
steps.outcome: SaaS configuration governance standard and SSPM monitoring implemented.

steps.title: Assign configuration ownership across SaaS estate
steps.desc: Assign a named owner responsible for security configuration review of each SaaS application in the tenant inventory.
steps.guidance: Incorporate into the SaaS vendor/application ownership register.
steps.outcome: Clear configuration ownership documented for all in-scope SaaS applications.

ITID-62521.def: An incident in which an adversary abused OAuth authorization grants, refresh tokens, or single sign-on trust relationships to gain or maintain unauthorized access to a third-party SaaS application without directly compromising the user's primary password.
ITID-62521.purpose: Captures abuse of OAuth tokens or single sign-on (SSO) trust relationships to gain unauthorized access to a third-party SaaS application.
scopeIncludes: A malicious OAuth application granted excessive scope by a phished user, later used to access SaaS data
Theft or replay of an OAuth refresh token to maintain persistent SaaS access after password reset
Abuse of a federated SSO trust relationship to pivot into a connected SaaS application
scopeExcludes: Organizational misconfiguration of the SaaS platform itself (route to ITID-62511)
Direct account takeover via credential theft/phishing without OAuth/SSO involvement (route to ITID-62531)
ITID-62521.severity: High — OAuth/SSO abuse frequently survives password resets and standard credential remediation.
ITID-62521.priority: P1 upon confirmation of an actively used malicious OAuth grant or token replay.
ITID-62521.escalation: Escalate to identity/IAM team immediately for token revocation and OAuth application review.
indicators: Unusual OAuth application consent grant in the identity provider's audit log
SaaS API access continuing after the associated user's password has been reset
Login activity from an unexpected federated identity provider not previously associated with the account
vectors: Use Alternate Authentication Material via OAuth token theft or SSO trust abuse
Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts leveraged through a persistent OAuth grant
rootCauses: Lack of periodic review and revocation of stale/excessive OAuth application grants
Absence of conditional access policies tied to token/session risk signals
controls: Periodic OAuth application consent grant review and revocation
Conditional access policies enforcing re-authentication on risk signals
ITID-62521.detection: Moderate — identity provider audit logs can reveal anomalous consent grants and token use, but many organizations lack dedicated OAuth grant monitoring.
ITID-62521.response: Revoke the malicious OAuth grant/token, force re-authentication, and audit all data accessed during the token's validity window.
metrics: Number of stale/excessive OAuth grants revoked per review cycle
Time to token revocation after detection
ITID-62521.notes: Sibling differentiator: this leaf is scoped to the identity/token trust mechanism (OAuth/SSO) specifically, as opposed to configuration issues (ITID-62511) or direct credential-based account takeover (ITID-62531).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General OAuth/SSO Abuse (Third-Party SaaS Context)
playbook.description: An attacker abuses OAuth authorization flows or SSO trust relationships to gain unauthorized access to third-party SaaS applications or data.

steps.title: Detect anomalous OAuth grant or SSO authentication activity
steps.desc: Investigate alerts of unusual OAuth consent grants, impossible-travel SSO logins, or unexpected token usage across SaaS applications.
steps.guidance: Review identity provider (IdP) logs and SaaS OAuth grant audit logs.
steps.outcome: Confirmed malicious OAuth grant or SSO abuse.

steps.title: Determine the malicious app/grant's scope and access
steps.desc: Identify the specific OAuth application or SSO session involved and what permissions/data it was granted access to.
steps.outcome: Scope of granted access and potential data exposure documented.

steps.title: Identify affected users and downstream applications
steps.desc: Determine which users granted the malicious consent and which downstream SaaS applications were accessed via the abused SSO trust.
steps.outcome: Full list of affected users and applications compiled.

steps.title: Revoke the malicious OAuth grant and SSO sessions
steps.desc: Revoke the OAuth application's access tokens and terminate all active SSO sessions for affected users.

steps.title: Force credential reset and re-authentication with MFA
steps.desc: Force affected users to reset credentials and re-authenticate with MFA enforced.
steps.outcome: User accounts secured against continued unauthorized access.

steps.title: Review and restrict OAuth app consent policy
steps.desc: Review the organization's OAuth app-consent policy and restrict end-user ability to grant consent to unverified/unreviewed third-party apps.
steps.guidance: Enable admin-consent-only workflows for new OAuth integrations.
steps.outcome: OAuth consent policy tightened to prevent recurrence.

steps.title: Audit all existing OAuth grants for similar risk
steps.desc: Review all existing third-party OAuth grants across the tenant for excessive scopes or suspicious applications.
steps.outcome: Existing OAuth grant inventory reviewed and remediated as needed.

steps.title: Restore normal access and monitor
steps.desc: Confirm affected users have normal, secure access restored and monitor for recurrence of suspicious OAuth activity.
steps.outcome: Access restored with heightened monitoring in place.

steps.title: Implement least-privilege OAuth scope review process
steps.desc: Document the incident and formalize periodic least-privilege review of OAuth application scopes across the SaaS estate.
steps.outcome: OAuth governance and periodic review process implemented.

ITID-62531.def: An incident in which an adversary obtained a legitimate user's direct login credentials for a third-party SaaS service (via phishing, credential stuffing, or password reuse) and used them to log in as that user.
ITID-62531.purpose: Captures direct takeover of a user's account credentials within a third-party SaaS service, without a distinct OAuth/SSO or misconfiguration mechanism.
scopeIncludes: Credential-stuffing login success against a SaaS service using passwords reused from an unrelated breach
Phished SaaS login credentials used to directly authenticate as the victim
scopeExcludes: OAuth token or SSO trust abuse without direct primary-credential compromise (route to ITID-62521)
Access resulting from organizational SaaS misconfiguration rather than credential theft (route to ITID-62511)
ITID-62531.severity: High if the account holds administrative or sensitive-data access; Medium for a standard user account.
ITID-62531.priority: P1 for administrative account takeover; P2 for standard user accounts.
ITID-62531.escalation: Escalate to identity/IAM team for immediate credential reset and session revocation.
indicators: Login from an unfamiliar geographic location or device immediately followed by unusual activity
Multiple failed login attempts preceding a successful authentication (credential stuffing pattern)
User report of unrecognized account activity
vectors: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts obtained via phishing or credential stuffing against the SaaS login portal
rootCauses: Lack of multi-factor authentication enforcement on the SaaS platform
Password reuse across personal and organizational SaaS accounts
controls: Mandatory multi-factor authentication for all SaaS accounts
Credential-stuffing detection via impossible-travel and failed-login-pattern alerting
ITID-62531.detection: Strong where SaaS login telemetry is ingested into the SIEM; impossible-travel and brute-force detection are mature capabilities.
ITID-62531.response: Reset credentials, revoke active sessions, enable MFA if not already active, and review account activity during the compromise window.
metrics: Number of SaaS accounts taken over per quarter
Time to credential reset and session revocation
ITID-62531.notes: Sibling differentiator: direct primary-credential compromise, as opposed to OAuth/SSO trust abuse (ITID-62521) which can persist independent of the primary password.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Account Takeover in Third-Party Service
playbook.description: An attacker takes over a user's or service account within a third-party SaaS service through credential compromise or session hijacking.

steps.title: Confirm account takeover indicators
steps.desc: Investigate alerts of anomalous login activity (impossible travel, new device, unusual access pattern) within the third-party SaaS service.
steps.guidance: Review SaaS/IdP audit logs and any CASB anomaly detection alerts.
steps.outcome: Confirmed account takeover in the third-party service.
steps.abort: If activity is a false positive (e.g., legitimate travel), close with documentation.

steps.title: Determine attacker actions taken within the account
steps.desc: Review the account's activity during the compromise window for data access, exfiltration, configuration changes, or lateral use to access other systems.
steps.outcome: Full scope of attacker actions documented.

steps.title: Revoke sessions and disable the compromised account
steps.desc: Immediately terminate all active sessions and temporarily disable or lock the compromised account within the SaaS service.
steps.outcome: Attacker access to the account terminated.

steps.title: Revoke any OAuth tokens/API keys issued from the compromised account
steps.desc: Revoke third-party OAuth grants, API keys, and application connections tied to the compromised account.
steps.outcome: All derived access from the compromised account revoked.

steps.title: Reset credentials and re-provision MFA
steps.desc: Force a full credential reset and re-enroll MFA for the affected user.
steps.outcome: Account secured with new, verified credentials and MFA.

steps.title: Revert unauthorized changes made during the compromise
steps.desc: Identify and revert any configuration, data, or permission changes made by the attacker during account control.
steps.outcome: SaaS account/tenant restored to known-good state.

steps.title: Restore account access and monitor
steps.desc: Return the account to normal use with heightened monitoring for a defined period.
steps.outcome: Account restored to legitimate user with confirmed normal activity.

steps.title: Strengthen third-party account security controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and reinforce MFA enforcement, conditional access policies, and anomaly detection for third-party SaaS accounts.
steps.outcome: Updated SaaS account security controls implemented.

ITID-62541.def: An incident in which an adversary exploited a design flaw, authorization weakness, or logic error in a third-party SaaS application's own API to access data or functionality beyond what the requesting party should be permitted.
ITID-62541.purpose: Captures exploitation of a vendor-side API vulnerability or logic flaw within a third-party SaaS application, as opposed to identity or configuration issues on the organization's side.
scopeIncludes: Broken object-level authorization in a SaaS vendor's API allowing cross-account data access
SaaS vendor API rate-limit or business-logic abuse resulting in bulk data extraction
scopeExcludes: Organizational misconfiguration of SaaS security settings (route to ITID-62511)
OAuth/SSO or direct credential-based account access issues (route to ITID-62521/62531)
Non-SaaS third-party application API exploitation, covered generally under Vulnerabilities in Third-Party Applications (route to ITID-62231)
ITID-62541.severity: High if the vulnerability enables cross-tenant or bulk data access; Medium for limited-scope logic flaws.
ITID-62541.priority: P1 if cross-tenant data exposure is confirmed; P2 otherwise.
ITID-62541.escalation: Escalate to the SaaS vendor's security team and internal privacy/legal if customer data exposure is confirmed.
indicators: Vendor security bulletin disclosing an API authorization flaw
Anomalous API response data inconsistent with the requesting tenant's expected access scope
vectors: Data from Information Repositories accessed via a SaaS vendor API authorization flaw
rootCauses: SaaS vendor API lacking robust tenant-isolation/object-level authorization checks
Lack of independent security testing of vendor APIs the organization depends on
controls: Vendor security assessment requirements including API authorization testing
Contractual right-to-audit clauses for critical SaaS vendors
ITID-62541.detection: Weak from the customer side alone; typically reliant on vendor disclosure or independent security research.
ITID-62541.response: Request vendor remediation confirmation, assess data exposure scope, and require a post-incident vendor security review before continued reliance.
metrics: Number of vendor API vulnerabilities disclosed affecting the organization per year
ITID-62541.notes: Sibling differentiator: vendor-side API logic/authorization flaw, as distinct from organizational misconfiguration (ITID-62511) or identity-based abuse (ITID-62521/62531).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Third-Party API Exploitation in SaaS
playbook.description: An attacker exploits an API exposed by a third-party SaaS application to gain unauthorized access to data or functionality.

steps.title: Detect anomalous SaaS API activity
steps.desc: Investigate alerts from CASB/API security tooling or the SaaS vendor's own audit logs indicating abnormal API request patterns.
steps.outcome: Confirmed anomalous/malicious API activity within the SaaS application.

steps.title: Identify the specific API vulnerability or abuse pattern
steps.desc: Determine the nature of the exploitation (authorization bypass, rate-limit evasion, data-scraping, injection).

steps.title: Assess data/records exposed
steps.desc: Determine what data was accessed, modified, or exfiltrated via the exploited API.

steps.title: Revoke abused API credentials/tokens
steps.desc: Revoke the API keys/OAuth tokens used in the exploitation.

steps.title: Engage the SaaS vendor to restrict/patch the vulnerable API
steps.desc: Report the exploitation to the vendor's security team and request immediate mitigation (rate limiting, WAF rule, endpoint disablement).
steps.outcome: Vendor applies interim mitigation for the vulnerable API.

steps.title: Coordinate vendor remediation and validate the fix
steps.desc: Track the vendor's permanent fix through to deployment and confirm it closes the exploited vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Vendor fix confirmed deployed and effective.

steps.title: Reissue credentials with least-privilege scopes
steps.desc: Reissue API credentials for the integration with minimal necessary permission scopes.

steps.title: Restore integration and validate
steps.desc: Restore the API integration and validate correct behavior and access scoping before full production use.
steps.outcome: Integration restored with verified secure configuration.

steps.title: Strengthen SaaS API risk assessment in vendor management
steps.desc: Document the incident and incorporate API security assessment into ongoing third-party SaaS vendor risk management.
steps.outcome: Updated vendor risk assessment criteria published.

ITID-62611.def: An incident in which an adversary injected malicious code, commands, or configuration into the organization's continuous integration (CI) pipeline, causing unauthorized code to execute during build, test, or packaging stages.
ITID-62611.purpose: Captures injection of unauthorized code into the organization's own continuous integration pipeline, as distinct from compromise of a third-party vendor's build pipeline.
scopeIncludes: A malicious pull request merged and executed within a CI build job
Compromised CI runner/agent configuration used to inject code into build output
CI pipeline environment variable or build-script tampering to alter build artifacts
scopeExcludes: Compromise of a third-party vendor's build pipeline that produces software the organization consumes (route to ITID-62141)
Compromise of the code repository platform itself as the entry point (route to ITID-62621)
ITID-62611.severity: High to Critical given CI pipelines typically have broad access to source code, secrets, and deployment targets.
ITID-62611.priority: P1 upon confirmation of any unauthorized code execution within a production-bound CI pipeline.
ITID-62611.escalation: Escalate to DevOps/platform engineering and application security immediately; halt all pipeline runs pending scope assessment.
indicators: Unexpected build steps or scripts appearing in CI configuration not matching the source-controlled definition
CI job output or artifact hash mismatch against expected build results
Anomalous outbound network activity from a CI runner during a build
vectors: Compromise of Software Dependencies and Development Tools via a poisoned CI configuration or malicious pull request
rootCauses: CI pipeline lacking mandatory code review gates before merge-triggered builds
CI runners granted excessive credentials/secrets beyond what a given build stage requires
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Mandatory code review/approval gates before CI-triggered builds execute
Least-privilege scoping of CI runner credentials and secrets
ITID-62611.detection: Moderate — build artifact integrity checks and CI configuration drift monitoring can catch this, but visibility depends on maturity of the DevSecOps program.
ITID-62611.response: Halt affected pipelines, roll back to the last known-good build configuration, and audit all artifacts produced during the compromise window.
metrics: Number of CI pipeline compromise incidents per year
Time to pipeline halt after detection
ITID-62611.notes: Scoped to the organization's own internal CI pipeline as the compromised asset, distinct from a third-party vendor's cloud build infrastructure (ITID-62141).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General CI Pipeline Code Injection
playbook.description: An attacker injects malicious code or commands into a Continuous Integration pipeline, executing during the build/test process.

steps.title: Detect anomalous CI pipeline behavior
steps.desc: Investigate unexpected build steps, unusual outbound network calls from build agents, or unauthorized pipeline configuration changes.
steps.guidance: Review CI/CD platform audit logs and build agent EDR telemetry.
steps.outcome: Confirmed malicious code injection into the CI pipeline.

steps.title: Identify the injection vector
steps.desc: Determine how the injection occurred (malicious pull request, compromised pipeline config file, poisoned dependency, compromised contributor credentials).

steps.title: Determine scope of affected builds/artifacts
steps.desc: Identify all builds, artifacts, and downstream deployments that ran through the compromised pipeline stage.
steps.outcome: Complete scope of affected builds/artifacts documented.

steps.title: Halt the affected pipeline immediately
steps.desc: Disable or pause the compromised CI pipeline to prevent further malicious builds.
steps.outcome: No further compromised builds are produced.

steps.title: Quarantine affected build artifacts
steps.desc: Prevent deployment/promotion of any artifacts produced during the compromise window.
steps.outcome: Compromised artifacts blocked from reaching production.

steps.title: Rotate secrets accessible to the build environment
steps.desc: Rotate all credentials, tokens, and secrets that were accessible to the compromised pipeline run.

steps.title: Remove malicious code and restore pipeline configuration from known-good state
steps.desc: Revert the pipeline configuration and any affected repository code to the last known-good, verified state.
steps.outcome: Pipeline and code restored to a clean, trusted state.

steps.title: Verify build provenance and re-sign artifacts
steps.desc: Rebuild affected artifacts from clean source and verify build provenance/signing before redeployment.
steps.guidance: Use SLSA-style provenance attestation if available.

steps.title: Resume pipeline operations with hardened controls
steps.desc: Re-enable the CI pipeline with additional access controls and monitoring, and validate normal build operation.
steps.outcome: Pipeline restored to secure, monitored operation.

steps.title: Harden CI pipeline access controls and code review gates
steps.desc: Document the incident and implement mandatory code review, branch protection, and least-privilege pipeline permissions to prevent recurrence.

ITID-62621.def: An incident in which an adversary gained unauthorized access to the organization's code repository hosting platform — through stolen credentials, exploited platform vulnerabilities, or misconfigured access controls — enabling tampering with source code prior to any CI pipeline stage.
ITID-62621.purpose: Captures compromise of the organization's code repository platform itself (e.g., source control server or hosted git service configuration) as the entry point into the software supply chain.
scopeIncludes: Stolen developer credentials used to push unauthorized commits directly to a protected branch
Exploited vulnerability in a self-hosted git server granting unauthorized repository access
Misconfigured repository access controls allowing an external party to modify source code
scopeExcludes: Malicious code injected specifically during the CI build/execution stage rather than at the repository level (route to ITID-62611)
Open-source project repository hijacking (route to ITID-62341, a distinct Tier-4 group)
ITID-62621.severity: Critical — repository-level compromise represents the earliest possible point of tampering in the software supply chain.
ITID-62621.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of unauthorized repository access or commits.
ITID-62621.escalation: Escalate to DevOps/platform engineering and application security immediately; freeze affected repositories pending review.
indicators: Commits from an unfamiliar IP address or outside normal developer working hours
Branch protection rule changes not matching an approved change request
Git server access logs showing authentication from an unrecognized source
vectors: Compromise of Software Dependencies and Development Tools via stolen developer credentials or exploited repository platform vulnerabilities
rootCauses: Lack of mandatory MFA for developer repository access
Overly permissive branch protection or missing signed-commit requirements
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Mandatory MFA and signed commits for all repository write access
Branch protection rules with mandatory review before merge
ITID-62621.detection: Moderate — git server audit logs and commit-signing verification can reveal unauthorized access, but detection maturity varies widely by organization.
ITID-62621.response: Revoke compromised credentials, audit all commits during the compromise window, and force re-verification of affected code before further deployment.
metrics: Number of unauthorized commit events detected per year
Time to credential revocation after detection
detections: Git server access log anomaly monitoring
ITID-62621.notes: Sibling differentiator versus ITID-62611: this leaf covers compromise at the repository/source-control layer, upstream of the CI build execution stage.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Supply Chain Attack via Code Repository
playbook.description: An attacker compromises a source code repository (internal or upstream) used in the software supply chain to introduce malicious code or steal source/secrets.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized repository access or code change
steps.desc: Investigate alerts of unauthorized commits, force-pushes, or anomalous repository access, and confirm the scope of the compromise.
steps.guidance: Review Git platform audit logs (GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket) for anomalous commit authorship, IP addresses, or access-token usage.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized repository access and identification of the compromised account/token.

steps.title: Identify malicious commits and affected branches/tags
steps.desc: Diff suspicious commits against the known-good history to identify exactly what code was introduced or exfiltrated.
steps.outcome: Complete list of malicious commits, affected branches, and tags.

steps.title: Determine downstream build/deployment impact
steps.desc: Identify whether any builds or deployments consumed the malicious commits before detection.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised credentials/access token
steps.desc: Immediately revoke the compromised user account, SSH key, or personal access token used for unauthorized access.
steps.outcome: Attacker no longer has repository access.

steps.title: Lock down the affected repository
steps.desc: Temporarily restrict write access to the repository to trusted maintainers only, and enable required branch protection/review rules.
steps.outcome: Further unauthorized changes to the repository prevented.

steps.title: Halt downstream pipelines consuming the affected repository
steps.desc: Pause CI/CD pipelines that build from the affected repository until the code is verified clean.

steps.title: Revert malicious commits and restore known-good state
steps.desc: Revert or remove the malicious commits, restoring the repository to the last verified clean state.
steps.guidance: Do not simply force-push over history without preserving forensic evidence first.
steps.outcome: Repository restored to a clean, trusted state.

steps.title: Rotate secrets exposed in the repository or accessible to compromised credentials
steps.desc: Rotate any secrets, API keys, or credentials stored in or accessible via the compromised repository/account.

steps.title: Rebuild and redeploy from clean source
steps.desc: Rebuild affected artifacts from the clean repository state and redeploy after verification.

steps.title: Strengthen repository access controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and implement mandatory MFA, branch protection, and least-privilege access controls for all code repositories.

ITID-62631.def: An incident in which an adversary gained unauthorized access to a secrets manager or credential vault integrated with the organization's DevOps toolchain, exposing API keys, passwords, or certificates used across the pipeline.
ITID-62631.purpose: Captures compromise of a secrets manager or credential vault used by the DevOps pipeline, exposing sensitive credentials to unauthorized parties.
scopeIncludes: Exploited access-control misconfiguration on a secrets manager exposing stored credentials to an unauthorized pipeline stage or user
Stolen vault access token used to bulk-retrieve secrets outside normal usage patterns
scopeExcludes: Compromised infrastructure-as-code templates (route to ITID-62632)
Compromised artifact/package registry (route to ITID-62633)
ITID-62631.severity: Critical — secrets manager compromise typically exposes credentials with broad downstream access across multiple systems.
ITID-62631.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of unauthorized secrets manager access.
ITID-62631.escalation: Escalate to DevOps/platform engineering and security operations immediately; begin mass credential rotation.
indicators: Anomalous bulk secret-retrieval activity in vault access logs
Vault access from an unexpected identity, service account, or network location
Downstream systems showing use of credentials outside their expected pipeline context
vectors: Credentials in Files or vault misconfiguration exploited to access stored pipeline secrets
rootCauses: Secrets manager access policy overly broad (not scoped per-pipeline or per-service)
Lack of secret rotation and short-lived credential issuance practices
mitreTechniques: T1552.001 Unsecured Credentials: Credentials in Files
controls: Least-privilege, per-service scoping of secrets manager access policies
Short-lived, automatically rotated credentials issued to pipeline stages
ITID-62631.detection: Moderate to strong where vault access logging and anomaly detection are actively monitored.
ITID-62631.response: Rotate all exposed credentials immediately, audit downstream systems for unauthorized use, and review vault access policy scoping.
metrics: Number of secrets rotated per incident
Time to full credential rotation after detection
ITID-62631.notes: Sibling differentiator: this leaf is scoped to secrets manager/vault compromise specifically, distinct from IaC template tampering (ITID-62632) and artifact registry poisoning (ITID-62633).

playbook.name: Compromised Secrets Manager/Vault Exposing Credentials to Pipeline
playbook.description: The organization's secrets manager or vault is compromised, exposing credentials used by CI/CD pipelines and downstream systems.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized access to the secrets manager/vault
steps.desc: Investigate alerts of anomalous secret-read activity or unauthorized authentication to the vault, and confirm the scope of the compromise.
steps.guidance: Review vault audit logs (e.g., HashiCorp Vault audit device, AWS Secrets Manager CloudTrail events).
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized access and identification of the entry point.

steps.title: Enumerate all secrets accessed during the compromise window
steps.desc: Determine exactly which secrets, credentials, and certificates were read or could have been read during the exposure window.
steps.outcome: Complete inventory of potentially exposed secrets.

steps.title: Assess downstream systems dependent on exposed secrets
steps.desc: Map exposed secrets to the downstream systems, pipelines, and services that rely on them.
steps.outcome: Full blast radius of systems dependent on exposed secrets documented.

steps.title: Restrict vault access and revoke the compromised access path
steps.desc: Immediately revoke the compromised authentication method (token, AppRole, IAM role) used to access the vault.
steps.outcome: Attacker access to the vault terminated.

steps.title: Pause pipelines/services dependent on potentially exposed secrets
steps.desc: Temporarily halt CI/CD pipelines and services using the potentially exposed secrets until rotation is complete.
steps.outcome: Reduced risk of exploitation of exposed secrets during remediation.

steps.title: Rotate all exposed secrets and credentials
steps.desc: Rotate every secret identified as potentially exposed, prioritizing the most privileged/critical credentials first.
steps.guidance: Coordinate rotation order to avoid breaking dependent services; use automated rotation where the vault supports it.
steps.outcome: All exposed secrets invalidated and replaced.

steps.title: Patch or reconfigure the compromised vault access path
steps.desc: Identify and remediate the root cause of the vault compromise (misconfigured policy, leaked auth token, vulnerable vault version).

steps.title: Resume pipelines/services with rotated secrets
steps.desc: Resume affected pipelines and services using the newly rotated secrets and validate normal operation.
steps.outcome: Services and pipelines fully operational with rotated secrets.

steps.title: Strengthen vault access policy and monitoring
steps.desc: Document the incident and implement least-privilege vault access policies, short-lived credentials, and enhanced audit alerting.

ITID-62632.def: An incident in which an adversary modified an infrastructure-as-code template or configuration (e.g., Terraform, CloudFormation) to provision unauthorized cloud resources, backdoored network paths, or overly permissive access when the pipeline applies the change.
ITID-62632.purpose: Captures tampering with infrastructure-as-code (IaC) templates such that malicious or unauthorized cloud resources are provisioned during automated deployment.
