scopeIncludes: A malicious commit to an IaC repository adding an attacker-controlled security group rule or IAM role
IaC template tampering that provisions a rogue compute instance or storage bucket during automated deployment
scopeExcludes: Secrets manager/vault compromise specifically (route to ITID-62631)
Malicious container images used within the deployment rather than IaC templates themselves (route to ITID-6264x)
ITID-62632.severity: High to Critical, since IaC changes apply automatically and at scale across cloud environments.
ITID-62632.priority: P1 upon confirmation of any unauthorized resource provisioned via a tampered IaC template.
ITID-62632.escalation: Escalate to cloud platform engineering and security operations immediately; halt further IaC pipeline applies.
indicators: Cloud resource inventory drift not matching the approved IaC source of truth
IaC plan/apply output showing unexpected resource changes not corresponding to an approved pull request
Newly created IAM roles or security groups with unusually broad permissions
vectors: Compromise of Software Dependencies and Development Tools via a tampered IaC template merged into the deployment pipeline
Deploy Container or resource provisioning triggered by malicious IaC as the deployment mechanism
rootCauses: IaC pipeline lacking mandatory plan-review/approval before apply
Cloud drift detection not implemented to catch unauthorized resource changes
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Mandatory IaC plan review and approval gate before apply
Continuous cloud configuration drift detection against the IaC source of truth
ITID-62632.detection: Moderate to strong where cloud security posture management (CSPM) and drift detection tooling are deployed.
ITID-62632.response: Revert the tampered IaC template, tear down any unauthorized resources provisioned, and audit for lateral movement from the rogue resources.
metrics: Number of unauthorized cloud resources provisioned per incident
Time to drift detection and remediation
ITID-62632.notes: Sibling differentiator: this leaf is scoped to IaC template tampering specifically, distinct from secrets manager compromise (ITID-62631) and malicious container images (ITID-6264x).

playbook.name: Compromised Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) Template Injecting Malicious Resources
playbook.description: A malicious change is introduced into an Infrastructure-as-Code template (Terraform/CloudFormation/etc.), causing malicious cloud resources to be provisioned during deployment.

steps.title: Detect anomalous provisioned cloud resources
steps.desc: Investigate CSPM/cloud audit-log alerts showing unexpected resources (e.g., new IAM roles, backdoor security group rules, unauthorized compute instances) created via an IaC pipeline run.
steps.guidance: Correlate resource creation timestamps with the specific IaC apply/deployment run.
steps.outcome: Confirmed malicious resources traced to a specific IaC template change.

steps.title: Identify the malicious IaC template change
steps.desc: Diff the IaC template/module against the last known-good version to identify the injected malicious configuration.
steps.outcome: Specific malicious template change identified and its introduction point (PR, commit, module) documented.

steps.title: Determine full scope of malicious resources deployed
steps.desc: Enumerate all cloud resources created or modified as a result of the malicious template across all environments where it was applied.
steps.outcome: Complete inventory of malicious/unauthorized cloud resources.

steps.title: Halt further IaC deployments
steps.desc: Pause the IaC pipeline to prevent further application of the malicious template to additional environments.
steps.outcome: No additional environments receive the malicious configuration.

steps.title: Isolate or disable malicious cloud resources
steps.desc: Disable or restrict network/IAM access for the malicious resources (backdoor IAM roles, unauthorized instances) pending removal.
steps.outcome: Malicious resources' capability to cause further harm neutralized.

steps.title: Remove malicious resources and restore template to known-good state
steps.desc: Delete unauthorized cloud resources and revert the IaC template/module to its verified clean version.
steps.guidance: Use IaC drift detection to confirm full remediation of unauthorized state.
steps.outcome: Cloud environment and IaC source restored to clean, authorized state.

steps.title: Rotate credentials exposed by malicious IAM resources
steps.desc: Rotate any credentials or roles that may have been exposed or created with excessive privilege by the malicious template.

steps.title: Resume IaC pipeline with added review controls
steps.desc: Resume the IaC pipeline with mandatory plan-review and policy-as-code scanning gates before applying changes.
steps.guidance: Consider tools like Checkov/tfsec/OPA for automated IaC security policy enforcement.
steps.outcome: Pipeline resumed with enforced pre-apply security scanning.

steps.title: Mandate IaC security scanning and peer review
steps.desc: Document the incident and formalize mandatory automated security scanning and peer review for all IaC changes before deployment.
steps.outcome: IaC governance standard with enforced scanning gates published.

ITID-62633.def: An incident in which an adversary gained unauthorized write access to an internal artifact repository or package registry, replacing or injecting malicious versions of internally built software components consumed by downstream teams.
ITID-62633.purpose: Captures compromise or poisoning of an internal artifact repository (private package registry) used to distribute build outputs across the organization.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized publish of a tampered internal package version to a private registry, consumed by other internal teams
Compromise of artifact repository access controls allowing overwrite of a previously published internal package
scopeExcludes: Public open-source registry poisoning (route to ITID-62311/62321, a distinct Tier-4 group)
Secrets manager compromise (route to ITID-62631)
IaC template tampering (route to ITID-62632)
ITID-62633.severity: High to Critical given the potential for cascading compromise across every internal team consuming the affected package.
ITID-62633.priority: P1 upon confirmation of any tampered package published to the internal registry.
ITID-62633.escalation: Escalate to DevOps/platform engineering and all downstream teams consuming the affected internal package.
indicators: Internal package hash mismatch against the last known-good build
Unexpected publish event to the internal registry outside the normal CI release process
Downstream build failures or anomalous behavior traced to a recently updated internal dependency
vectors: Compromise of Software Dependencies and Development Tools via unauthorized write access to an internal artifact repository
rootCauses: Internal registry write access not scoped to the automated CI service account only
Lack of internal package signing/verification before consumption
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Internal artifact signing and verification before consumption by downstream builds
Registry write access restricted to the automated CI pipeline service account only
ITID-62633.detection: Moderate — artifact hash/signature verification can catch tampering if implemented, but many internal registries lack this control by default.
ITID-62633.response: Roll back to the last known-good internal package version, audit all downstream consumers, and restrict registry write access pending review.
metrics: Number of downstream teams affected by the poisoned internal package
Time to rollback across all consumers
sops: Internal Artifact Repository Compromise Response SOP
ITID-62633.notes: Sibling differentiator: internal/private artifact repository compromise, distinct from public open-source registry attacks tracked under the Manufacturing and Production Exploits Tier-4 group.

playbook.name: Compromised Artifact Repository (Internal Package Registry) Poisoning
playbook.description: The organization's internal artifact/package registry is compromised, allowing an attacker to poison internally-published packages consumed by other teams.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized publication to the internal registry
steps.desc: Investigate alerts of unexpected package versions published or registry admin activity, and confirm unauthorized/malicious publication.
steps.guidance: Review artifact registry (Artifactory/Nexus/npm/PyPI internal) audit logs for publisher identity and package hash changes.
steps.outcome: Confirmed malicious package version published to the internal registry.

steps.title: Identify all consumers of the poisoned package version
steps.desc: Determine which internal projects/builds pulled the malicious package version from the registry.

steps.title: Determine the compromise vector into the registry
steps.desc: Determine how the attacker gained publish access (compromised publisher credentials, registry vulnerability, misconfigured permissions).

steps.title: Remove/quarantine the malicious package version
steps.desc: Immediately unpublish or quarantine the malicious package version from the internal registry.
steps.outcome: Malicious package version no longer retrievable.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised publisher credentials
steps.desc: Revoke and reset the credentials/tokens that were used to publish the malicious package.

steps.title: Halt downstream builds consuming the poisoned package
steps.desc: Pause CI/CD pipelines for all identified consumers until they are updated to a clean package version.
steps.outcome: No further compromised builds produced downstream.

steps.title: Rebuild consuming services on a verified clean package version
steps.desc: Update all consuming projects to a verified clean version and rebuild/redeploy.
steps.outcome: All downstream services running on clean dependencies.

steps.title: Harden registry publish permissions and enable signing
steps.desc: Implement least-privilege publish permissions and require package signing/provenance verification for all internal packages.
steps.outcome: Registry publish controls hardened to prevent recurrence.

steps.title: Restore normal registry and build operations
steps.desc: Confirm the registry and all consuming services operate normally with clean, verified packages.
steps.outcome: Environment fully restored and validated clean.

steps.title: Formalize internal package signing and provenance policy
steps.desc: Document the incident and mandate package signing/provenance verification for all internally-published artifacts going forward.
steps.outcome: Internal package integrity policy implemented and enforced in CI.

ITID-62634.def: An incident involving compromise of a DevOps toolchain component whose specific type (secrets manager, IaC template, or artifact repository) has not yet been determined.
ITID-62634.purpose: Intake leaf for a compromised DevOps tool incident not yet attributed to the secrets-manager, IaC-template, or artifact-repository leaves in this group.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered DevOps tool compromise pending component-type triage
Compromise of a DevOps tool not covered by the more specific sibling leaves, such as a build orchestration or ticketing integration tool
scopeExcludes: Cases confirmed as secrets manager compromise (route to ITID-62631), IaC template tampering (route to ITID-62632), or artifact repository poisoning (route to ITID-62633)
ITID-62634.severity: High pending triage, consistent with the Compromised DevOps Tools group generally.
ITID-62634.priority: P1 pending triage; downgrade once component type and scope are confirmed.
ITID-62634.escalation: Escalate to DevOps/platform engineering for immediate containment while triage proceeds.
indicators: Anomalous activity within a DevOps toolchain component, specific type not yet determined
vectors: Compromise of Software Dependencies and Development Tools via an as-yet-uncharacterized DevOps tool compromise
rootCauses: Incomplete DevOps toolchain inventory delaying component-type determination
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Comprehensive DevOps toolchain inventory and access review
ITID-62634.detection: Varies by underlying component; treat detection as inherited from whichever specific leaf the case is eventually triaged to.
ITID-62634.response: Contain the affected tool and triage to ITID-62631, ITID-62632, or ITID-62633 as soon as component type is confirmed.
metrics: Time from detection to component-type triage
ITID-62634.notes: Unclassified/general intake leaf for the Compromised DevOps Tools group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Compromised DevOps Tool
playbook.description: A general or unclassified compromise involving a DevOps tool (build server, orchestration platform, monitoring agent) in the CI/CD toolchain.

steps.title: Confirm the DevOps tool compromise
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/report and confirm unauthorized access or malicious activity involving the specific DevOps tool.
steps.guidance: Review the tool's audit logs and associated EDR telemetry on the hosting system.
steps.outcome: Confirmed compromise and its scope within the DevOps toolchain.

steps.title: Determine downstream systems and pipelines affected
steps.desc: Identify all pipelines, builds, and systems that interact with the compromised tool.
steps.outcome: Full blast-radius map of affected downstream systems.

steps.title: Isolate or disable the compromised tool
steps.desc: Take the compromised DevOps tool offline or isolate it from the network to prevent further malicious activity.

steps.title: Rotate credentials/secrets accessible to the tool
steps.desc: Rotate all credentials, API keys, and service account tokens accessible to or stored within the compromised tool.

steps.title: Rebuild or patch the compromised tool
steps.desc: Rebuild the tool from a known-good configuration/image or apply the vendor patch that closes the exploited vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Tool restored to a clean, patched state.

steps.title: Audit for unauthorized changes made via the compromised tool
steps.desc: Review pipelines, configurations, and deployed artifacts for any unauthorized changes introduced while the tool was compromised.
steps.outcome: All unauthorized changes identified and reverted.

steps.title: Restore normal DevOps toolchain operations
steps.desc: Bring the tool back online and validate normal, secure operation of the broader toolchain.
steps.outcome: DevOps toolchain fully restored and validated.

steps.title: Strengthen DevOps toolchain security hardening
steps.desc: Document the incident and implement hardening standards (patch cadence, network segmentation, least privilege) for all DevOps tools in the pipeline.

ITID-62641.def: An incident in which a developer or automated pipeline pulled a malicious container image directly from a public container registry, introducing attacker-controlled code into a build or production environment.
ITID-62641.purpose: Captures use of a malicious public container image pulled from a public registry such as Docker Hub into the organization's build or runtime environment.
scopeIncludes: A publicly available container image on Docker Hub found to contain embedded malware or a cryptominer
A typosquatted public image name (e.g., misspelled popular base image) pulled by mistake
scopeExcludes: A malicious base image used internally across multiple builds after initial ingestion (route to ITID-62642)
Legitimate internal registry tag overwritten with malicious content (route to ITID-62643)
ITID-62641.severity: High if the image reached a production runtime; Medium if caught in a build/test environment only.
ITID-62641.priority: P1 if the malicious image was deployed to production; P2 if contained to build/test.
ITID-62641.escalation: Escalate to DevOps/platform engineering immediately to identify all pulls of the affected image tag.
indicators: Container image scanning tool flags a known-malicious image hash
Unexpected cryptomining or outbound C2 activity from a running container
Public registry security advisory naming a specific malicious image
vectors: Deploy Container using a malicious public image pulled directly from an unvetted public registry
rootCauses: Lack of a mandatory image-scanning gate before public images are pulled into pipelines
No allow-list restricting builds to vetted/mirrored base images
controls: Mandatory container image vulnerability/malware scanning before use
Internal mirror/allow-list of approved base images restricting direct public registry pulls
ITID-62641.detection: Strong where image scanning tooling is integrated into the pipeline; weak for organizations pulling public images ad hoc without scanning.
ITID-62641.response: Remove the malicious image from all environments, rebuild affected containers from a vetted base image, and audit runtime activity during the exposure window.
metrics: Number of malicious image pulls detected per quarter
Time to removal after detection
sops: Container Image Security Incident Response SOP
ITID-62641.notes: Sibling differentiator: this leaf covers the initial ingestion of a malicious image directly from a public registry, distinct from an already-ingested backdoored base image propagating internally (ITID-62642) or registry tag-overwrite poisoning (ITID-62643).

playbook.name: Malicious Public Container Image Pulled from Docker Hub
playbook.description: A malicious container image is pulled from a public registry (e.g., Docker Hub) and deployed within the organization's environment.

steps.title: Detect the malicious container image via scanning or runtime alert
steps.desc: Investigate an alert from container image scanning or runtime security tooling identifying a malicious image (embedded malware, cryptominer, backdoor).
steps.guidance: Check image scan reports and runtime behavioral detection (e.g., unexpected outbound mining pool connections).
steps.tool: Container Image Scanner / Runtime Security Tool

steps.title: Identify all running containers/deployments using the image
steps.desc: Query the container orchestration platform for all pods/containers running the malicious image across all clusters/environments.
steps.outcome: Complete list of affected running containers and deployments.

steps.title: Assess payload behavior and impact
steps.desc: Determine the malicious image's capability (cryptomining, data exfiltration, lateral movement into the cluster).

steps.title: Terminate and quarantine affected containers
steps.desc: Immediately stop/kill all running containers using the malicious image and prevent redeployment.

steps.title: Block the malicious image at the registry/admission-control layer
steps.desc: Add the malicious image digest to an admission-controller deny-list to prevent redeployment.
steps.outcome: Malicious image blocked from future deployment.

steps.title: Deploy verified clean image and rebuild affected services
steps.desc: Replace the malicious image with a verified clean/trusted image and redeploy affected services.
steps.outcome: Services running on clean, verified container images.

steps.title: Implement image provenance/allowlist policy for public images
steps.desc: Restrict future image pulls to an approved, scanned image allowlist or require mandatory internal mirroring/scanning of all public base images.
steps.guidance: Consistent with prior ITID-30000/40000 container-security hardening conventions.
steps.outcome: Public image pull policy hardened across the cluster.

steps.title: Restore services and validate cluster integrity
steps.desc: Confirm affected services are restored and the cluster is free of residual malicious workloads.
steps.outcome: Cluster confirmed clean and services fully operational.

steps.title: Mandate container image scanning in CI/CD
steps.desc: Document the incident and require mandatory vulnerability/malware scanning of all container images before deployment.
steps.outcome: Container image scanning gate enforced in CI/CD pipeline.

ITID-62642.def: An incident in which a container base image that had already been compromised (whether pulled maliciously or tampered with after ingestion) was used as the foundation for multiple internal application builds, propagating the backdoor across many downstream containers.
ITID-62642.purpose: Captures the downstream impact of a single backdoored base image being reused as the foundation for multiple internal container builds.
scopeIncludes: A backdoored internal base image discovered to have been used across several application teams' Dockerfiles
Propagation analysis identifying the scope of downstream images built from a single compromised base layer
scopeExcludes: The initial ingestion event of a malicious image from a public registry (route to ITID-62641)
Registry tag-overwrite poisoning of an otherwise-legitimate image (route to ITID-62643)
ITID-62642.severity: Critical given the multiplicative blast radius across every downstream image built from the compromised base.
ITID-62642.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of a compromised, widely reused base image.
ITID-62642.escalation: Escalate to all application teams identified as consumers of the affected base image; coordinate a fleet-wide rebuild.
indicators: Multiple unrelated application containers exhibiting the same anomalous behavior, traced to a shared base image layer
Image lineage/SBOM analysis revealing broad internal reuse of a flagged base image
vectors: Deploy Container using a compromised shared base image reused across the internal container build ecosystem
rootCauses: Lack of image lineage tracking to identify all downstream consumers of a given base image
No periodic re-scan of previously approved base images for newly disclosed compromise
controls: Container image lineage/SBOM tracking to identify all downstream consumers of a base image
Periodic re-scan of approved base images against updated threat intelligence
ITID-62642.detection: Moderate — requires image lineage tooling to efficiently scope; without it, identifying all affected downstream images is largely manual.
ITID-62642.response: Identify every downstream image built from the compromised base, rebuild each from a clean base image, and redeploy in coordinated fashion.
metrics: Number of downstream images traced to the compromised base
Time to fleet-wide rebuild completion
sops: Container Image Security Incident Response SOP
ITID-62642.notes: Sibling differentiator: this leaf is scoped to the propagation/reuse impact of an already-compromised base image, distinct from the initial ingestion event (ITID-62641).

playbook.name: Backdoored Base Image Used Across Multiple Internal Builds
playbook.description: A commonly-used internal base container image is found to contain a backdoor, propagating the compromise across every service built from it.

steps.title: Confirm the backdoor in the base image
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/finding and analyze the base image layers to confirm the presence and nature of the backdoor.
steps.guidance: Perform layer-by-layer image analysis to pinpoint where the malicious content was introduced.
steps.outcome: Confirmed backdoor and its introduction point in the base image build chain.

steps.title: Identify all downstream images/services built from the base image
steps.desc: Query the artifact registry/SBOM database for every image and service that inherits from the backdoored base image.

steps.title: Determine which downstream services are actively running the backdoored lineage
steps.desc: Cross-reference the dependency graph with running workloads to determine live exposure.
steps.outcome: Live exposure inventory documented across all clusters/environments.

steps.title: Halt builds using the backdoored base image
steps.desc: Immediately block the base image at the registry/build pipeline level to prevent further propagation.
steps.outcome: No new builds inherit the backdoor.

steps.title: Isolate or restrict running workloads on the backdoored lineage
steps.desc: Apply network policy restrictions or isolate running containers/pods built from the compromised base image pending remediation.
steps.outcome: Blast radius of active workloads contained.

steps.title: Rebuild a clean base image and cascade rebuilds
steps.desc: Rebuild the base image from a verified clean source, then trigger rebuilds of every downstream image and service.
steps.guidance: Coordinate a mass-rebuild campaign; prioritize internet-facing and privileged services first.
steps.outcome: All downstream services rebuilt on a clean base image.

steps.title: Verify no residual backdoor persists post-rebuild
steps.desc: Scan rebuilt images and running workloads to confirm complete removal of the backdoor.
steps.outcome: Confirmed clean across all rebuilt images and workloads.

steps.title: Redeploy clean workloads and validate
steps.desc: Redeploy all affected services on the clean base image lineage and validate functionality.
steps.outcome: All services operating normally on clean images.

steps.title: Establish base-image governance and provenance verification
steps.desc: Document the incident and formalize a centrally-managed, provenance-verified base-image program with mandatory periodic re-scanning.
steps.outcome: Base image governance program established with ongoing scanning requirements.

ITID-62643.def: An incident in which an adversary gained sufficient registry access to overwrite an existing, previously trusted container image tag with a malicious version, causing downstream pulls of that tag to silently receive attacker-controlled content.
ITID-62643.purpose: Captures poisoning of a container registry through overwriting a previously legitimate, trusted image tag with malicious content.
scopeIncludes: A mutable image tag (e.g., 'latest' or a pinned version tag) overwritten in a registry the organization pulls from
Registry access-control compromise enabling silent tag replacement without a corresponding new version number
scopeExcludes: Initial ingestion of a malicious image never previously trusted (route to ITID-62641)
Propagation of an already-compromised base image across internal builds (route to ITID-62642)
ITID-62643.severity: Critical — tag overwrite is designed to be silent, and pinned-tag consumers have no version-number signal that anything changed.
ITID-62643.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of any tag-overwrite event on a trusted registry.
ITID-62643.escalation: Escalate to DevOps/platform engineering and the registry operator immediately; freeze pulls from the affected registry.
indicators: Image digest/hash for a known tag changing without a corresponding version bump or release note
Registry audit log showing an unexpected push overwriting an existing tag
Immutable-tag policy violation alert from the registry platform
vectors: Deploy Container via a poisoned registry tag silently overwritten on a previously trusted image
rootCauses: Registry configured to allow mutable/overwritable tags rather than enforcing immutability
Lack of digest-pinning in deployment manifests, relying on mutable tags instead
controls: Registry tag immutability enforcement
Deployment manifests pinned to image digest rather than mutable tag
ITID-62643.detection: Moderate — digest-drift monitoring can catch this reliably where implemented, but many pipelines do not track digests independently of tags.
ITID-62643.response: Revert to the last known-good digest, enforce tag immutability, and audit all deployments that pulled the affected tag during the compromise window.
metrics: Number of deployments affected by the tag overwrite
Time to digest-drift detection
sops: Container Image Security Incident Response SOP
ITID-62643.notes: Sibling differentiator: this leaf is scoped to silent overwrite of a previously trusted tag, distinguishing it from first-time malicious ingestion (ITID-62641) and downstream base-image propagation (ITID-62642).

playbook.name: Container Image Registry Poisoning (Legitimate Tag Overwritten)
playbook.description: An attacker with unauthorized registry access overwrites a legitimate, trusted image tag with a malicious image, causing downstream pulls to retrieve the poisoned content.

steps.title: Detect the tag overwrite and confirm malicious content
steps.desc: Investigate an alert of an unexpected image digest change for a previously stable tag, and confirm the new image content is malicious.
steps.guidance: Compare current image digest against the historical/pinned digest recorded in deployment manifests or SBOM.
steps.outcome: Confirmed malicious overwrite of a legitimate tag.

steps.title: Determine unauthorized access vector to the registry
steps.desc: Determine how the attacker gained push access to overwrite the tag (compromised credentials, misconfigured registry permissions).

steps.title: Identify all deployments that pulled the poisoned tag
steps.desc: Determine which environments/clusters pulled the image after the overwrite occurred.
steps.outcome: Complete list of affected deployments and pull timestamps.

steps.title: Restore the legitimate image tag or remove the poisoned one
steps.desc: Revert the tag to point to the legitimate, known-good digest or remove the poisoned tag entirely.
steps.outcome: Registry tag no longer serves malicious content.

steps.title: Revoke the compromised push credentials
steps.desc: Revoke and reset the credentials/service account used to push the malicious overwrite.

steps.title: Redeploy affected workloads on the legitimate image
steps.desc: Force redeployment/restart of all workloads that pulled the poisoned tag so they run the restored legitimate image.
steps.outcome: All running workloads confirmed on legitimate image content.

steps.title: Enable immutable tags and digest pinning
steps.desc: Configure the registry to enforce immutable tags and require deployments to pin image digests rather than mutable tags.
steps.outcome: Registry configured to prevent future tag-overwrite attacks.

steps.title: Harden registry push permissions
steps.desc: Apply least-privilege, role-based push permissions to the registry, restricted to CI/CD service accounts only.

steps.title: Validate cluster integrity post-remediation
steps.desc: Confirm all workloads are running legitimate images and no residual malicious artifacts remain.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed fully restored and clean.

steps.title: Mandate digest pinning and image signing across the organization
steps.desc: Document the incident and require digest-pinning and cryptographic image signing (e.g., cosign) as a standard practice for all deployments.
steps.outcome: Image signing and pinning standard published and enforced.

ITID-62644.def: An incident involving a malicious container image whose specific mechanism (initial public-registry ingestion, internal base-image propagation, or registry tag overwrite) has not yet been determined.
ITID-62644.purpose: Intake leaf for a malicious container image incident not yet attributed to the initial-ingestion, base-image-propagation, or registry-tag-overwrite leaves in this group.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered malicious container image activity pending mechanism triage
scopeExcludes: Cases confirmed as initial ingestion (route to ITID-62641), base-image propagation (route to ITID-62642), or tag overwrite (route to ITID-62643)
ITID-62644.severity: High pending triage, consistent with the Malicious Container Images group generally.
ITID-62644.priority: P1 pending triage; downgrade once mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-62644.escalation: Escalate to DevOps/platform engineering for immediate containment while mechanism triage proceeds.
indicators: Malicious container activity detected, specific ingestion mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Deploy Container via an as-yet-uncharacterized malicious image compromise mechanism
rootCauses: Incomplete container image provenance tracking delaying mechanism determination
controls: Comprehensive container image provenance and scanning coverage across all registries in use
ITID-62644.detection: Varies by underlying mechanism; treat detection as inherited from whichever specific leaf the case is eventually triaged to.
ITID-62644.response: Contain the affected containers and triage to ITID-62641, ITID-62642, or ITID-62643 as soon as mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Time from detection to mechanism triage
sops: Container Image Security Incident Response SOP
ITID-62644.notes: Unclassified/general intake leaf for the Malicious Container Images group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Malicious Container Image
playbook.description: A general or unclassified incident involving a malicious container image that does not fit a more specific scenario.

steps.title: Confirm the malicious container image finding
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/report and confirm the container image contains malicious content or behavior.
steps.guidance: Use image scanning and runtime behavioral analysis.
steps.abort: If unconfirmed, close as false positive with documentation.

steps.title: Identify affected deployments
steps.desc: Determine all running containers/deployments using the malicious image across environments.

steps.title: Terminate affected containers
steps.desc: Stop and remove all running containers using the malicious image.

steps.title: Block the malicious image from redeployment
steps.desc: Add the image digest to a registry/admission-control deny-list.
steps.outcome: Malicious image blocked from future deployment.

steps.title: Deploy verified clean image
steps.desc: Replace the malicious image with a verified clean image and redeploy affected services.

steps.title: Validate cluster integrity
steps.desc: Confirm environment is free of residual malicious workloads and services are functioning normally.

steps.title: Strengthen container image scanning practices
steps.desc: Document the incident and reinforce mandatory image scanning and provenance verification in the deployment pipeline.

steps.title: Review broader image inventory for similar risk
steps.desc: Audit the broader container image inventory across the organization for similar risk patterns.
steps.outcome: Broader review completed and findings tracked.

ITID-62711.def: An incident in which a third-party application, granted OAuth authorization with an overly broad data-access scope, leaked or improperly exposed organizational data as a result of that excess permission rather than a direct attack.
ITID-62711.purpose: Captures data leakage from a third-party application caused by that application requesting or retaining an OAuth scope broader than its function requires.
scopeIncludes: A third-party productivity or analytics app leaking data it only had access to because of an unnecessarily broad OAuth scope grant
Vendor misconfiguration causing over-scoped data to be logged, cached, or exposed to unintended parties
scopeExcludes: Malicious OAuth abuse by an attacker (route to ITID-62521, Third-Party SaaS Application Exploits)
A vulnerability in the third-party app itself exposing data at rest, independent of OAuth scope (route to ITID-62712)
ITID-62711.severity: Medium-High depending on data sensitivity and volume exposed.
ITID-62711.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for regulated or high-volume data exposure.
ITID-62711.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal and the third-party app's business owner for scope reduction and vendor accountability.
indicators: OAuth scope audit revealing an app requesting far more data access than its stated function requires
Vendor breach notification tracing exposure to over-scoped access rather than a deliberate attack
vectors: Data from Information Repositories exposed as a byproduct of an over-permissioned OAuth integration
rootCauses: Lack of periodic OAuth scope review for installed third-party integrations
Third-party app onboarding without a least-privilege scope requirement
controls: Mandatory least-privilege OAuth scope review at third-party app onboarding
Periodic re-review and pruning of granted OAuth scopes
ITID-62711.detection: Weak as a proactive control absent scope auditing; typically discovered via vendor disclosure or a scheduled access review.
ITID-62711.response: Reduce the app's OAuth scope to the minimum required, assess data exposure, and notify affected parties as required.
metrics: Number of over-scoped third-party app integrations identified per review cycle
ITID-62711.notes: Sibling differentiator: excess-permission exposure (a governance/scope issue) rather than a direct application vulnerability, which is ITID-62712.

playbook.name: Third-Party App Over-Permissioned OAuth Scope Leaking Data
playbook.description: A third-party application is granted excessively broad OAuth scopes, resulting in unauthorized access to data beyond what the app's function requires.

steps.title: Identify the over-permissioned app and data exposure
steps.desc: Investigate the finding (audit, CASB alert, or incident report) confirming the third-party app holds OAuth scopes broader than necessary and has accessed data outside its functional need.
steps.guidance: Review the app's granted OAuth scopes against its stated purpose and actual API call history.
steps.outcome: Confirmed over-permissioning and scope of unnecessary data access.

steps.title: Determine what data was actually accessed under the excess scope
steps.desc: Review API access logs to determine what specific data the app accessed that fell outside its legitimate functional need.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of unnecessary data access/potential leakage.

steps.title: Revoke the app's OAuth access
steps.desc: Revoke the third-party app's OAuth grant/tokens to immediately stop further access.

steps.title: Re-authorize with least-privilege scopes
steps.desc: If the app is still needed, re-authorize it with the minimum necessary OAuth scopes for its actual function.
steps.outcome: App re-authorized under least-privilege scope, or removed if scope reduction is not supported.
steps.abort: If the vendor does not support granular scoping, evaluate replacing the app or accepting documented risk with compensating monitoring.

steps.title: Assess notification obligations for accessed data
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance to determine if the scope of data accessed triggers breach-notification obligations.
steps.outcome: Notification determination documented and executed if required.

steps.title: Restore app functionality under corrected scope
steps.desc: Confirm the app functions correctly under the reduced, least-privilege OAuth scope.
steps.outcome: App operating normally with appropriately scoped access.

steps.title: Implement OAuth scope review in third-party app approval process
steps.desc: Document the incident and require least-privilege OAuth scope review as a mandatory step in third-party app onboarding and periodic reassessment.
steps.outcome: Third-party app OAuth scope governance process implemented.

steps.title: Audit all existing third-party app grants for over-permissioning
steps.desc: Conduct a broader audit of all existing third-party OAuth grants for similarly excessive scopes.
steps.outcome: Broader audit completed and remediation tracked.

ITID-62712.def: An incident in which a security vulnerability in a third-party application — such as a misconfigured database, insecure storage bucket, or flawed access control — directly exposed customer data at rest.
ITID-62712.purpose: Captures data leakage caused by a security vulnerability in a third-party application exposing customer data at rest, independent of any OAuth scope issue.
scopeIncludes: A third-party vendor's insecurely configured cloud storage bucket exposing customer records
A vulnerability in a third-party application's data access layer exposing records to unauthenticated or under-authenticated requests
scopeExcludes: Data exposure caused by over-broad OAuth scope rather than a direct application vulnerability (route to ITID-62711)
Cross-tenant access issues in multi-tenant software specifically (route to ITID-62721)
ITID-62712.severity: High given direct exposure of data at rest, often at scale.
ITID-62712.priority: P1 if customer personal or regulated data is confirmed exposed; P2 for internal/non-sensitive data.
ITID-62712.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal immediately given likely customer notification and regulatory reporting obligations.
indicators: Security researcher or vendor disclosure of an exposed data store
Data appearing in an unauthorized location (paste site, dark web) traced to a specific vendor
Vendor breach notification confirming a data-at-rest exposure
vectors: Data from Cloud Storage exposed via a third-party vendor's misconfigured or vulnerable storage layer
rootCauses: Vendor storage configuration lacking access controls or encryption at rest
Lack of contractual security requirements/audits for vendors holding organizational data
controls: Contractual vendor security requirements including encryption at rest and access control audits
Regular third-party data-storage security assessments
ITID-62712.detection: Weak from the customer side alone; typically reliant on vendor disclosure, researcher reports, or dark-web monitoring.
ITID-62712.response: Confirm scope of data exposed, require vendor remediation, and initiate regulatory/customer notification as required.
metrics: Number of records exposed
Time to vendor remediation confirmation
ITID-62712.notes: Sibling differentiator: direct data-at-rest vulnerability exposure, distinct from OAuth over-permissioning (ITID-62711) and multi-tenant cross-tenant access (ITID-62721).

playbook.name: Third-Party App Vulnerability Exposing Customer Data at Rest
playbook.description: A vulnerability in a third-party application exposes customer data stored at rest (e.g., misconfigured storage, injection flaw, insufficient encryption) to unauthorized access.

steps.title: Confirm the vulnerability and exposure of data at rest
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/report and confirm the specific vulnerability in the third-party app that exposes stored customer data.
steps.guidance: Review vendor advisory, penetration test finding, or security researcher report for technical details.
steps.outcome: Confirmed vulnerability and exposure mechanism documented.

steps.title: Determine what data was accessible and for how long
steps.desc: Assess the classification, volume, and time window of customer data that was exposed via the vulnerability.
steps.guidance: Review application/storage access logs where available.
steps.outcome: Documented scope and duration of data exposure.

steps.title: Determine if unauthorized access actually occurred
steps.desc: Analyze available logs to distinguish between theoretical exposure and confirmed unauthorized access/exfiltration.
steps.outcome: Determined whether actual unauthorized access occurred, informing notification obligations.

steps.title: Restrict access to the vulnerable data store/feature
steps.desc: Apply immediate access restrictions (disable the vulnerable feature, restrict network access to the data store) to stop further exposure.

steps.title: Coordinate vendor patch or apply compensating encryption/access controls
steps.desc: Apply the vendor's fix for the vulnerability, or implement compensating controls (encryption at rest, access control tightening) if no immediate fix exists.

steps.title: Notify affected customers and regulators as required
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance to determine and execute breach notification obligations based on data classification and applicable regulations.
steps.outcome: Required notifications completed within regulatory timelines.
steps.abort: If notification thresholds are not met, document the determination.

steps.title: Restore normal operations and validate data protection
steps.desc: Confirm the application operates normally with data-at-rest protections verified in place.
steps.outcome: Application restored with confirmed data protection controls.

steps.title: Strengthen third-party data protection requirements
steps.desc: Document the incident and update vendor security requirements to mandate encryption at rest and periodic security assessment for any third-party app storing customer data.

ITID-62713.def: An incident involving data leakage from a third-party application whose specific mechanism (over-broad OAuth scope versus a direct data-at-rest vulnerability) has not yet been determined.
ITID-62713.purpose: Intake leaf for data leakage from a third-party app not yet attributed to the OAuth-scope or data-at-rest vulnerability leaves in this group.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered third-party app data leakage pending mechanism triage
scopeExcludes: Cases confirmed as OAuth over-permissioning (route to ITID-62711) or a data-at-rest vulnerability (route to ITID-62712)
ITID-62713.severity: High pending triage, consistent with the Data Leakage from Third-Party Apps group generally.
ITID-62713.priority: P1 pending triage; downgrade once mechanism and scope are confirmed.
ITID-62713.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal and the third-party app's business owner while mechanism triage proceeds.
indicators: Data leakage traced to a third-party app, specific mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Data from Information Repositories via an as-yet-uncharacterized third-party app leakage mechanism
rootCauses: Incomplete vendor access/architecture documentation delaying mechanism determination
controls: Vendor risk management program covering both access-scope and data-storage security review
ITID-62713.detection: Varies by underlying mechanism; treat detection as inherited from whichever specific leaf the case is eventually triaged to.
ITID-62713.response: Contain data exposure immediately and triage to ITID-62711 or ITID-62712 as soon as mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Time from detection to mechanism triage
ITID-62713.notes: Unclassified/general intake leaf for the Data Leakage from Third-Party Apps group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Data Leakage from Third-Party App
playbook.description: A general or unclassified incident involving data leakage from a third-party application that does not fit a more specific scenario.

steps.title: Confirm the data leakage and identify the source app
steps.desc: Investigate the report/alert of data leakage and identify which third-party app is the source.
steps.guidance: Review DLP alerts, CASB logs, or external report details.
steps.outcome: Confirmed leakage source and nature of the exposed data.

steps.title: Determine scope and sensitivity of leaked data
steps.desc: Quantify the volume and classification of data leaked.
steps.outcome: Scope and sensitivity of leaked data documented.

steps.title: Revoke or restrict the app's access
steps.desc: Revoke the app's access to organizational data or restrict its permissions to stop further leakage.

steps.title: Remediate the root cause of the leakage
steps.desc: Work with the vendor or internal configuration owner to remediate the specific cause of the leakage (misconfiguration, vulnerability, excessive permission).

steps.title: Assess and execute notification obligations
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on notification obligations to affected data subjects/regulators.
steps.abort: If not required, document the determination.

steps.title: Restore app access under corrected controls
steps.desc: Confirm the app operates under corrected access controls with no further leakage.

steps.title: Strengthen third-party app data-handling review
steps.desc: Document the incident and reinforce data-handling security review for third-party apps during vendor onboarding.

steps.title: Audit similar third-party apps for comparable risk
steps.desc: Review other third-party apps with similar data access for comparable leakage risk.
steps.outcome: Broader review completed and findings tracked.

ITID-62721.def: An incident in which a flaw in a multi-tenant third-party software platform's tenant-isolation mechanism allowed the organization's data to be accessed by, or the organization to inadvertently access, another customer's tenant environment.
ITID-62721.purpose: Captures a multi-tenant third-party software failure that allowed one customer/tenant to access another tenant's data.
scopeIncludes: A vendor's multi-tenant SaaS platform bug causing the organization's data to appear in another customer's account
The organization inadvertently gaining visibility into another tenant's data due to a vendor isolation failure
scopeExcludes: Data-at-rest exposure not related to tenant-isolation failure specifically (route to ITID-62712)
OAuth/API-driven data leakage not related to multi-tenancy (route to ITID-62711/62541)
ITID-62721.severity: High to Critical, since tenant-isolation failures can expose data bidirectionally and are systemic to the vendor's architecture.
ITID-62721.priority: P1 upon confirmation of any cross-tenant data exposure involving the organization's data.
ITID-62721.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal and the vendor's security team immediately; request full scope assessment of the isolation failure.
indicators: Vendor breach notification specifically describing a tenant-isolation failure
Organization's data discovered accessible from an unrelated tenant account
Vendor incident report referencing a multi-tenancy architecture defect
vectors: Trusted Relationship exploited via a multi-tenant vendor's failed isolation boundary between customer environments
rootCauses: Vendor multi-tenant architecture lacking robust per-tenant data isolation (e.g., shared database without row-level security)
Lack of independent vendor architecture security review prior to onboarding
controls: Contractual requirement for vendor multi-tenant isolation architecture review
Independent penetration testing focused on tenant-isolation boundaries for critical SaaS vendors
ITID-62721.detection: Weak from the customer side alone; almost always surfaced via vendor disclosure rather than customer-side telemetry.
ITID-62721.response: Demand full vendor scope assessment, determine what data was exposed to or from other tenants, and initiate notification processes as required.
metrics: Number of cross-tenant exposure incidents per vendor per year
ITID-62721.notes: This is the sole leaf in the Unauthorized Cross-Tenant Access group and is defined by the multi-tenancy isolation-failure mechanism specifically, distinguishing it from single-tenant data-at-rest or OAuth-driven leakage covered in sibling Tier-4 groups.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cross-Tenant Access (Third-Party Software Context)
playbook.description: A vulnerability or design flaw in a multi-tenant third-party software platform allows one tenant to access another tenant's data, largely outside the organization's direct remediation control.

steps.title: Confirm the cross-tenant access incident
steps.desc: Investigate the report/alert (from the vendor, security researcher, or internal detection) confirming unauthorized cross-tenant data access occurred within the shared SaaS platform.
steps.guidance: Correlate with the vendor's own incident notification where available.
steps.outcome: Confirmed cross-tenant access incident and its scope as it pertains to the organization's tenant.

steps.title: Determine what organizational data was exposed to or accessed by other tenants
steps.desc: Work with the vendor to determine exactly what data belonging to the organization's tenant was exposed, and conversely whether the organization's tenant accessed another tenant's data.
steps.outcome: Documented scope of data exposure in both directions.

steps.title: Obtain vendor's root-cause and remediation status
steps.desc: Request the vendor's technical root-cause analysis and status of their isolation-boundary fix, since remediation is largely outside the organization's direct control.
steps.guidance: Engage vendor's incident response/trust team formally.
steps.outcome: Documented vendor root-cause and remediation timeline.

steps.title: Request vendor isolate or suspend the affected functionality
steps.desc: Request the vendor immediately isolate or disable the specific feature/API responsible for the cross-tenant leak while their fix is developed.
steps.outcome: Vendor applies interim containment for the shared platform.
steps.abort: If the vendor cannot act quickly, evaluate temporarily limiting the organization's own use of the affected feature.

steps.title: Limit organizational exposure where possible
steps.desc: Where the organization has any configuration control, restrict data sharing or feature usage that increases cross-tenant exposure risk.
steps.outcome: Organizational exposure minimized within available control.

steps.title: Validate vendor's isolation-boundary fix
steps.desc: Obtain and review evidence (technical confirmation, third-party audit) that the vendor has fixed the tenant-isolation flaw.
steps.abort: If the vendor cannot demonstrate effective remediation, escalate to vendor management/legal for contractual remedy consideration.

steps.title: Resume normal use of the platform
steps.desc: Resume full use of the previously restricted feature/platform once vendor remediation is validated.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with confirmed tenant isolation restored.

steps.title: Update vendor risk assessment for multi-tenant isolation controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and incorporate tenant-isolation architecture review into ongoing third-party SaaS vendor risk assessments.
steps.outcome: Updated vendor risk assessment criteria published.

ITID-62731.def: An incident in which an adversary exploited a security vulnerability in a third-party file sharing or collaboration platform to gain unauthorized access to files or folders beyond what any legitimate sharing configuration intended.
ITID-62731.purpose: Captures exploitation of a vulnerability in a third-party file sharing platform to gain unauthorized access to shared content.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of an authentication or access-control vulnerability in a file sharing platform's core application
Exploitation of a platform bug allowing enumeration or brute-forcing of shared-file identifiers
scopeExcludes: Legitimate sharing-link permission logic being bypassed rather than a platform vulnerability being exploited (route to ITID-62732)
ERP/financial software exploits specifically (route to ITID-62741)
ITID-62731.severity: High if the platform holds sensitive corporate or customer files; Medium for low-sensitivity content.
ITID-62731.priority: P1 if bulk or sensitive-file exposure is confirmed; P2 otherwise.
ITID-62731.escalation: Escalate to the platform vendor and privacy/legal if sensitive data exposure is confirmed.
indicators: Vendor security bulletin describing a file sharing platform vulnerability
Anomalous bulk file access or download activity in platform audit logs
Files discovered exposed that were not intentionally shared externally
vectors: Data from Information Repositories accessed via a file sharing platform's own application vulnerability
rootCauses: Vendor platform vulnerability unpatched at the time of exploitation
Lack of monitoring for anomalous bulk-download activity on the platform
controls: Vendor patch management SLA for file sharing platform vulnerabilities
Bulk-download anomaly monitoring on file sharing platforms
ITID-62731.detection: Moderate — platform audit logs can reveal bulk access anomalies where actively monitored.
ITID-62731.response: Apply the vendor patch, audit access logs for the exposure window, and notify affected data owners.
metrics: Number of files exposed during the incident
Time to vendor patch application
detections: File sharing platform bulk-access anomaly monitoring
ITID-62731.notes: Sibling differentiator: this leaf covers exploitation of the platform's own application vulnerability, as opposed to permission-logic bypass on a legitimate sharing link (ITID-62732).

playbook.name: File Sharing Platform Vulnerability Exploited for Unauthorized Access
playbook.description: An attacker exploits a vulnerability in a third-party file-sharing platform to gain unauthorized access to shared organizational files.

steps.title: Confirm exploitation of the file-sharing platform vulnerability
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/report and confirm exploitation of a specific vulnerability in the file-sharing platform.
steps.guidance: Review vendor advisory and platform access logs for exploit indicators.

steps.title: Determine files/folders accessed
steps.desc: Identify which files, folders, and shared links were accessed or downloaded via the exploited vulnerability.
steps.outcome: Complete inventory of accessed content documented.

steps.title: Assess sensitivity of exposed content
steps.desc: Classify the sensitivity of the exposed files to inform notification and remediation priority.

steps.title: Restrict or disable the vulnerable platform feature
steps.desc: Disable the vulnerable feature/functionality or restrict platform access pending vendor fix.

steps.title: Revoke potentially compromised sharing links/sessions
steps.desc: Revoke any file-sharing links or sessions that may have been exploited or exposed.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized access via existing links/sessions terminated.

steps.title: Apply vendor patch and validate the fix
steps.desc: Apply the vendor's security patch for the platform vulnerability and validate it closes the exploit path.

steps.title: Notify affected data owners and regulators as required
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on notification obligations based on the classification of exposed files.
steps.abort: If not required, document the determination.

steps.title: Restore platform access and validate security
steps.desc: Restore normal file-sharing platform access and confirm the patched, secure state.
steps.outcome: Platform restored to normal, secure operation.

steps.title: Strengthen file-sharing platform security review
steps.desc: Document the incident and reinforce periodic security assessment and patch monitoring for the file-sharing platform.
steps.outcome: File-sharing platform security review process strengthened.

ITID-62732.def: An incident in which a flaw in a file sharing platform's link-permission logic allowed a party to access a shared file or folder beyond the access level, audience, or expiration the original sharer configured.
ITID-62732.purpose: Captures bypass of a file sharing link's intended permission scope, exposing content beyond what the sharer authorized.
scopeIncludes: A 'view only' sharing link that unexpectedly permitted download or edit access
A link scoped to a specific recipient list that was accessible to anyone with the URL
An expired sharing link that remained functional past its intended expiration
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a core platform vulnerability unrelated to link-permission logic specifically (route to ITID-62731)
Data exposure due to the sharer's own misconfiguration choice rather than a platform logic flaw (tracked under SaaS Misconfigurations, ITID-62511)
ITID-62732.severity: Medium-High depending on the sensitivity of content exposed via the bypassed link.
ITID-62732.priority: P2, escalating to P1 for sensitive or regulated content exposure.
ITID-62732.escalation: Escalate to the platform vendor for a permission-logic fix and to data owners for exposure assessment.
indicators: User report of unexpected access level on a shared link
Platform audit log showing access from parties outside the intended recipient scope
Security researcher disclosure of a sharing-link permission logic flaw
vectors: Data from Information Repositories accessed via a file sharing platform's link-permission logic flaw
rootCauses: Platform's link-permission enforcement implemented inconsistently across sharing methods
Lack of periodic audit of active sharing links against intended scope
controls: Periodic audit of active external sharing links against intended access scope
Vendor requirement for consistent, auditable link-permission enforcement
ITID-62732.detection: Moderate — link-access audit logging can reveal scope violations if actively reviewed; often discovered reactively via user report.
ITID-62732.response: Revoke the affected link, assess who accessed content beyond the intended scope, and request a platform fix from the vendor.
metrics: Number of sharing-link permission violations identified per audit cycle
ITID-62732.notes: Sibling differentiator: this leaf is scoped to link-permission logic bypass specifically, distinct from a core platform vulnerability (ITID-62731) or a sharer-caused misconfiguration (ITID-62511).

playbook.name: File Sharing Link Permission Bypass Vulnerability
playbook.description: A vulnerability in a file-sharing platform's link permission model allows unauthorized parties to access files intended to be restricted (e.g., link enumeration, expired-link reuse, permission scope bypass).

steps.title: Confirm the permission-bypass mechanism
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/report and confirm the specific technical mechanism allowing bypass of intended link permissions.
steps.guidance: Reproduce the bypass in a controlled test if feasible, or rely on vendor/researcher technical details.

steps.title: Identify all shared links potentially affected
steps.desc: Enumerate all active sharing links created by the organization that could be susceptible to the bypass technique.
steps.outcome: Complete inventory of at-risk shared links.

steps.title: Determine if unauthorized access via the bypass actually occurred
steps.desc: Review access logs on the identified links for evidence of access from unexpected/unauthorized parties.
steps.outcome: Confirmed whether actual unauthorized access occurred.

steps.title: Revoke or reissue at-risk sharing links
steps.desc: Revoke all identified at-risk sharing links and reissue with corrected permission settings where the content is still needed.
steps.outcome: At-risk links no longer accessible via the bypass technique.

steps.title: Coordinate vendor fix for the permission model flaw
steps.desc: Report the vulnerability to the vendor and track their fix for the underlying permission-model flaw.

steps.title: Notify affected data owners and regulators as required
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on notification obligations for any confirmed unauthorized access.
steps.abort: If not required, document the determination.

steps.title: Validate corrected permission enforcement
steps.desc: Confirm the platform correctly enforces link permissions post-fix.

steps.title: Implement periodic sharing-link audit
steps.desc: Document the incident and establish periodic auditing of active external sharing links for unintended over-exposure.

ITID-62733.def: An incident involving unauthorized file access through a third-party file sharing platform whose specific mechanism (core platform vulnerability versus link-permission bypass) has not yet been determined.
ITID-62733.purpose: Intake leaf for a third-party file sharing exploit not yet attributed to the platform-vulnerability or link-permission-bypass leaves in this group.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered file sharing exposure pending mechanism triage
scopeExcludes: Cases confirmed as a core platform vulnerability (route to ITID-62731) or link-permission bypass (route to ITID-62732)
ITID-62733.severity: Medium-High pending triage, consistent with the Third-Party File Sharing Exploits group generally.
ITID-62733.priority: P2 pending triage; escalate to P1 if sensitive data exposure is confirmed.
ITID-62733.escalation: Escalate to the platform vendor and data owners while mechanism triage proceeds.
indicators: Unauthorized file access via a third-party sharing platform, specific mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Data from Information Repositories via an as-yet-uncharacterized file sharing platform exposure
rootCauses: Incomplete platform access-log visibility delaying mechanism determination
controls: Comprehensive file sharing platform access-log retention and review
ITID-62733.detection: Varies by underlying mechanism; treat detection as inherited from whichever specific leaf the case is eventually triaged to.
ITID-62733.response: Contain exposure and triage to ITID-62731 or ITID-62732 as soon as mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Time from detection to mechanism triage
ITID-62733.notes: Unclassified/general intake leaf for the Third-Party File Sharing Exploits group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Third-Party File Sharing Exploit
playbook.description: A general or unclassified exploit involving a third-party file-sharing service that does not fit a more specific scenario.

steps.title: Confirm the exploit and identify affected content
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/report and confirm the nature of the exploit against the file-sharing service.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploit details and affected content identified.
steps.abort: If a specific known scenario applies, redirect to that specific playbook.

steps.title: Determine scope and sensitivity of exposed data
steps.desc: Assess what data was exposed or accessed and its sensitivity classification.

steps.title: Restrict access to affected content/feature
steps.desc: Disable the exploited feature or revoke access to affected shared content.

steps.title: Remediate the root cause
steps.desc: Apply the vendor fix or internal configuration change addressing the root cause of the exploit.

steps.title: Notify affected parties as required
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance on any required notifications.
steps.outcome: Notification determination made and executed if required.

steps.title: Restore service and validate security
steps.desc: Confirm the file-sharing service is restored to normal, secure operation.

steps.title: Strengthen file-sharing service security governance
steps.desc: Document the incident and reinforce security review requirements for third-party file-sharing services.

steps.title: Review other file-sharing usage for similar risk
steps.desc: Audit other file-sharing tools in use for similar risk exposure.

ITID-62741.def: An incident in which an adversary exploited a vulnerability or weakness in the core third-party ERP or financial software platform itself to gain unauthorized access to financial records, payroll data, or other sensitive business data.
ITID-62741.purpose: Captures unauthorized data access achieved through exploitation of third-party ERP or financial software, distinct from add-on/plugin-based ERP compromise tracked elsewhere.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a core ERP/financial platform vulnerability (not an add-on) to access general ledger, payroll, or vendor payment data
Unauthorized access to financial software achieved through a platform-level authentication or authorization flaw
scopeExcludes: Exploitation via a third-party ERP add-on/extension specifically (route to ITID-62431, a distinct Tier-4 group)
File sharing platform exploits (route to ITID-6273x)
ITID-62741.severity: High to Critical given the direct financial and regulatory exposure of compromised ERP/financial data.
ITID-62741.priority: P1 if financial fraud or bulk financial data exposure is confirmed; P2 otherwise.
ITID-62741.escalation: Escalate to finance leadership, internal audit, and privacy/legal immediately.
indicators: Anomalous financial transaction or ledger modification activity
ERP/financial platform audit log showing access inconsistent with the user's role
Vendor security bulletin describing a core platform vulnerability
vectors: Data from Information Repositories accessed via a core ERP/financial platform vulnerability
rootCauses: ERP/financial platform patch management lagging behind vendor releases
Lack of segregation-of-duties controls within the ERP/financial platform itself
controls: ERP/financial platform patch management SLA
Segregation-of-duties and anomaly monitoring within the financial platform
ITID-62741.detection: Moderate — financial platforms typically have audit trails, but anomaly detection maturity varies by organization.
ITID-62741.response: Apply the vendor patch, audit financial records for tampering, and coordinate with internal audit/finance on impact assessment.
metrics: Number of financial records accessed during the incident
Time to patch/remediation
ITID-62741.notes: This is the sole leaf in the ERP and Financial Software Exploits group under Unauthorized Data Access; scoped to core platform exploitation, distinct from add-on-based ERP compromise (ITID-62431) which sits under Third-Party Plugin and Extension Exploits.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General ERP/Financial Software Exploit (Data Access Context)
playbook.description: A general or unclassified exploit against a third-party ERP or financial software system resulting in unauthorized data access.

steps.title: Confirm the exploit and unauthorized data access
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/report and confirm unauthorized access to ERP/financial data via the exploited software.
steps.guidance: Review ERP/financial system audit logs for anomalous access or transaction patterns.
steps.outcome: Confirmed exploit and unauthorized data access.

steps.title: Determine scope of financial/business data accessed
steps.desc: Identify which financial records, transactions, or business data were accessed or modified.

steps.title: Assess for fraudulent transactions or data manipulation
steps.desc: Review for any fraudulent transactions, unauthorized payments, or manipulated financial records resulting from the access.
steps.guidance: Engage Internal Audit/Finance to reconcile affected records.
steps.outcome: Confirmed presence or absence of financial fraud/manipulation.

steps.title: Revoke unauthorized access and disable exploited functionality
steps.desc: Revoke the access used in the exploit and disable the vulnerable functionality/integration.

steps.title: Apply vendor patch or compensating controls
steps.desc: Apply the vendor's fix for the exploited vulnerability, or compensating access controls if no fix is yet available.

steps.title: Reconcile and correct affected financial records
steps.desc: Work with Finance to reconcile and correct any financial records affected by unauthorized access or manipulation.
steps.outcome: Financial records validated and corrected as needed.

steps.title: Restore ERP operations and validate integrity
steps.desc: Confirm ERP/financial system operates normally and data integrity is restored.
steps.outcome: System restored to normal, secure operation.

steps.title: Strengthen ERP/financial system access controls and monitoring
steps.desc: Document the incident and reinforce access control review and transaction-monitoring for the ERP/financial platform.
steps.outcome: Access control and monitoring standard strengthened.

ITID-62811.def: An incident in which an adversary used stolen or phished credentials to operate a legitimate, already-installed remote access software tool as their initial access or persistence mechanism, blending malicious activity with expected administrative tooling behavior.
ITID-62811.purpose: Captures use of legitimate remote monitoring and management (RMM) software — such as TeamViewer or AnyDesk — by an adversary who gained access via a stolen credential rather than exploiting the tool itself.
scopeIncludes: A stolen helpdesk or IT admin credential used to log into an already-deployed RMM tool and access endpoints
A phished user's credentials used to authorize an unexpected remote-access session via legitimate software
scopeExcludes: Exploitation of a vulnerability in the remote access software itself, independent of credential theft (route to ITID-62812)
Malware bundled with or disguised as a legitimate installer (route to ITID-62821)
ITID-62811.severity: High — RMM tool abuse is a well-documented, high-value technique for both initial access and persistence, and frequently evades traditional malware detection.
ITID-62811.priority: P1 upon confirmation of any unauthorized RMM session using valid credentials.
ITID-62811.escalation: Escalate to identity/IAM and endpoint security immediately for credential reset and RMM session termination.
indicators: RMM tool session initiated outside normal administrative hours or from an unrecognized source IP
RMM software installed or activated on an endpoint with no corresponding change ticket
EDR alert on RMM tool process behavior inconsistent with typical administrative use
vectors: Remote Access Software used by an adversary operating under a stolen or phished valid credential
rootCauses: Lack of MFA on RMM tool administrative accounts
No allow-list restricting which RMM tools are approved for use in the environment
controls: Mandatory MFA on all RMM administrative accounts
Allow-listing of approved RMM tools with alerting on any unapproved RMM software installation
ITID-62811.detection: Strong where EDR and RMM-tool-specific behavioral baselining are in place; weak where RMM traffic is treated as inherently trusted.
ITID-62811.response: Terminate the unauthorized session, reset the compromised credential, and audit all activity performed during the session.
metrics: Number of unauthorized RMM sessions detected per quarter
Time to session termination after detection
sops: Remote Access Software Abuse Response SOP
ITID-62811.notes: T1219 Remote Access Software is a precise, well-established ATT&CK technique for this scenario. No RMM-abuse leaves exist elsewhere in the taxonomy outside this Tier-4 group, confirmed via taxonomy search prior to authoring.

playbook.name: Legitimate Remote Access Software (TeamViewer/AnyDesk) Used by Attacker via Stolen Credential
playbook.description: An attacker uses stolen credentials to log into legitimate remote-access software (e.g., TeamViewer, AnyDesk) already installed in the environment to gain unauthorized remote control.

steps.title: Detect anomalous remote-access tool usage
steps.desc: Investigate alerts of unusual login times, geolocations, or session patterns for the remote-access software, and confirm unauthorized use.
steps.guidance: Review the remote-access tool's own connection logs and correlate with user's normal working patterns/location.
steps.outcome: Confirmed unauthorized use of the legitimate remote-access tool via stolen credentials.
steps.abort: If the activity is explained by legitimate user behavior, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine attacker actions taken during the session
steps.desc: Review session recordings/logs (if available) and endpoint telemetry for actions taken by the attacker during the remote session.
steps.outcome: Full scope of attacker actions during the session documented.

steps.title: Identify the credential compromise source
steps.desc: Determine how the credentials were stolen (phishing, credential stuffing, malware) to inform broader remediation.

steps.title: Terminate the active remote session and disable the account
steps.desc: Immediately terminate the attacker's active remote-access session and disable/lock the compromised account.

steps.title: Isolate the accessed endpoint
steps.desc: Apply EDR network isolation to the endpoint that was remotely accessed pending forensic review.

steps.title: Reset the compromised credentials and enforce MFA
steps.desc: Force a full credential reset for the affected user and enforce MFA on the remote-access tool going forward.

steps.title: Remove any malware/persistence installed during the session
steps.desc: Scan and remediate the accessed endpoint for any malware or persistence mechanisms installed by the attacker.
steps.outcome: Endpoint confirmed clean of attacker artifacts.

steps.title: Restore endpoint and account to normal use
steps.desc: Return the endpoint and account to normal operation with confirmed clean status.

steps.title: Restrict and monitor remote-access tool usage
steps.desc: Document the incident and implement application allowlisting to restrict unauthorized/unmanaged remote-access tools, plus enhanced monitoring for approved ones.
steps.guidance: Include user-awareness training on credential hygiene as a lessons-learned control.
steps.outcome: Remote-access tool governance and monitoring strengthened; user awareness training delivered.

ITID-62812.def: An incident in which an adversary exploited a software vulnerability in a remote access or RMM tool to gain unauthorized access, bypassing the need for valid credentials.
ITID-62812.purpose: Captures exploitation of a security vulnerability in a remote access software tool itself, as distinct from credential-based abuse of an already-legitimate session.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of an authentication-bypass vulnerability in an RMM tool's server or agent component
Exploitation of a remote code execution flaw in a remote access tool's client software
scopeExcludes: Use of a valid stolen credential to operate an unmodified RMM tool (route to ITID-62811)
Malware distributed disguised as a legitimate remote access installer (route to ITID-62821)
ITID-62812.severity: Critical if the vulnerability allows authentication bypass or remote code execution against the RMM infrastructure itself.
ITID-62812.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmation of exploitation.
ITID-62812.escalation: Escalate to vendor and endpoint security immediately; isolate affected RMM infrastructure.
indicators: Exploit attempt matching a known CVE in the RMM tool's server or agent
Unexpected administrative access to the RMM management console without corresponding valid login
Vendor security bulletin describing an actively exploited RMM vulnerability
vectors: Remote Access Software exploited via a vulnerability in the tool itself rather than credential theft
rootCauses: RMM tool not patched to the vendor's latest secure version
RMM management console exposed to the internet without additional access restriction
controls: RMM tool patch management SLA
Network restriction of RMM management console access to trusted networks only
ITID-62812.detection: Strong for known CVEs with published signatures; weaker for novel exploitation of RMM tool logic.
ITID-62812.response: Patch the vulnerable RMM tool immediately, audit for unauthorized access during the exposure window, and rotate all RMM-related credentials as a precaution.
metrics: Time to patch after CVE disclosure
Number of unauthorized sessions during the exposure window
sops: Remote Access Software Abuse Response SOP
ITID-62812.notes: Sibling differentiator: exploitation of the RMM tool's own vulnerability, as opposed to credential-based abuse of a functioning, unmodified tool (ITID-62811).

playbook.name: Remote Access Software Vulnerability Exploited for Unauthorized Access
playbook.description: An attacker exploits a software vulnerability in remote-access software (rather than stolen credentials) to gain unauthorized access to systems.

steps.title: Confirm exploitation of the remote-access software vulnerability
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/report and confirm exploitation of a specific vulnerability in the remote-access software (rather than credential theft).
steps.guidance: Check vendor security advisory for the specific CVE and exploit indicators.

steps.title: Determine affected systems and post-exploitation activity
steps.desc: Identify all systems running the vulnerable remote-access software and assess for post-exploitation activity.
