steps.outcome: Full scope of affected systems and impact documented.

steps.title: Isolate affected systems and disable the vulnerable service
steps.desc: Network-isolate affected systems and disable the vulnerable remote-access service/feature.
steps.outcome: Exploitation vector halted and systems contained.

steps.title: Apply virtual patch/firewall rule as interim mitigation
steps.desc: Block the specific exploit traffic pattern at the firewall/IPS while awaiting the vendor patch.
steps.outcome: Exploit attempts blocked at the perimeter.

steps.title: Apply the vendor security patch
steps.desc: Apply the vendor's patch for the vulnerability across all affected systems.
steps.abort: If no patch is yet available, escalate to zero-day handling and maintain compensating controls.

steps.title: Remove any persistence installed via the exploit
steps.desc: Remove backdoors, unauthorized accounts, or persistence mechanisms established during exploitation.
steps.outcome: Systems confirmed clean of attacker artifacts.

steps.title: Restore service and validate
steps.desc: Restore the remote-access service and confirm patched, secure operation.

steps.title: Strengthen remote-access software patch management
steps.desc: Document the incident and reinforce patch-compliance monitoring and application allowlisting for remote-access tools.
steps.outcome: Patch management and allowlisting policy strengthened.

ITID-62813.def: An incident involving unauthorized use of remote access software whose specific mechanism (stolen-credential abuse versus exploitation of the tool's own vulnerability) has not yet been determined.
ITID-62813.purpose: Intake leaf for a remote access software exploitation incident not yet attributed to the credential-abuse or tool-vulnerability leaves in this group.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered RMM tool abuse pending mechanism triage
scopeExcludes: Cases confirmed as credential-based abuse (route to ITID-62811) or tool vulnerability exploitation (route to ITID-62812)
ITID-62813.severity: High pending triage, consistent with the Remote Access Software Exploits group generally.
ITID-62813.priority: P1 pending triage; downgrade once mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-62813.escalation: Escalate to endpoint security for immediate session containment while mechanism triage proceeds.
indicators: Unauthorized RMM tool activity detected, specific mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Remote Access Software abused via an as-yet-uncharacterized mechanism
rootCauses: Incomplete session/access logging delaying mechanism determination
controls: Comprehensive RMM tool session and access logging
ITID-62813.detection: Varies by underlying mechanism; treat detection as inherited from whichever specific leaf the case is eventually triaged to.
ITID-62813.response: Terminate the unauthorized session and triage to ITID-62811 or ITID-62812 as soon as mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Time from detection to mechanism triage
sops: Remote Access Software Abuse Response SOP
ITID-62813.notes: Unclassified/general intake leaf for the Remote Access Software Exploits group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Remote Access Software Exploit
playbook.description: A general or unclassified incident involving exploitation or abuse of remote-access software that does not fit a more specific scenario.

steps.title: Investigate and classify the remote-access incident
steps.desc: Triage the alert/report and determine the nature of the remote-access software incident (credential abuse, vulnerability exploitation, or other misuse).
steps.guidance: Review remote-access tool logs and EDR telemetry.
steps.abort: If a specific known scenario applies, redirect to that specific playbook.

steps.title: Determine scope of unauthorized access
steps.desc: Identify affected systems, accounts, and any data or actions taken during unauthorized access.

steps.title: Terminate unauthorized sessions and disable affected accounts/tools
steps.desc: Terminate any active unauthorized sessions and disable the abused account or remote-access tool instance.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoints
steps.desc: Apply network isolation to affected endpoints pending investigation.

steps.title: Remediate the root cause
steps.desc: Reset compromised credentials, patch vulnerabilities, or remove unauthorized tool installations as applicable to the root cause.

steps.title: Restore normal operations and validate
steps.desc: Confirm affected systems and accounts are restored to normal, secure operation.

steps.title: Strengthen remote-access tool governance
steps.desc: Document the incident and reinforce application allowlisting, MFA enforcement, and monitoring for all remote-access tools.

steps.title: User awareness training on remote-access tool risks
steps.desc: Deliver user-awareness training addressing safe use and risks of remote-access software.

ITID-62821.def: An incident in which an adversary tampered with a legitimate software installer such that malicious code was bundled or embedded within it, and the tampered installer was then distributed via the vendor's official website or app store rather than an unofficial third-party source.
ITID-62821.purpose: Captures cases where a trojanized version of a legitimate software installer was distributed through the vendor's own official distribution channel.
scopeIncludes: A trojanized installer downloaded directly from the vendor's own official website
A malicious app store listing using the legitimate vendor's branding and official distribution mechanism
scopeExcludes: Malware bundled with freeware/utility software from an unofficial or third-party download aggregator (route to ITID-62822)
Malicious code injected into the vendor's build pipeline as the root cause, tracked under Software Supply Chain Attacks (route to ITID-62121)
ITID-62821.severity: High to Critical given exploitation of the trust users place in an official distribution channel.
ITID-62821.priority: P1 while the trojanized installer remains available on the official channel.
ITID-62821.escalation: Escalate to the vendor and endpoint security immediately; identify all users who downloaded the installer during the compromise window.
indicators: Installer hash mismatch against the vendor's published checksum
EDR alert triggered immediately following installation from an official-channel download
Vendor confirmation of a compromised installer on their official distribution point
vectors: Malicious File delivered via a trojanized installer distributed through the vendor's own official channel
rootCauses: Vendor's official download infrastructure compromised without the vendor's awareness
Lack of installer hash/signature verification by end users prior to execution
controls: Endpoint-enforced installer hash/signature verification prior to execution
Vendor download infrastructure integrity monitoring
ITID-62821.detection: Moderate — EDR post-install behavioral alerting and hash verification can catch this, though initial download typically evades signature-based tools.
ITID-62821.response: Remove the trojanized installer, isolate and remediate affected hosts, and notify all users who downloaded it during the exposure window.
metrics: Number of hosts that installed the trojanized version
Time to vendor takedown of the compromised installer
ITID-62821.notes: Sibling differentiator: official-channel distribution of a trojanized legitimate installer, distinct from unofficial-channel freeware bundling (ITID-62822).

playbook.name: Trojanized Legitimate Software Installer Distributed via Official Channel
playbook.description: A trojanized version of a legitimate software installer is distributed through the vendor's official download channel, infecting users who download it in good faith.

steps.title: Confirm the installer is trojanized and identify affected hosts
steps.desc: Investigate EDR/AV alerts following installation of the software and confirm the installer's hash does not match the vendor's official published hash.
steps.guidance: Compare downloaded installer hash against vendor-published checksums; check threat intel for public disclosure of the trojanized distribution.
steps.outcome: Confirmed trojanized installer and list of hosts that executed it.

steps.title: Analyze the trojan payload and capability
steps.desc: Reverse-engineer or sandbox-analyze the malicious payload embedded in the installer to determine its capability.

steps.title: Determine post-infection activity
steps.desc: Investigate for lateral movement, data exfiltration, or persistence established after the trojan executed.

steps.title: Isolate infected hosts
steps.desc: Apply EDR network isolation to all hosts confirmed to have executed the trojanized installer.

steps.title: Block further downloads of the trojanized installer
steps.desc: Block the malicious download URL/hash at the web proxy and notify users not to install the affected software until cleared.
steps.outcome: No further users infected via the same distribution.

steps.title: Remove malware and reimage as needed
steps.desc: Remove the trojan and any secondary payloads from affected hosts, reimaging where full extent of compromise cannot be assured.

steps.title: Install verified clean version of the software
steps.desc: Once the vendor confirms remediation of their distribution channel, reinstall the software from a verified clean source.
steps.guidance: Validate hash/signature before reinstalling.
steps.outcome: Legitimate, clean software installed where needed.

steps.title: Restore affected hosts and monitor
steps.desc: Return hosts to normal operation and monitor closely for recurrence of malicious behavior.
steps.outcome: Hosts fully operational and confirmed clean.

steps.title: Implement installer hash verification and allowlisting
steps.desc: Document the incident and require hash/signature verification before installing third-party software, plus application allowlisting where feasible.
steps.outcome: Installer verification and allowlisting policy implemented.

ITID-62822.def: An incident in which a user downloaded legitimate freeware or utility software from an unofficial or third-party aggregator site that had bundled additional malicious code with the installer.
ITID-62822.purpose: Captures malware distributed bundled alongside legitimate freeware or utility software, typically via unofficial download aggregators rather than the software's own official channel.
scopeIncludes: Malware bundled by a third-party download aggregator alongside a legitimate freeware utility
A 'free download' site wrapping a legitimate installer in a malicious installer wrapper
scopeExcludes: A trojanized installer distributed through the software vendor's own official channel (route to ITID-62821)
Fake meeting-invite or scheduling-tool social engineering (route to ITID-6283x)
ITID-62822.severity: Medium-High depending on the payload delivered alongside the freeware.
ITID-62822.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the bundled payload includes ransomware or credential-stealing malware.
ITID-62822.escalation: Escalate to endpoint security for immediate isolation and to end-user awareness teams to curb repeat behavior.
indicators: EDR alert on a secondary process spawned immediately after a freeware installation
User download history showing retrieval from an unofficial aggregator rather than the vendor's own site
Antivirus/EDR detection of a known bundler or potentially unwanted program (PUP) alongside the freeware
vectors: Malicious File delivered via a bundled installer from an unofficial freeware/utility download source
rootCauses: Lack of an application allow-list restricting software installation to approved sources
User awareness gap regarding risks of unofficial download aggregators
controls: Application allow-listing restricting installs to approved vendors/sources
User awareness training on risks of unofficial download aggregators
ITID-62822.detection: Moderate — antivirus/EDR commonly flags known bundlers and PUPs, though novel bundled payloads may evade initial detection.
ITID-62822.response: Remove the bundled malware, restore or reimage the affected host if persistence is confirmed, and reinforce approved-source software installation policy.
metrics: Number of bundled-malware incidents per quarter
Time to host remediation
ITID-62822.notes: Sibling differentiator: unofficial-channel bundling of malware with legitimate freeware, distinct from official-channel installer tampering (ITID-62821).

playbook.name: Malware Bundled with Legitimate Freeware/Utility Software
playbook.description: A user downloads and installs legitimate freeware or a utility tool that has malware bundled with it (adware, PUP, or more serious malware) as part of its installer.

steps.title: Detect the bundled malware and identify affected hosts
steps.desc: Investigate EDR/AV alerts following installation of the freeware and confirm bundled malware/PUP presence.
steps.guidance: Review installer contents/behavior via sandbox or endpoint telemetry.
steps.outcome: Confirmed bundled malware and list of affected hosts.

steps.title: Determine how the freeware was obtained
steps.desc: Identify the download source and whether it was via an approved channel or an unauthorized/unmanaged software download.
steps.outcome: Download source and policy compliance status documented.

steps.title: Assess payload behavior and impact
steps.desc: Determine the bundled malware's capability (adware, credential theft, more serious payload) and impact on the host.

steps.title: Isolate affected hosts
steps.desc: Apply EDR containment to hosts with confirmed bundled malware.

steps.title: Remove the malware/PUP and the freeware if necessary
steps.desc: Clean the malware/PUP from affected hosts, removing the freeware application entirely if it cannot be safely separated from the bundled payload.
steps.outcome: Hosts confirmed clean of bundled malware.

steps.title: Enforce software installation policy controls
steps.desc: Apply or reinforce application allowlisting/software restriction policy preventing installation of unapproved freeware/utilities.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized software installation blocked going forward.

steps.title: Restore hosts and validate
steps.desc: Return affected hosts to normal operation and confirm clean status.
steps.outcome: Hosts fully operational and confirmed clean.

steps.title: User awareness training on unauthorized software downloads
steps.desc: Document the incident and deliver user-awareness training on the risks of downloading unapproved freeware/utility software.
steps.outcome: Awareness training delivered and software policy reinforced.

ITID-62823.def: An incident involving malware distributed alongside otherwise-legitimate software whose specific distribution channel (official vendor channel versus unofficial aggregator) has not yet been determined.
ITID-62823.purpose: Intake leaf for a malware-distribution-via-legitimate-software incident not yet attributed to the official-channel-trojanization or unofficial-bundling leaves in this group.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered malware-via-legitimate-software incident pending channel triage
scopeExcludes: Cases confirmed as official-channel trojanization (route to ITID-62821) or unofficial-channel bundling (route to ITID-62822)
ITID-62823.severity: Medium-High pending triage, consistent with the Malware Distribution via Legitimate Software group generally.
ITID-62823.priority: P2 pending triage; escalate to P1 if a destructive or credential-stealing payload is confirmed.
ITID-62823.escalation: Escalate to endpoint security for immediate containment while channel triage proceeds.
indicators: Malware execution traced to a legitimate-appearing software installation, specific channel not yet determined
vectors: Malicious File delivered via an as-yet-uncharacterized legitimate-software distribution channel
rootCauses: Incomplete download/installation provenance logging delaying channel determination
controls: Endpoint download provenance logging to support rapid channel triage
ITID-62823.detection: Varies by underlying channel; treat detection as inherited from whichever specific leaf the case is eventually triaged to.
ITID-62823.response: Contain the affected host and triage to ITID-62821 or ITID-62822 as soon as channel is confirmed.
metrics: Time from detection to channel triage
ITID-62823.notes: Unclassified/general intake leaf for the Malware Distribution via Legitimate Software group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Malware Distribution via Legitimate Software
playbook.description: A general or unclassified incident involving malware distributed through otherwise legitimate third-party software that does not fit a more specific scenario.

steps.title: Confirm malware distribution via the legitimate software
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/report and confirm the specific legitimate software vector used to distribute malware.
steps.outcome: Confirmed distribution vector and malware presence.
steps.abort: If a specific known scenario applies (trojanized installer, bundled freeware), redirect to that specific playbook.

steps.title: Determine affected hosts and impact
steps.desc: Identify all affected hosts and assess the malware's impact and capability.

steps.title: Isolate affected hosts
steps.desc: Apply EDR containment to affected hosts.

steps.title: Block further distribution
steps.desc: Block the distribution source/URL at the web proxy or email gateway.

steps.title: Remove malware from affected hosts
steps.desc: Clean or reimage affected hosts as necessary based on severity.

steps.title: Restore hosts and validate
steps.desc: Return affected hosts to normal operation and confirm clean status.
steps.outcome: Hosts fully operational and confirmed clean.

steps.title: Strengthen software download and installation controls
steps.desc: Document the incident and reinforce application allowlisting and software approval processes.

steps.title: User awareness training
steps.desc: Deliver user-awareness training on safe software download practices.

ITID-62831.def: An incident in which an adversary sent a fraudulent meeting invitation impersonating a legitimate video-conferencing tool (such as Zoom or Microsoft Teams) containing a link to a credential-harvesting page.
ITID-62831.purpose: Captures phishing attacks that impersonate a legitimate video-conferencing platform's meeting-invite format specifically to harvest credentials.
scopeIncludes: A fake Zoom/Teams meeting-invite email or calendar entry linking to a spoofed login page
A fraudulent 'join meeting' link embedded in an otherwise plausible business email thread
scopeExcludes: Fake calendar/scheduling-tool invites not specifically impersonating a video-conferencing platform (route to ITID-62832)
Vulnerable CRM system exploitation (route to ITID-62841)
ITID-62831.severity: Medium-High depending on the seniority/access level of the targeted user and whether credentials were successfully harvested.
ITID-62831.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if credentials were entered and the account was subsequently used maliciously.
ITID-62831.escalation: Escalate to identity/IAM for immediate credential reset if any user reports entering credentials.
indicators: Email/calendar invite with a sender domain not matching the legitimate video-conferencing vendor
User report of a suspicious meeting-invite link requesting login credentials
URL/domain reputation flag on the meeting-invite link
vectors: Phishing via a spoofed video-conferencing meeting invite leading to credential harvesting
rootCauses: Email security controls not flagging spoofed vendor-branded invite domains
Lack of user awareness training specific to meeting-invite phishing patterns
controls: Email security filtering tuned for spoofed video-conferencing vendor domains
User awareness training on meeting-invite phishing patterns
ITID-62831.detection: Moderate — email security gateways with domain-reputation and brand-impersonation detection can catch many cases; targeted/novel domains may evade filtering.
ITID-62831.response: Reset credentials for any user who submitted them, block the malicious domain, and notify all recipients of the phishing campaign.
metrics: Number of users who clicked/entered credentials per campaign
Time to domain block after detection
ITID-62831.notes: Sibling differentiator: impersonation of a video-conferencing platform specifically, versus general calendar/scheduling-tool impersonation (ITID-62832).

playbook.name: Fake Meeting Invite (Zoom/Teams) Link Used for Credential Phishing
playbook.description: An attacker sends a fake meeting invite mimicking a legitimate video conferencing tool (Zoom, Teams) to lure users into entering credentials on a phishing page.

steps.title: Confirm the phishing campaign and identify targeted users
steps.desc: Investigate reported phishing emails/messages and confirm the fake meeting invite lure, identifying all users who received it.
steps.guidance: Review email gateway logs for the phishing campaign's sender/URL indicators.
steps.outcome: Confirmed phishing campaign and full list of targeted recipients.

steps.title: Identify users who clicked the link or entered credentials
steps.desc: Determine which users clicked the malicious link and, more critically, which entered credentials on the phishing page.
steps.guidance: Review proxy/URL-click logs and any available phishing-page analytics.
steps.outcome: List of users who clicked and/or submitted credentials.

steps.title: Assess for account compromise following credential entry
steps.desc: Check for suspicious login activity on affected accounts following the phishing incident.
steps.outcome: Determined whether any accounts show signs of compromise.

steps.title: Block the phishing domain/URL and remove emails from mailboxes
steps.desc: Block the malicious domain at the web proxy/email gateway and retroactively remove the phishing email from all recipient mailboxes.
steps.outcome: Phishing threat neutralized across the environment.

steps.title: Force password reset and session revocation for affected users
steps.desc: Force credential reset and terminate active sessions for all users who entered credentials on the phishing page.

steps.title: Remediate any confirmed account compromise
steps.desc: Investigate and remediate any confirmed unauthorized account access resulting from the phishing (e.g., mailbox rules, forwarding, data access).
steps.outcome: All confirmed compromised accounts fully remediated.
steps.abort: If no compromise occurred beyond credential entry, mark not applicable.

steps.title: Restore normal access for affected users
steps.desc: Confirm affected users have normal, secure access restored with MFA enforced.
steps.outcome: Users restored to normal, secure access.

steps.title: User awareness training on meeting-invite phishing
steps.desc: Document the incident and deliver targeted phishing-awareness training addressing fake meeting-invite lures, plus reinforce email authentication (DMARC/DKIM/SPF) controls.
steps.outcome: Awareness training delivered and email authentication controls reviewed.

ITID-62832.def: An incident in which an adversary sent a fraudulent calendar or scheduling-tool invitation (such as a fake Calendly or Outlook scheduling link) to deliver a phishing link or malicious payload to the recipient.
ITID-62832.purpose: Captures phishing attacks that impersonate a calendar or meeting-scheduling tool (distinct from a video-conferencing platform) to deliver a malicious link or payload.
scopeIncludes: A fake scheduling-tool booking confirmation email containing a credential-harvesting or malware-delivery link
A spoofed calendar invite from a scheduling platform not impersonating a video-conferencing brand specifically
scopeExcludes: Fake video-conferencing meeting invites specifically (route to ITID-62831)
Vulnerable CRM system exploitation (route to ITID-62841)
ITID-62832.severity: Medium-High depending on the seniority/access level of the targeted user and payload delivered.
ITID-62832.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if malware execution or credential compromise is confirmed.
ITID-62832.escalation: Escalate to identity/IAM or endpoint security depending on whether the payload was credential-harvesting or malware.
indicators: Scheduling-tool notification with a sender domain not matching the legitimate platform
User report of an unexpected scheduling confirmation containing a suspicious link
URL/domain reputation flag on the scheduling-tool link
vectors: Phishing via a spoofed calendar/scheduling-tool invite leading to credential harvesting or malware delivery
rootCauses: Email security controls not tuned to detect spoofed scheduling-tool domains
Lack of user awareness training specific to scheduling-tool phishing patterns
controls: Email security filtering tuned for spoofed scheduling-tool domains
User awareness training on scheduling-tool phishing patterns
ITID-62832.detection: Moderate — similar to video-conferencing phishing, dependent on brand-impersonation detection maturity.
ITID-62832.response: Reset credentials or remediate affected hosts as applicable, block the malicious domain, and notify all recipients.
metrics: Number of users who clicked per campaign
Time to domain block after detection
ITID-62832.notes: Sibling differentiator: impersonation of a calendar/scheduling tool distinct from a video-conferencing platform brand (ITID-62831).

playbook.name: Fake Calendar/Scheduling Tool Invite Used as Phishing Vector
playbook.description: An attacker sends a fake calendar or scheduling-tool (e.g., Calendly) invite as a phishing vector to lure users into clicking malicious links or entering credentials.

steps.title: Confirm the phishing campaign and identify targeted users
steps.desc: Investigate reported phishing calendar invites and confirm the malicious lure, identifying all targeted users.
steps.guidance: Review email gateway/calendar system logs for the campaign's indicators.
steps.outcome: Confirmed phishing campaign and target list.

steps.title: Identify users who interacted with the malicious invite
steps.desc: Determine which users accepted the invite, clicked embedded links, or entered credentials.

steps.title: Assess for account compromise
steps.desc: Check for suspicious login activity on affected accounts following the phishing interaction.
steps.outcome: Determined whether any accounts show signs of compromise.

steps.title: Remove the malicious invite and block the phishing domain
steps.desc: Remove the phishing calendar invite from affected calendars/mailboxes and block the malicious domain.

steps.title: Force password reset for affected users
steps.desc: Force credential reset and session revocation for users who entered credentials.

steps.title: Remediate any confirmed account compromise
steps.desc: Investigate and remediate any confirmed unauthorized account access resulting from the phishing.
steps.abort: If no compromise occurred, mark not applicable.

steps.title: Restore normal access for affected users
steps.desc: Confirm affected users have normal, secure access restored with MFA enforced.
steps.outcome: Users restored to normal, secure access.

steps.title: User awareness training on scheduling-tool phishing
steps.desc: Document the incident and deliver targeted awareness training addressing fake calendar/scheduling-invite lures.

ITID-62833.def: An incident involving social engineering conducted through impersonation of a third-party productivity or collaboration tool whose specific type (video-conferencing versus scheduling tool) has not yet been determined.
ITID-62833.purpose: Intake leaf for social engineering via a third-party tool not yet attributed to the video-conferencing or scheduling-tool impersonation leaves in this group.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered third-party-tool impersonation phishing pending tool-type triage
scopeExcludes: Cases confirmed as video-conferencing impersonation (route to ITID-62831) or scheduling-tool impersonation (route to ITID-62832)
ITID-62833.severity: Medium-High pending triage, consistent with the Social Engineering via Third-Party Tools group generally.
ITID-62833.priority: P2 pending triage; escalate to P1 if credential or malware compromise is confirmed.
ITID-62833.escalation: Escalate to identity/IAM or endpoint security while tool-type triage proceeds.
indicators: Third-party-tool-impersonation phishing detected, specific tool type not yet determined
vectors: Phishing via an as-yet-uncharacterized third-party tool impersonation
rootCauses: Incomplete email header/domain analysis delaying tool-type determination
controls: Email security filtering with brand-impersonation detection across common third-party tools
ITID-62833.detection: Varies by underlying tool type; treat detection as inherited from whichever specific leaf the case is eventually triaged to.
ITID-62833.response: Contain the exposure and triage to ITID-62831 or ITID-62832 as soon as tool type is confirmed.
metrics: Time from detection to tool-type triage
ITID-62833.notes: Unclassified/general intake leaf for the Social Engineering via Third-Party Tools group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Social Engineering via Third-Party Tool
playbook.description: A general or unclassified social-engineering incident that abuses a legitimate third-party tool as its vector, not fitting a more specific scenario.

steps.title: Confirm the social-engineering vector and campaign
steps.desc: Investigate the report/alert and confirm the specific third-party tool abused as the social-engineering vector.
steps.abort: If a specific known scenario applies, redirect to that specific playbook.

steps.title: Identify targeted and affected users
steps.desc: Determine which users were targeted and which interacted with the malicious content.

steps.title: Block the malicious content/domain
steps.desc: Block the malicious link/domain and remove the offending content from affected systems.

steps.title: Reset credentials for affected users
steps.desc: Force credential reset for users who may have been compromised.
steps.abort: If no credential entry occurred, mark not applicable.

steps.title: Remediate any confirmed compromise
steps.desc: Investigate and remediate any confirmed unauthorized access resulting from the social-engineering attempt.

steps.title: Restore normal access and validate
steps.desc: Confirm affected users/systems are restored to normal, secure state.

steps.title: User awareness training
steps.desc: Document the incident and deliver targeted user-awareness training addressing the specific social-engineering technique observed.

steps.title: Review email/tool authentication controls
steps.desc: Review and strengthen email authentication and third-party tool integration controls to reduce spoofing risk.

ITID-62841.def: An incident in which an adversary exploited a vulnerability in the core third-party CRM platform itself to gain unauthorized initial access to the organization's environment or customer data.
ITID-62841.purpose: Captures exploitation of a vulnerability in a third-party customer relationship management (CRM) system used directly as an initial-access vector, distinct from marketplace-app-based CRM compromise tracked elsewhere.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a core CRM platform authentication or authorization vulnerability to gain unauthorized system access
A vulnerable CRM login portal exploited as the entry point for broader account or data compromise
scopeExcludes: Compromise via a CRM marketplace app/extension specifically (route to ITID-62432, a distinct Tier-4 group)
Social engineering via calendar/video-conferencing tools (route to ITID-6283x)
ITID-62841.severity: High given CRM systems typically hold sensitive customer and sales data central to business operations.
ITID-62841.priority: P1 if the exploited vulnerability grants broad customer data access; P2 for limited-scope exposure.
ITID-62841.escalation: Escalate to the CRM vendor and privacy/legal if customer data exposure is confirmed.
indicators: Exploit attempt matching a known CVE in the CRM platform's login or API layer
Anomalous administrative access or bulk export activity in CRM audit logs
Vendor security bulletin describing a core CRM platform vulnerability
vectors: Exploit Public-Facing Application against a vulnerable core CRM platform used as an initial-access vector
rootCauses: CRM platform patch management lagging behind vendor security releases
Lack of monitoring for anomalous bulk-export activity within the CRM
controls: CRM platform patch management SLA
Bulk-export anomaly monitoring within the CRM platform
ITID-62841.detection: Moderate — CRM audit logs and vulnerability scanning provide coverage where actively monitored.
ITID-62841.response: Apply the vendor patch, audit access logs for the exposure window, and notify affected customers as required.
metrics: Number of customer records exposed
Time to patch after CVE disclosure
ITID-62841.notes: This is the sole leaf in the Vulnerable CRM System group under Initial Access; scoped to core CRM platform exploitation as an entry vector, distinct from marketplace-app-based CRM compromise (ITID-62432) which sits under Third-Party Plugin and Extension Exploits.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Vulnerable CRM System
playbook.description: A general or unclassified vulnerability in a customer relationship management (CRM) system is exploited or discovered, creating a foothold for initial access.

steps.title: Confirm the CRM vulnerability and any exploitation
steps.desc: Investigate the alert/report and confirm the specific vulnerability in the CRM system, and whether it has been exploited.
steps.guidance: Review vendor advisory and CRM access/audit logs for exploit indicators.
steps.outcome: Confirmed vulnerability details and exploitation status.

steps.title: Determine scope of access gained
steps.desc: If exploited, determine what access or data the attacker obtained via the CRM vulnerability, including any use as a pivot for further access.

steps.title: Restrict access to the vulnerable CRM functionality
steps.desc: Disable or restrict the vulnerable feature/endpoint pending remediation.

steps.title: Isolate any pivoted internal access
steps.desc: If the CRM vulnerability was used to pivot to internal systems, isolate the affected internal systems.
steps.abort: If no pivot occurred, mark not applicable.

steps.title: Apply vendor patch and remove attacker artifacts
steps.desc: Apply the vendor's fix for the vulnerability and remove any backdoors/unauthorized accounts created via the exploit.
steps.outcome: Vulnerability remediated and CRM system confirmed clean.

steps.title: Restore CRM operations and validate
steps.desc: Confirm the CRM system operates normally and is confirmed patched and clean.
steps.outcome: CRM system fully restored and secure.

steps.title: Strengthen CRM patch management and monitoring
steps.desc: Document the incident and reinforce patch-compliance monitoring and vulnerability scanning for the CRM system.
steps.outcome: CRM security monitoring and patch process strengthened.

steps.title: Review CRM as an initial-access risk in vendor risk assessment
steps.desc: Incorporate the CRM system's exposure as an initial-access vector into the broader third-party vendor risk assessment.

ITID-62911.def: A governance finding, not a technical security incident, in which the organization is found to have failed to establish or maintain an ongoing security-monitoring process for a third-party software vendor, leaving vendor-side risk unassessed over time.
ITID-62911.purpose: Tracks organizational governance failures where the organization did not maintain ongoing security monitoring of a third-party software vendor it relies on.
scopeIncludes: Audit finding that no periodic vendor security assessment has been performed for a critical software vendor
Absence of a process to track and act on vendor security advisories or breach notifications
scopeExcludes: A specific vendor's failure to meet an agreed security standard, which is itself the finding (route to ITID-62921)
Any specific technical incident that resulted from the monitoring gap (route to the relevant technical leaf in this Tier-2 category)
ITID-62911.severity: Low from a direct-technical standpoint; Medium-High as a risk-management/governance finding given the exposure it represents.
ITID-62911.priority: P3 for SOC tracking; actual remediation priority set by vendor risk management/GRC.
ITID-62911.escalation: Escalate to vendor risk management and GRC for process remediation; SOC role is limited to logging and cross-referencing.
indicators: Internal audit or GRC review finding no vendor security monitoring cadence in place
Vendor breach notification received with no prior tracking of that vendor's security posture
vectors: Third-party software component's security posture never re-assessed after initial integration, missing newly disclosed vulnerabilities
No subscription to vendor security advisories or CVE feeds for embedded third-party software
rootCauses: No formal third-party risk management (TPRM) program covering ongoing vendor monitoring
Vendor inventory incomplete or not tied to a risk-tiering process
mitreTechniques: T1195.001 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Dependencies and Development Tools
controls: Formal third-party risk management (TPRM) program with periodic vendor security review
Vendor security advisory intake and tracking process
ITID-62911.detection: Not a technical detection surface — findings originate from GRC/audit review, not security telemetry.
ITID-62911.response: SOC logs the finding and hands off to vendor risk management/GRC; no containment action expected.
metrics: Number of critical vendors without an active security-monitoring cadence
ITID-62911.notes: Vendor software governance/compliance issue — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Failure to Monitor Third-Party Software Security
playbook.description: An internal or external review discovers that the organization has failed to maintain adequate security monitoring over a third-party software product, representing a governance gap rather than a specific attacker-driven incident.

steps.title: Confirm the monitoring gap finding
steps.desc: Compliance/Security Governance reviews the audit or assessment finding confirming inadequate monitoring coverage for the specific third-party software.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the finding against the vendor risk management/security monitoring inventory.
steps.outcome: Confirmed monitoring gap and its scope documented.
steps.abort: If monitoring is confirmed adequate and the finding is inaccurate, close with documentation.
steps.tool: Vendor Risk Register / SIEM Coverage Inventory

steps.title: Assess actual risk exposure resulting from the gap
steps.desc: Determine whether the lack of monitoring allowed any undetected security events to occur during the gap period.
steps.guidance: Retrospectively review any available logs for missed indicators.
steps.outcome: Documented assessment of any undetected risk exposure.

steps.title: Legal/Compliance risk and regulatory obligation review
steps.desc: Legal/Compliance assess whether the monitoring gap constitutes a regulatory compliance failure (e.g., under contractual or regulatory security-monitoring obligations).
steps.guidance: This is a governance finding — frame the response around remediation and control improvement, not attacker response.

steps.title: Implement interim monitoring coverage
steps.desc: Stand up interim/manual monitoring for the third-party software while a permanent monitoring integration is implemented.

steps.title: Implement permanent security monitoring integration
steps.desc: Integrate the third-party software's logs/telemetry into the organization's SIEM/monitoring stack on a permanent basis.
steps.outcome: Permanent monitoring integration implemented and validated.

steps.title: Validate monitoring coverage and close the gap
steps.desc: Confirm the new monitoring integration provides adequate coverage and generates expected alerts under test conditions.

steps.title: Update vendor onboarding to require monitoring integration
steps.desc: Document the finding and require security-monitoring integration as a mandatory step in future third-party software onboarding.
steps.outcome: Vendor onboarding checklist updated with monitoring requirement.

steps.title: Audit remaining third-party software inventory for similar gaps
steps.desc: Review the broader third-party software inventory for similar monitoring coverage gaps.
steps.outcome: Broader monitoring coverage audit completed and remediation tracked.

ITID-62921.def: A governance finding, not a technical security incident, in which a specific third-party software vendor is found to be non-compliant with a contractually required or industry-standard security control or certification.
ITID-62921.purpose: Tracks findings that a specific third-party software vendor failed to meet an agreed-upon or industry-standard security requirement.
scopeIncludes: A vendor's SOC 2/ISO 27001 certification lapsing or failing to renew as contractually required
A vendor audit revealing a security control gap relative to the organization's vendor security requirements
scopeExcludes: The organization's own failure to monitor vendor security posture as a general governance gap (route to ITID-62911)
Any specific technical incident resulting from the vendor's non-compliance (route to the relevant technical leaf in this Tier-2 category)
ITID-62921.severity: Low from a direct-technical standpoint; Medium-High as a vendor risk/compliance finding given potential contractual and regulatory exposure.
ITID-62921.priority: P3 for SOC tracking; actual remediation priority set by vendor risk management/GRC.
ITID-62921.escalation: Escalate to vendor risk management, procurement, and legal for contractual remediation or vendor replacement consideration.
indicators: Vendor's compliance certification (SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS) found lapsed or revoked
Vendor audit response revealing a security control gap against contractual requirements
vectors: Third-party software vendor failed to meet an agreed security standard governing the software's development or maintenance
No contractual mechanism requiring the software vendor to demonstrate ongoing standards compliance
rootCauses: Vendor contracts lacking enforceable security compliance requirements or audit rights
Lack of periodic re-verification of vendor compliance certifications
controls: Contractual security compliance requirements with periodic re-verification
Vendor security certification tracking as part of the TPRM program
ITID-62921.detection: Not a technical detection surface — findings originate from vendor audits and compliance tracking, not security telemetry.
ITID-62921.response: SOC logs the finding and hands off to vendor risk management/GRC; no containment action expected.
metrics: Number of vendors found non-compliant per review cycle
ITID-62921.notes: Vendor software governance/compliance issue — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Vendor Non-Compliance with Security Standards (Third-Party Software Context)
playbook.description: A vendor is found to be non-compliant with contractually or regulatorily required security standards for their third-party software product, a governance/compliance matter led by Legal and vendor management.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor non-compliance finding
steps.desc: Vendor Management/Compliance reviews the audit, certification lapse, or assessment finding confirming the vendor's non-compliance with required security standards (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001, contractual security addendum).
steps.guidance: Cross-reference against the vendor's contractual security requirements and most recent compliance attestation.
steps.outcome: Confirmed non-compliance finding and specific standard(s) violated.
steps.abort: If the finding is inaccurate or the vendor has since remediated, close with documentation.

steps.title: Assess risk exposure from the vendor's non-compliance
steps.desc: Determine what organizational data or systems are exposed to risk as a result of the vendor's non-compliant security posture.

steps.title: Legal/contract review of remediation and remedy options
steps.desc: Legal and Vendor Management review the contract for remediation clauses, right-to-audit provisions, and potential remedies (penalties, termination rights).
steps.guidance: This is a governance/compliance matter led by Legal and Vendor Management, not a technical incident response.
steps.outcome: Documented contractual remediation path and any applicable remedies.

steps.title: Restrict data/access shared with the non-compliant vendor pending remediation
steps.desc: Where feasible, limit data sharing or system access with the vendor until compliance is restored.
steps.outcome: Organizational exposure to the vendor's non-compliance minimized.
steps.abort: If restricting access is not operationally feasible, document risk acceptance with executive sign-off.

steps.title: Require and track vendor remediation plan
steps.desc: Formally require the vendor to submit and execute a remediation plan to achieve compliance, with defined milestones and deadlines.
steps.outcome: Vendor remediation plan obtained and tracked to completion.

steps.title: Validate vendor compliance restoration
steps.desc: Obtain updated compliance attestation or independent verification that the vendor has achieved the required security standard.
steps.abort: If the vendor cannot achieve compliance within an acceptable timeframe, escalate to consider vendor replacement.

steps.title: Strengthen ongoing vendor compliance monitoring
steps.desc: Document the finding and implement periodic re-verification of vendor security compliance attestations rather than one-time onboarding checks.
steps.outcome: Ongoing vendor compliance monitoring process implemented.

steps.title: Review comparable vendors for similar compliance gaps
steps.desc: Assess other vendors with similar contractual security obligations for comparable compliance risk.
steps.outcome: Broader vendor compliance review completed and findings tracked.

ITID-62931.def: An incident in which a third-party vendor's software is found to contain undisclosed telemetry or data-collection functionality that transmits organizational or customer data to the vendor or a third party without authorization or disclosure.
ITID-62931.purpose: Captures discovery that a third-party vendor's software collects and transmits data that was never disclosed to the organization, representing a genuine covert data-collection technique rather than a mere governance gap.
scopeIncludes: Network traffic analysis revealing undisclosed outbound telemetry from a vendor application to an unexpected destination
Vendor software found collecting data categories (keystrokes, screen content, file metadata) never disclosed in its privacy documentation
scopeExcludes: A deliberate, vendor-installed covert backdoor granting the vendor direct remote access (route to ITID-62932)
General vendor non-compliance with a security standard absent any covert data collection (route to ITID-62921)
ITID-62931.severity: High given the genuine covert-collection mechanism represents an active, ongoing data-exfiltration technique regardless of vendor intent.
ITID-62931.priority: P1 upon confirmation of undisclosed data collection actively transmitting organizational data.
ITID-62931.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal, vendor management, and the SOC for network-level containment while the vendor relationship is reassessed.
indicators: Network/DLP monitoring revealing undisclosed outbound data flows from vendor software
Independent security research or teardown analysis disclosing hidden telemetry functionality
Vendor privacy policy found materially inconsistent with the software's actual observed data-collection behavior
vectors: Automated Collection performed covertly by vendor software beyond its disclosed functionality
rootCauses: Lack of network traffic analysis/DLP monitoring of vendor software's outbound behavior
Vendor security review process not including independent behavioral/traffic analysis prior to deployment
controls: Network traffic analysis and DLP monitoring of vendor software's outbound data flows
Independent behavioral/traffic analysis as part of vendor security onboarding review
ITID-62931.detection: Moderate — network/DLP monitoring can reveal undisclosed outbound flows where actively deployed; often first surfaced by independent security researchers.
ITID-62931.response: Block the undisclosed data flow, demand vendor disclosure and remediation, and reassess the vendor relationship for continued use.
metrics: Volume/duration of undisclosed data transmitted before detection
Time to network-level block after discovery
ITID-62931.notes: This leaf describes a genuine deliberate technical data-collection mechanism, so it carries a real ATT&CK mapping unlike most of this Tier-3 group's governance-only leaves. Sibling differentiator versus ITID-62932: undisclosed passive/active data collection, as opposed to a direct remote-access backdoor for the vendor's own use.

playbook.name: Vendor Software Found to Contain Undisclosed Data Collection/Telemetry
playbook.description: Vendor software in use is discovered to collect and transmit telemetry or usage data beyond what was disclosed in its documentation or privacy terms, raising privacy and contractual compliance concerns.

steps.title: Confirm the undisclosed data collection
steps.desc: Investigate the finding (network traffic analysis, security researcher report, or audit) confirming the software transmits data beyond its disclosed scope.
steps.guidance: Perform network traffic capture/analysis of the software's outbound communications to characterize the undisclosed telemetry.
steps.outcome: Confirmed undisclosed data collection and its content/destination.
steps.abort: If the data collection is in fact disclosed in terms the organization had accepted, close with documentation.

steps.title: Determine what data was collected and where it was sent
steps.desc: Classify the type and sensitivity of data collected (telemetry only vs. potentially sensitive business/customer data) and identify the destination(s).
steps.outcome: Documented data classification and destination for the undisclosed collection.

steps.title: Legal/Privacy/Compliance risk assessment
steps.desc: Legal, Privacy, and Compliance teams assess regulatory (e.g., GDPR/CCPA) and contractual exposure from the undisclosed data collection.
steps.guidance: Frame this as a privacy/compliance governance matter led by Legal/Privacy, not a technical attacker-driven incident.
steps.outcome: Documented legal/privacy risk assessment and required actions.

steps.title: Restrict or disable the undisclosed telemetry where technically possible
steps.desc: Apply available configuration options to disable the telemetry feature, or restrict network access to the collection endpoint.
steps.outcome: Undisclosed data collection halted or minimized.
steps.abort: If no technical control exists to disable telemetry, escalate to vendor contract enforcement.

steps.title: Formally engage the vendor for disclosure correction or contract remedy
steps.desc: Legal/Vendor Management formally engage the vendor to require disclosure correction, contractual remedy, or removal of the undisclosed collection capability.
steps.outcome: Vendor response and remediation commitment obtained.
steps.abort: If the vendor is unresponsive or non-compliant, escalate toward vendor replacement/termination consideration.

steps.title: Notify affected data subjects/regulators as required
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance to determine and execute any required notifications to data subjects or regulators.
steps.outcome: Required notifications completed within regulatory timelines.
steps.abort: If notification thresholds are not met, document the determination.

steps.title: Validate remediation and resume use if appropriate
steps.desc: Confirm the undisclosed data collection has been disabled or the vendor has corrected disclosure/contractual terms before resuming full use.
steps.outcome: Confirmed remediation and appropriate resumption decision documented.

steps.title: Strengthen vendor privacy/data-handling due diligence
steps.desc: Document the incident and require periodic technical verification (e.g., network traffic review) of vendor data-handling practices, not just contractual attestation.

ITID-62932.def: An incident in which a third-party vendor's software is found to contain an undisclosed backdoor providing the vendor (or a party acting on the vendor's behalf) covert remote access to the organization's systems or data, independent of any legitimate support or maintenance access agreement.
ITID-62932.purpose: Captures discovery that a third-party vendor deliberately built a covert remote-access mechanism into its software for the vendor's own use, without customer disclosure or authorization.
scopeIncludes: A vendor support/maintenance mechanism found to grant access far beyond what was disclosed or contractually authorized
Discovery of hardcoded vendor credentials or a hidden administrative interface providing undisclosed remote access
scopeExcludes: Undisclosed data-collection/telemetry without a direct remote-access mechanism (route to ITID-62931)
A third party (non-vendor attacker) exploiting a vulnerability to gain backdoor-like access, tracked under the relevant technical leaf elsewhere in this Tier-2 category
ITID-62932.severity: Critical — a vendor-controlled covert backdoor represents standing, deliberate unauthorized access at the vendor's discretion.
ITID-62932.escalation: Escalate to executive leadership, legal, and privacy immediately; treat as an active compromise pending vendor relationship review.
indicators: Discovery of hardcoded credentials or an undocumented administrative interface in vendor software
Network monitoring revealing remote access sessions initiated by the vendor without a corresponding support request
Independent security research disclosing a covert access mechanism in the vendor's product
vectors: Compromise Software Supply Chain via a deliberately embedded, vendor-controlled covert access mechanism
rootCauses: Lack of independent security testing/reverse engineering of vendor software prior to deployment
Vendor contract lacking explicit prohibition and audit rights against undisclosed remote-access mechanisms
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Independent security testing/reverse engineering of critical vendor software prior to deployment
Contractual prohibition and audit rights against undisclosed vendor remote-access mechanisms
ITID-62932.detection: Weak — by design, a vendor-controlled covert backdoor is built to evade standard detection; typically surfaced via independent security research or whistleblower disclosure.
ITID-62932.response: Isolate affected systems from the vendor's access path immediately, terminate the vendor relationship pending investigation, and notify regulators/customers as required.
metrics: Time to access-path isolation after discovery
Scope of systems/data exposed to the covert access mechanism
ITID-62932.notes: This leaf describes a deliberate genuine technical backdoor and carries a real ATT&CK mapping, unlike most of this Tier-3 group's governance-only leaves. Sibling differentiator versus ITID-62931: direct covert remote-access capability for the vendor's own use, rather than passive/active undisclosed data collection.

playbook.name: Vendor Software Found to Contain Covert Backdoor Access for Vendor's Own Use
playbook.description: Vendor software in use is discovered to contain a deliberate covert backdoor maintained by the vendor for its own access, raising severe security, contractual, and legal exposure beyond an attacker-driven compromise.

steps.title: Confirm the vendor-maintained backdoor
steps.desc: Investigate the finding (security research, reverse engineering, or disclosure) confirming the software contains a deliberate access mechanism controlled by the vendor rather than an external attacker.
steps.guidance: Perform independent technical verification (code/binary analysis, network traffic review) to confirm the backdoor and rule out third-party attacker compromise.
steps.outcome: Confirmed vendor-controlled backdoor and its access capability documented.
steps.abort: If analysis instead reveals an external attacker compromise rather than vendor-controlled access, redirect to standard technical IR.

steps.title: Determine what access/data the backdoor exposes
steps.desc: Assess the scope of access and data the vendor's backdoor provides, and whether it has been exercised.
steps.outcome: Documented backdoor capability and any evidence of use.

steps.title: Legal/Compliance/security leadership risk assessment
steps.desc: Legal, Compliance, and security leadership jointly assess the severity of this finding, given it represents a fundamental breach of vendor trust and contractual obligations rather than a typical attacker incident.
steps.guidance: Frame the response around vendor trust, contract, and legal exposure rather than standard technical containment alone.
steps.outcome: Documented executive-level risk assessment and response strategy.

steps.title: Isolate or disable the software's backdoor access path
steps.desc: Apply network-level blocking of the backdoor's communication channel or disable the software entirely if the backdoor cannot be isolated.
steps.abort: If the backdoor cannot be technically isolated without disabling the software, escalate the decision to remove the software to leadership.

steps.title: Rotate credentials/secrets potentially exposed to the vendor via the backdoor
steps.desc: Rotate any credentials, keys, or sensitive data that may have been accessible through the backdoor.

steps.title: Formally engage the vendor and pursue contractual/legal remedy
steps.desc: Legal formally engages the vendor demanding explanation, removal of the backdoor, and pursues contractual remedies (termination, damages) as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Formal vendor engagement and legal remedy process initiated.

steps.title: Replace or remove the affected software
steps.desc: Given the severity of a vendor-controlled backdoor, plan and execute removal/replacement of the software with a trusted alternative.
steps.outcome: Affected software removed or replaced across the environment.

steps.title: Notify affected stakeholders, customers, and regulators as required
steps.desc: Coordinate with Legal/Compliance to determine and execute notification obligations to affected customers, partners, and regulators.
steps.outcome: Required notifications completed within regulatory timelines.

steps.title: Validate environment is free of the vendor's backdoor access
steps.desc: Confirm the software has been removed/replaced and no residual backdoor access remains.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed free of the vendor-controlled backdoor.

steps.title: Overhaul vendor security due diligence and right-to-audit practices
steps.desc: Document the incident and mandate independent security testing (including reverse engineering/binary analysis where appropriate) and contractual right-to-audit clauses for future critical vendor software.
steps.outcome: Vendor due-diligence and audit rights standard strengthened.

ITID-62933.def: An incident involving suspected hidden telemetry or spyware functionality in third-party vendor software whose specific mechanism (undisclosed data collection versus a deliberate covert remote-access backdoor) has not yet been determined.
ITID-62933.purpose: Intake leaf for a hidden telemetry or spyware finding not yet attributed to the undisclosed-data-collection or covert-backdoor leaves in this group.
scopeIncludes: Newly discovered suspicious vendor software behavior pending mechanism triage
scopeExcludes: Cases confirmed as undisclosed data collection/telemetry (route to ITID-62931) or a covert remote-access backdoor (route to ITID-62932)
ITID-62933.severity: High pending triage given both sibling mechanisms carry a real, deliberate technical exploitation surface.
ITID-62933.priority: P1 pending triage; downgrade only if triage determines a lower-severity mechanism.
ITID-62933.escalation: Escalate to privacy/legal and the SOC for network-level containment while mechanism triage proceeds.
indicators: Suspicious vendor software behavior detected, specific mechanism not yet determined
vectors: Automated Collection or Compromise Software Supply Chain, pending confirmation of the specific mechanism
rootCauses: Incomplete network/behavioral analysis delaying mechanism determination
controls: Network traffic analysis and independent behavioral review of vendor software
ITID-62933.detection: Varies by underlying mechanism; treat detection as inherited from whichever specific leaf the case is eventually triaged to.
ITID-62933.response: Contain the suspicious data flow/access and triage to ITID-62931 or ITID-62932 as soon as mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Time from detection to mechanism triage
ITID-62933.notes: Unclassified/general intake leaf for the Third-Party Software with Hidden Telemetry or Spyware group. Unlike most Tier-3 governance-only leaves in this category, both specific sibling leaves carry real ATT&CK mappings, so this intake leaf does as well pending triage.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Hidden Telemetry or Spyware in Third-Party Software
playbook.description: A general or unclassified finding of hidden telemetry or spyware-like behavior in third-party software that does not fit a more specific scenario.

steps.title: Confirm the hidden telemetry/spyware finding
steps.desc: Investigate the finding and confirm the software exhibits undisclosed data collection or spyware-like behavior.
steps.guidance: Perform network traffic analysis or review third-party security research on the software.
steps.abort: If unconfirmed, close as false positive with documentation.

steps.title: Determine data collected and risk exposure
steps.desc: Classify the type and sensitivity of data collected and assess privacy/security risk exposure.
steps.outcome: Documented data classification and risk exposure.

steps.title: Legal/Privacy/Compliance assessment
steps.desc: Legal, Privacy, and Compliance assess regulatory and contractual exposure from the finding.
steps.guidance: Frame as a privacy/compliance governance matter.
steps.outcome: Documented risk assessment and required actions.

steps.title: Restrict or disable the identified data collection
steps.desc: Apply available configuration controls to disable the telemetry, or restrict network access to the collection endpoint.

steps.title: Engage the vendor for correction or contract remedy
steps.desc: Legal/Vendor Management formally engage the vendor to require correction or contractual remedy.
steps.outcome: Vendor response and remediation commitment obtained.

steps.title: Validate remediation and resume use if appropriate
steps.desc: Confirm remediation before resuming full use of the software.
steps.outcome: Confirmed remediation and resumption decision documented.

steps.title: Strengthen vendor data-handling due diligence
steps.desc: Document the incident and require periodic technical verification of vendor data-handling practices.

steps.title: Audit similar third-party software for comparable risk
steps.desc: Review comparable third-party software for similar undisclosed data-collection risk.
steps.outcome: Broader review completed and findings tracked.

ITID-62941.def: A legal risk finding, not a technical security incident, in which the organization becomes the subject of class action litigation as a downstream consequence of a data breach originating in a third-party software vendor's environment or product.
ITID-62941.purpose: Tracks class action litigation filed against the organization following a data breach caused by a third-party software vendor.
scopeIncludes: A filed or threatened class action lawsuit naming the organization following a vendor-caused breach affecting the organization's customers
Legal discovery requests received in connection with vendor-caused breach litigation
scopeExcludes: The underlying technical breach event itself, which is tracked under the relevant technical leaf elsewhere in this Tier-2 category
A regulatory fine (as opposed to civil litigation) imposed for the same underlying event (route to ITID-62942)
ITID-62941.severity: Low from a direct-technical standpoint; High as a legal/financial risk finding given potential litigation costs and reputational impact.
ITID-62941.priority: P3 for SOC tracking; actual priority and response owned by legal counsel.
ITID-62941.escalation: Escalate to legal counsel and executive leadership immediately upon notice of litigation.
indicators: Legal notice or court filing naming the organization in connection with a vendor-caused breach
Plaintiff's counsel outreach referencing a specific vendor security incident
vectors: Vendor-caused data breach exposed customer data, resulting in class action litigation naming the organization as a co-defendant
Contractual indemnification/liability allocation for vendor breaches was absent or insufficient
rootCauses: Underlying vendor-caused data breach with insufficient contractual liability allocation to the vendor
Lack of cyber liability insurance coverage adequate for vendor-caused breach exposure
controls: Contractual liability allocation and indemnification clauses with third-party vendors
Cyber liability insurance coverage review for vendor-caused breach exposure
ITID-62941.detection: Not a technical detection surface — findings originate from legal notices and litigation filings, not security telemetry.
ITID-62941.response: SOC logs the finding and hands off entirely to legal counsel; no containment action expected.
metrics: Number of active litigation matters tied to vendor-caused breaches
ITID-62941.notes: Vendor software governance/compliance issue — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels.

playbook.name: Class Action Litigation Following Vendor-Caused Data Breach
playbook.description: The organization faces class action litigation from customers or employees following a data breach caused by a third-party vendor's security failure, a legal governance matter requiring Legal-led coordination.

steps.title: Confirm the litigation filing and its connection to the vendor breach
steps.desc: Legal confirms receipt of the class action filing and its specific factual basis tying the claimed harm to the vendor-caused data breach.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with outside counsel to review the complaint in detail.
steps.outcome: Confirmed litigation details and its connection to the specific vendor incident documented.

steps.title: Compile the underlying breach incident record
steps.desc: Gather the complete incident response record, forensic findings, and vendor communications from the original vendor-caused breach relevant to the litigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the security/IR team that handled the original incident to compile the evidentiary record.
steps.outcome: Complete incident record compiled and preserved under legal hold.

steps.title: Assess insurance coverage and vendor indemnification obligations
steps.desc: Legal and Risk Management assess applicable cyber-insurance coverage and the vendor's contractual indemnification obligations for the litigation.

steps.title: Issue litigation hold and engage outside counsel
steps.desc: Issue a formal litigation hold across relevant records/custodians and engage outside counsel to manage the defense.
steps.outcome: Litigation hold issued and outside counsel engaged.

steps.title: Coordinate public/customer communications through Legal and Communications
steps.desc: Ensure all external communications regarding the litigation and underlying breach are coordinated through Legal and Corporate Communications.
steps.outcome: Controlled, consistent external communication approach established.

steps.title: Pursue vendor indemnification/contribution claims
steps.desc: Legal pursues indemnification or contribution claims against the vendor responsible for the underlying breach per contractual terms.
steps.abort: If no contractual indemnification exists, document the gap for future contract negotiations.

steps.title: Remediate underlying vendor security gap if not already resolved
steps.desc: Confirm the underlying vendor security failure that caused the breach has been fully remediated to prevent recurrence and mitigate ongoing litigation risk.
steps.outcome: Underlying vendor security gap confirmed remediated.

steps.title: Track litigation to resolution and implement settlement/judgment terms
steps.desc: Track the litigation through resolution (settlement or judgment) and implement any resulting obligations (notification, credit monitoring, process changes).
steps.outcome: Litigation resolved and resulting obligations implemented.

steps.title: Strengthen vendor contract indemnification and breach-response coordination
steps.desc: Document the litigation experience and strengthen vendor contract indemnification clauses and the coordination process between Legal and Security for future vendor-caused incidents.
steps.outcome: Updated vendor contract standards and cross-functional breach-response coordination process published.

ITID-62942.def: A legal/regulatory risk finding, not a technical security incident, in which a regulator imposes a fine or penalty on the organization for a security or privacy failure whose root cause traces to a third-party software vendor.
ITID-62942.purpose: Tracks regulatory fines imposed on the organization for a security failure attributable to a third-party software vendor rather than the organization's own controls.
scopeIncludes: A data protection authority fine issued to the organization following a vendor-caused personal data breach
A sector-specific regulatory penalty (financial services, healthcare, etc.) attributed to a vendor security failure
scopeExcludes: Civil class action litigation for the same underlying event (route to ITID-62941)
The underlying technical breach event itself, tracked under the relevant technical leaf elsewhere in this Tier-2 category
ITID-62942.severity: Low from a direct-technical standpoint; High as a legal/financial risk finding given the direct monetary and reputational penalty.
ITID-62942.priority: P3 for SOC tracking; actual priority and response owned by legal/compliance.
ITID-62942.escalation: Escalate to legal counsel, compliance, and executive leadership immediately upon regulatory notice.
indicators: Formal regulatory notice of intent to fine or a finalized penalty decision
Regulatory investigation opened specifically citing vendor-caused failure
vectors: Regulator imposed a fine directly on the organization stemming from a security failure at a third-party software vendor
Vendor due-diligence process failed to catch the compliance gap that ultimately triggered regulatory action
rootCauses: Underlying vendor-caused data breach subject to a regulatory reporting/protection obligation
Insufficient vendor due diligence documented to demonstrate reasonable care to the regulator
controls: Documented vendor due-diligence and risk-assessment process to demonstrate reasonable care
Regulatory breach notification process covering vendor-caused incidents
ITID-62942.detection: Not a technical detection surface — findings originate from regulatory notices, not security telemetry.
ITID-62942.response: SOC logs the finding and hands off entirely to legal/compliance; no containment action expected.
metrics: Number of regulatory fines tied to vendor-caused failures per year
ITID-62942.notes: Vendor software governance/compliance issue — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels.

playbook.name: Regulatory Fine Imposed on Organization for Vendor's Security Failure
playbook.description: A regulator imposes a fine on the organization for a security or compliance failure attributable to a third-party vendor, a Legal/Compliance-led governance matter.

steps.title: Confirm the regulatory action and its basis in the vendor's failure
steps.desc: Legal/Compliance confirms receipt of the regulatory notice/fine and reviews the specific findings tying the penalty to the vendor's security failure.
steps.guidance: Review the regulator's formal findings/decision document in detail.
steps.outcome: Confirmed regulatory action and its factual basis documented.

steps.title: Compile the underlying vendor incident and compliance record
steps.desc: Gather the complete record of the vendor relationship, security assessments, and the underlying incident that led to the regulatory action.

steps.title: Assess appeal options and vendor liability apportionment
steps.desc: Legal assesses whether the regulatory decision can be appealed or negotiated, and reviews the vendor contract for liability apportionment/indemnification.
steps.outcome: Documented appeal/negotiation strategy and vendor liability position.

steps.title: Respond to the regulator within required timelines
steps.desc: Prepare and submit the organization's formal response to the regulator within the mandated response window.
steps.outcome: Timely, compliant response submitted to the regulator.

steps.title: Coordinate vendor liability and indemnification claim
steps.desc: Legal formally pursues indemnification or liability apportionment from the vendor for the fine, where the contract supports it.
steps.abort: If no contractual indemnification exists, document the gap.

steps.title: Implement the regulator's required remediation plan
steps.desc: Implement any specific remediation measures mandated by the regulator's decision (e.g., enhanced vendor oversight, specific technical controls).

steps.title: Reassess and, if necessary, terminate the vendor relationship
steps.desc: Evaluate whether the vendor relationship should continue given the demonstrated security failure and resulting regulatory exposure.
steps.outcome: Documented decision on vendor relationship continuation or termination.

steps.title: Confirm regulatory closure and payment/remediation completion
steps.desc: Confirm the fine is paid/resolved and all regulator-mandated remediation is verified complete.

steps.title: Strengthen third-party vendor oversight program
steps.desc: Document the incident and strengthen the third-party vendor risk oversight program, including enhanced due diligence and ongoing compliance monitoring to prevent recurrence.

ITID-62943.def: A legal risk finding, not a technical security incident, involving legal exposure from a vendor-caused security failure whose specific form (civil litigation versus regulatory fine) has not yet been determined, or which takes a different legal form entirely (e.g., contractual dispute, indemnification claim).
ITID-62943.purpose: Intake leaf for a legal risk arising from a third-party software breach not yet attributed to the class-action or regulatory-fine leaves in this group.
scopeIncludes: Newly received legal notice tied to a vendor-caused breach pending classification
Contractual dispute or indemnification claim arising from a vendor security failure
scopeExcludes: Cases confirmed as class action litigation (route to ITID-62941) or a regulatory fine (route to ITID-62942)
ITID-62943.severity: Low from a direct-technical standpoint; High as a legal/financial risk finding pending classification.
ITID-62943.priority: P3 for SOC tracking; actual priority and response owned by legal counsel.
ITID-62943.escalation: Escalate to legal counsel immediately upon any vendor-related legal notice.
indicators: Legal notice or claim tied to a vendor security failure, specific legal form not yet determined
vectors: Generic legal risk arising from a third-party software breach not captured by a more specific sub-category
No pre-negotiated liability allocation for software vendor security failures affecting the organization
rootCauses: Underlying vendor-caused security failure with legal exposure not yet fully characterized
controls: Contractual liability allocation and indemnification clauses with third-party vendors
ITID-62943.detection: Not a technical detection surface — findings originate from legal notices, not security telemetry.
ITID-62943.response: SOC logs the finding and hands off entirely to legal counsel; no containment action expected.
metrics: Number of unclassified vendor-related legal matters pending review
ITID-62943.notes: Vendor software governance/compliance issue — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via legal, privacy, and vendor-management channels. Unclassified/general intake leaf for the Legal Risks from Third-Party Software Breaches group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Legal Risk from Third-Party Software Breach
playbook.description: A general or unclassified legal risk arising from a third-party software breach that does not fit a more specific litigation or regulatory-fine scenario.

steps.title: Confirm the legal risk and its connection to the vendor/software breach
steps.desc: Legal confirms the nature of the legal risk (demand letter, threatened claim, contractual dispute) and its connection to the specific third-party software breach.
steps.outcome: Confirmed legal risk details and factual basis documented.

steps.title: Compile the underlying incident and vendor relationship record
steps.desc: Gather the complete incident response record and vendor contract/relationship documentation relevant to the legal risk.
steps.outcome: Complete record compiled and preserved under legal hold if applicable.

steps.title: Assess vendor liability and indemnification position
steps.desc: Legal reviews the vendor contract for liability apportionment and indemnification obligations relevant to the legal risk.

steps.title: Issue litigation hold if applicable and engage counsel
steps.desc: Issue a litigation hold if litigation is reasonably anticipated, and engage internal/outside counsel to manage the matter.
steps.outcome: Litigation hold issued if applicable and counsel engaged.
steps.abort: If no litigation hold is warranted at this stage, document the determination.

steps.title: Pursue vendor indemnification/contribution where applicable
steps.desc: Legal pursues indemnification or contribution from the vendor per contractual terms.
steps.outcome: Vendor indemnification/contribution process initiated where applicable.

steps.title: Remediate underlying vendor security/compliance gap
steps.desc: Confirm the underlying vendor issue that gave rise to the legal risk has been remediated.

steps.title: Track the legal matter to resolution
steps.desc: Track the legal matter through to resolution and implement any resulting obligations.
steps.outcome: Legal matter resolved and obligations implemented.

steps.title: Strengthen vendor contract terms and legal risk review process
steps.desc: Document the matter and strengthen vendor contract terms (indemnification, liability caps) and the legal risk review process for third-party software relationships.
steps.outcome: Updated vendor contract standards and legal risk review process published.
