ITID-63213.def: The use of a fabricated or impersonated freight-brokerage identity to insert an adversary into a legitimate shipping transaction, allowing them to take possession of cargo, redirect payment, or both.
ITID-63213.purpose: Captures fraud in which an adversary poses as a legitimate freight broker to gain control of a shipment or payment intended for a real carrier.
scopeIncludes: A fictitious broker entity registered to intercept load postings and take possession of cargo
Impersonation of a legitimate, registered broker's identity or credentials to divert a load
Double-brokering fraud where a load is re-brokered without the shipper's knowledge to an unvetted carrier
scopeExcludes: Direct falsification of delivery-address instructions without a broker impersonation element (ITID-63212)
Outright physical hijacking with no fraudulent brokerage element (ITID-63211)
ITID-63213.severity: Medium-High, scaled to the value of the shipment and whether payment was also diverted.
ITID-63213.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 for high-value shipments or confirmed repeat targeting by an organized fraud ring.
ITID-63213.escalation: Escalate to logistics security and vendor/procurement management; report to industry fraud-reporting bodies and law enforcement.
indicators: Broker entity not verifiable in industry registries (e.g., FMCSA/DOT-equivalent) or with a very recently created registration
Load re-brokered to a carrier not vetted by the original shipper
Payment redirected to an account inconsistent with the broker's known banking details
vectors: Registration of a fraudulent brokerage entity to intercept load postings on freight marketplaces
Impersonation of a legitimate broker's identity/credentials to reroute a load
Unauthorized double-brokering of a load to an unvetted downstream carrier
rootCauses: No verification of broker/carrier legitimacy before releasing a load
Lack of monitoring for double-brokering on freight marketplace platforms
Insufficient vetting of new broker relationships before high-value loads are assigned
controls: Broker/carrier identity verification against industry registries before load release
Monitoring for unauthorized double-brokering
Out-of-band payment verification for freight-brokerage transactions
ITID-63213.detection: Physical logistics crime — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and logistics-partner coordination.
ITID-63213.response: Report to industry fraud databases and law enforcement, attempt to recover the shipment/payment, and review broker-vetting procedures for the affected lane.
metrics: Number of fictitious broker fraud incidents per quarter
Value of shipments/payments lost
Percentage of new broker relationships verified before first load
ITID-63213.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf specifically involves a fabricated or impersonated broker identity, distinguishing it from address-diversion fraud (ITID-63212) and outright hijacking (ITID-63211).

playbook.name: Fictitious Freight Broker Fraud
playbook.description: A fraudulent entity posing as a legitimate freight broker or carrier arranged to transport a shipment and absconded with the goods.

steps.title: Confirm the broker's fraudulent identity
steps.desc: Verify the freight broker's licensing (e.g., FMCSA/MC number equivalent), business registration, and insurance against official registries.
steps.guidance: Cross-check the broker/carrier identity used for the booking against known legitimate operators; look for recently created or spoofed MC numbers.
steps.abort: If the broker is confirmed legitimate, close as a standard delivery issue.

steps.title: Reconstruct the booking and payment trail
steps.desc: Gather all communications, booking confirmations, and payment records related to the fraudulent broker engagement.
steps.guidance: Include how the broker was sourced (load board, referral, cold outreach) to identify the point of compromise.
steps.outcome: Full booking and payment trail documented.

steps.title: Determine shipment and financial loss
steps.desc: Quantify the value of goods lost and any payment made to the fraudulent broker.
steps.outcome: Total loss quantified for claims and law-enforcement reporting.

steps.title: Alert load board/industry platform and other shippers
steps.desc: Report the fraudulent broker identity to the load board or freight-matching platform used, and to industry fraud-alert networks.
steps.guidance: Rapid alerting can prevent the same fraudulent broker from victimizing other shippers.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent broker identity is flagged on relevant platforms.

steps.title: Notify law enforcement and file a fraud report
steps.desc: File a report with law enforcement (and, if interstate, the relevant transportation fraud task force) covering the fictitious broker scheme.
steps.outcome: Fraud report filed with case number.

steps.title: Attempt recovery of goods and payment
steps.desc: Coordinate with law enforcement and, where applicable, financial institutions to attempt recovery of diverted goods or payment.
steps.outcome: Recovery efforts documented and pursued to the extent feasible.

steps.title: Review other pending shipments booked through the same source
steps.desc: Check whether other shipments were booked through the same fraudulent broker or load-board contact.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of whether the fraud is isolated or part of a broader scheme.

steps.title: Arrange replacement shipment through verified carrier
steps.desc: Book replacement transport through a verified, properly licensed carrier or broker.
steps.guidance: Apply enhanced verification for this booking given the recent fraud.
steps.outcome: Replacement shipment delivered via a verified carrier.

steps.title: Strengthen broker/carrier vetting procedures
steps.desc: Implement or strengthen procedures for verifying broker/carrier legitimacy before booking, especially for load-board-sourced engagements.
steps.guidance: Consider requiring verified registration, insurance certificates, and reference checks for new broker relationships.

ITID-63214.def: General or not-yet-classified reports of theft or fraud affecting a shipment in the logistics/transportation chain.
ITID-63214.purpose: Intake bucket for supply chain theft and fraud incidents that do not fit cargo theft, fraudulent diversion, or fictitious broker fraud.
scopeIncludes: Theft or fraud reports where the specific mechanism is not yet determined
Novel or mixed logistics fraud patterns not covered by the more specific leaves
scopeExcludes: Cargo theft in transit (ITID-63211)
Fraudulent shipment diversion (ITID-63212)
Fictitious freight broker fraud (ITID-63213)
ITID-63214.priority: P3 pending triage; re-prioritize once the specific mechanism and shipment value are known.
ITID-63214.escalation: Escalate to logistics security for triage; reclassify to a specific leaf once the fraud mechanism is confirmed.
indicators: Shipment loss or discrepancy not yet attributed to a specific known fraud pattern
vectors: Unclassified logistics theft or fraud technique pending investigation
rootCauses: Gaps in logistics-partner vetting and shipment monitoring generally
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: General logistics security and shipment-monitoring program
ITID-63214.detection: Physical logistics crime — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and logistics-partner coordination.
ITID-63214.response: Triage the report and reclassify to a specific leaf once the fraud mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Count of general theft/fraud reports pending triage
Percentage subsequently reclassified
ITID-63214.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf for the Supply Chain Theft and Fraud Tier-4 group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Supply Chain Theft and Fraud
playbook.description: A theft or fraud incident of unspecified type has occurred within the supply chain and requires investigation under the general theft-and-fraud process.

steps.title: Establish the nature and scope of the theft/fraud
steps.desc: Gather initial facts on what was stolen or fraudulently obtained, when, and how the incident was detected.
steps.guidance: Interview the reporting party and pull relevant transaction, shipment, or inventory records.
steps.outcome: Initial case record established with scope and detection method documented.

steps.title: Quantify financial and inventory impact
steps.desc: Determine the value of goods, funds, or assets involved in the theft or fraud.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with finance for accurate valuation.

steps.title: Identify likely method and responsible party
steps.desc: Investigate available evidence to determine how the theft/fraud was carried out and by whom (external actor, insider, or collusion).
steps.outcome: Preliminary determination of method and suspected responsible party.

steps.title: Notify law enforcement and file a report
steps.desc: File a police report or equivalent covering the theft or fraud with all available evidence.

steps.title: Freeze or secure related accounts, access, or assets
steps.desc: Suspend any accounts, access, or processes that could allow continuation or repetition of the theft/fraud.

steps.title: Investigate and remediate the exploited control gap
steps.desc: Identify the specific process or control weakness that enabled the theft/fraud and remediate it.

steps.title: Pursue recovery of stolen assets or funds
steps.desc: Work with law enforcement, insurers, and financial institutions to recover stolen assets or funds where possible.

steps.title: Restore normal operations and affected records
steps.desc: Confirm inventory, financial, and operational records are corrected and operations have returned to normal.

steps.title: Review and strengthen anti-theft/fraud controls
steps.desc: Document root cause and update relevant controls, monitoring, or vetting procedures to prevent recurrence.

ITID-63221.def: An employee of a carrier, warehouse, or logistics partner who uses their legitimate access or role to directly facilitate the physical theft of cargo — for example, by diverting a load, disabling security controls, or colluding with external thieves during handling.
ITID-63221.purpose: Captures a logistics provider employee actively participating in or enabling the physical theft of cargo they have legitimate access to.
scopeIncludes: A driver or dock worker diverting or removing cargo for personal gain or on behalf of a criminal group
An employee disabling a vehicle's GPS tracker or alarm to enable theft
Collusion between a logistics employee and an external theft ring during a scheduled handoff
scopeExcludes: An employee merely passing shipment details to external thieves without directly facilitating the theft (ITID-63222)
Cargo theft with no insider involvement (ITID-63211)
ITID-63221.severity: High. Insider-facilitated theft is harder to detect via external controls and often recurs until identified.
ITID-63221.escalation: Escalate to HR, legal, physical security, and law enforcement; suspend the employee's access pending investigation.
indicators: Pattern of losses correlated with a specific employee's shifts or assigned routes
GPS/tracking device found deliberately disabled or tampered with
Employee's financial situation or associations raising insider-risk concern following an investigation
vectors: Employee directly removing or diverting cargo during handling
Employee disabling tracking/alarm systems to create a theft opportunity for confederates
rootCauses: Insufficient background vetting for personnel with cargo-handling access
Lack of loss-pattern analysis correlating theft incidents with staffing/shift data
Inadequate segregation of duties in cargo handling and vehicle access
controls: Background vetting for cargo-handling personnel
Loss-pattern analysis correlating incidents with staffing/route data
Segregation of duties for vehicle/cargo access and tracker deactivation
ITID-63221.detection: Physical logistics crime — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and logistics-partner coordination.
ITID-63221.response: Investigate through HR and physical security channels, suspend implicated personnel's access, and refer for law enforcement action where warranted.
metrics: Number of confirmed insider-facilitated theft incidents per year
Loss value attributed to insider involvement
Percentage of cargo-handling personnel with current background vetting
detections: Loss-pattern analysis correlated with staffing/shift data
ITID-63221.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is direct facilitation of theft, as opposed to information-leakage-only insider involvement (ITID-63222).

playbook.name: Logistics Employee Facilitating Cargo Theft
playbook.description: An employee of a third-party logistics provider is suspected of actively facilitating the theft of cargo entrusted to that provider.

steps.title: Document the suspicious pattern implicating the insider
steps.desc: Compile evidence pointing to the logistics employee's involvement — access patterns, route deviations, timing correlations with thefts, or informant tips.
steps.guidance: Work with the logistics provider's investigative team since the individual is their employee, not yours.
steps.outcome: Evidence package documenting the suspected insider's role.

steps.title: Quantify the scope of affected shipments
steps.desc: Identify all shipments potentially affected by the suspected insider's actions to date.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference the employee's work schedule/routes against known theft incidents.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected shipments identified.

steps.title: Formally notify the logistics provider's security/HR/Legal team
steps.desc: Escalate the suspected insider threat to the logistics provider's own security, HR, and legal teams, since the organization does not directly employ the individual.
steps.guidance: Provide the evidence package and request the provider suspend the employee's access pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Logistics provider opens a formal internal investigation and restricts the employee's access.
steps.abort: If the provider does not act promptly, escalate through contract/account management channels and consider contract remedies.

steps.title: Increase monitoring of shipments handled by the provider
steps.desc: Apply heightened tracking, verification, and chain-of-custody documentation to shipments routed through the affected provider or facility pending investigation outcome.
steps.outcome: Enhanced monitoring in place with no further undetected losses.

steps.title: Notify law enforcement
steps.desc: File a law-enforcement report covering the suspected theft-facilitation scheme, coordinating with the logistics provider's investigation.

steps.title: Confirm investigation outcome and provider's remedial action
steps.desc: Obtain confirmation from the logistics provider on the investigation outcome and any disciplinary, termination, or legal action taken.
steps.outcome: Documented confirmation of the provider's remedial action.

steps.title: Assess and pursue recovery of stolen goods
steps.desc: Work with law enforcement and the provider to recover stolen goods and quantify losses for claims purposes.

steps.title: Reassess the logistics provider relationship
steps.desc: Evaluate whether the provider's security practices and incident response were adequate, and decide whether to continue, modify, or terminate the relationship.
steps.guidance: Involve procurement/vendor management leadership in this decision.
steps.outcome: Documented decision on the ongoing provider relationship.

steps.title: Strengthen contractual security requirements for logistics providers
steps.desc: Update contracts and vendor-security requirements to include insider-threat controls, background-check standards, and incident-notification SLAs for logistics providers.
steps.outcome: Updated contractual requirements documented and applied to relevant vendor agreements.

ITID-63222.def: An employee of a carrier, warehouse, or logistics partner who discloses non-public shipment information (route, timing, contents, security details) to an external party, enabling that party to carry out a theft.
ITID-63222.purpose: Captures a logistics provider employee leaking shipment details to external parties who then use that information to commit theft, without the employee directly participating in the theft itself.
scopeIncludes: An employee selling or leaking route/timing/contents information to an external theft ring
An employee providing photographs, manifests, or schedules to facilitate later theft by others
scopeExcludes: An employee who directly participates in the physical theft (ITID-63221)
Theft with no evidence of an information-leakage insider component (ITID-63211)
ITID-63222.severity: High. Leaked shipment intelligence significantly increases the success rate and precision of subsequent theft.
ITID-63222.priority: P1 on confirmed leakage; P2 while investigating a suspected pattern.
ITID-63222.escalation: Escalate to HR, legal, physical security, and law enforcement; review the employee's information access and communications pending investigation.
indicators: Theft incidents that precisely target high-value or oddly specific shipments with no obvious external reconnaissance
Evidence of unauthorized information sharing (communications, financial payments) linking an employee to external thieves
Access logs showing an employee viewing shipment details outside their normal job function
vectors: Employee selling shipment schedules/contents information to a criminal contact
Employee photographing or copying manifests for external use
rootCauses: Overly broad access to sensitive shipment data beyond job necessity
No monitoring of anomalous access to shipment/routing systems
Insufficient vetting or financial-pressure screening for personnel with access to high-value shipment data
controls: Least-privilege access to shipment/routing data based on job necessity
Monitoring/alerting on anomalous access to sensitive shipment records
Background vetting for personnel with access to high-value shipment data
ITID-63222.detection: Physical logistics crime — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and logistics-partner coordination.
ITID-63222.response: Investigate through HR and physical security channels, restrict the implicated employee's data access, and refer for law enforcement action where warranted.
metrics: Number of confirmed information-leakage insider incidents per year
Percentage of shipment-data access reviewed for least-privilege compliance
detections: Anomalous access monitoring on shipment/routing systems
ITID-63222.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is information leakage enabling theft by others, as opposed to direct participation in the theft (ITID-63221).

playbook.name: Logistics Employee Providing Shipment Details to External Thieves
playbook.description: An employee of a third-party logistics provider is suspected of leaking shipment schedules, routes, or contents to external parties who then commit theft.

steps.title: Correlate thefts with shipment-detail exposure
steps.desc: Analyze the pattern of thefts against who had access to the leaked shipment details (schedules, routes, contents) to identify the likely insider.
steps.guidance: Look for a common employee, system, or access point across the affected shipments.
steps.outcome: Evidence correlating specific insider access with the thefts.

steps.title: Determine the leakage channel
steps.desc: Identify how shipment details were transmitted to external parties (phone, messaging app, in-person contact, compromised system access).
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the logistics provider for access log review of their systems.

steps.title: Notify the logistics provider's HR/Legal/security team
steps.desc: Escalate findings to the logistics provider's own HR, legal, and security teams to trigger their internal disciplinary and investigative process, since the individual is their employee.
steps.outcome: Provider opens formal investigation and restricts the employee's access to shipment data.
steps.abort: If the provider is unresponsive, escalate via account management and consider contractual remedies.

steps.title: Change shipment scheduling/routing information handling
steps.desc: Temporarily restrict distribution of detailed shipment schedules and routes to a minimal need-to-know set while the investigation is active.
steps.outcome: Sensitive shipment details are no longer broadly accessible.

steps.title: Notify law enforcement
steps.desc: File a report with law enforcement covering the information-leakage scheme facilitating theft.

steps.title: Confirm provider's remedial and disciplinary action
steps.desc: Obtain confirmation of the outcome of the provider's internal investigation and any action taken against the employee.

steps.title: Assess and pursue recovery for affected shipments
steps.desc: Quantify losses from affected shipments and pursue recovery via law enforcement, insurance, or the provider's claims process.

steps.title: Restore normal shipment information-sharing practices with enhanced controls
steps.desc: Resume normal shipment scheduling communication with the provider under stronger access controls and monitoring.
steps.outcome: Normal operations resumed with enhanced access controls in place.

steps.title: Strengthen data-sharing and vendor-access agreements
steps.desc: Update data-sharing agreements with logistics providers to limit shipment-detail access and require insider-threat controls on their end.

ITID-63223.def: General or not-yet-classified reports of a logistics provider employee acting maliciously against the shipments or operations they have legitimate access to.
ITID-63223.purpose: Intake bucket for malicious insider activity at a logistics provider that does not fit direct theft facilitation or information leakage.
scopeIncludes: Insider misconduct reports where the specific mechanism (direct theft facilitation vs. information leakage) is not yet determined
Other forms of insider misconduct at a logistics partner not covered by the more specific leaves
scopeExcludes: Direct facilitation of cargo theft (ITID-63221)
Information leakage enabling external theft (ITID-63222)
ITID-63223.priority: P2 pending triage; escalate to P1 on confirmation of direct theft facilitation or leakage.
ITID-63223.escalation: Escalate to HR and physical security for triage; reclassify to a specific leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.
indicators: Insider-risk indicators not yet attributed to a specific known pattern
vectors: Unclassified insider misconduct at a logistics partner, pending investigation
rootCauses: Gaps in insider-threat monitoring for third-party logistics personnel generally
controls: General third-party insider-threat monitoring program
ITID-63223.detection: Physical logistics crime — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and logistics-partner coordination.
ITID-63223.response: Triage the report and reclassify to a specific leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Count of general insider-threat reports pending triage
Percentage subsequently reclassified
detections: Anomalous access monitoring on shipment/routing systems
ITID-63223.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf for the Malicious Insider at a Logistics Provider Tier-4 group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Malicious Insider at a Logistics Provider
playbook.description: An employee of a third-party logistics provider is suspected of malicious activity harming shipments or shipment information of unspecified type.

steps.title: Document the suspected insider activity
steps.desc: Gather available evidence of the suspected malicious activity, its nature, and its apparent impact.

steps.title: Determine scope of affected shipments/data
steps.desc: Identify all shipments, data, or operations potentially affected by the suspected insider's activity.

steps.title: Notify the logistics provider's HR/Legal/security team
steps.desc: Escalate the matter to the provider's own HR, legal, and security functions, since the organization does not directly employ the individual.
steps.guidance: Request suspension of the employee's access pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Provider opens investigation and restricts access.
steps.abort: If unresponsive, escalate via account management and evaluate contractual remedies.

steps.title: Increase monitoring of affected shipments/operations
steps.desc: Apply heightened tracking and verification to shipments or operations handled by the provider pending investigation outcome.

steps.title: Confirm investigation outcome
steps.desc: Obtain confirmation of the provider's investigation findings and remedial/disciplinary action.

steps.title: Address any residual exposure or loss
steps.desc: Quantify and remediate any loss or exposure resulting from the insider's activity.

steps.title: Reassess the provider relationship and controls
steps.desc: Evaluate whether the provider's security posture is adequate and decide on the ongoing relationship.
steps.outcome: Documented decision on the provider relationship.

steps.title: Strengthen vendor insider-threat requirements
steps.desc: Update contracts and vendor-security requirements to include insider-threat controls and incident-notification obligations.

ITID-63231.def: An act of deliberate sabotage causing physical damage to a shipment of critical hardware, intended to render it unusable or delay its deployment, as opposed to theft or covert modification.
ITID-63231.purpose: Captures deliberate physical damage inflicted on a critical hardware shipment while in the logistics chain, intended to disrupt availability rather than steal or tamper covertly.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate physical destruction or damage to a shipment of critical infrastructure or mission-essential hardware
Sabotage of transport (e.g., disabling a refrigerated container or environmental control) to cause damage in transit
scopeExcludes: Theft of the shipment (ITID-63211)
Covert tampering intended to implant a backdoor rather than destroy (ITID-63121, ITID-63131)
Contamination/tampering of perishable or sensitive goods specifically (ITID-63232)
ITID-63231.severity: High-Critical, especially where the damaged hardware supports critical infrastructure or has a long replacement lead time.
ITID-63231.priority: P1 for shipments supporting critical infrastructure or mission-essential operations.
ITID-63231.escalation: Escalate to physical security, business continuity, and (where nation-state or organized sabotage is suspected) law enforcement/national authorities.
indicators: Physical damage to a shipment inconsistent with normal handling wear-and-tear
Environmental control systems (refrigeration, humidity) found deliberately disabled
Pattern of damage targeting a specific class of critical shipment across multiple incidents
vectors: Physical sabotage during a transfer point or unmonitored dwell time
Disabling of environmental/transport controls to cause damage in transit
rootCauses: Insufficient physical security or monitoring at transfer/dwell points for critical shipments
No tamper/condition monitoring on environmentally sensitive shipments
Lack of contingency stock for critical, long-lead-time hardware
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Condition monitoring (shock, temperature, humidity) on critical shipments with alerting
Enhanced physical security at transfer/dwell points for critical cargo
Contingency/buffer stock planning for long-lead-time critical hardware
ITID-63231.detection: Physical logistics crime — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and logistics-partner coordination.
ITID-63231.response: Assess business continuity impact, initiate replacement/expedite procurement, and investigate the transfer point where the sabotage occurred.
metrics: Number of sabotage incidents affecting critical shipments per year
Business impact/delay caused
Percentage of critical shipments under condition monitoring
ITID-63231.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is deliberate physical destruction/disruption of critical hardware, distinct from contamination/tampering of perishable or sensitive goods (ITID-63232).

playbook.name: Deliberate Damage to Critical Hardware Shipment
playbook.description: A shipment of critical hardware was deliberately damaged or sabotaged during transit.

steps.title: Document damage and confirm deliberate sabotage
steps.desc: Photograph and log the damage, and assess whether it is consistent with accidental transit damage or deliberate sabotage (cut cables, targeted impact points, deliberate contamination).
steps.guidance: Engage the carrier and, if needed, a forensic damage assessor to distinguish sabotage from accidental handling damage.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether damage is deliberate.
steps.abort: If damage is consistent with accidental handling, route to standard carrier claims process instead.

steps.title: Urgently assess scope of affected batch/shipment
steps.desc: Determine what else in the same shipment, batch, or transit leg may be affected by the same sabotage act.
steps.guidance: This is time-critical — other units in the same shipment may also be compromised or at continued risk.
steps.outcome: Full scope of potentially affected goods identified.

steps.title: Reconstruct custody chain to identify sabotage window
steps.desc: Obtain carrier custody and handling records to narrow down when and where the sabotage likely occurred.
steps.outcome: Custody timeline documented with candidate sabotage window identified.

steps.title: Quarantine the shipment and halt deployment of any critical hardware from it
steps.desc: Immediately hold all hardware from the affected shipment from installation or use until integrity is confirmed.
steps.guidance: Treat as urgent given the shipment's criticality.
steps.outcome: No damaged/sabotaged hardware is deployed into production.

steps.title: Notify carrier security and law enforcement
steps.desc: Report the sabotage to the carrier's security team and to law enforcement given the deliberate and potentially criminal nature of the act.

steps.title: Forensically assess all affected hardware
steps.desc: Inspect all hardware from the affected batch for damage or tampering, not just the initially reported unit.
steps.guidance: Engage hardware forensics for units suspected of tampering beyond visible physical damage.
steps.outcome: Full assessment of the affected batch's integrity.

steps.title: Replace damaged/sabotaged hardware
steps.desc: Source and deploy replacement hardware through verified channels for any units confirmed damaged or compromised.
steps.outcome: All critical hardware needs are met with verified-clean replacements.

steps.title: Validate replacement hardware and restore operations
steps.desc: Confirm replacement hardware is functioning correctly before returning to normal operations.

steps.title: File insurance claim for damaged goods
steps.desc: Submit a claim covering the value of the sabotaged hardware and any associated business disruption.

steps.title: Review critical shipment security requirements
steps.desc: Assess whether critical hardware shipments need enhanced security (tamper-evident packaging, security escorts, varied routing) and update requirements.

ITID-63232.def: An act of deliberate contamination, adulteration, or tampering with perishable or sensitive goods (e.g., pharmaceuticals, chemicals, sensitive materials) during transport, intended to render the goods unsafe, unusable, or non-compliant.
ITID-63232.purpose: Captures deliberate contamination or tampering with perishable or otherwise sensitive goods while in transit through the supply chain.
scopeIncludes: Deliberate introduction of a contaminant into perishable or sensitive cargo
Tampering with packaging/seals of sensitive goods (e.g., pharmaceuticals) in a way that compromises safety or compliance
Deliberate disruption of cold-chain or environmental controls to spoil sensitive goods
scopeExcludes: Deliberate destruction of critical hardware shipments (ITID-63231)
General in-transit tampering evidence not yet linked to contamination (ITID-63131)
ITID-63232.severity: High-Critical where public safety, health, or regulatory compliance is implicated.
ITID-63232.priority: P1 for any confirmed contamination of goods destined for consumption, medical use, or safety-critical application.
ITID-63232.escalation: Escalate immediately to quality/regulatory compliance, physical security, and (for public-safety-relevant goods) public health/regulatory authorities; quarantine the affected batch and all co-mingled shipments.
indicators: Cold-chain/temperature logs showing an unexplained excursion
Physical or chemical evidence of contamination on inspection
Packaging/seal inconsistencies on sensitive goods at receiving
vectors: Deliberate introduction of a contaminant during an unmonitored handling window
Sabotage of refrigeration/environmental control systems in transit
rootCauses: Insufficient cold-chain/condition monitoring with real-time alerting
Inadequate physical security at handling and transfer points for sensitive goods
No independent quality verification at receiving for high-risk goods categories
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Cold-chain/condition monitoring with real-time alerting
Tamper-evident, contamination-resistant packaging for sensitive goods
Independent quality/contamination testing at receiving for high-risk categories
ITID-63232.detection: Physical logistics crime — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and logistics-partner coordination.
ITID-63232.response: Quarantine the affected batch and any co-mingled shipments, notify quality/regulatory compliance and public health authorities as required, and investigate the point of contamination.
metrics: Number of contamination/tampering incidents per year
Value/volume of goods quarantined
Percentage of sensitive shipments under cold-chain/condition monitoring
sops: Product Quality and Contamination Incident SOP
ITID-63232.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is contamination/tampering of perishable or sensitive goods specifically, distinct from deliberate physical destruction of critical hardware (ITID-63231).

playbook.name: Contamination/Tampering of Perishable or Sensitive Goods in Transit
playbook.description: Perishable or sensitive goods were contaminated or tampered with while in transit, posing a potential safety or integrity risk.

steps.title: Confirm contamination/tampering and assess immediate safety risk
steps.desc: Verify evidence of contamination or tampering and assess whether affected goods pose an immediate health, safety, or operational risk.
steps.guidance: Engage quality assurance or relevant safety specialists immediately given potential health/safety exposure.
steps.outcome: Contamination/tampering confirmed and immediate risk level assessed.
steps.abort: If evidence does not support tampering, route through standard quality-control process instead.

steps.title: Urgently determine scope across the batch/shipment
steps.desc: Identify all units in the same batch or shipment that may share the same exposure.
steps.guidance: Treat this as time-critical given potential ongoing distribution of affected goods.
steps.outcome: Full scope of potentially affected goods identified.

steps.title: Reconstruct custody chain to identify tampering window
steps.desc: Obtain transit and handling records to narrow the time and location of the tampering/contamination.
steps.outcome: Custody timeline and candidate exposure window documented.

steps.title: Issue immediate hold and, if already distributed, recall
steps.desc: Halt further distribution or use of affected goods, and initiate a recall for any units already delivered or in use.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with quality, legal, and (for regulated goods) the relevant regulatory authority on recall scope and communication.
steps.outcome: Affected goods are held or recalled with no further use/consumption.

steps.title: Notify carrier security and law enforcement
steps.desc: Report the tampering to the carrier's security team and law enforcement given the deliberate and potentially criminal nature of the act.

steps.title: Laboratory test affected goods to determine contamination extent
steps.desc: Have accredited testing performed on affected goods to characterize the contamination and confirm which units are unsafe.
steps.outcome: Test results confirming contamination extent and affected unit boundaries.

steps.title: Dispose of confirmed-contaminated goods and replace
steps.desc: Safely dispose of confirmed-contaminated goods per regulatory requirements and arrange replacement through verified channels.
steps.outcome: Contaminated goods disposed of properly; replacements procured.

steps.title: Confirm recall completeness and notify stakeholders
steps.desc: Verify all affected goods have been recovered/recalled and notify customers, regulators, and partners as required.

steps.title: Review transit security and packaging integrity requirements
steps.desc: Assess whether tamper-evident packaging, sealed/monitored transit, or enhanced carrier vetting is needed for sensitive or perishable goods.

ITID-63233.def: General or not-yet-classified reports of destructive sabotage against a shipment in the logistics chain.
ITID-63233.purpose: Intake bucket for destructive sabotage of a critical shipment that does not fit the deliberate-damage or contamination leaves.
scopeIncludes: Sabotage reports where the specific mechanism (physical destruction vs. contamination) is not yet determined
Novel or mixed sabotage patterns not covered by the more specific leaves
scopeExcludes: Deliberate damage to critical hardware shipments (ITID-63231)
Contamination/tampering of perishable or sensitive goods (ITID-63232)
ITID-63233.priority: P2 pending triage; escalate to P1 once the specific shipment criticality and sabotage mechanism are confirmed.
ITID-63233.escalation: Escalate to physical security and business continuity for triage; reclassify to a specific leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.
indicators: Sabotage evidence not yet attributed to a specific known pattern
vectors: Unclassified sabotage technique pending investigation
rootCauses: Gaps in physical security/monitoring for critical shipments generally
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: General physical security and condition-monitoring program for critical shipments
ITID-63233.detection: Physical logistics crime — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and logistics-partner coordination.
ITID-63233.response: Triage the report and reclassify to a specific leaf once the sabotage mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Count of general sabotage reports pending triage
Percentage subsequently reclassified
ITID-63233.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf for the Destructive Sabotage of Critical Shipments Tier-4 group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Destructive Sabotage of Critical Shipment
playbook.description: A shipment considered critical was deliberately sabotaged or destroyed in a manner not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm sabotage and assess criticality of affected shipment
steps.desc: Verify evidence of deliberate sabotage and assess the operational criticality of the affected shipment.
steps.abort: If not confirmed deliberate, route to standard carrier claims process.

steps.title: Urgently assess scope across the batch/shipment
steps.desc: Determine what else in the same shipment or batch may be affected by the same sabotage act.
steps.guidance: Treat as time-critical.
steps.outcome: Full scope of potentially affected goods identified.

steps.title: Reconstruct custody chain
steps.desc: Obtain carrier custody and handling records to narrow the sabotage window and location.

steps.title: Quarantine affected shipment/batch
steps.desc: Hold all goods from the affected shipment or batch from use pending integrity confirmation.

steps.title: Notify carrier security and law enforcement
steps.desc: Report the sabotage to the carrier's security team and law enforcement.

steps.title: Assess and remediate affected goods
steps.desc: Inspect the affected batch and dispose of/replace compromised goods as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Compromised goods removed and replaced with verified goods.

steps.title: Restore operations and file insurance claim
steps.desc: Confirm replacement goods restore normal operations and file an insurance claim for losses.

steps.title: Review critical shipment security requirements
steps.desc: Assess and strengthen security requirements for critical shipments to prevent recurrence.

ITID-63311.def: The unauthorized manufacture of extra units of a legitimate device design by a contract manufacturer or OEM partner, beyond the quantity authorized by the design owner, typically sold covertly outside the authorized channel.
ITID-63311.purpose: Captures a contract manufacturer running unauthorized additional production ('third-shift' or overproduction) of a device beyond the ordering party's authorized quantity, introducing unaccounted units into the market or supply chain.
scopeIncludes: A contract manufacturer running additional unauthorized production shifts to produce excess units
Excess units sold through gray-market channels without the design owner's knowledge or royalty
Use of leftover authorized components to build additional unauthorized units
scopeExcludes: Cloning of a device design by an unrelated, unauthorized manufacturer with no legitimate production relationship (ITID-63312)
Introduction of a cloned device with a duplicated serial number/IMEI (ITID-63313)
ITID-63311.severity: Medium-High. Overproduction undermines revenue, quality assurance, and warranty integrity, and the unauthorized units bypass the design owner's security/quality controls.
ITID-63311.priority: P2 on discovery; escalate to P1 if overproduced units are found in the organization's own deployed environment.
ITID-63311.escalation: Escalate to procurement/supply-chain risk, legal (IP/contract enforcement), and the affected product/security engineering team.
indicators: Units in circulation exceeding the authorized production count reconciled against purchase orders
Devices with valid-looking serials that do not match the design owner's production/shipment records
Reports of the device being sold through unauthorized retail/reseller channels
vectors: A contract manufacturer running extra production shifts outside contracted quantities
Diversion of authorized-but-unused components into unauthorized unit assembly
rootCauses: Insufficient production-run auditing and component reconciliation at the contract manufacturer
No independent verification of production counts against component procurement
Weak contractual/audit rights over the manufacturing partner's production floor
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Production-run auditing and component reconciliation rights written into manufacturing contracts
Independent third-party audits of contract manufacturer production floors
Serial number issuance and tracking controlled by the design owner, not the manufacturer
ITID-63311.detection: Detection is primarily a supply-chain audit function; SOC visibility is limited unless overproduced units surface within the organization's own environment.
ITID-63311.response: Reconcile production and component records with the contract manufacturer, pursue contractual/legal remedies, and assess whether any overproduced units have entered the organization's own deployment.
metrics: Number of confirmed overproduction incidents per year
Units reconciled vs. discrepancy found in production audits
Percentage of contract manufacturers subject to independent production audit
sops: Hardware Receiving and Authenticity Verification SOP
ITID-63311.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is unauthorized overproduction by an otherwise-legitimate manufacturing partner, distinct from cloning by an unrelated party (ITID-63312) or a cloned unit with a duplicated identifier (ITID-63313).

playbook.name: Unauthorized Third-Shift Production Run at Contract Manufacturer (Overproduction Cloning)
playbook.description: A contract manufacturer is suspected of running unauthorized additional production shifts to produce excess units of a device for sale outside the authorized channel.

steps.title: Gather evidence of unauthorized overproduction
steps.desc: Collect evidence supporting the suspicion, such as component-order volumes exceeding authorized production quantities, whistleblower tips, or excess units observed in gray markets.
steps.guidance: Compare component purchase orders and BOM quantities against the authorized production volume for the contract.
steps.abort: If evidence does not support the suspicion, close the case with findings documented.

steps.title: Engage legal/IP counsel to assess contractual exposure
steps.desc: Review the manufacturing contract's exclusivity, quantity, and IP-protection clauses with legal counsel to determine what remedies are available.
steps.outcome: Legal assessment of contract violations and available remedies.

steps.title: Identify units in the gray/counterfeit market
steps.desc: Search resale marketplaces, distributors, and industry-monitoring sources for units matching the suspected overproduction that should not be in circulation.
steps.guidance: Note serial numbers or batch codes for correlation with legitimate production records.
steps.outcome: Gray-market units identified and cataloged where present.

steps.title: Formally notify the contract manufacturer
steps.desc: Issue a formal notice to the contract manufacturer citing the suspected unauthorized production and requesting immediate cessation and an audit.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with legal counsel on the notice's wording to preserve contractual and legal remedies.
steps.outcome: Manufacturer is formally notified and put on record.

steps.title: Request an independent production audit
steps.desc: Exercise contractual audit rights to have an independent auditor review the manufacturer's production records, component inventory, and shift logs.
steps.outcome: Independent audit confirms or refutes unauthorized production.
steps.abort: If the manufacturer refuses audit access, treat as a material breach and escalate legally.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedy and contract enforcement
steps.desc: Based on audit findings, pursue contractual remedies, damages, or contract termination with the manufacturer through legal counsel.
steps.outcome: Legal action or remedy is pursued per audit findings.

steps.title: Coordinate with customs/law enforcement on unauthorized units
steps.desc: Where unauthorized units have entered commerce, coordinate with customs and law enforcement for interdiction under counterfeit/IP-theft statutes.
steps.outcome: Interdiction efforts underway for identified unauthorized units.

steps.title: Transition production to a verified-compliant manufacturer if needed
steps.desc: If the relationship cannot be adequately secured, plan and execute a transition to an alternate contract manufacturer.
steps.outcome: Production continuity is maintained under a trustworthy arrangement.

steps.title: Strengthen contract-manufacturer oversight controls
steps.desc: Implement stronger production-volume monitoring, component-reconciliation audits, and unannounced audit rights in future manufacturing contracts.

ITID-63312.def: The unauthorized reproduction of a device's design, intellectual property, or trade dress by a manufacturer that has no legitimate authorization from the design owner, with the resulting devices sold as if they were genuine or equivalent.
ITID-63312.purpose: Captures a device's design or intellectual property being cloned by an unauthorized third-party manufacturer with no legitimate production relationship, and sold as counterfeit.
scopeIncludes: Reverse-engineering and manufacture of a device design by an unrelated, unauthorized party
Sale of a cloned device using the design owner's branding, trade dress, or model numbers without authorization
scopeExcludes: Overproduction by an otherwise-authorized contract manufacturer (ITID-63311)
A cloned device carrying a duplicated serial number/IMEI matching a genuine unit (ITID-63313, a more specific identifier-collision variant)
ITID-63312.severity: Medium-High. Cloned devices typically lack the design owner's security, quality, and update mechanisms, creating both brand and technical risk.
ITID-63312.priority: P2 on discovery; escalate to P1 if cloned devices are found deployed within the organization's own environment.
ITID-63312.escalation: Escalate to legal (IP enforcement), procurement/supply-chain risk, and product security engineering.
indicators: Device passes a visual/branding inspection but fails deeper technical or firmware verification
Device sourced from a channel with no relationship to the authorized manufacturer
Reports of counterfeit units in the market bearing the organization's branding
vectors: Reverse-engineering of a device's design/firmware to produce an unauthorized clone
Sale of cloned units through unauthorized retail or online marketplace channels
rootCauses: Insufficient anti-counterfeiting/authentication features embedded in the genuine device design
No active brand-protection/marketplace-monitoring program
Weak IP protection enforcement in the manufacturing jurisdiction
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Embedded anti-counterfeiting/authentication features in the genuine device design
Active brand-protection and marketplace-monitoring program
Legal IP enforcement action against confirmed cloning operations
ITID-63312.detection: Detection is primarily a brand-protection/procurement function; SOC visibility is limited unless a cloned device surfaces within the organization's own environment.
ITID-63312.response: Verify authenticity, pursue IP enforcement action, and check whether any cloned units have entered the organization's own procurement or deployment.
metrics: Number of confirmed device-cloning incidents identified per year
Percentage of genuine devices with active anti-counterfeiting features
sops: Hardware Receiving and Authenticity Verification SOP
Brand Protection and IP Enforcement Procedure
detections: Firmware/authenticity verification checks on suspect devices
ITID-63312.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is design/IP cloning by an unrelated unauthorized manufacturer, distinct from overproduction by an authorized partner (ITID-63311) and identifier-duplication cloning (ITID-63313).

playbook.name: Device Design/IP Cloned and Sold as Counterfeit by Unauthorized Manufacturer
playbook.description: An unauthorized manufacturer has cloned the organization's device design or intellectual property and is selling counterfeit units.

steps.title: Obtain and document a sample of the cloned device
steps.desc: Acquire a sample unit of the cloned device (via test purchase or seizure) and document its similarities to the genuine design.
steps.guidance: Use a controlled test purchase through legal counsel's guidance to preserve chain of custody for potential litigation.
steps.outcome: Documented sample with comparative evidence against the genuine design.

steps.title: Engage legal/IP counsel to assess infringement
steps.desc: Have IP counsel assess patent, trademark, copyright, or trade-secret infringement based on the cloned device's design and construction.
steps.outcome: Legal determination of infringement basis and available remedies.

steps.title: Identify the unauthorized manufacturer and distribution channels
steps.desc: Investigate the source of the cloned devices, including the manufacturer, distributors, and marketplaces selling the counterfeit units.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with brand-protection investigators or specialized counterfeit-investigation firms if internal resources are insufficient.

steps.title: Issue cease-and-desist and takedown requests
steps.desc: Send cease-and-desist notices to the unauthorized manufacturer and takedown requests to marketplaces/distributors selling the cloned devices.
steps.outcome: Cloned devices are removed from identified sales channels where takedowns succeed.

steps.title: Coordinate with customs/law enforcement for interdiction
steps.desc: File reports with customs and law enforcement (including IP-crime units) to interdict shipments of counterfeit units and pursue the unauthorized manufacturer.

steps.title: Pursue litigation or formal legal action
steps.desc: Initiate litigation against the unauthorized manufacturer and identified distributors for IP infringement, in coordination with legal counsel.
steps.outcome: Legal action filed and pursued to conclusion.

steps.title: Alert customers and channel partners to counterfeit risk
steps.desc: Communicate with customers and authorized channel partners about the cloned device and how to identify genuine units.
steps.outcome: Customers/partners informed and equipped to identify counterfeits.

steps.title: Assess and address brand/market impact
steps.desc: Evaluate the reputational and revenue impact of the cloning and implement remediation such as authenticity-verification tools for customers.
steps.guidance: Consider deploying serialized authentication features for future genuine products.
steps.outcome: Impact assessed and remediation measures implemented.

steps.title: Strengthen IP protection and anti-cloning measures
steps.desc: Review design-protection practices (patents, trade secrets, anti-cloning hardware features) and strengthen them based on findings.

ITID-63313.def: A cloned or counterfeit device programmed with a serial number, IMEI, or other unique identifier copied from a genuine unit, enabling it to pass identity-based validation checks or to impersonate the genuine device on a network.
ITID-63313.purpose: Captures a cloned device carrying a duplicated serial number or IMEI matching a genuine unit, introduced into the supply chain or network.
scopeIncludes: A device with a duplicated IMEI enabling network registration or fraud
A cloned device programmed with a copied serial number to pass asset/warranty validation
Multiple devices in circulation sharing the same unique identifier
scopeExcludes: General design/IP cloning without an identifier-duplication element (ITID-63312)
Overproduction by an authorized contract manufacturer using legitimately issued identifiers (ITID-63311)
ITID-63313.severity: High. Identifier duplication can enable network fraud, evade asset tracking, and complicate incident attribution.
ITID-63313.priority: P1 on confirmed identifier collision affecting production network or asset-management systems.
ITID-63313.escalation: Escalate to network/fraud operations, asset management, and legal; block or flag the duplicated identifier across all systems.
indicators: Asset management or network system detects two devices reporting the same serial/IMEI
Warranty or support system flags a duplicate identifier claim
Unexpected device behavior traced to an identifier collision
vectors: Cloning of a genuine device's identifier during unauthorized manufacture
Reprogramming a counterfeit device's identifier fields to match a genuine unit
rootCauses: Weak or absent identifier-uniqueness validation in network/asset systems
Identifier issuance process not adequately protected against cloning
No cross-checking of identifiers against the design owner's authoritative production records
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Identifier-uniqueness validation in network registration and asset-management systems
Cross-checking of device identifiers against authoritative production records
Cryptographic device-identity attestation where supported by the device class
ITID-63313.detection: Detection has a real technical signal here: network and asset-management systems can flag duplicate-identifier collisions programmatically.
ITID-63313.response: Flag and quarantine both/all devices sharing the duplicated identifier, verify authenticity of each, and investigate the source of the counterfeit unit.
metrics: Number of identifier-collision incidents detected per year
Time from collision detection to resolution
Percentage of device classes with identifier-uniqueness validation enabled
sops: Hardware Receiving and Authenticity Verification SOP
detections: Duplicate serial/IMEI detection in network registration and asset-management systems
ITID-63313.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is the identifier-duplication variant of cloning, distinguishable from ITID-63312 (design/IP cloning generally) by its real, system-detectable technical signal.

playbook.name: Cloned Device with Duplicate Serial Number/IMEI Introduced into Supply Chain
playbook.description: A device bearing a duplicate serial number or IMEI matching a legitimately issued unit has been introduced into the supply chain or network.

steps.title: Confirm the serial/IMEI duplication
steps.desc: Verify that two or more devices share the same serial number or IMEI by cross-checking the manufacturing/provisioning database.
steps.guidance: Check for simultaneous or overlapping activation/registration events for the duplicated identifier.
steps.outcome: Duplication confirmed with both devices identified.
steps.abort: If it is a database error rather than a physical duplicate device, correct the record and close.

steps.title: Determine which device is genuine
steps.desc: Use manufacturing records, physical inspection, and OEM verification to determine which unit is the legitimate original and which is the clone.
steps.outcome: Genuine and cloned units are distinguished.

steps.title: Assess network/service exposure from the cloned device
steps.desc: Determine what network access, services, or data the cloned device may have accessed using the duplicated identity.
steps.guidance: Review authentication and network logs tied to the duplicated identifier.
steps.outcome: Scope of exposure from the cloned device's activity is documented.

steps.title: Revoke or block the cloned device's network/service access
steps.desc: Block the cloned unit from network or service access using the duplicated identifier.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with network/telecom operations if the identifier is used for carrier-level authentication.
steps.outcome: Cloned device can no longer access services under the duplicated identity.

steps.title: Re-provision the genuine device with a verified identifier
steps.desc: Ensure the legitimate device retains uninterrupted, exclusive use of its identifier, re-provisioning if necessary.
steps.outcome: Genuine device operates normally with sole claim to its identifier.

steps.title: Investigate the source of the cloned identifier
steps.desc: Trace how the cloned device obtained the duplicated serial/IMEI (manufacturing leak, database breach, or physical cloning of a genuine unit).

steps.title: Report to law enforcement/regulator where applicable
steps.desc: For IMEI cloning, report to the relevant telecom regulator or law-enforcement body responsible for device-identity fraud.

steps.title: Audit for additional duplicate identifiers
steps.desc: Scan the broader device/identifier database for other potential duplications stemming from the same source.
steps.outcome: Confirmation of whether the issue is isolated or systemic.

steps.title: Strengthen identifier provisioning and validation controls
steps.desc: Review and strengthen controls preventing duplicate identifier issuance or cloning in manufacturing and provisioning systems.

ITID-63314.def: General or not-yet-classified reports of unauthorized device cloning encountered in manufacturing or the supply chain.
ITID-63314.purpose: Intake bucket for unauthorized device cloning that does not fit overproduction, design/IP cloning, or identifier-duplication leaves.
scopeIncludes: Cloning reports where the specific mechanism is not yet determined
Novel or mixed cloning patterns not covered by the more specific leaves
scopeExcludes: Unauthorized overproduction by a contract manufacturer (ITID-63311)
Design/IP cloning by an unauthorized manufacturer (ITID-63312)
Identifier-duplication cloning (ITID-63313)
ITID-63314.priority: P2 pending triage; re-prioritize once the specific mechanism is known.
ITID-63314.escalation: Escalate to procurement/supply-chain risk and legal for triage; reclassify to a specific leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.
indicators: Cloning evidence not yet attributed to a specific known pattern
vectors: Unclassified device-cloning technique pending investigation
rootCauses: Gaps in manufacturing-partner oversight and authenticity verification generally
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: General hardware authenticity verification and manufacturing-partner audit program
ITID-63314.detection: Varies by mechanism; primarily a procurement/brand-protection function pending triage.
ITID-63314.response: Triage the report and reclassify to a specific leaf once the cloning mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Count of general device-cloning reports pending triage
Percentage subsequently reclassified
sops: Hardware Receiving and Authenticity Verification SOP
detections: Firmware/authenticity verification checks on suspect devices
ITID-63314.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf for the Unauthorized Cloning of Devices Tier-4 group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Unauthorized Device Cloning
playbook.description: A device is suspected of being an unauthorized clone of unspecified type introduced into the supply chain or market.

steps.title: Document evidence of suspected cloning
steps.desc: Gather available evidence supporting the suspicion that a device is an unauthorized clone.

steps.title: Engage legal/IP counsel and technical verification
steps.desc: Assess the device against genuine design/IP with legal and technical experts to confirm cloning.
steps.outcome: Cloning confirmed or refuted with documented basis.
steps.abort: If not confirmed, close the case with findings documented.

steps.title: Identify source and distribution of cloned units
steps.desc: Investigate the manufacturer and distribution channels responsible for the cloned units.

steps.title: Issue cease-and-desist / takedown requests
steps.desc: Send legal notices to the responsible party and takedown requests to sales channels.
steps.outcome: Cloned units removed from identified channels where takedowns succeed.

steps.title: Coordinate with law enforcement/customs where warranted
steps.desc: Report to law enforcement or customs for interdiction and investigation of the cloning operation.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedy against responsible parties
steps.desc: Initiate legal action for IP infringement or fraud against the manufacturer/distributor of the cloned units.
steps.outcome: Legal action pursued per counsel's recommendation.

steps.title: Notify affected customers/partners
steps.desc: Inform affected customers and partners of the cloning issue and how to identify genuine devices.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders informed and equipped to identify genuine units.

steps.title: Strengthen anti-cloning and IP protection measures
steps.desc: Review and enhance design-protection and anti-counterfeiting measures for the product line.

ITID-63411.def: The duplication of a legitimate RFID tag's identifier onto a cloned tag or device, used to make an unauthorized item removal appear as an authorized/tracked movement, or to bypass RFID-based exit alarms.
ITID-63411.purpose: Captures the cloning of RFID tags to enable unauthorized removal of inventory from a warehouse or storage facility without triggering tracking or alarm systems.
scopeIncludes: Cloned RFID tags used to disguise unauthorized removal of inventory as a legitimate scan
Use of an RFID cloning device near legitimate tags to harvest identifiers for later reuse
scopeExcludes: Barcode swap fraud, a visually-driven rather than RF-driven technique (ITID-63412)
Asset tag spoofing used to evade inventory tracking generally, without an RFID-cloning element specifically (ITID-63413)
ITID-63411.severity: Medium-High, scaled to the value of inventory at risk.
ITID-63411.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 for high-value inventory categories.
ITID-63411.escalation: Escalate to loss prevention/physical security; reconcile physical inventory against RFID system records for the affected zone.
indicators: RFID system shows a tag scan with no corresponding physical inventory movement (or vice versa)
Physical inventory count discrepancy against RFID-tracked records
Discovery of RFID-cloning equipment during a facility sweep
vectors: Use of an RFID cloning/skimming device to copy a legitimate tag's identifier
Reuse of a cloned tag to mask unauthorized removal as a routine tracked movement
rootCauses: Use of RFID tags without cryptographic authentication (clonable, read-only identifiers)
Insufficient reconciliation between RFID scan logs and physical inventory counts
Lack of exit-point RFID/physical inventory cross-checking
controls: Use of cryptographically authenticated RFID tags where inventory value warrants it
Regular reconciliation of RFID scan logs against physical inventory counts
Exit-point verification combining RFID and physical/visual inspection for high-value items
ITID-63411.detection: Physical/operational security incident — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and loss-prevention channels.
ITID-63411.response: Reconcile physical inventory against RFID records, sweep for cloning equipment, and review exit-point controls for the affected zone.
metrics: Number of RFID-cloning incidents detected per quarter
Inventory shrinkage value attributed to RFID cloning
Percentage of high-value inventory using cryptographically authenticated tags
ITID-63411.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is specifically RFID tag cloning, distinct from barcode swap fraud (ITID-63412) and general asset tag spoofing (ITID-63413).

playbook.name: RFID Tag Cloning for Unauthorized Inventory Removal
playbook.description: RFID tags on inventory items have been cloned or spoofed to enable unauthorized removal of goods from a warehouse or storage facility without triggering detection.

steps.title: Confirm RFID cloning/spoofing activity
steps.desc: Analyze RFID read logs for anomalies consistent with cloned tags — duplicate tag IDs read at implausible locations/times, or tags failing cryptographic authentication checks if supported.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference RFID system alerts with physical inventory discrepancies.
steps.outcome: Cloning/spoofing activity confirmed with affected tag IDs identified.
steps.abort: If discrepancies trace to a system error rather than cloning, correct and close.

steps.title: Reconcile physical inventory against RFID records
steps.desc: Perform a physical inventory count of affected items and compare against RFID system records to quantify actual loss.

steps.title: Review facility access and exit-point footage
steps.desc: Review CCTV and access logs at facility exit points during the window when cloned-tag activity occurred.
steps.outcome: Evidence of the removal method and, where possible, responsible party identified.

steps.title: Flag and isolate affected tag ranges
steps.desc: Mark the affected RFID tag ID ranges as compromised in the inventory system to prevent further use of cloned tags.
steps.outcome: Compromised tag ranges are flagged and monitored.

steps.title: Notify physical security and loss-prevention teams
steps.desc: Escalate to physical security/loss-prevention for heightened monitoring of the affected facility.
steps.outcome: Physical security engaged with enhanced monitoring in place.

steps.title: Re-tag affected inventory with secure RFID tags
steps.desc: Replace vulnerable or compromised RFID tags with tags using stronger anti-cloning features (cryptographic authentication where supported).
steps.outcome: Affected inventory is re-tagged with secure tags.

steps.title: Notify law enforcement if theft is confirmed
steps.desc: File a report with law enforcement for confirmed theft enabled by tag cloning.

steps.title: Reconcile inventory and update records
steps.desc: Finalize inventory reconciliation and update records to reflect confirmed losses.
steps.outcome: Inventory records accurately reflect the incident's impact.

steps.title: Strengthen RFID system security
steps.desc: Review RFID system design for anti-cloning weaknesses and implement stronger authentication, tag-read anomaly detection, or exit-point verification.

ITID-63412.def: The deliberate replacement or alteration of a barcode label on a physical item so that it scans as a different, typically lower-value, item or price, enabling fraudulent purchase, shipment, or inventory records.
ITID-63412.purpose: Captures barcode swap fraud, in which a barcode label is deliberately swapped or altered to misrepresent an item's price or identity.
scopeIncludes: Swapping a lower-price item's barcode onto a higher-value item
Applying a counterfeit or altered barcode label to misrepresent item identity during receiving or shipping
scopeExcludes: RFID tag cloning, a distinct RF-based technique (ITID-63411)
General asset tag spoofing for inventory-tracking evasion without a price/identity substitution element (ITID-63413)
ITID-63412.severity: Medium, scaled to the frequency and value of the substitution fraud.
ITID-63412.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the pattern indicates organized/repeated fraud at scale.
ITID-63412.escalation: Escalate to loss prevention; review point-of-scan footage and transaction records for the affected location.
indicators: Scanned item description/price inconsistent with physical item on manual verification
Repeated low-value scans for a category with historically higher shrinkage
Barcode label showing signs of physical tampering or replacement
vectors: Physical replacement of a genuine barcode label with a counterfeit or mismatched one
Printing and applying a fraudulent barcode label to a higher-value item
rootCauses: No random manual verification of scanned item vs. physical item
Insufficient tamper-evidence on barcode labeling for high-value items
Lack of anomaly detection on scan-price/weight discrepancies
mitreTechniques: T1565.001 Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation
controls: Random manual verification of scanned item against physical item for high-value categories
Tamper-evident barcode labeling for high-shrinkage item categories
Anomaly detection on scan-price/weight discrepancies at point of scan
ITID-63412.detection: Physical/operational security incident — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and loss-prevention channels.
ITID-63412.response: Review footage and transaction records for the affected location, identify the scope of the substitution pattern, and refer for loss-prevention/law enforcement action.
metrics: Number of barcode-swap incidents detected per quarter
Shrinkage value attributed to barcode-swap fraud
ITID-63412.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is barcode-based price/identity substitution, distinct from RFID cloning (ITID-63411) and general asset tag spoofing (ITID-63413).

playbook.name: Barcode Swap Fraud (Price/Item Substitution)
playbook.description: Barcodes on inventory items have been swapped or substituted to misrepresent item identity or price, enabling fraud.

steps.title: Confirm barcode substitution
steps.desc: Physically inspect flagged items to confirm barcode labels do not match the actual product, and identify the substituted barcode source.
steps.outcome: Barcode substitution confirmed with details documented.
steps.abort: If mismatch is a labeling error rather than fraud, correct and close.

steps.title: Quantify scope and financial impact
steps.desc: Review transaction and inventory records to determine how many items were affected and the resulting financial loss.

steps.title: Review access and handling records for the affected items
steps.desc: Identify who had access to the affected items and barcode-printing/labeling equipment during the relevant period.
steps.outcome: Candidate responsible parties or access points identified.

steps.title: Remove affected items from sale/use pending relabeling
steps.desc: Pull affected items from circulation until correctly relabeled and verified.
steps.outcome: Affected items are out of circulation with no further fraudulent transactions.

steps.title: Notify loss-prevention/physical security team
steps.desc: Escalate to loss-prevention for investigation and, if an employee is implicated, coordination with HR.

steps.title: Relabel and verify affected inventory
steps.desc: Correctly relabel all affected items and verify against the inventory system before returning to circulation.
steps.outcome: All affected items correctly labeled and verified.

steps.title: Take disciplinary/legal action against responsible party
steps.desc: Where an internal or external responsible party is identified, pursue disciplinary action (via HR) or law-enforcement referral as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Appropriate action taken against the responsible party.

steps.title: Reconcile financial and inventory records
steps.desc: Confirm financial and inventory records are corrected to reflect the true impact of the fraud.

steps.title: Strengthen barcode/label security controls
steps.desc: Review barcode label security (tamper-evident labels, restricted label-printer access) and update controls to prevent recurrence.

ITID-63413.def: The deliberate falsification, duplication, or removal of an asset tag so that an item's presence, location, or status in the inventory-tracking system no longer reflects reality, enabling the item to go unaccounted-for.
ITID-63413.purpose: Captures the spoofing or manipulation of an asset tag to evade inventory tracking systems generally, distinct from a price-substitution or RFID-cloning motive specifically.
scopeIncludes: Removing or defacing an asset tag so an item cannot be tracked or reconciled
Applying an asset tag from a different, decommissioned item to conceal an item's true status
Manipulating asset-tag data in the tracking system independent of the physical tag itself
scopeExcludes: RFID tag cloning specifically (ITID-63411)
Barcode-based price/identity substitution specifically (ITID-63412)
ITID-63413.severity: Medium, scaled to the value and sensitivity of the affected asset class.
ITID-63413.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 for high-value or sensitive asset categories.
ITID-63413.escalation: Escalate to loss prevention and asset management; reconcile the affected asset class against physical inventory.
indicators: Asset tag missing, defaced, or inconsistent with the tracking system record
Tracking system shows a status (e.g., decommissioned) inconsistent with the item's physical presence
Physical audit discrepancy against the asset-tracking database
vectors: Physical removal/defacement of an asset tag to break traceability
Reassignment of a tag from a decommissioned item to conceal an active item's true status
rootCauses: Infrequent physical asset audits against the tracking system
Asset tags lacking tamper-evidence
Insufficient reconciliation between decommissioning records and physical disposal
mitreTechniques: T1565.001 Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation
controls: Regular physical asset audits reconciled against the tracking system
Tamper-evident asset tagging for high-value categories
Reconciliation controls between decommissioning records and physical disposal
ITID-63413.detection: Physical/operational security incident — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and loss-prevention channels.
ITID-63413.response: Reconcile the affected asset class against physical inventory, investigate the specific tag manipulation, and refer for loss-prevention action.
metrics: Number of asset tag spoofing incidents detected per quarter
Physical audit discrepancy rate against the tracking system
ITID-63413.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is general asset-tag manipulation for tracking evasion, distinct from the RFID-cloning (ITID-63411) and barcode-substitution (ITID-63412) specific mechanisms.

playbook.name: Asset Tag Spoofing to Evade Inventory Tracking
playbook.description: Asset tags on equipment or goods have been spoofed or manipulated to evade inventory tracking systems, concealing unauthorized movement or removal.

steps.title: Confirm asset tag spoofing
steps.desc: Inspect flagged assets to confirm tag manipulation (swapped, duplicated, or falsified tags) and identify the extent of tracking evasion.
steps.outcome: Spoofing confirmed with affected assets identified.
steps.abort: If discrepancy is a data-entry error, correct and close.

steps.title: Reconcile physical assets against tracking records
steps.desc: Perform a physical audit of affected assets and reconcile against the inventory/asset-tracking system.
steps.outcome: Discrepancies between physical assets and records quantified.

steps.title: Review access and handling records
steps.desc: Identify who had access to the affected assets and tagging equipment during the relevant period.
steps.outcome: Candidate responsible parties or access points identified.

steps.title: Flag affected assets and restrict further movement
steps.desc: Mark affected assets in the tracking system and restrict their movement pending investigation.
steps.outcome: Affected assets flagged with no further undetected movement.

steps.title: Notify loss-prevention/physical security team
steps.desc: Escalate to loss-prevention for investigation and coordination with HR if an insider is implicated.

steps.title: Re-tag and re-verify affected assets
steps.desc: Replace compromised tags with new, verified tags and confirm asset identity against records.
steps.outcome: Affected assets correctly re-tagged and verified.

steps.title: Pursue disciplinary or legal action where warranted
steps.desc: Take appropriate action against any identified responsible party via HR or law enforcement.

steps.title: Reconcile asset records
steps.desc: Confirm asset tracking records are corrected to reflect verified physical status.

steps.title: Strengthen asset tagging security
steps.desc: Review and strengthen tag security (tamper-evident tags, periodic physical audits) to prevent recurrence.

ITID-63414.def: General or not-yet-classified reports of tag-based inventory-tracking spoofing encountered in a warehouse or storage facility.
ITID-63414.purpose: Intake bucket for RFID/barcode/asset tag spoofing incidents that do not fit the RFID-cloning, barcode-swap, or asset-tag leaves.
scopeIncludes: Tag-spoofing reports where the specific mechanism is not yet determined
Novel or mixed tag-spoofing patterns not covered by the more specific leaves
scopeExcludes: RFID tag cloning (ITID-63411)
Barcode swap fraud (ITID-63412)
General asset tag spoofing (ITID-63413)
