ITID-63414.priority: P3 pending triage; re-prioritize once the specific mechanism is known.
ITID-63414.escalation: Escalate to loss prevention for triage; reclassify to a specific leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.
indicators: Tag-spoofing evidence not yet attributed to a specific known pattern
vectors: Unclassified tag-spoofing technique pending investigation
rootCauses: Gaps in inventory-tracking reconciliation generally
mitreTechniques: T1565.001 Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation
controls: General inventory-tracking reconciliation and audit program
ITID-63414.detection: Physical/operational security incident — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and loss-prevention channels.
ITID-63414.response: Triage the report and reclassify to a specific leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Count of general tag-spoofing reports pending triage
Percentage subsequently reclassified
ITID-63414.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf for the RFID, Barcode, and Asset Tag Spoofing Tier-4 group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General RFID/Barcode/Asset Tag Spoofing
playbook.description: A tracking-tag spoofing incident of unspecified type (RFID, barcode, or asset tag) has been detected in inventory or asset tracking systems.

steps.title: Confirm tag spoofing activity
steps.desc: Investigate the reported anomaly to confirm tag spoofing/manipulation and identify affected items.
steps.outcome: Spoofing confirmed with affected items identified.
steps.abort: If not confirmed, correct any data error and close.

steps.title: Reconcile physical inventory/assets against tracking records
steps.desc: Perform a physical audit and compare against tracking system records to quantify discrepancies.

steps.title: Review access records for the affected items/area
steps.desc: Identify who had access to the affected items and tagging systems during the relevant period.
steps.outcome: Candidate responsible parties or access points identified.

steps.title: Flag affected items and restrict movement
steps.desc: Mark affected items/assets and restrict further movement pending investigation.
steps.outcome: No further undetected movement of affected items.

steps.title: Notify loss-prevention/physical security team
steps.desc: Escalate to loss-prevention for investigation.

steps.title: Re-tag and verify affected items
steps.desc: Replace compromised tags and verify item identity against records before returning to normal use.

steps.title: Reconcile tracking records
steps.desc: Confirm tracking records are corrected to reflect verified status.

steps.title: Strengthen tag/label security controls
steps.desc: Review and strengthen tagging/labeling security across RFID, barcode, and asset-tag systems.

ITID-63421.def: The act of an unauthorized individual gaining physical entry to a secure warehouse or storage facility by following closely behind an authorized person through a controlled access point, without presenting their own valid credential.
ITID-63421.purpose: Captures tailgating (piggybacking) into a secure warehouse facility, where an unauthorized person follows an authorized person through an access-controlled entry point.
scopeIncludes: An unauthorized individual following an employee through a badge-controlled door
Deliberate holding of a secure door open for an unverified follower
scopeExcludes: Entry using a compromised or stolen access badge (ITID-63422)
Unauthorized access gained through a technical bypass of the access-control system rather than social/physical piggybacking
ITID-63421.severity: Medium, scaled to the sensitivity of the facility and what the individual accessed once inside.
ITID-63421.priority: P2 on confirmed tailgating; escalate to P1 if the individual is found in a high-value or restricted zone.
ITID-63421.escalation: Escalate to physical security immediately; locate and challenge the unauthorized individual and review footage for the entry point.
indicators: Access-control logs showing a single badge scan followed by two people entering on camera
Employee report of an unfamiliar person following them through a secure door
Occupancy count mismatch between badge-in records and physical headcount
vectors: Following an employee closely through a badge-controlled door
Social engineering an employee into holding the door open
rootCauses: No employee training/culture around challenging unbadged individuals
Lack of mantrap or anti-tailgating physical controls at high-value entry points
Insufficient video monitoring/analytics at entry points
controls: Anti-tailgating physical controls (mantraps, turnstiles) at high-value entry points
Employee training to challenge unbadged individuals
Video analytics correlating badge scans to headcount at entry points
ITID-63421.detection: Physical/operational security incident — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and loss-prevention channels.
ITID-63421.response: Locate and identify the unauthorized individual, review footage and access logs, and assess what areas/inventory were accessed.
metrics: Number of confirmed tailgating incidents per quarter
Percentage of high-value entry points with anti-tailgating controls
ITID-63421.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is social/physical piggybacking through a legitimate access point, distinct from use of a compromised badge (ITID-63422).

playbook.name: Tailgating into Secure Warehouse Facility
playbook.description: An unauthorized individual gained physical entry to a secure warehouse facility by tailgating an authorized employee through an access-controlled door.

steps.title: Confirm the tailgating event via access logs and CCTV
steps.desc: Review badge-access logs and CCTV footage to confirm an unauthorized entry occurred and identify the individual if possible.
steps.guidance: Look for badge-in events with two people passing on a single credential swipe.
steps.outcome: Tailgating event confirmed with footage/log evidence.
steps.abort: If no unauthorized entry is confirmed, close as a false alarm.

steps.title: Determine areas accessed and time inside the facility
steps.desc: Trace the intruder's movement through the facility using internal CCTV and any interior access-point logs.
steps.outcome: Full path and dwell time of the unauthorized individual documented.

steps.title: Assess for theft, tampering, or reconnaissance
steps.desc: Inspect areas accessed by the intruder for signs of theft, tampering, or surveillance activity (e.g., photographs of inventory or security systems).
steps.outcome: Determination of what, if anything, was compromised.

steps.title: Alert on-site physical security/facilities team
steps.desc: Notify facilities and physical security personnel to search the premises for the intruder and secure the facility.
steps.outcome: Facility is confirmed clear and secured.

steps.title: Notify law enforcement if warranted
steps.desc: File a trespassing report with law enforcement, particularly if theft or tampering is suspected.

steps.title: Reinforce entry-point controls to prevent recurrence
steps.desc: Address the specific physical control gap that allowed tailgating (e.g., door propping, lack of mantrap, insufficient guard presence).
steps.guidance: Consider anti-tailgating technology (turnstiles, sensors) for high-value facilities.

steps.title: Reinforce employee security-awareness training
steps.desc: Conduct refresher training for facility staff on tailgating risks and the obligation to challenge unbadged individuals.

steps.title: Confirm no residual impact and resume normal operations
steps.desc: Confirm inventory and security systems are intact and the facility has returned to normal operating status.
steps.outcome: Facility confirmed secure and operating normally.

steps.title: Review physical access control design
steps.desc: Assess whether structural or procedural changes are needed to prevent future tailgating incidents.
steps.outcome: Updated physical access control requirements documented.

ITID-63422.def: The use of a lost, stolen, cloned, or otherwise compromised physical access badge/credential to gain unauthorized entry to a secure warehouse or storage facility.
ITID-63422.purpose: Captures unauthorized warehouse entry achieved through a compromised, stolen, or cloned access badge.
scopeIncludes: Use of a stolen or lost employee badge to gain entry
Use of a cloned/copied badge credential (e.g., via a proximity-card skimmer)
Continued use of a terminated employee's badge that was not deactivated
scopeExcludes: Tailgating/piggybacking through an access point without presenting any credential (ITID-63421)
ITID-63422.severity: Medium-High, scaled to the sensitivity of the facility and how long the compromised badge remained active.
ITID-63422.priority: P2 on confirmed compromised-badge use; escalate to P1 if a terminated employee's badge was involved or high-value zones were accessed.
ITID-63422.escalation: Escalate to physical security and HR immediately; deactivate the compromised badge and review all access events associated with it.
indicators: Badge access logged at a time/location inconsistent with the credentialed employee's known whereabouts
Access event from a badge belonging to a terminated or on-leave employee
Multiple simultaneous access events on the same badge at different locations
vectors: Theft or loss of a physical access badge later used by an unauthorized party
Skimming/cloning of a proximity-card credential
Failure to deactivate a terminated employee's badge promptly
rootCauses: No timely deactivation process for lost/stolen or terminated-employee badges
Use of legacy proximity-card technology vulnerable to cloning
Lack of anomaly detection on badge-access patterns
controls: Timely badge deactivation process tied to HR offboarding and loss reporting
Use of cryptographically secure, non-clonable access credentials
Anomaly detection/alerting on badge-access patterns inconsistent with the credentialed employee's norms
ITID-63422.detection: Physical/operational security incident — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and loss-prevention channels.
ITID-63422.response: Deactivate the compromised badge immediately, review all associated access history, and identify what was accessed during the unauthorized entry window.
metrics: Number of compromised-badge incidents per quarter
Average time from employee termination to badge deactivation
ITID-63422.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf involves use of an actual (compromised) credential, distinct from credential-less tailgating (ITID-63421).

playbook.name: Compromised Access Badge Used for Unauthorized Warehouse Entry
playbook.description: A lost, stolen, or cloned access badge was used to gain unauthorized entry into a warehouse facility.

steps.title: Identify the compromised badge and confirm unauthorized use
steps.desc: Review badge-access logs to identify the specific credential used and confirm the access pattern is inconsistent with the authorized holder's known activity.
steps.guidance: Cross-check the badge holder's whereabouts (e.g., were they on leave, at another site) to confirm unauthorized use.
steps.outcome: Compromised badge and unauthorized access event confirmed.
steps.abort: If access is confirmed legitimate, close the case.

steps.title: Determine how the badge was compromised
steps.desc: Investigate whether the badge was lost, stolen, or cloned (e.g., via RFID skimming) to understand the compromise vector.
steps.guidance: Interview the badge holder and review any loss/theft reports on file.

steps.title: Determine areas accessed and potential impact
steps.desc: Trace the unauthorized entrant's movement and dwell time within the facility using CCTV and interior access logs.
steps.outcome: Scope of physical access and potential impact documented.

steps.title: Immediately deactivate the compromised badge
steps.desc: Revoke the compromised credential in the access control system to prevent further use.
steps.outcome: Badge is deactivated and can no longer grant access.

steps.title: Search the facility and secure premises
steps.desc: Coordinate with on-site security to search for the unauthorized individual and secure the premises.

steps.title: Notify law enforcement if theft or tampering is found
steps.desc: File a report with law enforcement if theft, tampering, or other criminal activity is confirmed.

steps.title: Reissue a new credential to the legitimate holder
steps.desc: Issue a replacement badge to the legitimate employee and ensure the old credential remains permanently deactivated.
steps.outcome: Legitimate holder has working access; old badge is void.

steps.title: Assess for and remediate any theft or tampering found
steps.desc: Address any confirmed theft, tampering, or other impact discovered during the investigation.

steps.title: Confirm facility security posture and resume normal operations
steps.desc: Verify the facility's access control system and physical security are functioning normally.
steps.outcome: Facility confirmed secure and operating normally.

steps.title: Strengthen badge security and loss-reporting procedures
steps.desc: Review badge technology (consider anti-cloning credentials) and reinforce prompt loss/theft reporting requirements for staff.
steps.outcome: Updated badge security and reporting procedures documented.

ITID-63423.def: General or not-yet-classified reports of unauthorized physical access to a warehouse or storage facility.
ITID-63423.purpose: Intake bucket for unauthorized storage-facility access incidents that do not fit tailgating or compromised-badge use.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized access reports where the specific entry method is not yet determined
Other physical access-control bypass methods not covered by the more specific leaves
scopeExcludes: Tailgating/piggybacking (ITID-63421)
Use of a compromised access badge (ITID-63422)
ITID-63423.priority: P2 pending triage; re-prioritize once the entry method and area accessed are known.
ITID-63423.escalation: Escalate to physical security for triage; reclassify to a specific leaf once the entry method is confirmed.
indicators: Unauthorized presence detected with entry method not yet determined
vectors: Unclassified physical access-control bypass technique pending investigation
rootCauses: Gaps in physical access-control monitoring generally
controls: General physical access-control monitoring and audit program
ITID-63423.detection: Physical/operational security incident — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and loss-prevention channels.
ITID-63423.response: Triage the report and reclassify to a specific leaf once the entry method is confirmed.
metrics: Count of general unauthorized-access reports pending triage
Percentage subsequently reclassified
ITID-63423.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf for the Unauthorized Access to Storage Facilities Tier-4 group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Unauthorized Storage Facility Access
playbook.description: An unauthorized individual gained physical access to a storage facility by a method not otherwise classified.

steps.title: Confirm the unauthorized access event
steps.desc: Review access logs, CCTV, and physical evidence to confirm unauthorized entry occurred.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized access confirmed with supporting evidence.
steps.abort: If not confirmed, close as a false alarm.

steps.title: Determine access method and areas reached
steps.desc: Investigate how access was obtained and trace the individual's movement within the facility.
steps.outcome: Access method and scope of movement documented.

steps.title: Assess for theft, tampering, or reconnaissance
steps.desc: Inspect accessed areas for signs of theft, tampering, or surveillance activity.

steps.title: Secure the facility and close the access gap
steps.desc: Coordinate with facilities/security to secure the premises and close the specific gap that allowed entry.
steps.outcome: Facility secured with the access gap closed.

steps.title: Notify law enforcement if warranted
steps.desc: File a report with law enforcement if theft or criminal activity is confirmed.

steps.title: Remediate the specific control failure
steps.desc: Fix the underlying physical security control failure that enabled the unauthorized access.

steps.title: Confirm facility security and resume normal operations
steps.desc: Verify the facility is secure and operating normally.

steps.title: Review physical security controls
steps.desc: Assess and strengthen physical access controls for the facility to prevent recurrence.

ITID-63431.def: The deliberate alteration of inventory records — counts, movement logs, or reconciliation entries — to make stolen or missing goods appear accounted for, concealing an underlying theft.
ITID-63431.purpose: Captures deliberate falsification of inventory records to conceal theft or unauthorized removal of goods.
scopeIncludes: Falsifying a cycle-count record to hide a known shortage
Backdating or fabricating a movement/transfer record to explain missing stock
scopeExcludes: Manipulating the inventory system to fraudulently write off stock rather than conceal an existing theft (ITID-63432)
ITID-63431.severity: Medium-High, scaled to the value concealed and duration of the concealment.
ITID-63431.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the falsification is systemic or spans multiple reporting periods.
ITID-63431.escalation: Escalate to loss prevention, internal audit, and HR; preserve inventory system audit logs before further reconciliation activity.
indicators: Inventory record inconsistent with an independent physical count
Reconciliation entries made outside normal process timing or by an unauthorized user
Pattern of shortages consistently resolved by the same individual's adjustments
vectors: An employee with reconciliation access falsifying records to mask a known shortage
Backdating transfer/movement entries to explain a discrepancy
rootCauses: Insufficient segregation of duties between counting, reconciliation, and adjustment approval
No independent audit of reconciliation adjustments
Weak audit logging on inventory system record changes
mitreTechniques: T1565.001 Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation
controls: Segregation of duties between physical counting, reconciliation, and adjustment approval
Independent periodic audit of reconciliation adjustments
Immutable audit logging on inventory record changes
ITID-63431.detection: Physical/operational security incident — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and loss-prevention channels.
ITID-63431.response: Preserve system audit logs, conduct an independent physical recount, and investigate the individual(s) with reconciliation access during the affected period.
metrics: Number of confirmed inventory-falsification incidents per year
Value of shrinkage concealed
Percentage of reconciliation adjustments independently audited
ITID-63431.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is falsification to conceal an existing theft, distinct from fraudulent write-off manipulation (ITID-63432).

playbook.name: Inventory Record Falsification to Conceal Theft
playbook.description: Inventory records have been deliberately falsified to conceal theft of goods from a warehouse or storage facility.

steps.title: Confirm inventory record falsification
steps.desc: Perform a forensic-accounting-style reconciliation comparing physical inventory counts against system records to identify falsified entries.
steps.guidance: Look for adjustment entries, write-offs, or count overrides made outside normal process by a limited set of individuals.
steps.outcome: Falsification confirmed with specific discrepant records identified.
steps.abort: If discrepancies are due to legitimate process errors, correct and close.

steps.title: Quantify the scope of concealed theft
steps.desc: Determine the total value and quantity of goods stolen and concealed through the falsified records.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with finance for an accurate valuation.
steps.outcome: Full scope of concealed theft quantified.

steps.title: Identify who made the falsified entries
steps.desc: Review system audit trails to determine which user account(s) made the falsified adjustments.

steps.title: Restrict the implicated individual's system access
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict inventory-system access for the individual(s) implicated pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR before taking action against an employee.
steps.outcome: Implicated individual can no longer make inventory adjustments.

steps.title: Notify HR/Legal and law enforcement
steps.desc: Escalate the confirmed theft-and-falsification scheme to HR/Legal for disciplinary process and to law enforcement for criminal investigation.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal and law enforcement are engaged.

steps.title: Correct all falsified inventory records
steps.desc: Restore inventory records to reflect true, verified physical counts.
steps.guidance: Document each correction with supporting evidence for audit purposes.
steps.outcome: Inventory records corrected and verified accurate.

steps.title: Complete disciplinary/legal process against responsible party
steps.desc: Conclude the HR disciplinary process and support any law-enforcement prosecution of the responsible individual.

steps.title: Reconcile financial records and pursue recovery
steps.desc: Update financial records to reflect the loss and pursue recovery via insurance or restitution where possible.

steps.title: Strengthen inventory adjustment controls
steps.desc: Implement segregation-of-duties and approval requirements for inventory adjustments to prevent unilateral falsification.
steps.guidance: Consider requiring dual sign-off for write-offs above a threshold.

ITID-63432.def: The deliberate manipulation of inventory system write-off, damage, or obsolescence processes to remove stock from the books as a pretext for diverting it, rather than concealing a theft that has already occurred.
ITID-63432.purpose: Captures manipulation of the inventory system to fraudulently write off stock, enabling its removal without an accompanying theft-concealment record.
scopeIncludes: Fraudulently marking saleable stock as damaged/obsolete to justify its write-off and removal
Manipulating write-off approval workflows to bypass required review
scopeExcludes: Falsifying records to conceal a theft that already occurred (ITID-63431)
ITID-63432.severity: Medium-High, scaled to the value fraudulently written off.
ITID-63432.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the pattern is systemic or spans multiple locations.
ITID-63432.escalation: Escalate to loss prevention, internal audit, and HR; suspend write-off approval authority for implicated personnel pending investigation.
indicators: Write-off rate for a specific category/location statistically inconsistent with historical norms
Written-off stock not disposed of through the standard verified disposal channel
Write-off approvals concentrated in a single individual with no independent review
vectors: An employee with write-off authority marking saleable goods as damaged/obsolete
Bypassing or colluding to bypass required write-off approval controls
rootCauses: Insufficient segregation of duties in the write-off approval workflow
No verification requirement that written-off goods reach an approved disposal/destruction channel
Lack of statistical monitoring of write-off rates by location/individual
mitreTechniques: T1565.001 Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation
controls: Segregation of duties in write-off request, approval, and disposal verification
Statistical monitoring of write-off rates by location and approver
Verified disposal/destruction chain-of-custody for written-off goods
ITID-63432.detection: Physical/operational security incident — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and loss-prevention channels.
ITID-63432.response: Suspend the implicated approval authority, audit recent write-offs for the individual/location, and verify disposal chain-of-custody for flagged write-offs.
metrics: Write-off rate by location/approver against historical baseline
Value of fraudulent write-offs identified per year
ITID-63432.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is proactive manipulation of the write-off process itself, distinct from after-the-fact concealment of a theft (ITID-63431).

playbook.name: Inventory System Manipulation for Fraudulent Stock Write-Off
playbook.description: The inventory system was manipulated to fraudulently write off stock that was not actually lost, damaged, or obsolete, enabling diversion of the goods.

steps.title: Confirm fraudulent write-off activity
steps.desc: Reconcile write-off records against physical evidence (e.g., destruction certificates, actual damaged-goods disposal) to identify write-offs lacking legitimate basis.
steps.guidance: Focus on write-offs with missing or inconsistent supporting documentation.
steps.abort: If write-offs are legitimate, close the case.

steps.title: Quantify the scope of diverted stock
steps.desc: Determine the value and quantity of stock fraudulently written off and diverted.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with finance for valuation.

steps.title: Identify who authorized/executed the fraudulent write-offs
steps.desc: Review audit trails to determine responsible user account(s) and approval chain.

steps.title: Restrict write-off privileges for implicated accounts
steps.desc: Suspend inventory write-off authority for implicated individual(s) pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR before taking action.
steps.outcome: Implicated accounts can no longer authorize write-offs.

steps.title: Notify HR/Legal and law enforcement
steps.desc: Escalate to HR/Legal for disciplinary process and to law enforcement for criminal investigation.

steps.title: Reverse and correct fraudulent write-off records
steps.desc: Correct inventory and financial records to reverse the fraudulent write-offs.
steps.guidance: Document each correction with supporting evidence.

steps.title: Complete disciplinary/legal process
steps.desc: Conclude HR disciplinary action and support any law-enforcement prosecution.

steps.title: Pursue recovery and update financial records
steps.desc: Pursue recovery of diverted stock or its value and finalize financial record corrections.

steps.title: Strengthen write-off approval controls
steps.desc: Implement dual-approval and documentation requirements for stock write-offs to prevent unilateral fraudulent action.

ITID-63433.def: General or not-yet-classified reports of inventory data manipulation encountered in a warehouse or storage facility.
ITID-63433.purpose: Intake bucket for manipulated inventory data incidents that do not fit theft-concealment falsification or fraudulent write-off manipulation.
scopeIncludes: Inventory data manipulation reports where the specific mechanism is not yet determined
Novel or mixed inventory-manipulation patterns not covered by the more specific leaves
scopeExcludes: Falsification to conceal theft (ITID-63431)
Fraudulent write-off manipulation (ITID-63432)
ITID-63433.priority: P3 pending triage; re-prioritize once the specific mechanism and value are known.
ITID-63433.escalation: Escalate to internal audit/loss prevention for triage; reclassify to a specific leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.
indicators: Inventory data anomaly not yet attributed to a specific known pattern
vectors: Unclassified inventory-manipulation technique pending investigation
rootCauses: Gaps in inventory reconciliation and audit generally
mitreTechniques: T1565.001 Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation
controls: General inventory reconciliation and internal audit program
ITID-63433.detection: Physical/operational security incident — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and loss-prevention channels.
ITID-63433.response: Triage the report and reclassify to a specific leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Count of general inventory-manipulation reports pending triage
Percentage subsequently reclassified
ITID-63433.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf for the Manipulated Inventory Data Tier-4 group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Manipulated Inventory Data
playbook.description: Inventory data has been manipulated in a manner not otherwise classified, requiring forensic-accounting-style investigation.

steps.title: Confirm inventory data manipulation
steps.desc: Reconcile physical inventory against system records to confirm manipulation and identify affected records.
steps.outcome: Manipulation confirmed with affected records identified.
steps.abort: If discrepancies are legitimate process errors, correct and close.

steps.title: Quantify scope and impact
steps.desc: Determine the value and extent of the impact resulting from the manipulated data.

steps.title: Identify responsible party via audit trail review
steps.desc: Review system audit logs to determine which account(s) made the manipulated entries.

steps.title: Restrict implicated account access
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict system access for implicated individual(s) pending investigation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with HR as appropriate.

steps.title: Notify HR/Legal as appropriate
steps.desc: Escalate to HR/Legal for disciplinary process if an internal party is implicated.

steps.title: Correct manipulated inventory records
steps.desc: Restore inventory records to reflect verified accurate data.

steps.title: Reconcile and finalize records
steps.desc: Confirm all affected records are reconciled and accurate before closing the incident.

steps.title: Strengthen inventory data-integrity controls
steps.desc: Review and strengthen controls (audit logging, approval workflows) to prevent unauthorized inventory data manipulation.

ITID-63441.def: Malicious or negligent action by a warehouse employee or contractor that abuses their legitimate physical or system access to harm inventory integrity, security, or operations, not otherwise captured by the more specific access, inventory, or tag-spoofing leaves.
ITID-63441.purpose: Captures insider threat activity in a warehousing environment broadly, serving as the single leaf for this Tier-4 category pending future differentiation.
scopeIncludes: An employee abusing physical/system access for personal gain in ways not covered by the RFID/barcode, access-control, or inventory-data leaves
Collusion between warehouse staff to bypass security controls generally
scopeExcludes: RFID/barcode/asset tag spoofing (ITID-63411-63414)
Unauthorized facility access via tailgating or compromised badge (ITID-63421-63423)
Inventory data falsification/manipulation (ITID-63431-63433)
ITID-63441.severity: Medium-High, scaled to the scope and duration of the insider's access abuse.
ITID-63441.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 on confirmation of organized or high-value insider activity.
ITID-63441.escalation: Escalate to HR, legal, and physical security/loss prevention; suspend the individual's access pending investigation.
indicators: Behavioral or access-pattern anomalies inconsistent with the employee's normal role
Reports from co-workers or third parties of suspicious activity
Loss patterns correlated with a specific individual's shifts or access
vectors: An employee abusing legitimate physical or system access for personal or third-party gain
Collusion among warehouse staff to bypass standard security controls
rootCauses: Insufficient background vetting for warehouse personnel
Lack of behavioral/access anomaly monitoring in warehouse operations
Weak segregation of duties across physical and system access
controls: Background vetting for warehouse personnel
Behavioral/access anomaly monitoring
Segregation of duties across physical and system access in warehouse operations
ITID-63441.detection: Physical/operational security incident — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via physical security and loss-prevention channels.
ITID-63441.response: Investigate through HR and loss-prevention channels, suspend implicated personnel's access, and refer for law enforcement action where warranted.
metrics: Number of confirmed warehouse insider-threat incidents per year
Percentage of warehouse personnel with current background vetting
detections: Behavioral/access anomaly monitoring for warehouse personnel
ITID-63441.notes: This is currently the only leaf under Insider Threats in Warehousing and functions as the general/unclassified entry point; if a durable, distinct sub-pattern emerges it should be split into dedicated leaves in a future taxonomy revision.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Insider Threat in Warehousing
playbook.description: An employee within the organization's own warehousing operations is suspected of malicious insider activity of unspecified type.

steps.title: Document the suspected insider activity
steps.desc: Gather available evidence of the suspected insider's activity and its apparent impact on warehouse operations.

steps.title: Review access, inventory, and system logs tied to the individual
steps.desc: Correlate the individual's badge access, system activity, and inventory transactions with the suspected malicious activity.
steps.outcome: Evidence trail linking the individual to the activity documented.
steps.tool: Physical access control system / inventory management system

steps.title: Quantify scope of impact
steps.desc: Determine what goods, data, or operations were affected by the suspected insider's actions.

steps.title: Restrict the individual's access pending investigation
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict the employee's system and physical access pending the outcome of the investigation, coordinated with HR.
steps.outcome: Individual can no longer access sensitive systems or areas.

steps.title: Notify HR/Legal and, if warranted, law enforcement
steps.desc: Escalate to HR/Legal for the internal disciplinary process, and to law enforcement if criminal activity (theft, fraud, sabotage) is confirmed.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal and, where warranted, law enforcement are engaged.

steps.title: Remediate impact of the insider's activity
steps.desc: Correct any affected records, recover any diverted goods, and address other operational impact from the insider's actions.

steps.title: Conclude disciplinary/legal process
steps.desc: Complete the HR disciplinary process and support any law-enforcement prosecution.
steps.outcome: Process concluded with appropriate action taken.

steps.title: Restore normal warehouse operations
steps.desc: Confirm operations, records, and access controls have returned to normal, secure status.

steps.title: Strengthen insider-threat controls in warehousing
steps.desc: Review and strengthen access controls, monitoring, and separation-of-duties within warehousing operations to reduce insider-threat risk.

ITID-63511.def: Unauthorized access to or compromise of a cloud service environment supporting critical infrastructure, where the compromise originates from or is enabled by a physical supply chain weakness — such as compromised hardware supplied to the cloud provider, or credentials/access obtained through a physical intrusion or insider at a facility.
ITID-63511.purpose: Captures compromise of a cloud environment that underpins critical infrastructure, arising through a physical-supply-chain-adjacent vector (e.g., compromised hardware or credentials tied to a physical facility/provider).
scopeIncludes: Compromise of cloud infrastructure hardware (host servers, network gear) traced to a supply chain hardware compromise
Unauthorized cloud access enabled by credentials or access obtained via a physical facility intrusion or insider at a cloud/data-center provider
Exploitation of trusted relationships between a compromised on-premises/edge system and a cloud environment
scopeExcludes: Purely software/credential-based cloud compromise with no physical supply chain nexus (handled under the organization's Cloud Security ITID domain)
Telecommunications equipment compromise specifically (ITID-63521-63524)
ITID-63511.severity: Critical, given the potential blast radius across critical infrastructure workloads hosted in the affected cloud environment.
ITID-63511.escalation: Escalate immediately to CISO, cloud security engineering, the cloud provider's security team, and (for critical infrastructure) relevant regulatory/national authorities.
indicators: Anomalous authentication or resource access originating from a compromised physical host/facility
Cloud provider notification of compromised underlying hardware
Unexplained trust-relationship abuse between an edge/on-prem system and cloud resources
vectors: Compromised hardware supply chain feeding into cloud provider infrastructure (T1195.002/.003)
Valid account/credential abuse obtained via physical or insider compromise (T1078)
Exploitation of trusted relationships between compromised edge systems and cloud tenancy (T1199)
rootCauses: Insufficient hardware supply chain vetting by the cloud/infrastructure provider
Overly broad trust relationships between edge/physical systems and cloud environments
Weak physical security at facilities housing cloud infrastructure or its management access
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: Hardware supply chain vetting requirements for cloud/infrastructure providers
Least-privilege, monitored trust relationships between edge systems and cloud tenancy
Physical security controls at facilities with cloud infrastructure management access
ITID-63511.detection: Full technical detection surface: cloud provider security telemetry, authentication anomaly detection, and trust-relationship monitoring all apply directly here.
ITID-63511.response: Engage the cloud provider's incident response team, revoke/rotate affected credentials and trust relationships, and assess the blast radius across dependent critical infrastructure workloads.
metrics: Time from compromise detection to containment
Number of critical infrastructure workloads assessed as impacted
Percentage of cloud infrastructure hardware sourced through vetted supply chains
detections: Cloud authentication and trust-relationship anomaly monitoring
ITID-63511.notes: This is currently the only leaf under Cloud Environment Compromise within this Tier-2 category; it is scoped to compromises with a physical-supply-chain nexus, distinguishing it from purely cyber cloud-security incidents tracked elsewhere in the taxonomy.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cloud Environment Compromise (Critical Infrastructure Supply Chain Context)
playbook.description: A cloud environment supporting critical infrastructure or supply-chain operations is suspected of being compromised via a supply-chain vector.

steps.title: Confirm cloud environment compromise and scope
steps.desc: Analyze cloud provider logs, access records, and configuration state to confirm compromise and determine which resources are affected.
steps.guidance: Engage the cloud provider's security/incident-response team immediately given the shared-responsibility model.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed with affected resources identified.
steps.abort: If not confirmed, close as a false positive with findings documented.

steps.title: Determine the supply-chain vector of compromise
steps.desc: Investigate whether the compromise originated from a third-party software component, dependency, managed service, or supply-chain-provided credential.

steps.title: Assess criticality and downstream impact
steps.desc: Determine what critical infrastructure functions or downstream customers/partners depend on the affected cloud environment.

steps.title: Isolate affected cloud resources
steps.desc: Restrict network access, revoke compromised credentials/keys, and isolate affected cloud resources to stop further compromise.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with the cloud provider's incident-response team on isolation actions to avoid unintended service disruption.
steps.outcome: Affected resources isolated with no further attacker activity.

steps.title: Notify relevant critical-infrastructure authority and regulators
steps.desc: Given the critical-infrastructure context, notify the appropriate national critical-infrastructure protection authority and applicable regulators per notification obligations.

steps.title: Remove attacker access and remediate the supply-chain vector
steps.desc: Eliminate all attacker persistence mechanisms and remediate the specific supply-chain component or credential that enabled the compromise.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the affected third-party vendor on their remediation if the vector is a shared dependency.
steps.outcome: Attacker access is fully removed and the vector remediated.

steps.title: Rotate all potentially exposed credentials and keys
steps.desc: Rotate all cloud credentials, API keys, and secrets that may have been exposed during the compromise.
steps.outcome: All potentially exposed credentials are rotated.

steps.title: Validate cloud environment integrity before restoring service
steps.desc: Confirm the environment is free of attacker presence and functioning correctly before restoring full service.
steps.outcome: Environment validated clean and service restored.

steps.title: Notify affected customers/partners
steps.desc: Communicate with affected downstream customers or partners regarding the incident and remediation status.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders notified per obligations and expectations.

steps.title: Review cloud supply-chain security posture
steps.desc: Assess third-party dependency and cloud-provider risk management practices and strengthen supply-chain security requirements for cloud services.
steps.outcome: Updated cloud supply-chain security requirements documented.

ITID-63521.def: The compromise of a cellular base station or tower equipment through hardware introduced or altered somewhere in its supply chain, enabling covert access, interception, or disruption of the mobile network segment it serves.
ITID-63521.purpose: Captures compromise of a cell tower or base station's physical or embedded hardware, a direct telecom-infrastructure hardware supply chain risk.
scopeIncludes: Compromised radio access network (RAN) equipment installed at a cell site
Physically tampered base station hardware discovered during site inspection or maintenance
scopeExcludes: Compromise of carrier core network equipment (ITID-63522)
Compromise of a submarine cable landing station (ITID-63523)
ITID-63521.severity: High-Critical, given the potential for mass interception or localized network disruption.
ITID-63521.escalation: Escalate immediately to the telecom provider's security team, national telecom regulatory/security authorities, and CISO.
indicators: Site inspection reveals unauthorized hardware modification
Anomalous signaling or traffic patterns traced to a specific cell site
Equipment sourced from a vendor later identified in a hardware supply chain compromise advisory
vectors: Hardware supply chain compromise of RAN equipment before installation (T1195.003)
Physical tampering with base station equipment post-installation
rootCauses: Insufficient hardware authenticity verification for telecom infrastructure equipment
Inadequate physical security at remote/unmanned cell sites
Limited supply chain visibility into RAN equipment sub-tier manufacturing
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Hardware authenticity verification program for telecom infrastructure equipment
Enhanced physical security and tamper detection at cell sites
Supply chain traceability requirements for RAN equipment vendors
ITID-63521.detection: Limited direct technical detection; relies on physical site inspection and network-level anomaly monitoring for the affected segment.
ITID-63521.response: Isolate and forensically inspect the affected equipment, assess the scope of interception/disruption, and coordinate with the telecom provider and regulators on remediation.
metrics: Number of confirmed cell-site hardware compromises per year
Percentage of RAN equipment subject to authenticity verification
sops: Hardware Receiving and Authenticity Verification SOP
detections: Network signaling/traffic anomaly monitoring for cell-site segments
ITID-63521.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is RAN/base-station equipment specifically, distinct from carrier core network compromise (ITID-63522) and submarine cable landing station compromise (ITID-63523).

playbook.name: Compromised Cell Tower/Base Station Equipment
playbook.description: Cell tower or base station equipment has been compromised, potentially via a tampered hardware or firmware supply-chain vector, threatening telecommunications service integrity.

steps.title: Confirm compromise of the base station equipment
steps.desc: Analyze equipment logs, firmware integrity checks, and network behavior to confirm compromise of the affected cell tower/base station.
steps.guidance: Engage the equipment vendor's security team and, where relevant, the network operations center immediately.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed with affected equipment identified.
steps.abort: If not confirmed, close as a false positive with findings documented.

steps.title: Determine the supply-chain vector and scope
steps.desc: Investigate whether the compromise stems from tampered hardware, backdoored firmware, or a compromised update mechanism, and identify all affected sites sharing the same equipment/firmware.
steps.outcome: Vector identified and full scope of affected sites documented.

steps.title: Assess subscriber and service impact
steps.desc: Determine what subscriber communications, data, or location information may have been exposed or intercepted via the compromised equipment.

steps.title: Isolate or take the compromised equipment out of service
steps.desc: Remove the compromised base station/tower equipment from active service, coordinating with network operations to reroute traffic and minimize coverage loss.
steps.outcome: Compromised equipment is no longer processing live traffic.
steps.abort: If immediate removal would cause unacceptable coverage loss, apply compensating monitoring until a maintenance window is available.

steps.title: Notify the national critical-infrastructure/telecom regulatory authority
steps.desc: Report the compromise to the relevant telecommunications regulator and national critical-infrastructure protection authority given the criticality of telecom infrastructure.

steps.title: Forensically inspect and remediate or replace compromised equipment
steps.desc: Perform hardware/firmware forensic inspection and either remediate via verified clean firmware or fully replace compromised units.
steps.guidance: Engage the equipment vendor and, if a hardware implant is confirmed, hardware forensics specialists.
steps.outcome: All confirmed-compromised equipment is remediated or replaced.

steps.title: Coordinate law enforcement/counter-intelligence engagement
steps.desc: Given the potential national-security implications of compromised telecom infrastructure, engage law enforcement and counter-intelligence authorities as appropriate.

steps.title: Validate restored equipment and service integrity
steps.desc: Confirm remediated/replaced equipment is functioning correctly and securely before fully restoring service.

steps.title: Notify affected subscribers where required
steps.desc: Assess and fulfill any subscriber-notification obligations related to potential communications interception or data exposure.
steps.outcome: Notification obligations assessed and executed as required.

steps.title: Review telecom equipment supply-chain assurance program
steps.desc: Assess and strengthen supply-chain vetting, firmware-integrity verification, and vendor-trust requirements for telecom infrastructure equipment.

ITID-63522.def: A nation-state or nation-state-affiliated actor's compromise of a telecommunications carrier's core network equipment (switching, routing, or signaling infrastructure) via the hardware supply chain, enabling large-scale surveillance, interception, or disruption capability.
ITID-63522.purpose: Captures nation-state compromise of a telecom carrier's core network equipment, a high-severity, attributed hardware supply chain threat.
scopeIncludes: Nation-state implanted hardware in core switching/routing/signaling equipment
Attributed nation-state campaigns targeting carrier core infrastructure hardware
scopeExcludes: Compromise of edge/RAN equipment such as cell towers (ITID-63521)
Submarine cable landing station compromise (ITID-63523)
Non-attributed or criminal (non-nation-state) telecom equipment compromise (ITID-63524)
ITID-63522.severity: Critical. Core network compromise represents national-security-level risk with mass surveillance/disruption potential.
ITID-63522.escalation: Escalate immediately to CISO, national telecom security authorities, and law enforcement/intelligence liaison channels.
indicators: Forensic discovery of implanted hardware in core network equipment
Attribution intelligence linking equipment compromise to a known nation-state actor
Anomalous large-scale signaling/traffic interception patterns
vectors: Hardware supply chain compromise of core network equipment at the manufacturing or distribution stage (T1195.003)
Compromise of vendor infrastructure used to stage the hardware compromise (T1584 Compromise Infrastructure)
rootCauses: Reliance on core network equipment vendors with limited supply chain assurance
Insufficient national-level vetting of telecom equipment suppliers
Limited visibility into sub-tier component sourcing for core network hardware
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: National-level vendor security vetting for core network equipment
Independent forensic hardware verification for critical core infrastructure
Diversification of core network equipment vendors to reduce single-point supply chain risk
ITID-63522.detection: Limited direct technical detection at the hardware level; network-level anomaly monitoring and threat intelligence attribution are the primary detection paths.
ITID-63522.response: Coordinate with national telecom security authorities on forensic investigation and remediation; assess and disclose scope of surveillance/interception exposure as required.
metrics: Number of attributed nation-state core-network compromise incidents per year
Percentage of core network equipment from vendors with national security vetting
detections: Core network signaling/traffic anomaly monitoring with threat-intelligence correlation
ITID-63522.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is specifically nation-state-attributed core network equipment compromise, the highest-severity variant, distinct from RAN/cell-tower (ITID-63521) and submarine cable (ITID-63523) compromise.

playbook.name: Nation-State Compromise of Telecom Carrier Core Network Equipment
playbook.description: A nation-state actor has compromised core network equipment at a telecommunications carrier via a supply-chain vector, posing a severe national-security and privacy risk.

steps.title: Confirm compromise of core network equipment
steps.desc: Analyze core network equipment logs, configuration state, and traffic patterns to confirm compromise, engaging the equipment vendor's security team immediately.
steps.guidance: Treat as highest severity from the outset given the national-security implications of core network compromise.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed with affected core network elements identified.
steps.tool: Network operations center / element management system

steps.title: Attribute and characterize the nation-state actor's capability
steps.desc: Work with threat intelligence and government partners to characterize the actor's tactics, techniques, and likely objectives (surveillance, disruption, espionage).
steps.guidance: Engage national counter-intelligence and cybersecurity agencies for attribution support.
steps.outcome: Actor characterization and objective assessment documented.

steps.title: Assess scope of national infrastructure and subscriber impact
steps.desc: Determine the full extent of core network functions, subscriber communications, and interconnected carrier relationships affected.

steps.title: Engage full incident-response and government coordination immediately
steps.desc: Activate the organization's highest-severity incident-response process and immediately engage national critical-infrastructure, law-enforcement, and counter-intelligence authorities.
steps.guidance: Core network compromise by a nation-state actor typically triggers mandatory, immediate government notification.
steps.outcome: Full IR team and government authorities are engaged from the outset.

steps.title: Isolate compromised core network elements
steps.desc: Isolate or fail over compromised core network equipment to trusted redundant systems while preserving forensic evidence.
steps.guidance: Coordinate isolation actions carefully with network operations and, where directed, government technical advisors to avoid tipping off the actor prematurely if counter-intelligence operations are underway.
steps.outcome: Compromised elements isolated with service continuity maintained via trusted redundancy.

steps.title: Conduct full forensic investigation of compromised core equipment
steps.desc: Perform comprehensive hardware, firmware, and software forensic analysis of all core network equipment suspected of compromise.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with government forensic support given the national-security sensitivity.

steps.title: Remediate or replace all compromised core network equipment
steps.desc: Remediate via verified clean firmware/configuration or fully replace compromised core network equipment through a trusted supply channel.
steps.outcome: All confirmed-compromised equipment remediated or replaced.

steps.title: Rotate all potentially exposed keys, credentials, and lawful-intercept access controls
steps.desc: Rotate cryptographic keys, administrative credentials, and review lawful-intercept access controls that may have been exposed.
steps.outcome: All potentially exposed keys/credentials rotated and access controls reviewed.

steps.title: Validate restored core network integrity
steps.desc: Confirm remediated/replaced core network equipment is functioning correctly and securely before declaring full recovery.
steps.outcome: Core network validated clean and fully operational.

steps.title: Coordinate government and subscriber notification
steps.desc: Complete required notifications to government authorities, regulators, and, where applicable, affected subscribers.

steps.title: Conduct national-security-informed supply-chain review
steps.desc: Conduct a comprehensive review of core network equipment supply-chain assurance, vendor-trust programs, and government coordination protocols.
steps.guidance: Engage government partners in the review given the national-security dimension.
steps.outcome: Updated supply-chain assurance and coordination protocols documented.

ITID-63523.def: The compromise of a submarine cable landing station's physical or hardware infrastructure, enabling covert access, interception, or disruption of the international telecommunications traffic passing through it.
ITID-63523.purpose: Captures compromise of a submarine cable landing station, a physically concentrated chokepoint for international telecommunications traffic.
scopeIncludes: Physical intrusion or hardware tampering at a submarine cable landing station
Compromised equipment installed at the landing station via the hardware supply chain
scopeExcludes: Compromise of cell towers/base stations (ITID-63521)
Compromise of carrier core network equipment away from the landing station (ITID-63522)
ITID-63523.severity: Critical. Landing stations are high-value chokepoints; compromise can enable mass interception of international traffic.
ITID-63523.escalation: Escalate immediately to CISO, the cable consortium/operator's security team, national security authorities, and law enforcement.
indicators: Physical security breach or unauthorized access detected at a landing station facility
Forensic discovery of tampered or unauthorized equipment at the landing station
Anomalous traffic interception patterns traced to a specific landing station segment
vectors: Physical intrusion into a landing station facility to install interception equipment
Hardware supply chain compromise of landing station equipment before installation (T1195.003)
rootCauses: Insufficient physical security at landing station facilities
Limited hardware authenticity verification for landing station equipment
Inadequate monitoring of physical access to critical telecom chokepoints
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Enhanced physical security and access monitoring at landing station facilities
Hardware authenticity verification for landing station equipment
Coordinated security oversight with the cable consortium/operator
ITID-63523.detection: Limited direct technical detection; relies on physical security monitoring and traffic-level anomaly detection for the affected cable segment.
ITID-63523.response: Coordinate with the cable consortium/operator on forensic investigation, assess scope of traffic interception exposure, and remediate physical/hardware security gaps.
metrics: Number of confirmed landing station compromise incidents per year
Percentage of landing stations with enhanced physical security controls
detections: Physical access monitoring and traffic anomaly detection at landing station facilities
ITID-63523.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is specific to submarine cable landing station infrastructure, a distinct physical chokepoint from cell towers (ITID-63521) or general core network equipment (ITID-63522).

playbook.name: Compromised Submarine Cable Landing Station
playbook.description: A submarine cable landing station has been compromised, threatening the integrity and confidentiality of international telecommunications traffic.

steps.title: Confirm compromise of the landing station equipment/systems
steps.desc: Analyze landing-station equipment, monitoring systems, and access logs to confirm compromise, engaging the cable consortium's security team immediately.
steps.guidance: Treat as highest severity given the volume and sensitivity of international traffic transiting the facility.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed with affected systems identified.

steps.title: Assess scope of traffic and data at risk
steps.desc: Determine the volume, routes, and sensitivity of international traffic transiting the affected landing station during the compromise window.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the cable consortium and connected carriers for traffic mapping.

steps.title: Determine the supply-chain or access vector of compromise
steps.desc: Investigate whether the compromise originated from tampered equipment, a compromised vendor, or unauthorized physical/remote access.

steps.title: Notify national critical-infrastructure authority immediately
steps.desc: Immediately notify the national critical-infrastructure protection authority and relevant telecom regulators given the strategic importance of submarine cable infrastructure.
steps.outcome: Required authority notifications completed without delay.

steps.title: Isolate or reroute affected systems/traffic
steps.desc: Coordinate with the cable consortium and connected carriers to isolate compromised systems and reroute traffic through unaffected paths where possible.
steps.outcome: Compromised systems isolated with traffic continuity maintained via alternate routing.

steps.title: Engage law enforcement and counter-intelligence authorities
steps.desc: Given the strategic sensitivity of submarine cable infrastructure, engage law enforcement and counter-intelligence agencies for investigation and attribution support.

steps.title: Conduct full forensic investigation of the landing station
steps.desc: Perform comprehensive forensic analysis of landing-station equipment and systems to fully characterize the compromise.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with government forensic support given the strategic sensitivity.

steps.title: Remediate or replace compromised equipment
steps.desc: Remediate confirmed-compromised equipment via verified clean firmware/configuration or full replacement through a trusted supply channel.
steps.outcome: All confirmed-compromised equipment remediated or replaced.

steps.title: Validate restored landing station integrity and resume normal traffic routing
steps.desc: Confirm remediated equipment is functioning correctly and securely before restoring normal traffic routing through the facility.
steps.outcome: Landing station validated clean and normal operations restored.

steps.title: Strengthen submarine cable infrastructure security requirements
steps.desc: Review and strengthen physical and supply-chain security requirements for submarine cable landing stations in coordination with the cable consortium and government partners.

ITID-63524.def: General or not-yet-classified reports of compromised telecommunications equipment encountered in the critical infrastructure supply chain.
ITID-63524.purpose: Intake bucket for telecommunications equipment compromise incidents that do not fit cell tower, core network, or submarine cable landing station leaves.
scopeIncludes: Telecom equipment compromise reports where the specific infrastructure type is not yet determined
Other telecom infrastructure categories not covered by the more specific leaves
scopeExcludes: Cell tower/base station compromise (ITID-63521)
Carrier core network compromise (ITID-63522)
Submarine cable landing station compromise (ITID-63523)
ITID-63524.priority: P2 pending triage; escalate to P1 once the specific infrastructure type and scope are confirmed.
ITID-63524.escalation: Escalate to the telecom provider's security team and CISO for triage; reclassify to a specific leaf once the infrastructure type is confirmed.
indicators: Telecom equipment compromise evidence not yet attributed to a specific known category
vectors: Unclassified telecom hardware compromise technique pending investigation
rootCauses: Gaps in hardware supply chain vetting for telecom infrastructure generally
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: General hardware authenticity verification program for telecom infrastructure
ITID-63524.detection: Varies by infrastructure type; primarily physical/hardware inspection pending triage.
ITID-63524.response: Triage the report and reclassify to a specific leaf once the infrastructure type is confirmed.
metrics: Count of general telecom compromise reports pending triage
Percentage subsequently reclassified
ITID-63524.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf for the Telecommunications Equipment Compromise Tier-4 group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Telecommunications Equipment Compromise
playbook.description: Telecommunications equipment of unspecified type has been compromised via a supply-chain vector, requiring investigation under the standard critical-infrastructure IR process.

steps.title: Confirm compromise of the telecom equipment
steps.desc: Analyze equipment logs and behavior to confirm compromise, engaging the equipment vendor's security team.
steps.outcome: Compromise confirmed with affected equipment identified.
steps.abort: If not confirmed, close as a false positive with findings documented.

steps.title: Determine supply-chain vector and scope
steps.desc: Investigate the compromise vector and identify all affected equipment sharing the same source.

steps.title: Assess service and subscriber impact
steps.desc: Determine what service functions or subscriber data may be exposed via the compromised equipment.

steps.title: Isolate the compromised equipment
steps.desc: Remove or isolate the compromised equipment from active service while preserving continuity where possible.
steps.outcome: Compromised equipment isolated with no further exploitation.

steps.title: Notify relevant regulatory/critical-infrastructure authority
steps.desc: Notify the relevant telecom regulator and critical-infrastructure authority as required.

steps.title: Remediate or replace compromised equipment
steps.desc: Remediate via verified clean firmware or full replacement of confirmed-compromised equipment.

steps.title: Validate and restore service
steps.desc: Confirm equipment integrity before restoring full service.

steps.title: Strengthen telecom equipment supply-chain assurance
steps.desc: Review and strengthen supply-chain vetting and firmware-integrity requirements.

ITID-63611.def: Deliberate tampering with critical infrastructure or mission-essential equipment attributed to a nation-state or nation-state-affiliated actor, occurring at any point in the physical supply chain, intended to establish long-term strategic access, disruption capability, or intelligence advantage.
ITID-63611.purpose: Captures nation-state tampering with critical equipment across the physical supply chain, serving as the general leaf for this Tier-4 category within the APT-focused Tier-3.
scopeIncludes: Nation-state tampering with critical equipment not already covered by the Telecommunications Equipment Compromise or Cyber-Physical Hybrid Attacks leaves
Attributed nation-state hardware tampering campaigns targeting critical infrastructure sectors broadly (energy, water, transportation, etc.)
scopeExcludes: Telecommunications-specific equipment compromise (ITID-63521-63524)
Combined cyber-intrusion-plus-physical-implant attacks (ITID-63621) and cyber-triggered physical damage (ITID-63622), which are the more specific cyber-physical hybrid variants
ITID-63611.severity: Critical. Nation-state tampering with critical equipment represents a national-security-level threat.
ITID-63611.escalation: Escalate immediately to CISO, national critical infrastructure security authorities, and law enforcement/intelligence liaison channels.
indicators: Forensic discovery of hardware tampering attributed via threat intelligence to a known nation-state actor
Equipment sourced from a vendor identified in a nation-state supply chain compromise advisory
Anomalous access or beaconing patterns consistent with an established APT campaign
vectors: Hardware supply chain compromise at manufacturing or distribution (T1195.003)
Physical hardware additions to critical systems (T1200 Hardware Additions)
Compromise of upstream infrastructure used to stage the campaign (T1584 Compromise Infrastructure)
rootCauses: Reliance on critical infrastructure equipment vendors with limited supply chain assurance
Insufficient national-level vetting of critical equipment suppliers
Limited visibility into sub-tier manufacturing for critical infrastructure hardware
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: National-level vendor security vetting for critical infrastructure equipment
Independent forensic hardware verification programs
Threat-intelligence-driven monitoring for known nation-state supply chain TTPs
ITID-63611.detection: Limited direct technical detection at the hardware level; network-level anomaly monitoring and threat-intelligence attribution are the primary detection paths.
ITID-63611.response: Coordinate with national critical infrastructure security authorities on forensic investigation, assess strategic access/disruption exposure, and remediate affected equipment.
metrics: Number of attributed nation-state equipment-tampering incidents per year
Percentage of critical infrastructure equipment from nationally vetted vendors
ITID-63611.notes: This is currently the only leaf under Nation-State Tampering with Critical Equipment; it is scoped to critical-infrastructure-sector tampering broadly, distinct from the telecom-specific leaves (ITID-6352x) and the cyber-physical hybrid leaves (ITID-6362x).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Nation-State Tampering with Critical Equipment
playbook.description: A nation-state actor is suspected of tampering with critical equipment via the supply chain, posing a severe national-security risk.

steps.title: Confirm tampering and engage full incident-response immediately
steps.desc: Confirm evidence of nation-state-linked tampering with the critical equipment and immediately activate the highest-severity incident-response process.
steps.guidance: Engage hardware forensics, threat intelligence, and government liaison contacts from the outset.
steps.outcome: Tampering confirmed and full IR engagement activated.

steps.title: Characterize the actor and likely objective
steps.desc: Work with threat intelligence and government partners to attribute the activity and assess the likely objective (espionage, sabotage, pre-positioning).
steps.outcome: Actor characterization and objective assessment documented.

steps.title: Trace the supply-chain custody and identify all affected equipment
steps.desc: Reconstruct the equipment's manufacturing and custody chain to identify the tampering point and all other units potentially affected.
steps.outcome: Custody chain and full scope of affected equipment documented.

steps.title: Notify government/national-security authorities immediately
steps.desc: Immediately notify national counter-intelligence, law-enforcement, and critical-infrastructure authorities given the nation-state nexus.

steps.title: Isolate all confirmed and suspected tampered equipment
steps.desc: Remove or isolate all confirmed and suspected tampered equipment from operational use, preserving evidence per forensic guidance.
steps.guidance: Coordinate isolation timing with government technical advisors if counter-intelligence considerations apply.
steps.outcome: Tampered equipment isolated with no further exploitation.

steps.title: Conduct comprehensive forensic investigation
steps.desc: Perform thorough hardware and firmware forensic analysis of all affected equipment to fully characterize the tampering.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with government forensic support.

steps.title: Remove and replace all confirmed tampered equipment
steps.desc: Physically remove all confirmed tampered equipment and replace through a trusted, higher-assurance supply channel.
steps.outcome: No tampered equipment remains in operational use.

steps.title: Validate replacement equipment and restore operations
steps.desc: Confirm replacement equipment is verified clean and functioning correctly before restoring full operations.

steps.title: Complete government and stakeholder notifications
steps.desc: Fulfill all required notifications to government authorities, regulators, and affected stakeholders.

steps.title: Conduct national-security-informed supply-chain assurance review
steps.desc: Review and strengthen supply-chain assurance, trusted-sourcing, and government-coordination protocols for critical equipment.
steps.outcome: Updated assurance and coordination protocols documented.

ITID-63621.def: An attack in which an adversary combines remote cyber intrusion techniques with the physical installation of a hardware implant (an added component, device, or modification) on target infrastructure, using each vector to reinforce or enable the other.
ITID-63621.purpose: Captures a coordinated attack combining a cyber intrusion with a physical hardware implant, a signature nation-state/APT technique for establishing persistent, hard-to-detect access.
scopeIncludes: A cyber intrusion used to identify a target for physical implant placement, followed by physical access to install the implant
A physical hardware implant used to establish a foothold that is then leveraged for a broader cyber intrusion
scopeExcludes: A cyber attack that triggers physical equipment malfunction without a hardware implant component (ITID-63622)
A purely physical hardware implant with no coordinated cyber-intrusion component (ITID-63121, Hardware Backdoors)
ITID-63621.severity: Critical. Combined cyber-physical attacks are difficult to fully remediate and typically indicate a sophisticated, well-resourced adversary.
ITID-63621.escalation: Escalate immediately to CISO, physical security, national security authorities, and law enforcement.
indicators: Forensic discovery of a hardware implant combined with evidence of a related network intrusion
Physical access logs showing an anomalous visit correlated with a subsequent network compromise
Threat intelligence attributing the combined pattern to a known APT group
vectors: Cyber reconnaissance used to plan physical access for implant placement
Physical implant installation (T1200 Hardware Additions) used to enable follow-on network intrusion
Use of compromised infrastructure to stage and control the combined attack (T1584)
rootCauses: Siloed physical and cyber security functions with no coordinated threat detection
Insufficient physical access monitoring for facilities housing sensitive network infrastructure
Limited correlation between physical access events and network security telemetry
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Coordinated physical-cyber security operations with correlated event monitoring
Physical access monitoring for facilities housing sensitive network infrastructure
Regular hardware inspection program for high-value network/infrastructure equipment
ITID-63621.detection: Partial technical detection surface: network-side indicators (anomalous traffic, beaconing) can be monitored, but the physical-implant component still relies primarily on physical inspection.
ITID-63621.response: Treat as a full compromise: forensically examine both the physical implant and the network for lateral movement, coordinate physical and cyber incident response, and notify national security authorities where nation-state involvement is suspected.
metrics: Number of confirmed cyber-physical hybrid attacks per year
Time from physical implant discovery to full network compromise assessment
ITID-63621.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is the combined cyber-intrusion-plus-implant pattern, distinct from a purely cyber attack that damages physical equipment (ITID-63622).

playbook.name: Combined Cyber Intrusion and Physical Hardware Implant Attack
playbook.description: An adversary combined a cyber intrusion with a physical hardware implant to achieve persistent, high-assurance access to a critical system.

steps.title: Confirm both the cyber intrusion and physical implant
steps.desc: Correlate SIEM/EDR findings of the cyber intrusion with hardware forensic findings confirming a physical implant on the affected system.
steps.guidance: Engage both cyber incident response and hardware forensics teams jointly from the outset.
steps.outcome: Both attack components confirmed and linked as a single combined attack.

steps.title: Characterize the actor and full attack chain
steps.desc: Reconstruct the full attack chain from initial supply-chain implant placement through cyber intrusion and objective, attributing the actor where possible.
steps.guidance: Engage threat intelligence and, given the sophistication implied by a hybrid attack, consider nation-state attribution.
steps.outcome: Full attack chain and actor characterization documented.

steps.title: Assess scope of access and data/system compromise
steps.desc: Determine what systems, data, and network access the combined attack achieved.

steps.title: Activate full incident-response engagement and government liaison
steps.desc: Activate the highest-severity IR process and engage government/law-enforcement/counter-intelligence liaison given the hybrid physical-cyber sophistication.
steps.outcome: Full IR and government engagement activated.

steps.title: Isolate the implanted hardware and cut off cyber access
steps.desc: Physically isolate the implanted device and block network/cyber access paths used by the intrusion, preserving evidence per forensic guidance.
steps.outcome: Both the physical and cyber access vectors are cut off.

steps.title: Remove the physical implant and remediate all cyber persistence
steps.desc: Physically remove the implant and eliminate all cyber persistence mechanisms (backdoor accounts, malware, C2 channels) established via the combined attack.
steps.outcome: Both physical and cyber attack components are fully removed.

steps.title: Rotate all potentially exposed credentials and keys
steps.desc: Rotate all credentials, keys, and certificates that may have been exposed through the combined attack.

steps.title: Replace affected hardware through a trusted supply channel
steps.desc: Replace the compromised hardware with units sourced and verified through a higher-assurance supply chain.
steps.outcome: Affected hardware replaced with verified-clean units.

steps.title: Validate full system integrity before restoring operations
steps.desc: Confirm both physical and cyber remediation are complete and effective before restoring normal operations.
steps.outcome: System validated clean and fully operational.

steps.title: Conduct joint physical-cyber security review
steps.desc: Review supply-chain assurance, physical security, and cyber defenses jointly to address the combined attack surface exploited.
steps.guidance: Engage government partners given the sophistication and likely nation-state involvement.
steps.outcome: Updated joint physical-cyber security requirements documented.

ITID-63622.def: An attack conducted entirely through remote or network-based means that manipulates a system's control logic or firmware to cause physical malfunction, damage, or destruction of the equipment it controls.
ITID-63622.purpose: Captures a cyber attack that causes physical malfunction or damage to equipment, without a physical hardware implant component.
scopeIncludes: Malicious manipulation of industrial control system logic causing physical equipment damage
Remote exploitation of a device's firmware/control software to force it outside safe operating parameters
scopeExcludes: Attacks that also involve a physical hardware implant (ITID-63621)
Purely physical sabotage with no cyber component (ITID-63231, Destructive Sabotage of Critical Shipments)
ITID-63622.severity: Critical, given the potential for physical safety impact and equipment destruction.
ITID-63622.escalation: Escalate immediately to CISO, OT/ICS security engineering, physical safety teams, and national security authorities where nation-state involvement is suspected.
indicators: Equipment operating outside safe parameters with no legitimate operator command issued
Control system logs showing unauthorized command injection
Physical damage/malfunction correlated with a confirmed network intrusion into the control environment
vectors: Remote exploitation of an industrial control system or embedded device to issue malicious commands (T1195.002 Compromise Software Supply Chain, where the attack path runs through compromised control software)
Manipulation of firmware/control logic to force equipment beyond safe operating limits
rootCauses: Insufficient network segmentation between IT and OT/ICS environments
Lack of safety-interlock verification independent of the primary control logic
Weak authentication/authorization on control system command interfaces
