mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
controls: IT/OT network segmentation
Independent safety-interlock systems that cannot be overridden remotely
Strong authentication/authorization on control system command interfaces
ITID-63622.detection: A genuine technical detection surface exists here: OT/ICS network monitoring and control-system command auditing can directly detect this attack pattern.
ITID-63622.response: Isolate the affected control environment, halt equipment safely, forensically analyze the command injection path, and coordinate with OT/ICS engineering on safe recovery.
metrics: Number of confirmed cyber-triggered physical damage incidents per year
Percentage of OT/ICS environments with independent safety interlocks
detections: OT/ICS network and control-command anomaly monitoring
ITID-63622.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is purely cyber-triggered physical damage with no implant, distinct from the combined implant-plus-intrusion pattern (ITID-63621).

playbook.name: Cyber Attack Triggering Physical Equipment Malfunction/Damage
playbook.description: A cyber attack, likely enabled via a supply-chain vector, triggered physical malfunction or damage to critical equipment.

steps.title: Confirm the cyber-triggered physical malfunction/damage
steps.desc: Correlate cyber intrusion evidence with the physical malfunction or damage event to confirm causation.
steps.guidance: Engage both cyber incident response and physical/industrial-control engineering teams jointly.
steps.outcome: Causal link between the cyber attack and physical impact confirmed.
steps.abort: If no causal link is confirmed, route to standard equipment-failure investigation instead.

steps.title: Assess safety risk and ongoing physical hazard
steps.desc: Immediately assess whether the damaged/malfunctioning equipment poses an ongoing safety hazard to personnel or facilities.
steps.guidance: Engage safety engineering immediately given the physical risk dimension.
steps.outcome: Safety risk assessed and immediate hazards identified.

steps.title: Determine the supply-chain vector enabling the cyber access
steps.desc: Investigate how the attacker gained the access needed to trigger the physical effect, focusing on supply-chain-introduced vulnerabilities or backdoors.

steps.title: Isolate affected control systems and equipment
steps.desc: Immediately isolate the affected control systems from network access and, where necessary, place equipment in a safe state to prevent further damage.
steps.guidance: Coordinate closely with operations/engineering to avoid causing additional physical harm during isolation.
steps.outcome: Affected systems isolated and equipment in a safe state.

steps.title: Notify safety, regulatory, and critical-infrastructure authorities
steps.desc: Notify workplace safety authorities, sector regulators, and critical-infrastructure protection authorities given the physical damage and cyber-physical nature of the incident.

steps.title: Remove attacker access and remediate the exploited vulnerability
steps.desc: Eliminate all attacker persistence and remediate the specific supply-chain vulnerability or backdoor that enabled the physical-effect attack.
steps.outcome: Attacker access removed and vulnerability remediated.

steps.title: Repair or replace damaged physical equipment
steps.desc: Repair or replace the physically damaged equipment through verified, trusted channels.

steps.title: Validate safety and system integrity before restoring operations
steps.desc: Confirm the equipment is safe and the control system is free of attacker presence before restoring normal operations.
steps.outcome: Operations restored safely on verified systems.

steps.title: Review OT/ICS supply-chain and cyber-physical security
steps.desc: Review and strengthen supply-chain assurance and cyber-physical safety controls for operational technology to prevent recurrence.

ITID-63623.def: General or not-yet-classified reports of an attack combining cyber and physical elements against critical equipment in the supply chain.
ITID-63623.purpose: Intake bucket for cyber-physical hybrid attacks that do not fit the combined-implant or cyber-triggered-damage leaves.
scopeIncludes: Cyber-physical hybrid reports where the specific mechanism is not yet determined
Novel or mixed cyber-physical patterns not covered by the more specific leaves
scopeExcludes: Combined cyber intrusion and physical hardware implant attack (ITID-63621)
Cyber attack triggering physical equipment malfunction/damage (ITID-63622)
ITID-63623.escalation: Escalate to CISO and OT/ICS security engineering for triage; reclassify to a specific leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.
indicators: Cyber-physical hybrid evidence not yet attributed to a specific known pattern
vectors: Unclassified cyber-physical hybrid technique pending investigation
rootCauses: Gaps in coordinated physical-cyber security monitoring generally
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: General coordinated physical-cyber security monitoring program
ITID-63623.detection: Varies by mechanism; both physical inspection and network/OT monitoring may apply pending triage.
ITID-63623.response: Triage the report and reclassify to a specific leaf once the mechanism is confirmed.
metrics: Count of general cyber-physical hybrid reports pending triage
Percentage subsequently reclassified
ITID-63623.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf for the Cyber-Physical Hybrid Attacks Tier-4 group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cyber-Physical Hybrid Attack
playbook.description: A cyber-physical hybrid attack of unspecified type, likely enabled via a supply-chain vector, is suspected against organizational systems or equipment.

steps.title: Confirm the hybrid cyber-physical nature of the attack
steps.desc: Correlate cyber and physical evidence to confirm the attack combines both dimensions.
steps.guidance: Engage cyber IR and physical/hardware forensics teams jointly.
steps.outcome: Hybrid nature confirmed with both components documented.
steps.abort: If only one dimension is confirmed, route to the appropriate single-domain IR process.

steps.title: Assess safety and operational risk
steps.desc: Assess whether the attack poses an ongoing safety or operational hazard.
steps.outcome: Risk assessed and immediate hazards identified.

steps.title: Determine supply-chain vector and actor characterization
steps.desc: Investigate the supply-chain vector enabling the attack and characterize the likely actor and objective.

steps.title: Isolate affected systems/equipment
steps.desc: Isolate affected cyber and physical components to stop further impact, placing equipment in a safe state if necessary.

steps.title: Notify relevant regulatory/critical-infrastructure authorities
steps.desc: Notify applicable regulators and critical-infrastructure authorities given the hybrid nature of the incident.

steps.title: Remediate both cyber and physical attack components
steps.desc: Remove attacker cyber access and remediate/replace any physically compromised hardware.

steps.title: Validate integrity and restore operations
steps.desc: Confirm systems and equipment are safe and free of attacker presence before restoring normal operations.

steps.title: Review cyber-physical supply-chain security posture
steps.desc: Review and strengthen supply-chain assurance and cyber-physical security controls to prevent recurrence.

ITID-63631.def: The theft of proprietary intellectual property (designs, trade secrets, source material) by an adversary who gains access through a physical supply chain relationship — such as a contract manufacturer, component supplier, or logistics partner — rather than through a purely remote cyber intrusion.
ITID-63631.purpose: Captures theft of intellectual property achieved by exploiting a physical supply chain relationship or access point, attributed to nation-state or APT activity.
scopeIncludes: A contract manufacturer or supplier with legitimate access to IP exfiltrating it for a nation-state sponsor
Physical access at a supplier facility used to copy or exfiltrate proprietary designs/documentation
scopeExcludes: Purely remote/cyber IP theft with no physical supply chain access nexus (handled under the organization's general Intellectual Property Theft ITID domain)
ITID-63631.severity: Critical, given the strategic and competitive value of the compromised intellectual property.
ITID-63631.escalation: Escalate immediately to CISO, legal, national security authorities, and executive leadership.
indicators: A supplier/manufacturer facility found to have exfiltrated proprietary design data
Evidence of unauthorized copying/removal of design documentation at a supplier site
Threat intelligence attributing the theft to a known nation-state-sponsored program
vectors: Exploitation of legitimate supplier/manufacturer access to proprietary designs for exfiltration
Physical exfiltration of design documentation or prototypes at a supplier facility
rootCauses: Insufficient IP-access controls and data-loss prevention at contract manufacturer/supplier facilities
Lack of contractual audit rights over supplier IP-handling practices
Limited monitoring of physical document/prototype control at supplier sites
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Contractual IP-access and audit rights over supplier/manufacturer facilities
Data-loss prevention and physical document control at supplier sites
Compartmentalization of proprietary design data shared with manufacturing partners
ITID-63631.detection: Limited direct technical detection; relies primarily on supplier audit programs and physical document-control monitoring.
ITID-63631.response: Conduct a supplier audit and forensic review, assess the scope of IP compromised, and pursue legal/contractual remedies alongside national security coordination where warranted.
metrics: Number of confirmed supply-chain-enabled IP theft incidents per year
Percentage of manufacturing partners subject to IP-handling audit
sops: Brand Protection and IP Enforcement Procedure
detections: Physical document-control and data-loss-prevention monitoring at supplier sites
ITID-63631.notes: This is currently the only leaf under Intellectual Property Theft via Supply Chain Exploits; it is scoped to theft enabled through a physical supply chain access point specifically.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General IP Theft via Supply Chain Exploit
playbook.description: Intellectual property has been stolen through exploitation of a supply-chain relationship or access point.

steps.title: Confirm IP theft and identify the exposed intellectual property
steps.desc: Confirm that specific intellectual property (designs, source code, trade secrets, formulas) was accessed and exfiltrated via a supply-chain party's access.
steps.guidance: Engage legal/IP counsel and forensic investigators jointly given the dual technical and legal nature of the case.
steps.outcome: IP theft confirmed with the specific stolen materials identified.
steps.abort: If not confirmed, close as a false positive with findings documented.

steps.title: Identify the supply-chain party and access vector exploited
steps.desc: Determine which supply-chain partner's access, system, or credential was exploited to reach the stolen IP.
steps.outcome: Responsible access vector and party identified.

steps.title: Assess likely actor and downstream use of the stolen IP
steps.desc: Assess whether the theft appears to be nation-state-sponsored industrial espionage, a competitor, or opportunistic, and whether the IP has surfaced in products, patents, or markets.
steps.guidance: Engage threat intelligence and monitor for the IP's reappearance.
steps.outcome: Actor assessment and downstream-use monitoring in place.

steps.title: Revoke the exploited supply-chain access immediately
steps.desc: Revoke or restrict the compromised supply-chain partner's access to prevent further exfiltration.
steps.outcome: Exploited access is revoked with no further exfiltration occurring.

steps.title: Engage legal/IP counsel and consider law-enforcement referral
steps.desc: Engage legal/IP counsel to assess litigation options and, where warranted, refer the matter to law enforcement or relevant government IP-crime units.
steps.outcome: Legal and, where warranted, law-enforcement engagement initiated.

steps.title: Remediate the exploited access point
steps.desc: Close the specific vulnerability or excessive-access condition in the supply-chain relationship that enabled the theft.

steps.title: Pursue legal remedy against the responsible party
steps.desc: Pursue litigation, contractual remedy, or diplomatic/trade channels (for nation-state-linked theft) as advised by legal counsel.
steps.outcome: Legal remedy pursued per counsel's recommendation.

steps.title: Reassess the supply-chain relationship and access model
steps.desc: Evaluate whether the supply-chain relationship should continue and under what revised access controls.
steps.outcome: Documented decision on the relationship and access model.

steps.title: Strengthen IP-access controls for supply-chain partners
steps.desc: Review and strengthen least-privilege access, monitoring, and contractual IP-protection requirements for supply-chain partners with access to sensitive intellectual property.

ITID-63641.def: A coordinated, large-scale campaign by a nation-state or APT actor to manipulate multiple points in the physical supply chain (manufacturers, distributors, or logistics providers) simultaneously, intended to achieve broad strategic access or disruption capability across many downstream targets.
ITID-63641.purpose: Captures large-scale, systemic manipulation of the physical supply chain by a nation-state or APT actor, affecting multiple vendors, products, or sectors simultaneously.
scopeIncludes: A campaign compromising multiple manufacturers or component suppliers feeding into a common downstream product line
Coordinated tampering across multiple shipments/distributors as part of a single attributed campaign
scopeExcludes: A single, isolated instance of nation-state tampering with one piece of critical equipment (ITID-63611)
A single instance of a cyber-physical hybrid attack against one target (ITID-63621/63622)
ITID-63641.severity: Critical. Large-scale supply chain manipulation represents the highest-severity, highest-blast-radius category in this Tier-2 domain.
ITID-63641.escalation: Escalate immediately to CISO, executive leadership, national security authorities, and industry information-sharing bodies (ISACs).
indicators: Threat intelligence identifying a coordinated campaign affecting multiple vendors or product lines
Pattern of hardware tampering findings across geographically or organizationally unrelated supply chain nodes traced to a common actor
Industry-wide advisory or ISAC alert describing the campaign
vectors: Systemic hardware supply chain compromise across multiple manufacturers (T1195.003)
Coordinated compromise of shared upstream infrastructure used by multiple downstream vendors (T1584 Compromise Infrastructure)
Broad-spectrum initial access, persistence, and impact activity consistent with a full APT kill chain across many targets
rootCauses: Systemic, industry-wide gaps in hardware supply chain assurance
Concentration risk from many organizations relying on the same small set of upstream suppliers
Insufficient cross-industry information sharing on supply chain compromise indicators
mitreTechniques: T1195.002 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Software Supply Chain
T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Supply chain vendor diversification to reduce concentration risk
Participation in industry ISAC threat-intelligence sharing on supply chain campaigns
Independent, industry-coordinated hardware forensic verification programs
ITID-63641.detection: Detection depends heavily on cross-organizational threat intelligence sharing and coordinated forensic hardware inspection; no single organization's telemetry typically reveals the full campaign scope.
ITID-63641.response: Coordinate response through national security authorities and industry ISACs, forensically assess exposure across all potentially affected supply chain nodes, and participate in coordinated disclosure/remediation.
metrics: Number of large-scale supply chain manipulation campaigns identified affecting the organization per year
Percentage of critical suppliers covered by industry ISAC threat-intelligence sharing
detections: Cross-organizational threat-intelligence correlation on supply chain indicators
ITID-63641.notes: This is currently the only leaf under Large-Scale Supply Chain Manipulation; it is the top-severity, broadest-scope leaf in the Nation-State and APT Supply Chain Attacks Tier-3, reserved for coordinated multi-vendor/multi-sector campaigns rather than single-target incidents.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Large-Scale Supply Chain Manipulation
playbook.description: A large-scale manipulation of the supply chain, likely affecting multiple organizations, is suspected or confirmed.

steps.title: Confirm the large-scale manipulation and its multi-victim scope
steps.desc: Confirm evidence of supply-chain manipulation and assess indicators that other organizations are likely affected by the same scheme.
steps.guidance: Engage threat intelligence and, where relevant, industry ISAC contacts early given the likely multi-victim scope.
steps.outcome: Manipulation confirmed with multi-victim likelihood assessed.

steps.title: Characterize the actor and full scope of the scheme
steps.desc: Work with threat intelligence and government partners to characterize the actor and the full extent of the manipulation across the supply chain.
steps.outcome: Actor characterization and scheme scope documented.

steps.title: Assess own organization's specific exposure
steps.desc: Determine the specific systems, products, or data within the organization affected by the manipulation.

steps.title: Activate full incident-response and cross-organization/ISAC coordination
steps.desc: Activate the highest-severity IR process and share indicators with the relevant industry ISAC and government authorities to support coordinated multi-victim response.
steps.outcome: Cross-organization coordination established and IR fully engaged.

steps.title: Isolate affected internal systems/products
steps.desc: Isolate or quarantine the internal systems, products, or components affected by the supply-chain manipulation.

steps.title: Remediate or replace affected components/systems
steps.desc: Remediate or replace all internally affected components or systems through verified, trusted channels.
steps.outcome: All affected components/systems remediated or replaced.

steps.title: Contribute findings to the broader multi-victim investigation
steps.desc: Share forensic findings and indicators with the ISAC, government authorities, and, where appropriate, other affected organizations to support the broader investigation.
steps.outcome: Findings shared to support coordinated remediation across the industry.

steps.title: Validate internal integrity and restore operations
steps.desc: Confirm internal systems are free of the manipulation's effects before restoring normal operations.

steps.title: Notify affected customers/partners
steps.desc: Communicate with affected customers or partners regarding the incident and remediation status.

steps.title: Strengthen industry-wide supply-chain resilience posture
steps.desc: Participate in industry-wide efforts to strengthen supply-chain assurance and coordinate on shared threat indicators going forward.
steps.outcome: Updated internal and industry-coordination practices documented.

ITID-63711.def: A finding that a vendor, manufacturer, or logistics partner in the physical supply chain has failed to meet the security requirements specified in contract, policy, or applicable regulation, creating elevated risk exposure independent of whether an actual compromise has occurred.
ITID-63711.purpose: Captures a vendor's failure to comply with contractually or regulatorily required security requirements in the physical supply chain, a governance/compliance gap rather than an active attack.
scopeIncludes: A vendor found not to have implemented required physical security or chain-of-custody controls during an audit
A vendor failing to disclose a required security incident or control gap as contractually obligated
scopeExcludes: An actual confirmed hardware compromise or tampering event resulting from the non-compliance (log the specific compromise under the relevant Hardware and Device Tampering leaf; this leaf tracks the governance gap itself)
ITID-63711.severity: Medium-High, scaled to the criticality of the vendor's role and the severity of the compliance gap.
ITID-63711.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the vendor supports critical infrastructure or handles highly sensitive components.
ITID-63711.escalation: Escalate to procurement/vendor risk management and legal; require a remediation plan and timeline from the vendor.
indicators: Vendor security audit or assessment identifying a control gap against contractual requirements
Vendor unable to produce evidence of required security certifications or controls
Vendor failing to meet a contractually required incident-disclosure timeline
vectors: Physical supply chain vendor failed to meet contractually required security requirements (facility access controls, chain-of-custody procedures, background checks)
No independent verification step to confirm physical-security requirements were actually implemented on the vendor's site
rootCauses: Insufficient ongoing vendor security compliance monitoring after initial onboarding
Contracts lacking clear, auditable security requirements
No enforcement mechanism (penalties, remediation timelines) tied to compliance gaps
controls: Periodic vendor security compliance audits against contractual requirements
Contractual security requirements with defined enforcement/remediation mechanisms
Vendor risk tiering with compliance monitoring frequency scaled to criticality
ITID-63711.detection: Supply chain governance/vetting gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via supplier risk management and procurement compliance.
ITID-63711.response: Require a documented remediation plan from the vendor with a defined timeline, escalate to contract enforcement if unresolved, and reassess the vendor's risk tier.
metrics: Number of vendor non-compliance findings per year
Percentage of findings remediated within the required timeline
Percentage of critical vendors audited annually
ITID-63711.notes: This is currently the only leaf under Vendor Non-Compliance with Security Requirements; it tracks the governance/compliance gap itself, distinct from any resulting hardware compromise, which is logged under the relevant Hardware and Device Tampering leaf.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Vendor Non-Compliance with Security Requirements (Physical Supply Chain Context)
playbook.description: An audit or assessment has identified that a physical-supply-chain vendor is not compliant with contractually required security requirements.

steps.title: Document the specific non-compliance findings
steps.desc: Compile the audit or assessment findings detailing exactly which contractual security requirements the vendor is failing to meet.
steps.guidance: Reference the specific contract clauses and security standards the vendor agreed to.
steps.outcome: Documented findings with specific requirement-by-requirement gaps.

steps.title: Assess the risk exposure created by the non-compliance
steps.desc: Evaluate what risk the identified gaps create for the organization's goods, data, or operations handled by the vendor.

steps.title: Determine whether the gap has already been exploited
steps.desc: Investigate whether the compliance gap has resulted in any actual security incident or loss to date.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether this is a pure governance gap or one with realized impact.
steps.abort: If evidence of an active incident is found, route to the appropriate incident-specific playbook in addition to this governance process.

steps.title: Formally notify the vendor of the non-compliance
steps.desc: Issue a formal notice to the vendor detailing the non-compliance findings and required remediation timeline.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with legal/procurement on the notice's contractual language.
steps.outcome: Vendor formally notified with a documented remediation deadline.

steps.title: Apply interim risk-reduction measures
steps.desc: Implement interim compensating controls (enhanced monitoring, restricted data/goods sharing) while the vendor remediates.
steps.outcome: Risk is reduced pending full remediation.

steps.title: Verify vendor remediation of each identified gap
steps.desc: Conduct a follow-up assessment or audit to confirm the vendor has closed each identified compliance gap.
steps.outcome: Remediation verified against each specific finding.
steps.abort: If the vendor fails to remediate within the agreed timeline, escalate to contract enforcement or termination.

steps.title: Restore normal vendor relationship terms
steps.desc: Once remediation is verified, lift interim restrictions and restore normal operating terms with the vendor.

steps.title: Strengthen ongoing vendor compliance monitoring
steps.desc: Review how the compliance gap went undetected until this audit and strengthen periodic monitoring/audit cadence for this and similar vendors.
steps.outcome: Updated vendor compliance monitoring procedure documented.

ITID-63721.def: A finding that a supplier below the organization's direct (Tier-1) vendor relationships — a sub-tier or fourth-party supplier — is materially involved in producing components or services the organization relies on, but was not identified, assessed, or risk-rated as part of the supply chain risk management program.
ITID-63721.purpose: Captures the discovery that a sub-tier supplier is unknown or unmapped in the organization's supply chain risk assessment, a visibility gap that limits the organization's ability to assess its own risk.
scopeIncludes: A sub-tier component supplier discovered only after an incident or audit, with no prior risk assessment on file
A direct vendor unable to identify or disclose its own sub-tier suppliers upon request
scopeExcludes: Lack of chain-of-custody tracking for a component whose supplier is known but whose custody history is incomplete (ITID-63722)
A vendor that is known and mapped but has failed a specific security requirement (ITID-63711)
ITID-63721.severity: Medium-High, scaled to the criticality of the unmapped supplier's role in the product/service.
ITID-63721.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the unmapped supplier is later found to have a security issue or is in a high-risk jurisdiction.
ITID-63721.escalation: Escalate to procurement/supply-chain risk management; require the direct vendor to disclose and support a risk assessment of the sub-tier supplier.
indicators: Component-level investigation reveals a supplier not present in the supply chain risk register
A direct vendor cannot answer a sub-tier supplier disclosure request
A security advisory referencing a supplier the organization cannot confirm it does or does not use
vectors: Sub-tier supplier several levels removed from the primary vendor relationship was never identified or included in the supply chain risk assessment
Primary vendor's own supplier-disclosure obligations were not enforced, hiding downstream risk
rootCauses: No contractual requirement for vendors to disclose their own sub-tier suppliers
Supply chain risk assessment program scoped only to direct (Tier-1) vendors
Lack of a component-level bill-of-materials requirement for critical products
controls: Contractual sub-tier supplier disclosure requirements
Component-level bill-of-materials requirement for critical products
Extension of supply chain risk assessment to sub-tier/fourth-party suppliers for critical categories
ITID-63721.detection: Supply chain governance/vetting gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via supplier risk management and procurement compliance.
ITID-63721.response: Require the direct vendor to disclose the sub-tier supplier, conduct a retroactive risk assessment, and update the supply chain risk register.
metrics: Number of previously unmapped sub-tier suppliers identified per year
Percentage of critical products with a complete component-level bill-of-materials on file
ITID-63721.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is about a supplier's very existence/identity being unknown, distinct from chain-of-custody tracking gaps for a known supplier's components (ITID-63722).

playbook.name: Sub-Tier Supplier Unknown/Unmapped in Supply Chain Risk Assessment
playbook.description: A risk assessment or audit has revealed that a sub-tier (fourth-party or deeper) supplier involved in the supply chain is unknown or unmapped, creating a visibility gap.

steps.title: Document how the unmapped sub-tier supplier was discovered
steps.desc: Record the circumstances and evidence that revealed the existence of the unmapped sub-tier supplier.

steps.title: Identify the sub-tier supplier and its role
steps.desc: Determine the sub-tier supplier's identity, location, and specific role in producing or handling goods/components in the supply chain.
steps.guidance: Work with the direct (tier-1) supplier to obtain this information, as they typically hold the relationship.
steps.outcome: Sub-tier supplier identified with role documented.
steps.abort: If the tier-1 supplier cannot or will not identify the sub-tier supplier, treat as an escalated contractual issue with the tier-1 supplier.

steps.title: Assess risk exposure from the unmapped supplier
steps.desc: Evaluate what risk (security, quality, compliance, geopolitical) the unmapped sub-tier supplier introduces.

steps.title: Require the tier-1 supplier to formally disclose sub-tier relationships
steps.desc: Formally require the direct supplier to disclose all sub-tier suppliers involved and to obtain the organization's approval for any undisclosed ones going forward.
steps.outcome: Tier-1 supplier formally commits to sub-tier disclosure.

steps.title: Conduct risk assessment of the newly mapped sub-tier supplier
steps.desc: Perform the same risk assessment/vetting on the sub-tier supplier that would apply to a directly contracted supplier.
steps.outcome: Sub-tier supplier is assessed against standard vetting criteria.

steps.title: Remediate any unacceptable risk found in the sub-tier supplier
steps.desc: Require remediation of any unacceptable risk findings from the sub-tier supplier assessment, or require the tier-1 supplier to change sub-tier sourcing.
steps.outcome: Unacceptable risk is remediated or sourcing is changed.

steps.title: Update supply-chain mapping records
steps.desc: Update the supply-chain risk-assessment records and mapping documentation to reflect the newly identified sub-tier supplier.

steps.title: Strengthen sub-tier visibility requirements
steps.desc: Implement contractual requirements for ongoing sub-tier supplier disclosure and periodic supply-chain mapping exercises to prevent future blind spots.

ITID-63722.def: A finding that a critical component's chain-of-custody records — the documented history of its handling from manufacture through delivery — are incomplete, missing, or otherwise insufficient to verify the component's provenance and integrity.
ITID-63722.purpose: Captures the absence of adequate chain-of-custody tracking for critical components, limiting the organization's ability to verify a component's provenance and handling history.
scopeIncludes: A critical component received with gaps in its custody/handling documentation
A supplier unable to produce required chain-of-custody records upon request
scopeExcludes: A sub-tier supplier being entirely unknown/unmapped (ITID-63721)
Actual tampering evidence found on a shipment, which is a Hardware and Device Tampering finding (ITID-63131) rather than a documentation gap
ITID-63722.severity: Medium-High, scaled to the criticality of the component whose custody history is incomplete.
ITID-63722.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 for components supporting critical infrastructure or classified systems.
ITID-63722.escalation: Escalate to procurement/supply-chain risk management; require the supplier to remediate its chain-of-custody documentation practices.
indicators: Component received without a complete custody/handling record
Audit reveals custody documentation gaps for a class of critical components
Supplier contract lacks a chain-of-custody documentation requirement
vectors: Critical component moved through multiple handoffs in the supply chain with no chain-of-custody record, obscuring where tampering could have occurred
No serialized tracking or tamper-evident packaging to establish provenance at each handoff
rootCauses: No contractual requirement for end-to-end chain-of-custody documentation on critical components
Inconsistent custody documentation practices across multiple carriers/handlers in a component's path
Lack of audit verification of custody records at receiving
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Contractual chain-of-custody documentation requirements for critical components
Custody record verification at receiving for critical component categories
Standardized custody documentation format across all handlers in the component's path
ITID-63722.detection: Supply chain governance/vetting gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via supplier risk management and procurement compliance.
ITID-63722.response: Require the supplier to remediate documentation gaps, retroactively verify the component's provenance where possible, and consider enhanced inspection for components lacking complete custody records.
metrics: Percentage of critical components with complete chain-of-custody documentation
Number of custody documentation gaps identified per year
ITID-63722.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is about incomplete custody documentation for a known supplier's known component, distinct from the supplier itself being unmapped (ITID-63721).

playbook.name: Lack of Chain-of-Custody Tracking for Critical Components
playbook.description: An audit or assessment has revealed that critical components lack adequate chain-of-custody tracking through the supply chain.

steps.title: Document the chain-of-custody gap
steps.desc: Identify specifically where custody tracking is missing or inadequate for the affected critical components (which stages, which suppliers/carriers).
steps.outcome: Gap documented with specific stages/parties lacking tracking.

steps.title: Assess risk exposure from the tracking gap
steps.desc: Evaluate the risk this creates — inability to detect tampering, counterfeiting, or diversion of the affected components.

steps.title: Determine whether any components may already be compromised
steps.desc: Given the tracking gap, assess whether there is reason to believe components currently in use may have been tampered with or substituted without detection.
steps.outcome: Determination of whether active investigation of in-use components is warranted.
steps.abort: If evidence of actual compromise is found, route to the appropriate tampered-hardware/shipment playbook in addition to this governance process.

steps.title: Implement interim manual custody tracking
steps.desc: Apply interim manual chain-of-custody documentation for the affected components while a permanent tracking solution is implemented.
steps.outcome: Interim tracking is in place with no further custody gaps.

steps.title: Implement a permanent chain-of-custody tracking solution
steps.desc: Deploy a robust chain-of-custody tracking mechanism (serialized tracking, tamper-evident seals with logging, blockchain or ledger-based tracking as appropriate) for the critical components.
steps.outcome: Permanent tracking solution implemented and operational.

steps.title: Require suppliers/carriers to support the tracking requirement
steps.desc: Update contracts and operational agreements with suppliers and carriers to require compliance with the new chain-of-custody tracking requirement.
steps.outcome: Suppliers/carriers contractually bound to the tracking requirement.

steps.title: Verify tracking coverage across the supply chain
steps.desc: Confirm the new tracking solution provides complete coverage across all stages previously identified as gaps.

steps.title: Review chain-of-custody requirements across other critical component categories
steps.desc: Assess whether similar tracking gaps exist for other critical component categories and extend the remediation as needed.

ITID-63723.def: General or not-yet-classified reports of a gap in the organization's visibility into its physical supply chain.
ITID-63723.purpose: Intake bucket for supply chain visibility failures that do not fit the unmapped sub-tier supplier or chain-of-custody documentation leaves.
scopeIncludes: Visibility-gap reports where the specific mechanism is not yet determined
Novel or mixed supply chain visibility gaps not covered by the more specific leaves
scopeExcludes: Sub-tier supplier unknown/unmapped (ITID-63721)
Lack of chain-of-custody tracking (ITID-63722)
ITID-63723.priority: P3 pending triage; re-prioritize once the specific gap and component criticality are known.
ITID-63723.escalation: Escalate to procurement/supply-chain risk management for triage; reclassify to a specific leaf once the gap is confirmed.
indicators: Visibility-gap evidence not yet attributed to a specific known pattern
vectors: Generic supply chain visibility failure not captured by a more specific sub-category
No end-to-end mapping of the supply chain to identify where visibility gaps exist
rootCauses: Gaps in supply chain risk assessment program scope generally
controls: General supply chain risk assessment and visibility program
ITID-63723.detection: Supply chain governance/vetting gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via supplier risk management and procurement compliance.
ITID-63723.response: Triage the report and reclassify to a specific leaf once the gap is confirmed.
metrics: Count of general visibility-gap reports pending triage
Percentage subsequently reclassified
ITID-63723.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf for the Supply Chain Visibility Failures Tier-4 group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Supply Chain Visibility Failure
playbook.description: An audit or assessment has identified a supply-chain visibility failure of unspecified type, requiring governance-focused remediation.

steps.title: Document the specific visibility gap
steps.desc: Identify precisely what visibility is lacking (supplier identity, component provenance, custody tracking, or other) and where in the supply chain.

steps.title: Assess risk exposure from the visibility gap
steps.desc: Evaluate the risk this visibility gap creates for the organization.

steps.title: Determine whether the gap has already resulted in undetected impact
steps.desc: Assess whether the visibility failure may have already allowed an undetected security or quality issue.
steps.abort: If evidence of an actual incident is found, route to the applicable incident-specific playbook in addition to this process.

steps.title: Apply interim compensating oversight measures
steps.desc: Implement interim manual or enhanced oversight measures to reduce risk while a permanent visibility solution is developed.

steps.title: Notify affected internal stakeholders and vendor management
steps.desc: Notify relevant internal stakeholders (procurement, vendor management, affected business units) of the identified visibility gap and interim measures being applied.
steps.guidance: Ensure stakeholders understand the interim compensating measures and any temporary operational impact.
steps.outcome: Stakeholders are informed and aligned on interim handling of the gap.

steps.title: Implement a permanent visibility solution
steps.desc: Deploy the appropriate tooling or process improvement (supplier mapping, tracking system, reporting requirement) to close the visibility gap.

steps.title: Verify closure of the visibility gap
steps.desc: Confirm the new solution provides adequate visibility across the previously identified gap.

steps.title: Review for similar visibility gaps elsewhere in the supply chain
steps.desc: Assess whether similar visibility gaps exist elsewhere and extend remediation as needed.

ITID-63731.def: A finding that a supplier or third-party manufacturer was granted an active role in the physical supply chain without completing the organization's required background, security, or risk vetting process.
ITID-63731.purpose: Captures a supplier being onboarded into the supply chain without required background or security vetting, a preventable governance failure.
scopeIncludes: A supplier discovered to be active in the supply chain with no completed vetting record on file
Vetting steps skipped or overridden due to urgency without a documented risk acceptance
scopeExcludes: A vetted supplier's undisclosed use of an additional, unauthorized fourth-party subcontractor (ITID-63732)
ITID-63731.severity: Medium-High, scaled to the criticality of the supplier's role and the sensitivity of what they handle.
ITID-63731.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the unvetted supplier handles critical infrastructure components or sensitive data.
ITID-63731.escalation: Escalate to procurement/vendor risk management; initiate retroactive vetting immediately and consider suspending the relationship pending completion.
indicators: Supplier active in procurement/production systems with no vetting record
Audit reveals a vetting step was bypassed without documented risk acceptance
New supplier onboarded under time pressure with vetting deferred and never completed
vectors: Supplier onboarded and granted access to facilities, systems, or components without background checks or security vetting
Onboarding process prioritized speed/cost over verifying the supplier's security posture and personnel trustworthiness
rootCauses: Vetting process bypassed under business/schedule pressure
No hard gate preventing an unvetted supplier from being activated in procurement systems
Insufficient tracking of vetting completion status across the supplier lifecycle
controls: Hard system gate preventing supplier activation without completed vetting
Documented risk-acceptance process for any expedited/deferred vetting
Periodic audit of active suppliers against vetting completion records
ITID-63731.detection: Supply chain governance/vetting gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via supplier risk management and procurement compliance.
ITID-63731.response: Initiate retroactive vetting immediately, assess risk exposure from the period of non-compliance, and consider suspension pending completion for high-risk suppliers.
metrics: Number of unvetted-supplier findings per year
Percentage of active suppliers with completed vetting on file
Average time to complete retroactive vetting once identified
ITID-63731.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is about a primary supplier's own vetting being skipped, distinct from an already-vetted supplier's undisclosed use of a further subcontractor (ITID-63732).

playbook.name: Supplier Onboarded Without Background/Security Vetting
playbook.description: An audit or assessment has revealed that a supplier was onboarded into the supply chain without required background or security vetting.

steps.title: Confirm the vetting was not performed
steps.desc: Review onboarding records to confirm the required background/security vetting was not completed for the supplier.
steps.abort: If vetting records are found but were misfiled, close the case with corrected documentation.

steps.title: Assess the supplier's current access and role
steps.desc: Determine what goods, data, facilities, or systems the unvetted supplier currently has access to or influence over.

steps.title: Determine how the vetting step was bypassed
steps.desc: Investigate the process failure that allowed onboarding without vetting (exception granted, process skipped, urgent procurement bypass).
steps.outcome: Root cause of the process failure identified.

steps.title: Apply interim risk-reduction measures pending vetting
steps.desc: Restrict the supplier's access or role to the minimum necessary while retroactive vetting is conducted.
steps.outcome: Risk is reduced pending vetting outcome.

steps.title: Conduct retroactive background/security vetting
steps.desc: Perform the full required vetting process on the supplier retroactively.
steps.outcome: Vetting completed with a documented outcome.
steps.abort: If the supplier fails vetting, proceed to relationship termination.

steps.title: Act on the vetting outcome
steps.desc: Based on the vetting result, either restore full supplier standing, apply ongoing enhanced monitoring, or terminate the relationship.
steps.outcome: Documented decision and action taken based on vetting outcome.

steps.title: Restore or adjust supplier relationship terms
steps.desc: Implement the decided relationship terms (normal, enhanced monitoring, or termination) with the supplier.

steps.title: Close the onboarding process gap
steps.desc: Fix the onboarding process control that allowed vetting to be bypassed, and audit other recently onboarded suppliers for the same gap.
steps.outcome: Onboarding process strengthened; other suppliers audited.

ITID-63732.def: A finding that a properly vetted, authorized supplier has engaged a fourth-party subcontractor to perform work without disclosing this relationship to the organization, bypassing the requirement for the organization to assess and approve that subcontractor.
ITID-63732.purpose: Captures the discovery that a vetted supplier has used an unauthorized fourth-party subcontractor without disclosure, extending unassessed risk further into the supply chain.
scopeIncludes: A vetted supplier subcontracting production or handling to an undisclosed third party
Discovery of an undisclosed subcontractor's involvement through an audit, incident, or product marking
scopeExcludes: A primary supplier itself being onboarded without vetting (ITID-63731)
ITID-63732.severity: Medium-High, scaled to the criticality of the work performed by the undisclosed subcontractor.
ITID-63732.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the undisclosed subcontractor handled critical or sensitive components.
ITID-63732.escalation: Escalate to procurement/vendor risk management and legal; require immediate disclosure of all subcontracting relationships and assess the undisclosed party's risk.
indicators: Audit or product marking revealing an unauthorized subcontractor's involvement
Contractual subcontracting-disclosure clause found to have been violated
A security incident traced to a party not on the organization's approved supplier list
vectors: Approved supplier subcontracted work to an undisclosed fourth-party without the organization's knowledge or approval
Contractual flow-down requirements for subcontractor disclosure and vetting were not enforced
rootCauses: Contracts lacking an enforceable subcontracting-disclosure and pre-approval requirement
No audit mechanism to verify a supplier's actual production/handling chain against its disclosed one
Insufficient penalties or enforcement for undisclosed subcontracting
controls: Contractual subcontracting-disclosure and pre-approval requirements
Periodic audit verifying a supplier's actual production/handling chain against disclosures
Enforcement mechanisms (penalties, contract termination) for undisclosed subcontracting
ITID-63732.detection: Supply chain governance/vetting gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via supplier risk management and procurement compliance.
ITID-63732.response: Require immediate full disclosure of subcontracting relationships, retroactively vet the undisclosed subcontractor, and pursue contractual remedies against the primary supplier.
metrics: Number of undisclosed subcontractor findings per year
Percentage of suppliers audited for subcontracting-chain accuracy
ITID-63732.notes: Differentiator within this Tier-4 group: this leaf is about an undisclosed additional layer beneath an already-vetted supplier, distinct from the primary supplier itself lacking vetting (ITID-63731).

playbook.name: Unauthorized Fourth-Party Subcontractor Used Without Disclosure
playbook.description: A supplier is discovered to be using an undisclosed fourth-party subcontractor in violation of contractual disclosure requirements.

steps.title: Confirm the undisclosed subcontractor relationship
steps.desc: Verify evidence that the supplier is using a fourth-party subcontractor that was not disclosed as required by contract.
steps.abort: If the relationship was in fact properly disclosed, close the case.

steps.title: Identify the subcontractor and its role
steps.desc: Determine the subcontractor's identity, location, and role in the supply chain.

steps.title: Assess risk exposure from the undisclosed subcontractor
steps.desc: Evaluate what risk (security, quality, compliance, geopolitical) the undisclosed subcontractor introduces.

steps.title: Formally notify the supplier of the contract violation
steps.desc: Issue formal notice to the supplier citing the non-disclosure violation and requiring immediate remediation.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with legal/procurement on notice language and contractual remedies available.

steps.title: Vet the subcontractor against standard supplier criteria
steps.desc: Perform the same risk assessment/vetting on the subcontractor that would apply to a directly contracted supplier.
steps.outcome: Subcontractor assessed against standard vetting criteria.

steps.title: Require remediation or termination of the subcontractor arrangement
steps.desc: Based on the vetting outcome, require the supplier to either formally disclose and maintain the subcontractor under approved terms, or discontinue using it.
steps.outcome: Documented decision and required action communicated to the supplier.

steps.title: Update supply-chain records
steps.desc: Update supply-chain mapping and vendor records to reflect the subcontractor relationship status.

steps.title: Strengthen subcontractor disclosure enforcement
steps.desc: Implement stronger contractual audit rights and periodic subcontractor-disclosure verification to prevent recurrence.

ITID-63733.def: General or not-yet-classified reports of a supplier or manufacturer operating in the physical supply chain without adequate verification.
ITID-63733.purpose: Intake bucket for unverified supplier or manufacturer findings that do not fit the unvetted-onboarding or undisclosed-subcontractor leaves.
scopeIncludes: Unverified-supplier reports where the specific mechanism is not yet determined
Novel or mixed unverified-supplier patterns not covered by the more specific leaves
scopeExcludes: Supplier onboarded without background/security vetting (ITID-63731)
Unauthorized fourth-party subcontractor used without disclosure (ITID-63732)
ITID-63733.priority: P3 pending triage; re-prioritize once the specific gap and supplier criticality are known.
ITID-63733.escalation: Escalate to procurement/vendor risk management for triage; reclassify to a specific leaf once the gap is confirmed.
indicators: Unverified-supplier evidence not yet attributed to a specific known pattern
vectors: Generic unverified supplier or manufacturer relationship not captured by a more specific sub-category
No standardized supplier vetting checklist applied consistently across the procurement process
rootCauses: Gaps in supplier vetting/verification program scope generally
controls: General supplier vetting and verification program
ITID-63733.detection: Supply chain governance/vetting gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via supplier risk management and procurement compliance.
ITID-63733.response: Triage the report and reclassify to a specific leaf once the gap is confirmed.
metrics: Count of general unverified-supplier reports pending triage
Percentage subsequently reclassified
ITID-63733.notes: Catch-all/intake leaf for the Unverified Suppliers and Third-Party Manufacturers Tier-4 group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Unverified Supplier or Manufacturer
playbook.description: An audit or assessment has identified a supplier or manufacturer in the supply chain that has not undergone required verification of unspecified type.

steps.title: Confirm the verification gap
steps.desc: Confirm that the required verification of the supplier/manufacturer was not completed and identify what verification is missing.
steps.abort: If verification was in fact completed but undocumented, correct the record and close.

steps.title: Assess the supplier/manufacturer's current role and exposure
steps.desc: Determine what goods, data, or processes the unverified party currently affects.

steps.title: Determine how the verification step was bypassed
steps.desc: Investigate the process failure that allowed the party to be used without required verification.

steps.title: Apply interim risk-reduction measures
steps.desc: Restrict the party's role or access to the minimum necessary while verification is completed.

steps.title: Conduct the required verification
steps.desc: Complete the full required verification process for the supplier/manufacturer.
steps.abort: If verification fails, proceed to relationship termination.

steps.title: Act on the verification outcome
steps.desc: Based on the result, restore full standing, apply enhanced monitoring, or terminate the relationship.

steps.title: Update supplier records
steps.desc: Update vendor management records to reflect the verification outcome and any resulting relationship changes.

steps.title: Close the verification process gap
steps.desc: Fix the process control that allowed the verification step to be bypassed, and audit other suppliers for the same gap.

ITID-63741.def: A finding, typically surfaced through supplier audit, procurement compliance review, or regulatory inspection, that a counterfeit or otherwise unauthorized (non-genuine, unapproved-source) component has entered the supply chain, considered here as a governance/vetting failure rather than an active-attack event.
ITID-63741.purpose: Captures discovery of a counterfeit or unauthorized component in the supply chain from a compliance/procurement-audit angle, complementing the operational Counterfeit Hardware leaves under Hardware and Device Tampering.
scopeIncludes: A compliance audit or procurement review identifying a counterfeit component that was not caught at receiving
A regulatory inspection flagging an unauthorized-source component in a delivered product
Retroactive discovery of counterfeit parts through a recall or field-failure investigation
scopeExcludes: Operational discovery of counterfeit hardware at receiving/inspection, which is logged under the Counterfeit Hardware leaves (ITID-63111-63113) — this leaf is for the same underlying issue when it surfaces through a compliance/governance channel rather than a receiving inspection
ITID-63741.severity: Medium-High, scaled to the criticality of the component and how widely it has propagated before discovery.
ITID-63741.priority: P2 by default; escalate to P1 if the component is already deployed in critical infrastructure or safety-relevant systems.
ITID-63741.escalation: Escalate to procurement/supply-chain risk management, legal, and (for regulated industries) the relevant regulator; quarantine all known units and trace back to the source.
indicators: Supplier audit or procurement compliance review flags a component lacking valid authenticity documentation
Regulatory inspection identifies an unauthorized-source component in a delivered product
Field-failure or recall investigation traces root cause to a counterfeit component
vectors: Counterfeit or unauthorized component substituted into the supply chain, discovered during inspection or after field failure
No component-authentication or anti-counterfeit verification step at incoming inspection
rootCauses: Compliance/audit program not scoped to catch component-level counterfeiting
Procurement documentation requirements insufficiently verified before component approval
Gaps between receiving-inspection controls and downstream compliance audit coverage
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Compliance audit program scoped to include component-level authenticity verification
Procurement documentation verification requirements for component approval
Coordinated tracking between receiving-inspection findings and compliance audit programs
ITID-63741.detection: Supply chain governance/vetting gap — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via supplier risk management and procurement compliance, though this leaf references T1195.003 because it is the same underlying hardware-integrity issue as ITID-63111-63113, viewed from a compliance-discovery angle rather than a receiving-inspection one.
ITID-63741.response: Quarantine all known affected units, trace the component back to its source, notify affected business units/regulators as required, and close the compliance gap that allowed the counterfeit to go undetected.
metrics: Number of counterfeit-component findings surfaced via compliance/audit channels per year
Percentage of components with verified authenticity documentation
sops: Hardware Receiving and Authenticity Verification SOP
ITID-63741.notes: This is currently the only leaf under Counterfeit or Unauthorized Components in Supply Chain; it is the compliance-discovery counterpart to the operational Counterfeit Hardware leaves (ITID-63111-63113) and should be cross-referenced rather than duplicated when the same underlying component issue is logged in both places.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Counterfeit or Unauthorized Component in Supply Chain
playbook.description: An audit or assessment has identified a counterfeit or unauthorized component present in the supply chain of unspecified type.

steps.title: Confirm the component is counterfeit or unauthorized
steps.desc: Verify against OEM records or vendor authentication whether the flagged component is counterfeit or otherwise unauthorized for use.
steps.abort: If confirmed genuine and authorized, close the case.

steps.title: Determine scope of affected products/inventory
steps.desc: Identify all products or inventory containing the counterfeit or unauthorized component.
steps.outcome: Full scope of affected products/inventory identified.

steps.title: Trace the component's entry point into the supply chain
steps.desc: Investigate how and where the counterfeit/unauthorized component entered the supply chain.

steps.title: Quarantine affected inventory and hold from further use
steps.desc: Hold all affected inventory and in-progress production from further use or shipment pending resolution.
steps.outcome: No further use of the affected component occurs.

steps.title: Notify the supplying vendor and, where warranted, law enforcement
steps.desc: Report the counterfeit/unauthorized component to the supplying vendor and, for confirmed counterfeit goods, to law enforcement or customs.

steps.title: Remove and replace the counterfeit/unauthorized component
steps.desc: Remove the component from affected products/inventory and replace with a verified, authorized component.
steps.outcome: No counterfeit/unauthorized components remain in use.

steps.title: Validate replacement components and restore normal operations
steps.desc: Confirm replacement components are verified genuine before resuming normal production/use.

steps.title: Strengthen component sourcing and receiving verification
steps.desc: Review and strengthen sourcing and receiving-inspection controls to prevent future counterfeit/unauthorized components from entering the supply chain.

ITID-64111.def: An adversary impersonates a trusted executive (real name, title, or authority) to manipulate a supplier, partner, or internal staff member into taking an action they would not otherwise take, where the operative mechanism is abuse of the trust placed in that executive's identity rather than a technical compromise of an account or system.
ITID-64111.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for executive impersonation attacks pursued through the supply chain's trust-exploitation angle that do not fit a more specific leaf in this branch.
scopeIncludes: Reports of executive impersonation via phone, voicemail, or messaging apps not covered by the email-specific BEC leaves elsewhere in the taxonomy
Impersonation of a board member, auditor, or regulator acting 'on behalf of' an executive
Cases pending triage before routing to a more specific ITID
scopeExcludes: Email-channel executive impersonation with a defined BEC pattern (see ITID-22411 through ITID-22414 and ITID-53111)
Spear phishing that relies on a prior trusted relationship rather than executive authority (ITID-64121)
ITID-64111.severity: Medium, escalating to High if a financial or access-granting action was requested or taken.
ITID-64111.priority: P2 at report; P1 if any transaction, credential, or data disclosure occurred.
ITID-64111.escalation: Escalate to SOC and the impersonated executive's office for confirmation; loop in finance if a payment or transfer was requested.
indicators: Urgent, out-of-band request purportedly from a senior executive
Pressure to bypass normal verification or approval steps
Contact channel inconsistent with the executive's normal practice
vectors: Voice or messaging-app impersonation using publicly available executive information
Impersonation via a spoofed or lookalike phone number
rootCauses: No standard callback-verification step for high-authority requests
Over-availability of executive contact patterns and travel schedules in public/social sources
controls: Mandatory out-of-band verification for high-authority requests
Executive impersonation awareness training
ITID-64111.detection: Largely dependent on employee reporting; limited technical telemetry exists for voice/in-person impersonation.
ITID-64111.response: Verify the request through an independent, pre-established channel before any action is taken or reversed if already taken.
metrics: Count of executive impersonation reports by channel
Time to verification
ITID-64111.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. The fuller, pattern-specific executive impersonation treatment lives in the BEC domain (ITID-22411-ITID-22414, ITID-53111); this leaf exists to capture non-email, trust-exploitation-flavored variants specific to the supply chain context.

playbook.name: Executive Impersonation Attack
playbook.description: An attacker impersonates a senior executive (via spoofed email, deepfake voice, or compromised account) to pressure an employee into an urgent unauthorized action.

steps.title: Flag report of urgent executive request
steps.desc: Intake the employee's report of a request purportedly from an executive (email, text, call, or deepfake audio/video) involving urgency, secrecy, or bypassing normal process.
steps.guidance: Note the channel used, exact wording, requested action, and any pressure/urgency/confidentiality language. These are the classic social-engineering markers.
steps.outcome: Incident ticket opened with full context of the impersonation attempt.

steps.title: Verify sender identity out-of-band
steps.desc: Contact the purported executive through a known-good channel (e.g. direct phone call to a verified number, not one supplied in the suspicious message).
steps.guidance: Never use contact details provided in the suspicious message itself. Use directory-listed or previously verified numbers.
steps.outcome: Confirmation the executive did or did not send the request.
steps.abort: If the executive confirms the request is legitimate, close as false positive and document the verification method used for training purposes.

steps.title: Analyze message/call artifacts for spoofing indicators
steps.desc: Review email headers, sender domain, reply-to address, or call metadata/voice characteristics for signs of spoofing or deepfake generation.
steps.guidance: Check for lookalike domains, display-name spoofing, header anomalies, and audio artifacts typical of voice-cloning tools.
steps.outcome: Technical evidence of impersonation method documented.

steps.title: Halt the requested action
steps.desc: Immediately instruct the targeted employee and any involved parties (e.g. finance, IT) to pause or reverse any action already taken in response to the request.
steps.guidance: Speed matters most in wire-transfer or credential-disclosure scenarios; contact the bank or platform immediately if funds moved.
steps.outcome: Requested action stopped before completion, or reversal initiated if already executed.

steps.title: Block sender and related infrastructure
steps.desc: Block the spoofed sender address/domain and any phone numbers used, and search mail logs for other recipients of similar messages.
steps.guidance: Use email gateway blocklists and check for a broader campaign targeting multiple employees.
steps.outcome: Malicious sender blocked org-wide; scope of campaign known.

steps.title: Notify affected employee population
steps.desc: Alert employees who commonly receive executive requests (finance, EA staff, procurement) about the specific impersonation tactic observed.
steps.guidance: Include example artifacts (sanitized) so staff can recognize similar future attempts.
steps.outcome: Relevant staff informed and alert to the specific pretext used.

steps.title: Implement/reinforce callback verification requirement
steps.desc: Formalize or reinforce a mandatory out-of-band callback verification step for any urgent financial or credential-related request purportedly from an executive.
steps.guidance: Tie this to finance and IT process documentation, not just awareness training.
steps.outcome: Verification requirement documented and communicated as policy.

steps.title: Confirm no residual exposure
steps.desc: Confirm no funds, credentials, or data were disclosed, or that recovery/reversal actions for any disclosed items are complete.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with finance/bank or IT as applicable to confirm final status.
steps.outcome: Organization confirmed to have no outstanding exposure from the attempt.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review and update training
steps.desc: Review the incident with stakeholders and update security-awareness training and verification procedures based on the specific pretext and channel used.
steps.guidance: Capture the pretext, channel, and any process gap that allowed the attempt to progress.
steps.outcome: Training materials and process documentation updated; lessons captured in the case record.

ITID-64121.def: A targeted phishing attempt that derives its credibility not from generic impersonation but from genuine knowledge of, or access to, an established trust relationship (a real vendor contact, a real internal colleague, a real project history) between the sender and the target.
ITID-64121.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for spear phishing that succeeds specifically by abusing an existing, legitimate trusted relationship between sender and target.
scopeIncludes: Spear phishing referencing real, current project or transaction details known only to the trusted party
Phishing sent from a genuinely compromised trusted contact's account, where the compromise itself is tracked elsewhere but the trust-abuse pattern is tracked here
scopeExcludes: Generic spear phishing with no genuine trust relationship being abused (tracked under ITID-10000's phishing domain)
Fully impersonated vendor identity with no real prior relationship (ITID-64131)
ITID-64121.severity: Medium-High, given the elevated success rate of trust-based spear phishing over generic phishing.
ITID-64121.priority: P2, escalating to P1 on click-through or credential entry.
ITID-64121.escalation: Escalate immediately if the trusted party's account may itself be compromised, since that expands scope beyond a single target.
indicators: Phishing content referencing accurate, non-public relationship details
Sudden change in a trusted contact's communication pattern or requests
vectors: Email sent from a genuinely compromised trusted-partner mailbox
Reconnaissance of a real business relationship prior to crafting the lure
rootCauses: Insufficient verification of unusual requests even from known, trusted senders
Lack of visibility into a partner's own security posture
controls: Anomaly detection on trusted-sender behavior changes
Verification protocol for unusual requests regardless of sender trust level
ITID-64121.detection: Email security tooling can flag anomalies, but the trust-abuse element itself is best caught by employee suspicion and out-of-band verification.
ITID-64121.response: Treat any suspected compromise of the trusted sender as a potential supply-chain-wide exposure, not an isolated phishing report.
metrics: Count of trust-based spear phishing reports
Percentage traced to a genuinely compromised trusted account
detections: Email anomaly detection on known trusted senders
ITID-64121.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. Cross-references the fuller phishing treatment in ITID-10000 and the BEC-specific patterns in ITID-50000; this leaf is scoped narrowly to the trust-relationship-abuse angle.

playbook.name: Trust-Based Spear Phishing
playbook.description: An attacker crafts a spear-phishing message that abuses an existing trusted relationship (colleague, partner, vendor contact) to increase credibility and bypass suspicion.

steps.title: Intake reported spear-phishing message
steps.desc: Collect the suspicious message and identify the trusted relationship being impersonated or abused (known colleague, partner contact, prior email thread).
steps.guidance: Determine whether the sender account is spoofed or genuinely compromised (thread hijacking).
steps.outcome: Message preserved with headers; trust relationship being exploited identified.

steps.title: Determine if trusted account is compromised or spoofed
steps.desc: Check whether the apparent sender's actual account/mailbox shows signs of compromise (login anomalies, forwarding rules, sent-items) versus simple display-name/domain spoofing.
steps.guidance: If the trusted party's account is compromised, this becomes a joint incident with them.
steps.outcome: Root cause established: spoofed identity vs. compromised trusted account.

steps.title: Identify other recipients targeted via same trust chain
steps.desc: Search mail logs for other messages sent from the same spoofed/compromised identity to determine the blast radius.
steps.guidance: Pay special attention to recipients who would extend high trust to the impersonated party.
steps.outcome: Full list of targeted recipients compiled.

steps.title: Quarantine phishing messages and block indicators
steps.desc: Remove the phishing messages from all mailboxes and block associated URLs/attachments/sender infrastructure.
steps.guidance: Use mail admin center to purge across the tenant.
steps.outcome: Phishing messages removed from all inboxes; malicious indicators blocked.

steps.title: Notify and coordinate with the impersonated trusted party
steps.desc: If the trusted party's own account was compromised, notify them (or their security team, if external) to coordinate joint containment.
steps.guidance: For external partners, use a verified contact channel, not the compromised one.
steps.outcome: Trusted party notified and joint remediation underway if applicable.
steps.abort: If the trust relationship is internal only, skip external coordination.

steps.title: Remediate compromised account if applicable
steps.desc: If the trusted account was compromised, reset credentials, revoke sessions, and remove malicious mail rules/forwarding.
steps.guidance: Follow standard account-compromise eradication steps.
steps.abort: Not applicable if only spoofing (no compromise) occurred.

steps.title: Reinforce verification for trust-based requests
steps.desc: Update guidance so employees verify unusual requests even from known/trusted contacts, especially those involving credentials, payments, or data.
steps.guidance: Emphasize that trust in the sender's identity is not sufficient verification of the request's legitimacy.
steps.outcome: Updated guidance issued to affected teams.

steps.title: Confirm no credential or data compromise among targets
steps.desc: Confirm targeted recipients did not submit credentials or sensitive data, or complete resets/notifications for those who did.
steps.guidance: Cross-check with any linked landing-page telemetry if the phish included one.
steps.outcome: All targeted recipients confirmed safe or fully remediated.

steps.title: Document trust-chain exploitation pattern
steps.desc: Record how the trusted relationship was identified/abused by the attacker and share findings for future detection tuning.
steps.guidance: Feed indicators into phishing-detection rules where the pretext relies on relationship context.
steps.outcome: Findings documented and detection rules updated.

ITID-64131.def: An adversary fabricates or impersonates a vendor/supplier identity (invoicing, onboarding, or account-update contact) with no genuine prior relationship, exploiting the general trust organizations extend to counterparties presenting as legitimate suppliers.
ITID-64131.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for scams in which an adversary poses as a vendor or supplier to defraud or manipulate the organization.
scopeIncludes: Fake new-vendor onboarding requests
Unsolicited 'updated banking details' notices from a purported existing supplier
Fraudulent invoices from an entity impersonating a real or fictitious supplier
scopeExcludes: Compromise of a genuine, existing vendor's real communication channel (ITID-64221, Misuse of Trusted Third-Party Access)
Wire fraud following a confirmed banking-detail change scam (ITID-53211, tracked in Financial Fraud)
ITID-64131.severity: Medium, escalating to High where a payment was executed or vendor master-data was altered.
ITID-64131.priority: P2 at report; P1 upon confirmed financial loss or master-data change.
ITID-64131.escalation: Escalate to accounts payable and finance immediately on any banking-detail-change request; freeze pending payments to the vendor in question.
indicators: Unsolicited banking-detail change request
New vendor with minimal verifiable business history
Invoice inconsistent with known purchase orders
vectors: Fraudulent vendor onboarding submission
Spoofed vendor domain used to request payment changes
rootCauses: Weak vendor identity verification at onboarding
No independent callback verification for banking-detail changes
controls: Vendor onboarding identity verification
Mandatory callback verification for banking-detail changes
ITID-64131.detection: Primarily a process-control detection surface (AP workflow checks) rather than a technical telemetry one.
ITID-64131.response: Verify any vendor detail change through a pre-established, independent contact before honoring it.
metrics: Count of fake vendor scam attempts detected pre-payment
Value of attempted fraud prevented
ITID-64131.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. Distinct from ITID-64221 (a genuinely trusted third party's access is misused) and from the Financial Fraud wire-transfer leaves, which track the downstream payment loss.

playbook.name: Fake Vendor/Supplier Scam
playbook.description: An attacker poses as a known or plausible vendor/supplier to redirect payments, extract data, or gain access by exploiting the trust of an established or expected business relationship.

steps.title: Intake suspicious vendor communication
steps.desc: Collect the communication claiming to be from a vendor/supplier (invoice, payment-detail change request, purchase order) and note inconsistencies.
steps.guidance: Common red flags: changed bank details, new contact email slightly different from known vendor domain, urgency to process payment.
steps.outcome: Suspicious communication logged with full details.

steps.title: Verify vendor identity and request via known channel
steps.desc: Contact the actual vendor using previously established contact information (not details in the suspicious communication) to confirm legitimacy.
steps.guidance: Check accounts-payable records for the vendor's on-file contact and banking details.
steps.outcome: Vendor confirms or denies the communication and any requested changes.
steps.abort: If vendor confirms the request as legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Check for real vendor account compromise
steps.desc: If the vendor confirms they did not send the message, determine whether their actual email/systems were compromised (real vendor breach) versus pure spoofing.
steps.guidance: Ask the vendor to check their own logs if their domain was used directly rather than a lookalike.
steps.outcome: Root cause (spoofed lookalike vs. genuine vendor compromise) established.

steps.title: Halt pending payments to the reported account
steps.desc: Immediately place a hold on any pending or recent payments tied to the changed/suspicious bank details.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with accounts payable and the bank for reversal if funds already transferred.
steps.outcome: Fraudulent payment halted or reversal initiated.

steps.title: Block malicious sender and flag vendor record
steps.desc: Block the fraudulent sender domain/address and flag the vendor's record in the procurement system pending verification.
steps.guidance: Prevent further invoices from being processed against the vendor record until verified.
steps.outcome: Vendor record flagged; no further payments processed without verification.

steps.title: Require secondary approval for vendor banking-detail changes
steps.desc: Implement or reinforce a policy requiring dual approval and out-of-band verification for any change to vendor payment details.
steps.guidance: This is the primary control gap in most fake-vendor scams.

steps.title: Coordinate with genuine vendor if their systems were compromised
steps.desc: If the real vendor was compromised, coordinate remediation and advise them to notify other customers who may be similarly targeted.
steps.abort: Not applicable for pure spoofing without vendor compromise.

steps.title: Confirm financial recovery status and restore normal processing
steps.desc: Confirm final status of any fraudulent payment (recovered/written off) and resume normal processing with the verified vendor.
steps.guidance: Document with finance and legal for potential insurance or law-enforcement recovery efforts.
steps.outcome: Financial impact quantified and resolved to the extent possible.

steps.title: Review procurement process and update training
steps.desc: Conduct post-incident review with accounts payable/procurement and update training and controls to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Process gaps documented and closed; staff trained on the specific scam pattern.
