ITID-64321.escalation: Escalate to network security and privacy/legal teams given the volume of decrypted traffic potentially exposed.
indicators: Access to TLS inspection logs/decrypted traffic outside documented policy or business need
Anomalous administrative access to the inspection proxy itself
vectors: Insider access to decrypted traffic beyond authorized scope
External compromise of the inspection proxy's administrative interface
rootCauses: Insufficient access controls and logging on TLS inspection infrastructure
Overly broad interception policy scope
controls: Least-privilege access to TLS inspection logs and administration
Audit logging of all access to decrypted traffic
ITID-64321.detection: Good where access to inspection infrastructure is itself logged and monitored.
ITID-64321.response: Restrict access to the inspection proxy pending investigation and audit the scope of traffic actually accessed.
metrics: Count of out-of-policy access events to inspection infrastructure
Volume of traffic assessed as exposed per incident
sops: TLS Inspection Proxy Misuse Response SOP
ITID-64321.notes: Differentiated from ITID-64322 by axis: this leaf is misuse of an organization's own sanctioned interception capability; ITID-64322 is an externally introduced rogue certificate.

playbook.name: Corporate TLS Inspection Proxy Abused for Unauthorized Interception
playbook.description: The organization's own legitimate TLS inspection/proxy infrastructure is abused (by an insider or attacker with access to it) to intercept traffic beyond its authorized scope or policy.

steps.title: Confirm unauthorized use of the legitimate TLS inspection proxy
steps.desc: Validate reports/logs indicating the organization's own TLS inspection proxy is being used to intercept traffic outside its documented policy or authorized scope.
steps.guidance: Distinguish this from an attacker-installed rogue certificate — this is abuse of the org's OWN legitimate inspection capability.
steps.outcome: Confirmed scope-abuse of the legitimate proxy.
steps.abort: If interception is within approved policy, close as false positive.

steps.title: Identify who accessed the proxy's decrypted traffic or configuration
steps.desc: Determine which individual(s) or accounts accessed the proxy's decrypted traffic streams, logs, or configuration beyond authorized policy.
steps.guidance: Review proxy admin access logs and traffic-export/logging configuration changes.

steps.title: Determine scope of intercepted/exposed traffic
steps.desc: Assess what traffic (users, domains, data types) was intercepted or exposed outside policy, including any sensitive categories that should have been excluded (e.g. banking, healthcare).
steps.outcome: Scope of improperly intercepted traffic documented.

steps.title: Restrict access to proxy configuration and decrypted logs
steps.desc: Immediately restrict or revoke the offending party's access to the proxy's administrative interface and decrypted traffic logs/exports.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized access to proxy capabilities halted.

steps.title: Correct proxy policy/bypass-list configuration
steps.desc: Restore the TLS inspection policy to its approved scope, including any bypass lists for excluded categories that were removed or ignored.
steps.outcome: Proxy policy restored to approved, documented scope.

steps.title: Investigate for HR/Legal-relevant misconduct
steps.desc: If the abuse was intentional misuse by an employee/administrator, engage HR and Legal for evidence preservation and disciplinary/legal process.
steps.guidance: Preserve logs and access records per legal hold requirements before any remediation that could alter evidence.
steps.outcome: HR/Legal engaged where misconduct is confirmed; evidence preserved.
steps.abort: Not applicable if abuse was accidental misconfiguration rather than intentional misconduct.

steps.title: Implement access controls and audit logging on inspection infrastructure
steps.desc: Implement dual-control/least-privilege access to the TLS inspection proxy's configuration and decrypted-traffic access, with comprehensive audit logging.

steps.title: Notify affected individuals if required and restore normal operation
steps.desc: Determine notification obligations for individuals whose traffic was improperly intercepted and confirm proxy operates within policy going forward.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with legal/privacy office on notification requirements.
steps.outcome: Notifications handled as required; proxy confirmed compliant.

steps.title: Review TLS inspection governance and update policy
steps.desc: Review governance over the TLS inspection program and update policy, access controls, and audit cadence to prevent recurrence.
steps.outcome: Governance and policy updated; findings documented.

ITID-64322.def: An adversary installs a rogue root or intermediate certificate into an endpoint's trust store (via social engineering, malware, or physical access) to enable transparent interception of that endpoint's TLS traffic, exploiting the trust the operating system places in its certificate store.
ITID-64322.purpose: Captures cases where an adversary installs an unauthorized rogue certificate on an endpoint to enable TLS interception.
scopeIncludes: Malware or a malicious profile installing a rogue trusted root certificate on an endpoint
Social-engineering-driven installation of a fraudulent 'security' or 'VPN' certificate enabling interception
scopeExcludes: Misuse of an organization's own sanctioned TLS inspection proxy (ITID-64321)
Interception enabled by a stolen legitimate TLS private key (ITID-64212)
ITID-64322.severity: High, given full visibility into the endpoint's encrypted traffic once the rogue certificate is trusted.
ITID-64322.priority: P1 upon confirmed unauthorized root/intermediate certificate installation.
ITID-64322.escalation: Escalate to endpoint security to remove the rogue certificate and assess what traffic may have been intercepted.
indicators: Unrecognized root or intermediate certificate present in an endpoint's trust store
Endpoint protection alert on certificate store modification
vectors: Malware that silently installs a rogue trusted certificate
Social engineering the user into installing a fraudulent security/VPN certificate
rootCauses: Insufficient endpoint monitoring of trust-store modifications
Users with local administrative rights able to modify the trust store
mitreTechniques: T1553.004 Subvert Trust Controls: Install Root Certificate
controls: Endpoint monitoring of certificate trust-store modifications
Restriction of local administrative rights
ITID-64322.detection: Good with endpoint detection tooling that monitors trust-store changes; weak without it.
ITID-64322.response: Remove the rogue certificate, reimage if malware-driven, and assess the scope of intercepted traffic.
metrics: Count of rogue certificate installations detected
Time to remediate affected endpoints
ITID-64322.notes: Differentiated from ITID-64321 by axis: this leaf is an externally introduced rogue certificate on an endpoint; ITID-64321 is misuse of the organization's own sanctioned inspection infrastructure.

playbook.name: Rogue Certificate Installed on Endpoint to Enable TLS Interception
playbook.description: An attacker installs a rogue root/CA certificate on a victim endpoint (via malware or physical/social access) to enable TLS interception, abusing the endpoint's certificate-trust store.

steps.title: Confirm rogue certificate installed in endpoint trust store
steps.desc: Validate detection of an unauthorized/rogue root or CA certificate installed in a victim endpoint's trust store enabling TLS interception.
steps.guidance: Distinguish from the org's own legitimate inspection proxy certificate — this is an attacker-installed, unauthorized certificate.
steps.outcome: Rogue certificate confirmed with details of issuer and installation method.
steps.abort: If the certificate is the organization's own authorized inspection root, redirect to the corporate-proxy-abuse playbook.

steps.title: Determine installation vector
steps.desc: Investigate how the rogue certificate was installed (malware, malicious profile/MDM push, physical access, social engineering).

steps.title: Assess scope of intercepted traffic and other affected endpoints
steps.desc: Determine what traffic was likely intercepted and whether other endpoints show the same rogue certificate or installation vector.
steps.outcome: Scope of affected endpoints and intercepted traffic documented.

steps.title: Isolate affected endpoint(s)
steps.desc: Isolate the affected endpoint(s) from the network to prevent further interception and potential malware propagation.

steps.title: Remove rogue certificate from trust store
steps.desc: Remove the rogue certificate from the endpoint's trust store and remediate any associated malware/malicious profile.
steps.outcome: Rogue certificate removed; endpoint trust store restored to known-good state.

steps.title: Reimage or fully remediate compromised endpoints
steps.desc: Reimage affected endpoints or perform full malware remediation to ensure no persistence mechanisms remain.

steps.title: Reset credentials used during the interception window
steps.desc: Reset credentials for any accounts accessed from the affected endpoint during the period the rogue certificate was active.

steps.title: Deploy detection for unauthorized trust-store modifications
steps.desc: Implement or tune endpoint monitoring to detect unauthorized additions to certificate trust stores going forward.

steps.title: Restore endpoint to service and validate clean trust store
steps.desc: Return the remediated endpoint to service and confirm the trust store contains only authorized certificates.

steps.title: Document findings and update endpoint hardening baseline
steps.desc: Document the installation vector and update endpoint hardening/detection baselines to prevent recurrence.

ITID-64323.def: A generalized case of TLS interception undermining trust in encrypted communications, where the specific mechanism does not yet map to a more specific leaf.
ITID-64323.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for man-in-the-middle-via-TLS-interception cases that do not fit the proxy-misuse or rogue-certificate leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reports of suspected TLS interception pending determination of mechanism
Network-level anomalies suggestive of interception without a confirmed rogue certificate or proxy-misuse finding yet
scopeExcludes: Confirmed sanctioned-proxy misuse (ITID-64321)
Confirmed rogue endpoint certificate (ITID-64322)
ITID-64323.severity: High pending classification of the specific interception mechanism.
ITID-64323.priority: P1 at report; reclassify once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-64323.escalation: Escalate to network and endpoint security teams immediately regardless of classification status.
indicators: Certificate warnings or chain anomalies reported by users or monitoring tools without a confirmed cause
vectors: Unclassified TLS interception vector pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail available to attribute root cause
controls: Network traffic anomaly monitoring
Endpoint trust-store monitoring
ITID-64323.detection: Variable; depends on the mechanism once classified.
ITID-64323.response: Classify the interception mechanism promptly and route to the applicable specific leaf.
metrics: Count of general TLS interception reports pending classification
ITID-64323.notes: Catch-all intake leaf for the Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) via TLS Interception group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General MitM via TLS Interception
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident involving man-in-the-middle interception of TLS-protected traffic.

steps.title: Confirm TLS interception and determine source
steps.desc: Validate evidence of TLS interception and determine whether it originates from the organization's own inspection infrastructure (abused) or an attacker-installed rogue certificate.
steps.guidance: This distinction determines the containment path — internal policy correction vs. endpoint remediation.
steps.abort: If interception is fully within approved policy, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine scope of affected traffic and systems
steps.desc: Identify the traffic, users, and systems affected by the interception.

steps.title: Contain the interception source
steps.desc: Depending on classification, either restrict/correct the internal inspection proxy's scope, or isolate and remediate the affected endpoint(s) with the rogue certificate.

steps.title: Reset potentially exposed credentials
steps.desc: Reset credentials for accounts whose traffic may have been intercepted during the exposure window.

steps.title: Remediate the underlying cause
steps.desc: Fully remediate the underlying cause identified — policy misconfiguration/abuse, or malware/rogue certificate installation.

steps.title: Harden certificate trust and inspection controls
steps.desc: Implement hardening appropriate to the root cause (access controls on inspection infrastructure, or endpoint trust-store monitoring).

steps.title: Validate restored secure communications
steps.desc: Confirm affected traffic paths are no longer subject to unauthorized interception.

steps.title: Document findings and update relevant policy
steps.desc: Document root cause and update the relevant TLS inspection or endpoint security policy.

ITID-64331.def: A covert, technical weakening of the entropy or algorithm behind a cryptographic library's random number generator (e.g., a deliberately predictable or backdoored PRNG), undermining the trust users place in the library's stated cryptographic strength.
ITID-64331.purpose: Captures cases where a cryptographic library's random number generator is covertly weakened to make its encryption breakable by those aware of the flaw.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of a deliberately weakened or predictable RNG in a widely trusted cryptographic library
Confirmed exploitation of a known-weak RNG to break encryption believed to be strong
scopeExcludes: An openly mandated key-escrow mechanism (ITID-64332)
Accidental, non-deliberate cryptographic weakness (tracked under vulnerability management rather than trust exploitation)
ITID-64331.severity: Critical, given the silent, wide-reaching nature of a backdoored RNG across all consumers of the library.
ITID-64331.priority: P1 immediately upon credible evidence of a deliberate RNG weakness.
ITID-64331.escalation: Escalate to all downstream consumers of the affected library; treat all keys generated using it as potentially compromised.
indicators: Independent cryptographic research identifying statistically anomalous or predictable output from the RNG
Confirmed successful decryption of traffic believed to be strongly encrypted
vectors: Deliberate insertion of a weakened RNG by a compromised or coerced library maintainer
Supply-chain insertion of a backdoored cryptographic dependency
rootCauses: Insufficient independent audit of cryptographic library internals prior to widespread adoption
Closed-source or unauditable cryptographic implementations
controls: Independent cryptographic audit of libraries prior to adoption
Preference for open, peer-reviewed cryptographic implementations
ITID-64331.detection: Weak; discovery typically relies on independent academic or research disclosure rather than internal telemetry.
ITID-64331.response: Replace the affected library, regenerate all keys/material produced under it, and reassess the confidentiality of data protected by it.
metrics: Time from public disclosure to library replacement
Number of systems remediated
detections: Cryptographic library inventory and version tracking
ITID-64331.notes: Differentiated from ITID-64332 by axis: this leaf is covert/deliberately hidden weakening; ITID-64332 is an openly mandated backdoor.

playbook.name: Weakened Random Number Generator Backdoor in Cryptographic Library
playbook.description: A trusted cryptographic library is found to contain a deliberately weakened random number generator, undermining the security of every key/certificate generated with it.

steps.title: Confirm weakened RNG backdoor in cryptographic library
steps.desc: Validate research/advisory/audit findings that a cryptographic library used within the organization contains a deliberately weakened random number generator.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference with public CVE/vendor advisories or independent cryptographic audit findings.
steps.outcome: Confirmed backdoor and specific library/version identified.

steps.title: Inventory all systems using the affected library
steps.desc: Identify every system, application, and service using the affected cryptographic library, and every key/certificate generated with it.
steps.guidance: Use software composition analysis / dependency inventory tooling.
steps.outcome: Full inventory of affected systems and generated key material.

steps.title: Assess exploitability and evidence of exploitation
steps.desc: Assess whether the weakened RNG has been actively exploited (e.g. predictable keys observed, factored certificates) versus a theoretical risk.

steps.title: Restrict use of affected library for new key generation
steps.desc: Immediately halt use of the affected library for generating any new cryptographic material.
steps.outcome: No further weak key material generated.

steps.title: Migrate to a verified-secure cryptographic library
steps.desc: Replace the affected library across all identified systems with a verified-secure alternative.
steps.guidance: Prioritize systems with the highest-sensitivity key material.
steps.outcome: All affected systems migrated to a secure library.

steps.title: Regenerate and reissue all affected keys/certificates
steps.desc: Regenerate all keys and certificates that were created using the weakened RNG, and revoke/reissue as needed.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with the CA for certificate reissuance where applicable.
steps.outcome: All affected key material regenerated with a secure RNG.

steps.title: Audit cryptographic library selection and approval process
steps.desc: Review how the compromised library was approved for use and strengthen the cryptographic library vetting/approval process.

steps.title: Validate integrity of regenerated key material
steps.desc: Verify all regenerated keys/certificates are functioning correctly and were generated with a secure RNG.
steps.outcome: Regenerated key material validated as secure and functional.

steps.title: Document findings and share advisory internally/externally as warranted
steps.desc: Document the finding, remediation timeline, and share an advisory with affected internal teams or, if warranted, the broader community.

ITID-64332.def: An adversary (or an authorized party acting beyond legitimate scope) exploits an overtly built-in, policy-mandated key-escrow or backdoor mechanism in an encryption product to access data or communications the mechanism was ostensibly restricted to authorize, undermining trust in the product's confidentiality guarantees.
ITID-64332.purpose: Captures cases where an openly mandated key-escrow or backdoor mechanism in an encryption product is exploited or misused.
scopeIncludes: Unauthorized use of a legally mandated key-escrow mechanism to access data beyond its authorized scope
Compromise of the key-escrow holder's own systems exposing escrowed keys
scopeExcludes: A covert, undisclosed RNG weakness (ITID-64331)
ITID-64332.severity: Critical, given that a key-escrow compromise can expose all data protected under the escrowed keys.
ITID-64332.priority: P1 upon confirmed unauthorized use or compromise of the escrow mechanism.
ITID-64332.escalation: Escalate to legal/compliance and the escrow authority; assess the scope of data or communications exposed.
indicators: Evidence of escrowed-key access outside its authorized legal or policy scope
Breach disclosure at a key-escrow holder
vectors: Insider misuse of legitimate escrow access
External compromise of the escrow holder's key storage systems
rootCauses: Concentration of decryption capability in a single escrow point, creating a high-value target
Insufficient oversight of escrow-access authorization
controls: Strict, auditable authorization controls on escrow access
Independent oversight of escrow-holder security posture
ITID-64332.detection: Weak; dependent almost entirely on escrow-holder audit trails and disclosure.
ITID-64332.response: Assess and disclose the scope of data exposed via unauthorized escrow access; pursue key rotation where feasible.
metrics: Number of unauthorized escrow-access events identified
Time to detect escrow holder compromise
ITID-64332.notes: Differentiated from ITID-64331 by axis: this leaf is an overt, policy-mandated mechanism being misused or compromised; ITID-64331 is a covert, undisclosed weakness.

playbook.name: Key Escrow Backdoor Mandated in Encryption Product
playbook.description: An encryption product used by the organization is found to contain a mandated key-escrow backdoor allowing a third party (vendor, government, or attacker who compromises the escrow) to decrypt protected data.

steps.title: Confirm key-escrow backdoor in encryption product
steps.desc: Validate findings (research disclosure, vendor admission, regulatory disclosure) that an encryption product in use contains a mandated key-escrow mechanism.
steps.outcome: Backdoor confirmed and specific product/version identified.

steps.title: Inventory data and systems protected by the affected product
steps.desc: Identify all data, systems, and communications protected using the affected encryption product.

steps.title: Assess whether the escrow key/mechanism has been compromised or misused
steps.desc: Determine whether there is evidence the escrow mechanism has actually been accessed/misused (beyond theoretical exposure), including by the vendor, government body, or an attacker.

steps.title: Restrict use of the affected product for new sensitive data
steps.desc: Halt use of the affected encryption product for protecting new sensitive data pending remediation.
steps.outcome: No new sensitive data exposed to the backdoor.

steps.title: Migrate to encryption without mandated key escrow
steps.desc: Replace the affected product with an encryption solution verified to have no key-escrow backdoor.
steps.guidance: Prioritize the most sensitive data categories.
steps.outcome: Migration to a verified-secure encryption solution completed.

steps.title: Re-encrypt previously exposed data where feasible
steps.desc: Re-encrypt data previously protected under the backdoored product using the new solution, prioritizing highest-sensitivity data.
steps.outcome: Previously exposed data re-encrypted where feasible.

steps.title: Engage legal/compliance on disclosure and vendor obligations
steps.desc: Engage legal and compliance to assess breach-notification obligations and any contractual/vendor accountability issues.
steps.outcome: Legal/compliance review completed with any required actions identified.

steps.title: Validate new encryption solution integrity
steps.desc: Confirm the replacement encryption solution is properly protecting data with no similar backdoor.

steps.title: Update cryptographic product vetting standards
steps.desc: Update the organization's standards for vetting encryption products to screen for undisclosed key-escrow or backdoor mechanisms going forward.

ITID-64333.def: A generalized case of a cryptographic backdoor undermining trust in a product's encryption, where the specific mechanism does not yet map to a more specific leaf.
ITID-64333.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for cryptographic backdoor cases that do not fit the RNG-weakening or key-escrow leaves.
scopeIncludes: Suspected but not yet characterized cryptographic backdoor
Reports pending determination of whether the mechanism is covert (RNG-style) or overt (escrow-style)
scopeExcludes: Confirmed covert RNG weakening (ITID-64331)
Confirmed overt key-escrow mechanism misuse (ITID-64332)
ITID-64333.severity: Critical pending classification of the specific mechanism.
ITID-64333.priority: P1 at report; reclassify once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-64333.escalation: Escalate to cryptography/security architecture team immediately regardless of classification status.
indicators: Any unexplained cryptographic weakness not yet attributed to a specific mechanism
vectors: Unclassified cryptographic backdoor vector pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail available to attribute root cause
controls: Cryptographic architecture review process
Independent audit of cryptographic products prior to adoption
ITID-64333.detection: Variable; depends on the mechanism once classified.
ITID-64333.response: Classify the mechanism promptly and route to the applicable specific leaf.
metrics: Count of general cryptographic backdoor reports pending classification
ITID-64333.notes: Catch-all intake leaf for the Cryptographic Backdoors in Trusted Software group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Cryptographic Backdoor in Trusted Software
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident involving a deliberately introduced cryptographic backdoor discovered in trusted software.

steps.title: Confirm cryptographic backdoor and classify mechanism
steps.desc: Validate the finding of a cryptographic backdoor in trusted software and classify the mechanism (weak RNG, key escrow, hardcoded key, algorithm flaw).

steps.title: Inventory affected systems and protected data
steps.desc: Identify all systems using the affected software and the data/communications it protects.

steps.title: Restrict use of affected software for new sensitive operations
steps.desc: Halt use of the affected software for new sensitive cryptographic operations pending remediation.
steps.outcome: No further exposure from new use.

steps.title: Migrate to verified-secure alternative
steps.desc: Replace the affected software/library with a verified-secure alternative across all identified systems.

steps.title: Regenerate/re-protect affected cryptographic material and data
steps.desc: Regenerate keys/certificates or re-encrypt data that was protected using the backdoored software.

steps.title: Strengthen cryptographic software vetting process
steps.desc: Update the vetting/approval process for cryptographic software to catch similar issues in the future.

steps.title: Validate replacement solution integrity
steps.desc: Confirm the replacement cryptographic solution is functioning correctly and securely.

steps.title: Document findings and disseminate advisory
steps.desc: Document the finding and remediation, and share an advisory internally or externally as warranted.

ITID-64341.def: An adversary exploits a technical bypass in an operating system's or application's code-signing verification logic (rather than obtaining a valid or stolen certificate) to make malicious code appear as validly signed, exploiting the trust the verification mechanism is supposed to guarantee.
ITID-64341.purpose: Captures cases where a technical flaw in a code-signing verification implementation is exploited to make unsigned or improperly signed code appear validly signed.
scopeIncludes: Exploitation of a signature-verification logic flaw allowing unsigned or tampered code to pass as signed
Exploitation of a hash-collision or parsing-ambiguity flaw in a signing format
scopeExcludes: Use of a genuinely stolen valid certificate to sign malware (ITID-64211)
Use of a lookalike publisher name rather than a technical verification bypass (ITID-64342)
ITID-64341.severity: Critical, given that a verification bypass can defeat signature-based trust checks across an entire platform.
ITID-64341.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmed exploitation of a verification bypass.
ITID-64341.escalation: Escalate to the platform/OS vendor for emergency patching; treat all code passing verification as suspect until patched.
indicators: Malware confirmed to pass signature verification despite lacking a valid, properly issued signature
Vendor advisory describing a signature-verification bypass matching observed behavior
vectors: Exploitation of a parsing ambiguity between the signed and executed portions of a binary
Exploitation of a cryptographic weakness in the signature-verification algorithm
rootCauses: Complexity of signature-verification implementations creating room for logic flaws
Delayed patching of platform-level verification components
mitreTechniques: T1553.002 Subvert Trust Controls: Code Signing
controls: Rapid patch management for platform signature-verification components
Defense-in-depth beyond signature checks alone (e.g., behavioral detection)
ITID-64341.detection: Weak until the bypass is publicly disclosed; behavioral/EDR detection can provide a secondary layer independent of signature trust.
ITID-64341.response: Apply the vendor patch immediately and treat previously 'verified' code from the exposure window as unverified pending re-scan.
metrics: Time to patch a disclosed verification bypass
Number of previously trusted binaries re-scanned post-patch
sops: Code Signing Verification Bypass Response SOP
detections: Behavioral/EDR detection independent of signature trust
ITID-64341.notes: Differentiated from ITID-64342 by axis: this leaf is a technical verification-logic bypass; ITID-64342 is social/visual spoofing via a lookalike publisher name.

playbook.name: Code Signing Verification Bypass Exploit
playbook.description: An attacker exploits a flaw in code-signing verification logic (OS, application, or update mechanism) to run unsigned or improperly signed code as if it were trusted.

steps.title: Confirm code-signing verification bypass exploitation
steps.desc: Validate evidence that malicious code executed despite lacking a valid signature, due to a flaw in the verification logic.
steps.guidance: Review EDR alerts for unsigned/improperly-signed executables that were permitted to run.
steps.outcome: Bypass confirmed with technical details of the flaw.

steps.title: Identify the specific verification flaw and affected systems
steps.desc: Determine the exact flaw in the signature-verification logic (e.g. OS component, application, or update mechanism) and which systems run the vulnerable component.
steps.outcome: Vulnerable component and affected system inventory documented.

steps.title: Assess scope of malicious code execution
steps.desc: Determine what malicious code executed via the bypass and on which systems, and what actions it took.

steps.title: Isolate affected systems
steps.desc: Isolate systems where the bypass was exploited to prevent further spread or damage.

steps.title: Apply interim mitigation for the verification flaw
steps.desc: Apply available compensating controls (e.g. application allowlisting, disabling the vulnerable verification path) pending a vendor patch.
steps.outcome: Attack surface reduced pending permanent fix.

steps.title: Remove malicious code and apply vendor patch
steps.desc: Remove the malicious payload from affected systems and apply the vendor's patch for the verification flaw once available.

steps.title: Audit for persistence established via the bypass
steps.desc: Review affected systems for persistence mechanisms established using the improperly trusted code.
steps.outcome: No residual persistence confirmed, or persistence removed.

steps.title: Restore systems to service and validate signature enforcement
steps.desc: Restore affected systems to service and confirm signature verification now correctly enforces trust.
steps.outcome: Systems restored with validated, correct signature enforcement.

steps.title: Document findings and update code-execution trust controls
steps.desc: Document the flaw and remediation, and review broader code-execution trust controls (allowlisting, verification hardening) for similar gaps.
steps.outcome: Findings documented; trust controls reviewed and updated.

ITID-64342.def: An adversary registers or presents a publisher/signer name that is visually or semantically similar to a legitimate, trusted vendor (e.g., a homoglyph or near-identical company name) to induce users or systems to trust signed code that is not actually from the vendor it appears to represent.
ITID-64342.purpose: Captures cases where an adversary uses a fake or lookalike publisher name to make code appear to come from a trusted signer.
scopeIncludes: Malware signed under a certificate issued to a lookalike company name closely resembling a trusted vendor
Use of homoglyph characters in a registered publisher name to imitate a known-trusted signer
scopeExcludes: A technical bypass of signature verification logic itself (ITID-64341)
Use of a genuinely stolen certificate belonging to the real vendor (ITID-64211)
ITID-64342.severity: Medium-High, since the malicious code is genuinely signed (just under a deceptive identity) and may pass basic 'is it signed' checks.
ITID-64342.priority: P2, escalating to P1 if the lookalike-signed code is observed in active distribution.
ITID-64342.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence to identify scope of distribution and to the impersonated vendor for awareness.
indicators: Publisher name in a signature nearly but not exactly matching a known trusted vendor
User or endpoint tooling reports flagging an unfamiliar but 'valid' signer
vectors: Legitimate CA issuance of a certificate to a deceptively named shell entity
Registration of a company name designed to be mistaken for a trusted vendor at a glance
rootCauses: CA issuance processes that verify legal entity existence but not brand-confusion risk
Users and automated tooling that trust 'any valid signature' without verifying publisher identity precisely
mitreTechniques: T1553.002 Subvert Trust Controls: Code Signing
T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
controls: Publisher allowlisting with exact-match verification rather than 'any valid signature'
Brand-monitoring for lookalike company registrations
ITID-64342.detection: Moderate; requires precise publisher-name allowlisting rather than generic signature validation to catch.
ITID-64342.response: Block the lookalike publisher, alert affected endpoints, and notify the impersonated vendor.
metrics: Count of lookalike-publisher detections
Time to add a confirmed lookalike publisher to blocklist
ITID-64342.notes: Differentiated from ITID-64341 by axis: this leaf is social/visual spoofing of identity, not a technical verification-logic bypass.

playbook.name: Fake/Lookalike Publisher Name Used to Spoof Trusted Signer
playbook.description: An attacker obtains a legitimately-issued code-signing certificate under a fake or lookalike publisher name to make malware appear as if it comes from a trusted software vendor.

steps.title: Confirm lookalike publisher name used to sign malicious software
steps.desc: Validate that malware was signed with a certificate issued to a publisher name deceptively similar to a legitimate, trusted vendor.
steps.guidance: Compare the certificate's subject/publisher field character-by-character against known legitimate vendor names.
steps.outcome: Lookalike publisher confirmed and the impersonated legitimate vendor identified.

steps.title: Identify the issuing CA and validation process used
steps.desc: Determine which CA issued the certificate under the lookalike name and what validation level (e.g. OV/EV) was used.
steps.outcome: Issuing CA and validation gap identified.

steps.title: Assess scope of malware distribution using the spoofed signature
steps.desc: Determine how widely the falsely-signed malware has been distributed and which systems may have executed it based on trusting the signature.

steps.title: Report certificate for revocation to the issuing CA
steps.desc: Report the fraudulently-obtained certificate to the issuing CA and request immediate revocation.
steps.outcome: Certificate revoked by the issuing CA.

steps.title: Block the malicious publisher/certificate thumbprint org-wide
steps.desc: Add the certificate thumbprint and publisher name to blocklists across EDR/application-control tooling.
steps.outcome: Malicious signed binaries blocked from executing.

steps.title: Remove malware from affected systems
steps.desc: Remove the falsely-signed malware from any systems where it executed and remediate any resulting compromise.

steps.title: Notify the legitimately impersonated vendor
steps.desc: Notify the legitimate vendor whose brand/name was impersonated so they can warn customers and pursue action against the CA/attacker if warranted.

steps.title: Strengthen publisher-name verification for internal trust decisions
steps.desc: Update internal application-control/allowlisting policy to require verification beyond publisher name alone (e.g. certificate thumbprint pinning) for trusted vendors.

steps.title: Confirm systems clean and monitor for further lookalike certificates
steps.desc: Confirm affected systems are clean and monitor CT logs for further lookalike-publisher certificate issuance.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean; monitoring in place.

steps.title: Document findings and update detection rules
steps.desc: Document the lookalike-name pattern used and update detection rules to catch similar spoofing attempts.

ITID-64343.def: A generalized case of code-signing mechanism spoofing undermining trust in signed code, where the specific technique does not yet map to a more specific leaf.
ITID-64343.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for code-signing spoofing cases that do not fit the verification-bypass or lookalike-publisher leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reports of suspicious signed code pending determination of the spoofing technique used
Novel code-signing spoofing techniques not yet enumerated as their own leaf
scopeExcludes: Confirmed technical verification bypass (ITID-64341)
Confirmed lookalike-publisher spoofing (ITID-64342)
ITID-64343.severity: Medium-High pending classification of the specific technique.
ITID-64343.priority: P2 at report; reclassify once the technique is confirmed.
ITID-64343.escalation: Escalate to threat intelligence and platform security for classification support.
indicators: Signed code exhibiting suspicious characteristics not yet attributable to a specific technique
vectors: Unclassified code-signing spoofing vector pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail available to attribute root cause
mitreTechniques: T1553.002 Subvert Trust Controls: Code Signing
T1036.005 Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
controls: Publisher allowlisting
Behavioral detection independent of signature trust
ITID-64343.detection: Variable; depends on the technique once classified.
ITID-64343.response: Classify the spoofing technique promptly and route to the applicable specific leaf.
metrics: Count of general code-signing spoofing reports pending classification
ITID-64343.notes: Catch-all intake leaf for the Spoofing Code Signing Mechanisms group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Code Signing Mechanism Spoofing
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident involving spoofing of a code-signing mechanism to lend false trust to malicious software.

steps.title: Confirm code signing spoofing and classify method
steps.desc: Validate the report of code-signing spoofing and classify the method (verification bypass, lookalike publisher, or other).

steps.title: Assess scope of affected systems and distribution
steps.desc: Determine what systems executed the falsely-trusted code and how it was distributed.

steps.title: Block the malicious code/certificate
steps.desc: Block the malicious binary, certificate thumbprint, or publisher across EDR/application-control tooling, and request certificate revocation where applicable.
steps.outcome: Malicious code blocked from further execution.

steps.title: Isolate affected systems
steps.desc: Isolate any systems where the spoofed code executed.

steps.title: Remove malicious code from affected systems
steps.desc: Remove the malicious payload and remediate any resulting compromise.

steps.title: Strengthen code-signing verification/trust process
steps.desc: Update the relevant verification or trust-decision process to close the gap that allowed the spoofing.

steps.title: Confirm systems clean and restore normal operation
steps.desc: Confirm affected systems are clean and operating normally.

steps.title: Document findings and update detection rules
steps.desc: Document findings and update detection rules to catch similar spoofing attempts.

ITID-64411.def: An adversary, or a compromised legitimate actor, exploits the trust extended to a formal business partner (joint venture, reseller, distributor, franchise) to gain access, information, or advantage beyond the scope of the legitimate partnership.
ITID-64411.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for cases where a trusted business partner relationship is abused to gain unauthorized access or benefit.
scopeIncludes: A compromised business partner's systems used to pivot into the organization's environment
A partner exceeding the data-sharing or access scope defined in the partnership agreement
scopeExcludes: Abuse of standing technical access granted to an MSP/vendor (ITID-64221)
A software dependency relationship (ITID-64431)
ITID-64411.severity: High, given the breadth of access and information typically shared with formal business partners.
ITID-64411.priority: P1 upon confirmed abuse of a business-partner trust relationship.
ITID-64411.escalation: Escalate to the business relationship owner and legal/contracts team in parallel with technical containment.
indicators: Data or access usage inconsistent with the partnership agreement's defined scope
Anomalous activity on a partner-facing access path
vectors: Compromise of a partner organization used as a pivot point
Contractual scope creep exploited by a partner acting in bad faith
rootCauses: Partnership agreements lacking clearly defined and enforced access/data scope
Insufficient monitoring of partner-facing access paths
controls: Contractually defined and technically enforced partner access scope
Continuous monitoring of partner-facing access paths
ITID-64411.detection: Moderate; dependent on whether partner access paths are instrumented separately from general third-party access.
ITID-64411.response: Restrict the partner's access to contractually defined scope immediately upon suspicion; investigate before restoring broader access.
metrics: Count of business-partner trust abuse incidents
Percentage of partner access paths under continuous monitoring
sops: Business Partner Trust Abuse Response SOP
ITID-64411.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. Distinct from ITID-64221 (technical MSP/vendor access misuse) by focusing on the formal business-relationship dimension of trust.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Abuse of Trusted Business Partner
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident in which an attacker abuses the trust relationship with a business partner to gain access, extract data, or commit fraud.

steps.title: Intake report of suspected business-partner trust abuse
steps.desc: Collect details of the suspected abuse of the business-partner relationship, including the communication or access channel exploited.

steps.title: Verify legitimacy of the request/activity with the partner
steps.desc: Contact the business partner through a verified, independent channel to confirm or deny the legitimacy of the request or activity in question.
steps.guidance: Do not use contact details provided in the suspicious communication.
steps.outcome: Legitimacy confirmed or denied by the partner.
steps.abort: If the partner confirms legitimacy, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine whether the partner's systems were compromised
steps.desc: Assess whether the partner's own systems/accounts were compromised (enabling the abuse) versus pure impersonation.

steps.title: Restrict the partner's access pending verification
steps.desc: Temporarily restrict or suspend the business partner's system access or data-sharing channel pending verification and remediation.
steps.guidance: Balance against business continuity needs; coordinate with the relationship owner.

steps.title: Halt any pending transactions or data transfers
steps.desc: Halt any pending financial transactions, data transfers, or actions initiated through the abused relationship.
steps.outcome: Pending actions halted or reversed where possible.

steps.title: Coordinate remediation with the partner organization
steps.desc: If the partner's systems were compromised, coordinate joint remediation; otherwise, work with the partner to close the impersonation vector.

steps.title: Review and harden the business-partner access model
steps.desc: Review the scope and controls of the partner's access/integration and apply least-privilege and verification hardening.

steps.title: Restore verified partner access and confirm normal operations
steps.desc: Restore the partner's access under corrected controls and confirm normal business operations resume.

steps.title: Review vendor/partner risk-management process
steps.desc: Conduct post-incident review with vendor-management stakeholders and update partner risk-assessment and verification processes.

ITID-64421.def: An adversary defrauds the organization or a supply chain partner by exploiting the trust inherent in an established supply chain relationship (e.g., falsified shipment confirmations, fraudulent purchase order diversion, counterfeit goods passed off as genuine via a trusted channel).
ITID-64421.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for supply chain fraud that operates by exploiting the trust between supply chain participants rather than a technical vulnerability.
scopeIncludes: Fraudulent purchase order or shipment-confirmation scheme exploiting an established supplier relationship
Counterfeit goods introduced into the supply chain via a trusted distribution channel
scopeExcludes: Fake vendor scams with no genuine prior relationship (ITID-64131)
Wire fraud tracked specifically under the Financial Fraud domain's BEC/wire-transfer leaves (ITID-53211, ITID-53212)
ITID-64421.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High on confirmed financial loss or goods substitution affecting safety/quality.
ITID-64421.priority: P2 at report; P1 upon confirmed financial loss or safety-relevant counterfeit substitution.
ITID-64421.escalation: Escalate to procurement, finance, and quality assurance depending on the fraud's nature.
indicators: Shipment or purchase-order discrepancies inconsistent with the established supplier relationship
Quality or provenance anomalies in received goods from a trusted supplier channel
vectors: Exploitation of established purchase-order approval trust to divert goods or payment
Introduction of counterfeit goods via a trusted but insufficiently verified distribution tier
rootCauses: Insufficient independent verification of supply chain transactions at each tier
Overreliance on established relationship history in lieu of ongoing verification
controls: Independent verification checkpoints across supply chain tiers
Provenance tracking for physical goods
ITID-64421.detection: Primarily a process-control detection surface (procurement/QA checks) rather than a technical telemetry one.
ITID-64421.response: Verify the transaction or shipment independently and halt further processing pending confirmation.
metrics: Count of supply chain fraud attempts detected
Value of loss prevented or incurred
ITID-64421.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. Cross-referenced against ITID-53211/53212 (wire transfer fraud) and ITID-64131 (fake vendor scams); scoped here strictly to fraud that exploits an existing, genuine supply chain relationship.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Supply Chain Fraud via Trust Exploitation
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident in which an attacker commits fraud within the supply chain by exploiting an established trust relationship between the organization and a supplier or partner.

steps.title: Intake report of suspected supply chain fraud
steps.desc: Collect details of the suspected fraudulent activity within the supply chain (e.g. fraudulent invoices, altered purchase orders, diverted shipments) and the trust relationship exploited.
steps.outcome: Incident logged with initial fraud indicators.

steps.title: Verify legitimacy with the actual supply chain partner
steps.desc: Contact the legitimate supplier/partner via a verified channel to confirm whether the transaction/communication in question is genuine.
steps.abort: If confirmed legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Quantify financial or operational impact
steps.desc: Determine the financial loss, goods diverted, or operational disruption resulting from the fraud.

steps.title: Halt affected transactions and shipments
steps.desc: Halt any pending payments, orders, or shipments connected to the fraudulent activity.

steps.title: Flag affected supplier record pending investigation
steps.desc: Flag the supplier record in procurement/ERP systems to prevent further processing until verified.

steps.title: Engage legal and law enforcement as appropriate
steps.desc: Engage legal counsel and, if warranted, law enforcement to pursue recovery and accountability for the fraud.
steps.abort: Not applicable for minor incidents resolved administratively.

steps.title: Strengthen supply chain verification controls
steps.desc: Implement or reinforce dual-approval and out-of-band verification controls for supply chain transactions (payment changes, order modifications).

steps.title: Confirm financial recovery status and resume normal operations
steps.desc: Confirm the status of any financial recovery efforts and resume normal supply chain operations with the verified partner.
steps.outcome: Financial impact resolved to the extent possible; operations resumed.

steps.title: Review procurement/supply chain fraud controls
steps.desc: Conduct post-incident review with procurement and finance to identify and close control gaps.

ITID-64431.def: An adversary exploits the trust an organization places in a software dependency's maintainer identity, publishing account, or distribution channel (e.g., a compromised or socially engineered maintainer account pushing a malicious update) rather than exploiting a code-level vulnerability in the dependency itself.
ITID-64431.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for cases where the trust placed in a software dependency's maintainers or distribution channel is exploited, as distinct from a purely technical vulnerability in the dependency's code.
scopeIncludes: A maintainer account for a widely used package compromised or socially engineered into publishing a malicious update
A dependency's ownership transferred to an adversary who then publishes malicious updates under the trusted package name
scopeExcludes: A code-level vulnerability in a dependency with no trust-relationship compromise involved (tracked under vulnerability/exploitation domains elsewhere in the taxonomy)
Misuse of a vendor's granted operational access to the organization's environment (ITID-64221)
ITID-64431.severity: Critical, given the wide, often silent distribution of dependency updates to all downstream consumers.
ITID-64431.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmed compromise of a maintainer identity or publishing channel for a dependency in use.
ITID-64431.escalation: Escalate to engineering leadership and pin/roll back the affected dependency version across all consuming systems.
indicators: Unexpected or unsigned-off update to a dependency, especially one introducing new network or execution behavior
Package registry or maintainer-account anomaly disclosed by the ecosystem's security team
vectors: Social engineering or credential theft against a package maintainer
Acquisition of an abandoned but still-trusted package by an adversary
rootCauses: Lack of maintainer account security requirements (e.g., MFA) enforced by package registries
Insufficient internal review of dependency updates before adoption
controls: Dependency update review and staged rollout before production adoption
Software bill of materials (SBOM) and pinned-version management
Monitoring of ecosystem security advisories for dependencies in use
ITID-64431.detection: Moderate; dependent on SBOM visibility and ecosystem-level advisory monitoring rather than internal telemetry alone.
ITID-64431.response: Pin back to a known-good version immediately, audit for any malicious behavior introduced during the exposure window, and monitor ecosystem advisories going forward.
metrics: Time to roll back a compromised dependency once disclosed
Percentage of dependencies covered by SBOM and pinned-version management
ITID-64431.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. Scoped specifically to the trust-relationship-abuse angle of dependency compromise (maintainer identity/publishing trust), not general dependency vulnerability exploitation, which is tracked elsewhere.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Exploiting Trust in Software Dependency
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident in which an attacker exploits the implicit trust placed in a software dependency (open-source package, library, or component) to introduce malicious functionality.

steps.title: Confirm malicious dependency and identify affected package
steps.desc: Validate reports/advisories indicating a software dependency used by the organization contains malicious code or has been compromised (e.g. typosquat package, compromised maintainer account, malicious version bump).
steps.guidance: Cross-reference with public dependency-security advisories (e.g. GitHub Security Advisories, OSV).
steps.outcome: Malicious dependency confirmed and specific package/version identified.

steps.title: Inventory all systems/applications using the dependency
steps.desc: Identify every application, build, or system that includes the affected dependency, directly or transitively.

steps.title: Assess scope of exploitation
steps.desc: Determine whether the malicious dependency's functionality has actually executed in the environment and what actions it performed.

steps.title: Pin/block the malicious dependency version
steps.desc: Block installation/update to the malicious version across build systems and package registries used internally.
steps.outcome: Malicious version blocked from further deployment.

steps.title: Isolate affected systems/builds
steps.desc: Isolate any running systems or build pipelines confirmed to have executed the malicious dependency code.

steps.title: Roll back to a known-good dependency version
steps.desc: Roll back all affected applications/builds to a verified clean version of the dependency, or migrate to a safe alternative.
steps.outcome: All affected systems running clean dependency version.

steps.title: Remove any malicious payload deployed via the dependency
steps.desc: Remove any malware, backdoors, or unauthorized changes introduced through the compromised dependency's execution.
steps.outcome: Systems confirmed clean of the payload.

steps.title: Implement dependency integrity verification
steps.desc: Implement or strengthen dependency pinning, checksum/signature verification, and a vetting process for new dependencies and version updates.
steps.outcome: Dependency integrity controls implemented and documented.

steps.title: Validate builds and deploy clean releases
steps.desc: Rebuild and redeploy affected applications with the clean dependency, and validate normal functionality.

steps.title: Document findings and update dependency governance
steps.desc: Document the incident and update software dependency governance/vetting standards to reduce recurrence risk.

ITID-64441.def: An adversary crafts and delivers a forged webhook payload to a system that trusts webhook callbacks from a given source, inducing the receiving system to take an unauthorized action (e.g., marking a payment as confirmed, releasing goods, granting access) based on the forged event.
ITID-64441.purpose: Captures cases where a forged webhook payload is injected to trigger an unauthorized action, such as a fake payment confirmation.
scopeIncludes: Forged 'payment confirmed' webhook triggering unauthorized order fulfillment or access grant
Injection of a fabricated event payload exploiting insufficient webhook signature validation
scopeExcludes: Interception of a genuine webhook callback via a spoofed endpoint (ITID-64442)
Exploitation of a compromised legitimate third-party account to send a genuine but fraudulent request (ITID-64221)
ITID-64441.severity: High, given the direct, often automated business-logic consequence of a trusted webhook event.
ITID-64441.priority: P1 upon confirmed forged webhook triggering an unauthorized action.
ITID-64441.escalation: Escalate to the application/finance owner of the affected workflow to reverse any unauthorized action taken.
indicators: Webhook payload received without a valid or verifiable signature
Business-logic action taken (fulfillment, access grant) with no corresponding legitimate upstream event
vectors: Exploitation of missing or weak webhook signature verification
Replay or fabrication of a webhook payload structure learned through reconnaissance
rootCauses: Webhook endpoints that trust payload content without cryptographic signature verification
Absence of idempotency or reconciliation checks against the purported upstream source of truth
mitreTechniques: T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
controls: Mandatory cryptographic signature verification on all inbound webhooks
Reconciliation of webhook-triggered actions against the actual upstream source of truth
ITID-64441.detection: Good where webhook signature verification and reconciliation logging are in place; weak without them.
ITID-64441.response: Reverse the unauthorized action, enforce signature verification if missing, and audit for other forged events in the same window.
metrics: Count of forged webhook events detected/blocked
Percentage of webhook endpoints enforcing signature verification
ITID-64441.notes: Webhook forgery has no single dedicated ATT&CK Enterprise technique; T1071.001 is used as the closest fit for the delivery channel, applied with honest acknowledgment of the mapping's imprecision. Differentiated from ITID-64442 by direction: this leaf is payload injection/fabrication, not endpoint interception.

playbook.name: Fake Webhook Payload Injected to Trigger Unauthorized Action (Fake Payment Confirmation)
playbook.description: An attacker injects a forged webhook payload (e.g. a fake payment-confirmation callback) into a system that trusts inbound webhooks without adequate verification, triggering an unauthorized action such as releasing goods or services.

steps.title: Confirm forged webhook payload triggered unauthorized action
steps.desc: Validate that an unauthorized action (e.g. order fulfillment, access grant) was triggered by a webhook payload that did not originate from the legitimate expected source.
steps.guidance: Check the webhook receiver's logs for the payload's source IP, signature (if any), and correlate against the legitimate payment/service provider's actual records.
steps.outcome: Forged webhook confirmed and the triggered unauthorized action identified.
steps.abort: If the payload is confirmed legitimate upon provider check, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine why signature/authenticity verification failed or was absent
steps.desc: Determine whether the webhook endpoint lacked signature verification (e.g. HMAC) entirely, or whether verification was present but bypassed/misconfigured.
steps.guidance: This is the core technical root cause in most webhook-spoofing incidents.
steps.outcome: Root cause of verification failure identified.

steps.title: Assess scope of unauthorized actions triggered
steps.desc: Search logs for other instances of forged webhook payloads and quantify the total unauthorized actions taken (goods released, access granted, etc.).
steps.outcome: Full scope of unauthorized actions documented.

steps.title: Disable or restrict the vulnerable webhook endpoint
steps.desc: Immediately disable the affected webhook endpoint or restrict it (e.g. IP allowlist to the legitimate provider) pending a fix.

steps.title: Reverse or hold the unauthorized action where possible
steps.desc: Reverse or place a hold on the unauthorized action triggered by the forged webhook (e.g. halt shipment, revoke granted access) if not yet fully completed.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized action reversed or held where feasible.

steps.title: Implement webhook signature (HMAC) verification
steps.desc: Implement mandatory HMAC (or equivalent) signature verification on the webhook endpoint, validating against a shared secret with the legitimate provider.
steps.guidance: This is the core eradication step for this ITID category — treat it as mandatory, not optional hardening.
steps.outcome: Webhook endpoint enforces cryptographic signature verification on all inbound payloads.

steps.title: Add replay-protection and idempotency checks
steps.desc: Implement timestamp/nonce-based replay protection and idempotency keys to prevent reuse of captured legitimate payloads.

steps.title: Validate webhook security and resume normal processing
steps.desc: Test the hardened webhook endpoint to confirm it correctly rejects unsigned/forged payloads and accepts legitimate ones, then resume normal processing.
steps.outcome: Webhook endpoint validated as secure; normal processing resumed.

steps.title: Audit other webhook integrations for the same gap
steps.desc: Review all other inbound webhook integrations across the organization for the same missing-verification gap and remediate proactively.
steps.outcome: All webhook integrations audited; gaps closed.

ITID-64442.def: An adversary registers or configures a spoofed webhook endpoint (e.g., via a subdomain takeover, DNS manipulation, or configuration tampering) to receive callbacks intended for a legitimate trusted endpoint, intercepting the data or triggering downstream effects that depend on the callback reaching only the legitimate party.
ITID-64442.purpose: Captures cases where a webhook endpoint is spoofed to intercept a legitimate, trusted callback intended for the real endpoint.
scopeIncludes: Subdomain takeover used to intercept webhook callbacks intended for a decommissioned but still-referenced endpoint
Configuration tampering redirecting a webhook subscription to an attacker-controlled endpoint
scopeExcludes: Fabrication/injection of a forged payload to a legitimate endpoint (ITID-64441)
ITID-64442.severity: High, given the potential for sensitive callback data (payment confirmations, personal data) to be exposed or diverted.
ITID-64442.priority: P1 upon confirmed interception of a legitimate webhook callback.
ITID-64442.escalation: Escalate to the integration/platform owner to revoke the spoofed endpoint registration and rotate any exposed credentials or tokens.
indicators: Webhook subscription pointing to an unrecognized or recently changed endpoint
Decommissioned subdomain still referenced in an active webhook configuration
vectors: Subdomain takeover of a decommissioned but still-referenced callback URL
Unauthorized modification of webhook subscription configuration
rootCauses: Inadequate lifecycle management of decommissioned subdomains/endpoints still referenced in integrations
Insufficient access control on webhook subscription configuration
mitreTechniques: T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
controls: Regular audit and cleanup of decommissioned subdomains and DNS records
Access control and change monitoring on webhook subscription configuration
ITID-64442.detection: Moderate; subdomain takeover detection tooling and configuration change monitoring provide meaningful signal.
ITID-64442.response: Revoke the spoofed endpoint, restore the legitimate callback configuration, and assess what data was exposed during the interception window.
metrics: Count of spoofed webhook endpoints identified
Time to remediate a subdomain-takeover-enabled interception
ITID-64442.notes: As with ITID-64441, webhook-specific interception has no single dedicated ATT&CK ID; T1071.001 combined with T1584.006 is used as the closest fit, noted honestly as an approximation.

playbook.name: Webhook Endpoint Spoofed to Intercept Legitimate Trusted Callback
playbook.description: An attacker stands up a spoofed webhook endpoint or redirects a legitimate callback URL to intercept trusted data (e.g. payment confirmations, OAuth tokens) intended for the organization's real receiver.

steps.title: Confirm legitimate callback was intercepted via spoofed endpoint
steps.desc: Validate that a trusted callback (payment confirmation, OAuth token delivery, status update) was diverted to or intercepted by an attacker-controlled endpoint instead of the legitimate receiver.
steps.guidance: Check webhook/callback URL configuration in the third-party platform for unauthorized changes, and DNS/routing for the legitimate endpoint.
steps.outcome: Interception confirmed and diversion mechanism identified.

steps.title: Determine how the callback URL was changed or redirected
steps.desc: Investigate whether the callback/webhook URL configuration was changed via compromised admin access, DNS manipulation, or a vulnerability in the URL-registration process.
steps.outcome: Root cause of the redirection identified.

steps.title: Assess what data was intercepted
steps.desc: Determine the type and sensitivity of data intercepted (payment data, tokens, PII) and the potential downstream impact.

steps.title: Restore the correct callback/webhook URL configuration
steps.desc: Immediately correct the webhook/callback URL configuration in the third-party platform to point back to the legitimate endpoint.
steps.outcome: Callback traffic restored to the legitimate endpoint.

steps.title: Revoke any tokens/credentials intercepted
steps.desc: Revoke any OAuth tokens, API keys, or credentials that may have been intercepted via the spoofed endpoint.

steps.title: Secure the callback-URL configuration and registration process
steps.desc: Lock down who/what can change the registered callback/webhook URL, requiring authenticated, logged, and approved changes.

steps.title: Implement webhook signature verification and endpoint pinning
steps.desc: Implement HMAC signature verification on inbound callbacks and, where supported, certificate/endpoint pinning to detect future redirection attempts.

steps.title: Validate restored callback flow and monitor for anomalies
steps.desc: Confirm callbacks are flowing correctly to the legitimate endpoint and monitor for further configuration tampering.
steps.outcome: Callback flow validated as restored and secure.

steps.title: Audit other third-party integrations for similar exposure
steps.desc: Review all third-party integrations with configurable callback URLs for the same exposure and remediate proactively.

ITID-64443.def: A generalized case of API or webhook manipulation undermining trust in an automated integration, where the specific mechanism does not yet map to a more specific leaf.
ITID-64443.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for API and webhook manipulation cases that do not fit the payload-injection or endpoint-spoofing leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reports of suspicious API/webhook activity pending determination of mechanism
Novel API manipulation techniques not yet enumerated as their own leaf
scopeExcludes: Confirmed forged webhook payload injection (ITID-64441)
Confirmed webhook endpoint spoofing (ITID-64442)
ITID-64443.severity: High pending classification of the specific mechanism.
ITID-64443.priority: P1 at report; reclassify once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-64443.escalation: Escalate to the integration/platform owner immediately regardless of classification status.
indicators: Any API or webhook anomaly not yet attributable to a specific mechanism
vectors: Unclassified API/webhook manipulation vector pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail available to attribute root cause
mitreTechniques: T1071.001 Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
controls: API/webhook integration security review process
ITID-64443.detection: Variable; depends on the mechanism once classified.
ITID-64443.response: Classify the mechanism promptly and route to the applicable specific leaf.
metrics: Count of general API/webhook manipulation reports pending classification
sops: API and Webhook Manipulation Triage SOP
ITID-64443.notes: Catch-all intake leaf for the API and Webhook Manipulation group; webhook-specific attacks lack a single dedicated ATT&CK ID across this whole group, as noted on its siblings.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General API and Webhook Manipulation
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident involving manipulation of an API or webhook mechanism that a system trusts without adequate verification.

steps.title: Confirm API/webhook manipulation and classify mechanism
steps.desc: Validate the report of API or webhook manipulation and classify the mechanism (forged payload, spoofed endpoint, or other manipulation).

steps.title: Assess scope of unauthorized actions or data exposure
steps.desc: Determine what unauthorized actions were triggered or what data was exposed as a result of the manipulation.

steps.title: Disable or restrict the affected API/webhook endpoint
steps.desc: Immediately disable or restrict the vulnerable endpoint pending remediation.

steps.title: Reverse or hold unauthorized actions where possible
steps.desc: Reverse or place a hold on any unauthorized action triggered via the manipulated API/webhook if not yet fully completed.
steps.outcome: Unauthorized action reversed or held where feasible.

steps.title: Implement signature verification (HMAC) and authentication hardening
steps.desc: Implement or strengthen cryptographic signature verification and authentication on the affected API/webhook mechanism.

steps.title: Add replay-protection and input validation
steps.desc: Implement replay protection and thorough input validation on the affected endpoint.

steps.title: Validate hardened endpoint and resume normal processing
steps.desc: Test the hardened endpoint and resume normal processing once validated secure.
steps.outcome: Endpoint validated secure; normal processing resumed.

steps.title: Audit similar integrations for the same gap
steps.desc: Review other API/webhook integrations for similar verification gaps and remediate proactively.

ITID-64511.def: A currently employed individual holding a position of significant organizational trust (executive, administrator, or otherwise privileged role) deliberately abuses that position for personal gain, sabotage, or on behalf of a third party, exploiting the trust inherent in their role.
ITID-64511.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for cases where a currently employed individual in a position of organizational trust deliberately acts against the organization's interest.
scopeIncludes: A trusted employee deliberately exfiltrating sensitive data for personal or third-party benefit
A trusted employee sabotaging systems or processes from within
scopeExcludes: A former employee retaining access after departure (ITID-64541)
Privilege abuse limited to technical over-permissioning without deliberate malicious intent (ITID-64521)
ITID-64511.severity: High, given the elevated access and trust typically associated with the roles this leaf covers.
ITID-64511.priority: P1 upon confirmed deliberate malicious action by a currently employed trusted individual.
ITID-64511.escalation: Escalate to HR, legal, and executive leadership in parallel with technical containment, given employment and legal implications.
indicators: Data access or exfiltration inconsistent with the employee's job function
Behavioral indicators of grievance, financial distress, or external solicitation
vectors: Direct misuse of legitimately held privileged access
Collusion with an external party while retaining a trusted internal role
rootCauses: Insufficient behavioral monitoring for high-trust roles
Lack of separation of duties even for senior/trusted positions
controls: User and entity behavior analytics on privileged roles
Mandatory separation of duties regardless of seniority
ITID-64511.detection: Moderate; UEBA and DLP tooling can surface anomalies, but intent is ultimately confirmed through investigation, not telemetry alone.
ITID-64511.response: Suspend access immediately upon credible suspicion, coordinate with HR/legal, and conduct a full forensic review of the individual's activity.
metrics: Count of confirmed rogue-employee incidents
Time from first anomaly to access suspension
detections: UEBA anomaly detection on privileged roles
ITID-64511.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. Distinct from ITID-64521 (privilege abuse without necessarily malicious intent) and ITID-64541 (access retained post-departure).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Rogue Employee in Trusted Position
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident involving an employee in a position of significant trust (e.g. IT admin, finance, executive assistant) intentionally abusing that position for malicious purposes.

steps.title: Intake and validate report of rogue employee activity
steps.desc: Collect the initial report or detection of suspected malicious insider activity by an employee in a trusted position.
steps.guidance: Handle with strict confidentiality; involve HR and Legal from the outset given the employment and evidentiary implications.

steps.title: Engage HR and Legal for coordinated investigation
steps.desc: Formally engage HR and Legal to establish an investigation plan consistent with employment law and evidentiary requirements.
steps.guidance: Follow established insider-threat investigation conventions; ensure any monitoring is legally authorized.

steps.title: Preserve evidence of the trusted position's activity
steps.desc: Preserve logs, system access records, communications, and any other evidence of the employee's activity under legal hold, without alerting the employee prematurely.
steps.guidance: Coordinate timing of evidence preservation with HR/Legal to avoid tipping off the subject before containment is ready.

steps.title: Scope the extent of trust abuse
steps.desc: Determine the full scope of systems, data, and transactions the employee accessed or manipulated using their trusted position.

steps.title: Suspend access coordinated with HR/Legal action
steps.desc: Suspend the employee's system access at the moment HR/Legal executes any employment action, to prevent destruction of evidence or retaliatory action.
steps.guidance: Timing must be tightly coordinated between IT, HR, Legal, and physical security.
steps.outcome: Access suspended without alerting the subject prematurely.

steps.title: Secure physical and digital assets
steps.desc: Secure any physical assets (badge, devices, keys) and digital assets (accounts, data) associated with the employee.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with physical security for badge deactivation.

steps.title: Remediate any unauthorized changes or backdoors
steps.desc: Identify and remediate any unauthorized changes, backdoors, or persistence mechanisms the employee established using their trusted access.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed free of unauthorized changes.

steps.title: Review and tighten controls for the trusted position
steps.desc: Review the access model and controls (segregation of duties, monitoring) for the trusted position to prevent recurrence.

steps.title: Restore normal operations and reassign trusted duties
steps.desc: Restore normal business operations and reassign the trusted duties/access to appropriately vetted personnel.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review with HR, Legal, and security leadership
steps.desc: Conduct a joint post-incident review to capture findings and update insider-threat detection and trusted-position governance.

ITID-64521.def: An insider uses privileged access legitimately granted for their role to take actions beyond their intended authorization, exploiting the organizational trust that access was granted to be used only within its intended scope.
ITID-64521.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for cases where an insider's legitimately granted privileged access is misused, viewed through the trust-exploitation lens rather than as a pure access-control failure.
scopeIncludes: An administrator using standing privileged access to view or modify data outside their job function's need
A privileged user disabling logging or monitoring to cover unauthorized activity
scopeExcludes: Deliberate, malicious action by a trusted individual with clear intent to harm the organization (ITID-64511)
Governance-level segregation-of-duties bypass without a technical access-abuse component (ITID-64531)
ITID-64521.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High where sensitive data or critical systems are affected.
ITID-64521.priority: P2 at report; P1 upon confirmed access to sensitive data or critical systems outside authorized scope.
ITID-64521.escalation: Escalate to the access owner and security team to review and restrict the scope of privileged access.
indicators: Privileged access used for actions unrelated to job function
Logging or monitoring disabled or evaded by a privileged user without change-control approval
vectors: Standing, overly broad privileged access with no just-in-time restriction
Lack of activity review for privileged accounts
rootCauses: Privileged access not scoped to least privilege or reviewed periodically
Insufficient logging and review of privileged-account activity
controls: Just-in-time privileged access management
Periodic access review and recertification
Privileged activity logging and review
ITID-64521.detection: Good where privileged access management (PAM) tooling and activity logging are deployed; weak without them.
ITID-64521.response: Restrict privileged access to least-privilege scope and review activity logs for the extent of out-of-scope use.
metrics: Count of privileged access misuse incidents
Percentage of privileged accounts under PAM/just-in-time control
detections: PAM activity logging and anomaly alerting
ITID-64521.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. Distinct from ITID-64511 by intent/severity (access-scope misuse vs. deliberate malicious action) and from ITID-64531 (purely procedural, non-technical governance bypass).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Insider Abuse of Privileged Access (Trust Exploitation Context)
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident involving an insider abusing their privileged system access, exploiting the trust granted through that access for unauthorized purposes.

steps.title: Intake and validate report of privileged access abuse
steps.desc: Collect the initial report/detection of suspected abuse of privileged access by an insider.
steps.guidance: Engage HR and Legal early given the employment and evidentiary implications.

steps.title: Review privileged access logs and activity
steps.desc: Pull privileged-access session logs (PAM, admin activity, database access) to establish a timeline of the suspected abuse.
steps.abort: If activity is within authorized scope, close as false positive.

steps.title: Preserve evidence under legal hold
steps.desc: Preserve relevant logs and records under legal hold, coordinated with HR/Legal, without alerting the subject prematurely.

steps.title: Restrict or suspend privileged access
