steps.desc: Restrict or suspend the individual's privileged access, timed with HR/Legal action to prevent evidence tampering.

steps.title: Review and revoke any unauthorized access grants made by the individual
steps.desc: If the individual used their privileges to grant themselves or others additional unauthorized access, identify and revoke those grants.

steps.title: Remediate unauthorized changes made using privileged access
steps.desc: Identify and remediate any unauthorized changes, data exfiltration, or persistence mechanisms established via the abused privileged access.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed free of unauthorized changes.

steps.title: Strengthen privileged-access monitoring and segregation of duties
steps.desc: Implement enhanced monitoring, session recording, and segregation-of-duties controls for privileged access going forward.

steps.title: Restore normal operations with corrected access controls
steps.desc: Restore normal operations, reassigning privileged duties as needed under the strengthened controls.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review with HR, Legal, and security leadership
steps.desc: Conduct a joint post-incident review and update privileged-access governance based on findings.

ITID-64531.def: Two or more individuals who each legitimately hold a portion of an approval workflow's required authorization collude to jointly approve a transaction or action that segregation-of-duties controls were specifically designed to prevent any single individual from approving alone, exploiting the organizational trust placed in the segregation control's integrity.
ITID-64531.purpose: Captures cases where two or more individuals with approval authority collude to bypass a segregation-of-duties control.
scopeIncludes: Two approvers colluding to jointly authorize a fraudulent payment that neither could approve alone
Collusive rubber-stamping of a control that requires independent, good-faith review at each stage
scopeExcludes: A single individual abusing delegated authority beyond its intended scope without collusion (ITID-64532)
A workflow-level technical bypass of an approval gate (ITID-64533)
ITID-64531.severity: High, given that collusion defeats a control specifically designed to require independent bad actors, indicating deliberate coordinated fraud.
ITID-64531.priority: P1 upon confirmed collusive bypass of a segregation-of-duties control.
ITID-64531.escalation: Escalate to internal audit, legal, and HR immediately; treat as a coordinated fraud investigation rather than an isolated policy violation.
indicators: Approval patterns showing suspiciously consistent pairing of the same individuals on high-risk transactions
Audit findings of substantively identical review notes suggesting non-independent review
vectors: Pre-arranged collusion between approvers with complementary authorization scope
Exploitation of predictable or static approver-pairing patterns
rootCauses: Static, predictable segregation-of-duties pairings not rotated or independently audited
Insufficient audit sampling of high-risk, dual-approved transactions
controls: Rotation of segregation-of-duties pairings
Independent audit sampling of dual-approved high-risk transactions
Behavioral analytics on approver pairing patterns
ITID-64531.detection: Weak from a technical telemetry standpoint; this is fundamentally an audit and behavioral-analytics detection surface.
ITID-64531.response: Suspend the involved approvers' authority pending investigation and conduct a full audit of transactions they jointly approved.
metrics: Count of confirmed collusive segregation-of-duties bypasses
Percentage of high-risk dual-approvals independently audited
ITID-64531.notes: authorization/governance control bypass — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal controls and audit. Differentiated from ITID-64532 (single-actor delegated-authority abuse, no collusion) and ITID-64533 (technical workflow bypass).

playbook.name: Segregation-of-Duties Bypass via Colluding Trusted Approvers
playbook.description: Two or more employees with trusted approval authority collude to bypass segregation-of-duties controls, jointly authorizing a transaction or action neither could approve alone.

steps.title: Intake and validate report of collusive SoD bypass
steps.desc: Collect the initial report/detection (e.g. audit finding, anomaly detection) of suspected collusion between trusted approvers to bypass segregation-of-duties controls.
steps.guidance: Engage HR, Legal, and Internal Audit given the multi-party and evidentiary nature.

steps.title: Map the approval chain and identify colluding parties
steps.desc: Reconstruct the approval workflow for the transaction(s) in question and identify all individuals involved in the approval chain.
steps.guidance: Review audit trails for approval timestamps, patterns, and any out-of-band communication evidence.
steps.outcome: Colluding parties and approval pattern identified.

steps.title: Preserve evidence under legal hold
steps.desc: Preserve approval records, communications, and transaction data under legal hold, coordinated with HR/Legal.

steps.title: Quantify scope and financial/operational impact
steps.desc: Determine the full scope of transactions bypassed via the collusion and the resulting financial or operational impact.

steps.title: Suspend approval authority for involved individuals
steps.desc: Suspend or restrict the approval authority/privileges of all individuals confirmed to be involved in the collusion, timed with HR/Legal action.

steps.title: Halt or reverse affected transactions
steps.desc: Halt any pending transactions and reverse completed ones where feasible and legally appropriate.

steps.title: Redesign segregation-of-duties controls to prevent collusion
steps.desc: Redesign the approval workflow to reduce collusion risk (e.g. rotating approvers, independent verification, system-enforced conflict checks).

steps.title: Implement analytics to detect approval-pattern anomalies
steps.desc: Deploy or tune analytics to detect unusual approval patterns (e.g. same pairs repeatedly approving each other's transactions) going forward.

steps.title: Restore normal approval operations under new controls
steps.desc: Restore normal transaction-approval operations with reassigned approvers and the redesigned controls in place.

steps.title: Conduct joint post-incident review with Internal Audit, HR, and Legal
steps.desc: Conduct a joint review to capture findings and update governance, training, and control-testing processes.

ITID-64532.def: An individual who has been delegated approval authority (e.g., to act on behalf of a manager while they are unavailable) uses that delegated authority to approve actions outside the scope, value threshold, or time window for which the delegation was intended, exploiting the trust placed in the delegation arrangement.
ITID-64532.purpose: Captures cases where an individual holding delegated approval authority uses it beyond the scope for which it was granted.
scopeIncludes: A delegate approving transactions above the value threshold intended for their delegated authority
A delegate continuing to exercise delegated authority after the delegation period has formally ended
scopeExcludes: Collusive bypass involving multiple colluding approvers (ITID-64531)
A technical workflow flaw enabling bypass rather than a human exceeding delegated scope (ITID-64533)
ITID-64532.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High where the delegated authority was used to approve a high-value or high-risk action.
ITID-64532.priority: P2 at report; P1 upon confirmed high-value or high-risk action approved outside delegation scope.
ITID-64532.escalation: Escalate to the delegating manager and internal audit to assess the scope and value of out-of-bounds approvals.
indicators: Delegated-authority approvals exceeding the documented value threshold
Delegated authority exercised outside its documented time window
vectors: Ambiguous or undocumented delegation scope allowing self-interpretation of authority limits
Lack of automated enforcement of delegation thresholds in the approval system
rootCauses: Delegation of authority not technically enforced with hard thresholds/time bounds in the workflow system
Insufficient post-hoc review of delegated approvals
controls: System-enforced delegation thresholds and time bounds
Periodic review of delegated-authority usage against documented scope
ITID-64532.detection: Weak from a technical telemetry standpoint absent system-enforced thresholds; primarily a workflow-audit detection surface.
ITID-64532.response: Revoke or correct the delegation scope and review all approvals made outside the intended bounds.
metrics: Count of confirmed out-of-scope delegated approvals
Percentage of delegation arrangements with system-enforced thresholds
ITID-64532.notes: authorization/governance control bypass — no ATT&CK Enterprise technique applies; tracked via internal controls and audit. Differentiated from ITID-64531 (collusion between multiple approvers) and ITID-64533 (workflow-level technical bypass).

playbook.name: Delegated Approval Authority Abused Beyond Intended Scope
playbook.description: An employee granted temporary or delegated approval authority (e.g. covering for an absent manager) uses that trust-based authority beyond its intended scope or duration.

steps.title: Intake and validate report of delegated-authority abuse
steps.desc: Collect the initial report/detection of suspected abuse of delegated approval authority beyond its intended scope, purpose, or duration.
steps.guidance: Engage HR and Legal given the employment implications.

steps.title: Determine the original scope/duration of the delegation
steps.desc: Review the delegation record (who granted it, for what purpose, and for how long) and compare against actual usage.
steps.abort: If usage was within the granted scope/duration, close as false positive.

steps.title: Assess actions taken under the excess delegated authority
steps.desc: Identify all approvals or actions taken using the delegated authority outside its intended scope.
steps.outcome: Full scope of out-of-bounds actions documented.

steps.title: Revoke the delegated authority
steps.desc: Immediately revoke the delegated approval authority.
steps.outcome: Delegated authority revoked; further abuse prevented.

steps.title: Review and hold affected approvals pending validation
steps.desc: Place any approvals made outside the intended scope on hold pending review and re-validation by properly authorized personnel.

steps.title: Re-validate or reverse out-of-scope approvals
steps.desc: Have properly authorized personnel re-validate or reverse the actions taken outside the delegation's intended scope.

steps.title: Implement time-bound and scope-bound delegation controls
steps.desc: Implement system-enforced expiration and scope limits on delegated authority so it cannot be exercised beyond its intended bounds.

steps.title: Restore normal approval workflow
steps.desc: Restore approval authority to the properly designated individual and confirm normal workflow operation.

steps.title: Review delegation policy and update training
steps.desc: Review the incident with HR and process owners, and update delegation policy and training on its proper use.
steps.outcome: Policy and training updated; findings documented.

ITID-64533.def: An individual with genuine, authorized access exploits a workflow's auto-approval mechanism (e.g., a threshold designed to auto-approve low-risk, low-value transactions) by deliberately structuring transactions to fall within the auto-approval criteria, bypassing the human review the workflow was designed to trigger above that threshold.
ITID-64533.purpose: Captures cases where a trusted auto-approval workflow mechanism is deliberately exploited to bypass required human review.
scopeIncludes: Deliberately splitting a transaction into smaller amounts to stay under an auto-approval threshold ('smurfing' an approval workflow)
Exploiting a system configuration flaw that causes items to be mis-categorized as auto-approval-eligible
scopeExcludes: Pure procedural collusion between human approvers with no auto-approval system component (ITID-64531)
A delegate simply exceeding a manually-granted authority scope (ITID-64532)
ITID-64533.severity: High, given this leaf has a genuine technical/system access-abuse component beyond pure procedural collusion.
ITID-64533.priority: P1 upon confirmed deliberate exploitation of an auto-approval mechanism.
ITID-64533.escalation: Escalate to the workflow system owner to correct the auto-approval logic and to internal audit to assess transactions processed under it.
indicators: Pattern of transactions clustered just below an auto-approval threshold
Anomalous volume of auto-approved transactions from a single requester
vectors: Deliberate transaction-splitting to exploit a known auto-approval threshold
Exploitation of a system misconfiguration in auto-approval criteria
rootCauses: Static, publicly known auto-approval thresholds not monitored for pattern-splitting abuse
Insufficient system-level anomaly detection on auto-approved transaction patterns
controls: Anomaly detection on transaction-splitting patterns near auto-approval thresholds
Periodic randomized human review of auto-approved transactions
ITID-64533.detection: Moderate; transaction-pattern analytics can surface threshold-gaming behavior where implemented.
ITID-64533.response: Correct the auto-approval logic/thresholds and audit all transactions processed under the exploited pattern.
metrics: Count of confirmed auto-approval exploitation incidents
Percentage of auto-approved transactions covered by anomaly detection
ITID-64533.notes: Unlike its siblings ITID-64531/64532, this leaf has a genuine technical access-abuse component (exploiting a system's auto-approval logic) and is therefore mapped to T1078 rather than left as a pure governance gap.

playbook.name: Trusted Auto-Approval Workflow Exploited to Bypass Review
playbook.description: An employee or attacker exploits a workflow's automatic-approval rule (e.g. auto-approve below a dollar threshold, trusted-requester fast path) to push transactions through without the intended human review.

steps.title: Confirm auto-approval rule was exploited to bypass review
steps.desc: Validate that transactions were structured or manipulated specifically to qualify for an automatic-approval rule and avoid human review.
steps.guidance: Look for patterns like transaction-splitting just under an auto-approval threshold, or repeated use of a fast-path exemption.
steps.outcome: Exploitation of the auto-approval rule confirmed.

steps.title: Identify who structured the transactions and why
steps.desc: Determine which individual(s) structured transactions to exploit the auto-approval path and assess intent (fraud vs. process shortcut).
steps.guidance: Engage HR/Legal if intentional fraud is suspected.

steps.title: Quantify scope and impact of bypassed transactions
steps.desc: Identify all transactions that bypassed review via this method and quantify financial/operational impact.

steps.title: Disable or tighten the auto-approval rule
steps.desc: Immediately disable the exploited auto-approval rule or tighten its threshold/conditions pending review.

steps.title: Hold or reverse affected transactions
steps.desc: Place a hold on pending transactions that used the exploited path, and reverse completed ones where feasible.

steps.title: Redesign the auto-approval workflow with anti-structuring controls
steps.desc: Redesign the workflow to detect and prevent transaction-structuring (e.g. aggregate spend limits across a time window, requester-based anomaly detection).

steps.title: Address individual accountability per HR/Legal findings
steps.desc: If intentional misuse is confirmed, coordinate with HR/Legal on appropriate accountability measures.
steps.abort: Not applicable if the bypass was an unintentional process gap rather than misconduct.

steps.title: Restore normal workflow operation with monitoring
steps.desc: Restore the transaction-approval workflow under the redesigned controls and confirm monitoring is active.

steps.title: Review other auto-approval rules for similar exposure
steps.desc: Review all other auto-approval/fast-path rules across the organization for similar structuring exposure.

ITID-64534.def: A generalized case of a trust-based authorization mechanism being bypassed or misused, where the specific mechanism does not yet map to a more specific leaf.
ITID-64534.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for misuse of trust-based authorization mechanisms that does not fit the collusion, delegated-authority, or auto-approval leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reports of authorization-control bypass pending determination of the specific mechanism
Novel authorization-bypass patterns not yet enumerated as their own leaf
scopeExcludes: Confirmed collusive segregation-of-duties bypass (ITID-64531)
Confirmed delegated-authority scope abuse (ITID-64532)
Confirmed auto-approval workflow exploitation (ITID-64533)
ITID-64534.severity: Medium-High pending classification of the specific mechanism.
ITID-64534.priority: P2 at report; reclassify once the mechanism is confirmed.
ITID-64534.escalation: Escalate to internal audit and the relevant workflow system owner.
indicators: Any authorization-control anomaly not yet attributable to a specific mechanism
vectors: Unclassified authorization-bypass vector pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail available to attribute root cause
controls: Authorization workflow review process
Internal audit sampling of high-risk approvals
ITID-64534.detection: Variable; depends on the mechanism once classified.
ITID-64534.response: Classify the mechanism promptly and route to the applicable specific leaf.
metrics: Count of general authorization-mechanism misuse reports pending classification
ITID-64534.notes: Catch-all intake leaf for the Misuse of Trust-Based Authorization Mechanisms group. As with its siblings, apply mapped_mitre = [] unless a genuine technical access-abuse component is confirmed upon classification, per the governance-vs-technical distinction established for this group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Misuse of Trust-Based Authorization Mechanism
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident involving misuse of a trust-based authorization mechanism (delegation, auto-approval, or collusive approval) to bypass intended controls.

steps.title: Confirm misuse of trust-based authorization mechanism
steps.desc: Validate the report and classify the specific authorization mechanism misused (delegation, auto-approval rule, collusive approval, or other).

steps.title: Determine scope and impact
steps.desc: Identify all transactions/actions affected and quantify impact.
steps.guidance: Engage HR/Legal if intentional employee misconduct is suspected.

steps.title: Restrict or disable the exploited authorization mechanism
steps.desc: Restrict or disable the specific authorization mechanism being misused pending review.

steps.title: Hold or reverse affected actions
steps.desc: Place holds on pending actions and reverse completed ones where feasible.

steps.title: Redesign the authorization mechanism with stronger controls
steps.desc: Redesign the mechanism to close the specific gap exploited (scope limits, anomaly detection, dual control).

steps.title: Address accountability per findings
steps.desc: Coordinate with HR/Legal on accountability if intentional misuse is confirmed.
steps.abort: Not applicable for unintentional process gaps.

steps.title: Restore normal operation under hardened controls
steps.desc: Restore normal operation with the redesigned controls and confirm monitoring is active.

steps.title: Review similar authorization mechanisms organization-wide
steps.desc: Review other trust-based authorization mechanisms for similar exposure and remediate proactively.

ITID-64541.def: An individual whose employment, contract, or partnership with the organization has formally ended retains functional access to organizational systems, accounts, or data (due to incomplete offboarding) and uses that access, exploiting the residual trust embedded in credentials or accounts that should have been revoked.
ITID-64541.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for cases where a former employee, contractor, or partner retains and uses access after their relationship with the organization has ended.
scopeIncludes: A terminated employee's account not disabled in a timely manner and subsequently used to access systems
A former contractor retaining VPN or application access past their engagement end date
scopeExcludes: A currently employed individual abusing active, legitimate access (ITID-64511, ITID-64521)
ITID-64541.severity: Medium-High, escalating to High where the access is used to exfiltrate data or sabotage systems.
ITID-64541.priority: P1 upon confirmed use of access by a former employee/contractor/partner post-departure.
ITID-64541.escalation: Escalate to IT/identity management to immediately disable all residual access and to HR/legal given the offboarding failure.
indicators: Authentication activity from an account associated with a departed individual
Active accounts found during audit with no corresponding current employment/contract record
vectors: Incomplete or delayed offboarding failing to revoke all access
Shared or default accounts not tied to individual identity lifecycle management
rootCauses: Offboarding process not integrated with identity lifecycle management across all systems
Lack of periodic access recertification to catch orphaned accounts
controls: Automated, identity-lifecycle-integrated offboarding across all systems
Periodic access recertification and orphaned-account audits
ITID-64541.detection: Good where identity lifecycle management is centralized and monitored; weak in fragmented environments with manual offboarding.
ITID-64541.response: Disable all residual access immediately and audit activity conducted after the individual's formal departure date.
metrics: Time from departure to full access revocation
Count of orphaned accounts identified per audit cycle
ITID-64541.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. T1078.001 (Default Accounts) is used where the retained access is a shared/generic account; general T1078 applies where it is the individual's own named account left active.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Former Employee Retaining Access
playbook.description: A departed employee retains active access to organizational systems or data due to an offboarding process failure, rather than intentional malicious action.

steps.title: Confirm former employee retains active access
steps.desc: Validate that a specific former employee's accounts, credentials, or physical access remain active following their departure.
steps.guidance: Cross-reference HR termination records against active-directory/IAM account status and badge systems.
steps.outcome: Retained access confirmed with specific systems/accounts identified.

steps.title: Check for any activity on the account since departure
steps.desc: Review login/access logs for the former employee's accounts since their departure date to determine if the retained access was actually used.
steps.guidance: This determines whether this remains a low-severity process-failure issue or escalates to a suspected malicious-use investigation.

steps.title: Immediately revoke all retained access
steps.desc: Disable all accounts, revoke credentials, VPN access, and physical access (badges, keys) for the former employee across every system found.
steps.guidance: Treat as urgent regardless of whether misuse is found — the exposure window is the primary risk.

steps.title: Escalate to investigation if evidence of malicious use found
steps.desc: If post-departure activity indicates malicious use, escalate to a full insider-threat investigation with HR/Legal involvement.
steps.outcome: Escalated appropriately if malicious use found.
steps.abort: Not applicable if no post-departure activity is found — proceed with process remediation only, in a less adversarial tone.

steps.title: Audit for other former employees with retained access
steps.desc: Conduct a broader audit comparing all recent departures against active account status to catch other instances of the same offboarding gap.
steps.outcome: Full scope of the offboarding gap identified and remediated.

steps.title: Fix the offboarding process gap
steps.desc: Identify why the offboarding process failed to revoke access (e.g. missing automation, manual step skipped, system not included in checklist) and remediate the process.
steps.guidance: Frame as a process-failure remediation, not an adversarial investigation, absent evidence of malicious use.

steps.title: Implement automated deprovisioning controls
steps.desc: Implement or improve automated deprovisioning triggered directly by HR termination records to prevent recurrence.

steps.title: Confirm no residual access or data exposure remains
steps.desc: Confirm no residual access or data exposure remains for the former employee across all systems.

steps.title: Review offboarding process with HR and IT
steps.desc: Conduct a joint review with HR and IT of the offboarding checklist and update it to prevent similar gaps.

ITID-64611.def: Hardware (network equipment, industrial control system components, sensors) deployed within critical infrastructure and trusted as legitimate is found to contain a covert backdoor introduced by a supplier, manufacturer, or an adversary who compromised the manufacturing/distribution supply chain, exploiting the trust placed in the hardware's provenance.
ITID-64611.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for cases where hardware trusted and deployed within critical infrastructure is found to contain a covert backdoor introduced during manufacturing or the supply chain.
scopeIncludes: Discovery of a covert backdoor in trusted network or ICS hardware traced to the manufacturing or distribution supply chain
Hardware implants introduced during shipping/distribution to critical infrastructure operators
scopeExcludes: Spoofed sensor/telemetry data from otherwise-legitimate hardware (ITID-64632)
A trust-based network breach not involving hardware-level implantation (ITID-64621)
ITID-64611.severity: Critical, given the direct physical/operational safety implications within critical infrastructure.
ITID-64611.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmed discovery of backdoored hardware in critical infrastructure.
ITID-64611.escalation: Escalate to critical infrastructure operations, national CI/CERT authorities where applicable, and the equipment supplier.
indicators: Unexplained network communication from hardware with no legitimate reason to originate it
Physical inspection or teardown revealing unauthorized components
Supply chain security assessment flagging an untrusted manufacturing link
vectors: Compromise of a hardware manufacturer's production line
Interdiction of hardware during shipping to implant a backdoor
rootCauses: Insufficient hardware supply chain provenance verification
Lack of independent hardware/firmware inspection prior to deployment in critical environments
mitreTechniques: T1195.003 Supply Chain Compromise: Compromise Hardware Supply Chain
controls: Hardware provenance verification and chain-of-custody tracking
Independent hardware/firmware inspection prior to deployment
ITID-64611.detection: Weak via standard network monitoring alone; strong when paired with dedicated hardware/firmware inspection and anomalous-communication baselining.
ITID-64611.response: Isolate and remove the affected hardware, notify the supplier and relevant authorities, and reassess supply chain provenance controls.
metrics: Count of hardware supply chain compromises identified
Percentage of critical infrastructure hardware under provenance verification
ITID-64611.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. Differentiated from ITID-64632 (data manipulation from otherwise-legitimate sensors) by focusing on the hardware's own compromised provenance.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Backdoored Trusted Hardware (Critical Infrastructure Context)
playbook.description: Hardware trusted and deployed within critical infrastructure is found to contain a manufacturer- or supply-chain-introduced backdoor, undermining the physical trust boundary of the environment.

steps.title: Confirm backdoored hardware and classify the mechanism
steps.desc: Validate findings (independent research, vendor disclosure, forensic analysis) that deployed hardware contains a backdoor, and classify the mechanism (firmware implant, hardware trojan, undocumented remote-access feature).
steps.guidance: Engage full incident response given the critical-infrastructure context and potential severity.

steps.title: Inventory all deployed units of the affected hardware
steps.desc: Identify every unit of the affected hardware deployed across the environment, including criticality and network exposure of each.
steps.outcome: Full deployment inventory compiled and prioritized by criticality.

steps.title: Assess evidence of exploitation via the backdoor
steps.desc: Determine whether the backdoor has been actively exploited, and if so, what access or actions occurred.

steps.title: Isolate or air-gap affected hardware
steps.desc: Isolate the affected hardware from the network, or air-gap it if it cannot be safely removed from operation immediately, prioritizing the most critical/exposed units first.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with operations to avoid unsafe shutdown of critical infrastructure components.

steps.title: Engage full incident response and relevant authorities
steps.desc: Engage the full incident response process, including executive leadership, and notify relevant regulatory/sector authorities (e.g. CISA, sector-ISAC) given the critical-infrastructure context.
steps.outcome: Full IR engaged; relevant authorities notified.

steps.title: Replace or remediate backdoored hardware
steps.desc: Replace the affected hardware with verified-trusted units, or apply a vendor-provided remediation (firmware update removing the backdoor) if replacement is not immediately feasible and the fix is verified effective.
steps.outcome: Backdoor removed or hardware replaced across the environment.

steps.title: Review supply chain vetting for hardware procurement
steps.desc: Review and strengthen supply-chain vetting and hardware-integrity verification processes for future procurement.

steps.title: Validate replacement hardware and restore operations
steps.desc: Validate replacement/remediated hardware is functioning correctly and free of the backdoor, then restore normal operations.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review with sector/regulatory stakeholders
steps.desc: Conduct a comprehensive post-incident review, including relevant sector/regulatory stakeholders given the critical-infrastructure impact.
steps.outcome: Findings documented and shared with relevant stakeholders.

ITID-64621.def: An adversary breaches a critical infrastructure network by exploiting a trust relationship it maintains with another network or organization (e.g., an IT/OT boundary trust, a vendor remote-access trust, an interconnection with a less-secure partner utility), rather than exploiting a vulnerability directly in the critical infrastructure environment.
ITID-64621.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for cases where a critical infrastructure network is breached by exploiting a trust relationship rather than a direct technical vulnerability in the target itself.
scopeIncludes: Pivot from a trusted corporate IT network into an operational technology (OT) environment via an insufficiently segmented trust boundary
Breach via a vendor's remote access trusted by a critical infrastructure operator
scopeExcludes: Compromise via backdoored hardware provenance (ITID-64611)
Manipulation of trusted data sources consumed by critical infrastructure systems (ITID-64631 through ITID-64634)
ITID-64621.severity: Critical, given the potential operational and safety impact of a critical infrastructure breach.
ITID-64621.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmed breach via a trust relationship into critical infrastructure.
ITID-64621.escalation: Escalate to OT security, critical infrastructure operations leadership, and relevant regulatory/national authorities.
indicators: Unauthorized traffic crossing an IT/OT trust boundary
Anomalous activity on a vendor remote-access path into OT environments
vectors: Insufficient IT/OT network segmentation exploited to pivot across the trust boundary
Compromise of a vendor's remote-access trust into the OT environment
rootCauses: Inadequate segmentation between IT and OT trust zones
Overly broad or unmonitored vendor remote access into OT environments
controls: Strict IT/OT network segmentation
Monitored, least-privilege vendor remote access into OT environments
ITID-64621.detection: Moderate; dependent on the maturity of IT/OT boundary monitoring, which is often less mature than IT-side monitoring.
ITID-64621.response: Sever the abused trust path immediately, assess OT impact, and coordinate with operational teams given potential safety implications.
metrics: Count of trust-based critical infrastructure breach attempts detected
Percentage of IT/OT boundaries with active monitoring
sops: Critical Infrastructure Trust Breach Response SOP
ITID-64621.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. Differentiated from ITID-64611 (compromised hardware provenance) and the Manipulation of Trusted Data Sources group (data-level manipulation rather than network-access breach).

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Trust-Based Network Breach
playbook.description: An attacker breaches critical infrastructure network defenses by abusing an established trust relationship between network segments, partners, or systems.

steps.title: Confirm breach via abused network trust relationship
steps.desc: Validate evidence of an intrusion that traversed a trusted network boundary (segmentation trust, partner network peering, trusted-zone assumption) into the critical-infrastructure environment.
steps.guidance: Engage full incident response given the critical-infrastructure context.
steps.outcome: Breach confirmed and the abused trust boundary identified.

steps.title: Map attacker lateral movement across trust boundaries
steps.desc: Trace the attacker's path across network segments/trust boundaries to establish the full extent of the intrusion.

steps.title: Assess impact on operational/critical systems
steps.desc: Determine whether operational technology or critical systems were reached or affected, and assess safety implications.
steps.outcome: Operational impact and safety implications assessed.

steps.title: Sever or restrict the abused trust boundary
steps.desc: Immediately sever or tightly restrict the network trust relationship/segmentation path used for the breach.
steps.guidance: Coordinate with operations to avoid unsafe disruption of critical processes.

steps.title: Engage full incident response and relevant authorities
steps.desc: Engage full IR process and notify relevant regulatory/sector authorities given the critical-infrastructure context.
steps.outcome: Full IR engaged; authorities notified as required.

steps.title: Remove attacker presence and persistence
steps.desc: Identify and remove all attacker footholds, persistence mechanisms, and unauthorized changes across affected systems.
steps.outcome: Environment confirmed clean of attacker presence.

steps.title: Redesign network segmentation and trust architecture
steps.desc: Redesign the network segmentation/trust architecture to eliminate the exploited implicit-trust assumption, applying zero-trust principles where feasible.
steps.outcome: Hardened network architecture documented and implemented.

steps.title: Validate restored network integrity and resume operations
steps.desc: Validate the network is free of attacker presence and resume normal operations under the hardened architecture.

steps.title: Conduct full post-incident review with sector/regulatory stakeholders
steps.desc: Conduct a comprehensive post-incident review, including relevant sector/regulatory stakeholders given the critical-infrastructure impact.
steps.outcome: Findings documented and shared with relevant stakeholders.

ITID-64631.def: An adversary manipulates or poisons a threat intelligence feed (indicator lists, reputation databases) that automated defenses trust and act on directly, causing those defenses to take incorrect action (blocking legitimate resources, ignoring malicious ones, or triggering unwarranted response actions), exploiting the trust automated systems place in the feed's data integrity.
ITID-64631.purpose: Captures cases where a poisoned threat intelligence feed is trusted and acted upon by automated defensive systems.
scopeIncludes: Injection of false indicators of compromise into a trusted threat intelligence feed
Manipulation of a shared reputation database causing automated blocking of legitimate infrastructure
scopeExcludes: Manipulation of real-time sensor/telemetry data feeding an industrial control system (ITID-64632)
Manipulation of DNS or time-synchronization sources (ITID-64633)
ITID-64631.severity: High, given that automated defenses acting on poisoned data can cause both false-negative security gaps and disruptive false-positive blocking.
ITID-64631.priority: P1 upon confirmed poisoning of a threat intelligence feed in active use.
ITID-64631.escalation: Escalate to the threat intelligence platform owner and disable automated action on the affected feed pending validation.
indicators: Automated blocking or alerting on indicators with no corroborating evidence from independent sources
Threat intelligence provider disclosure of a feed integrity incident
vectors: Compromise of a threat intelligence feed provider's publishing pipeline
Submission of false indicators to a crowd-sourced or community threat intelligence platform
rootCauses: Automated action taken on a single feed source without cross-validation
Insufficient integrity verification on ingested threat intelligence data
mitreTechniques: T1565.001 Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation
controls: Cross-validation of threat intelligence indicators across multiple independent sources before automated action
Integrity verification (signing) of ingested threat intelligence data
ITID-64631.detection: Moderate; feed-integrity monitoring and cross-source validation can surface poisoning, but a single trusted feed with no cross-check offers weak detection.
ITID-64631.response: Suspend automated action on the affected feed, validate indicators against independent sources, and reverse any incorrect automated actions taken.
metrics: Count of poisoned indicators identified
Number of automated actions reversed following poisoning confirmation
sops: Threat Intelligence Feed Poisoning Response SOP
ITID-64631.notes: Differentiated from siblings by data type/mechanism: this leaf concerns stored indicator/reputation data (T1565.001) rather than transmitted telemetry (ITID-64632, T1565.002) or runtime-consumed data (ITID-64633, T1565.003).

playbook.name: Poisoned Threat Intelligence Feed Trusted by Automated Defenses
playbook.description: A threat intelligence feed consumed by automated defenses (SIEM, firewall blocklists, EDR) is poisoned with false or malicious indicators, causing automated systems to take incorrect action based on blind trust in a single data source.

steps.title: Confirm threat intel feed poisoning and its automated impact
steps.desc: Validate that a consumed threat-intelligence feed contains false/malicious indicators and confirm what automated actions (blocking, alerting, quarantine) resulted.
steps.guidance: Look for unexplained mass-blocking of legitimate traffic/domains or suspicious new indicators lacking corroboration.
steps.outcome: Poisoning confirmed and automated impact identified.

steps.title: Identify the compromised feed source and injection point
steps.desc: Determine which specific feed/provider was poisoned and how (compromised feed account, MITM on feed delivery, malicious contributor in a shared/open feed).
steps.outcome: Compromised source and injection method identified.

steps.title: Cross-validate indicators against independent sources
steps.desc: Cross-check the suspect indicators against multiple independent threat-intelligence sources to identify which are false and which (if any) are legitimate.
steps.guidance: This cross-validation is the core technical control for this scenario — no single feed should be blindly trusted.
steps.outcome: False indicators identified and separated from legitimate ones.

steps.title: Disable or quarantine the poisoned feed
steps.desc: Immediately disable ingestion of the poisoned feed or quarantine it from automated action while investigation continues.
steps.outcome: Poisoned feed no longer driving automated actions.

steps.title: Reverse incorrect automated actions taken on false indicators
steps.desc: Reverse any blocking, quarantine, or alerting actions taken against legitimate traffic/entities based on the false indicators.
steps.outcome: Legitimate operations restored; false-positive impact reversed.

steps.title: Remediate the feed compromise with the provider
steps.desc: Coordinate with the feed provider to remediate the compromise (e.g. reset compromised contributor credentials, remove malicious submissions).

steps.title: Implement multi-source corroboration before automated action
steps.desc: Implement a requirement that automated defensive actions (especially high-impact blocking) require corroboration across multiple independent threat-intel sources before executing, rather than trusting a single feed.
steps.guidance: This is the core lessons-learned/eradication control for this ITID category.

steps.title: Validate automated defenses operating on corroborated data
steps.desc: Confirm automated defense systems are now operating on corroborated, validated threat data and functioning normally.
steps.outcome: Automated defenses validated as restored and hardened.

steps.title: Review feed vetting and trust model for all threat intel sources
steps.desc: Review the vetting and trust model for all consumed threat-intelligence feeds and apply the same corroboration/hardening principle broadly.
steps.outcome: Feed trust model reviewed and hardened organization-wide.

ITID-64632.def: An adversary transmits spoofed or manipulated sensor/telemetry data to an industrial control system (ICS) that trusts data received from its field devices, causing the ICS to make incorrect operational decisions based on falsified conditions, exploiting the trust the control system places in its telemetry inputs.
ITID-64632.purpose: Captures cases where spoofed sensor or telemetry data is trusted and acted upon by an industrial control system.
scopeIncludes: Spoofed sensor readings transmitted to an ICS causing an incorrect automated control action
Man-in-the-middle manipulation of telemetry in transit between a field device and its controller
scopeExcludes: Poisoning of a threat intelligence/reputation feed (ITID-64631)
Manipulation of DNS or time-synchronization sources (ITID-64633)
Backdoored hardware provenance without active data manipulation (ITID-64611)
ITID-64632.severity: Critical, given the direct physical/operational safety consequence of an ICS acting on falsified telemetry.
ITID-64632.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmed spoofed telemetry affecting ICS operation.
ITID-64632.escalation: Escalate to OT/ICS operations and safety teams immediately given potential physical consequences.
indicators: Sensor readings physically inconsistent with corroborating instrumentation or physical reality
ICS control action inconsistent with actual field conditions
vectors: Interception and manipulation of telemetry in transit between field device and controller
Compromise of a field device to transmit falsified readings
rootCauses: Lack of cryptographic integrity protection on telemetry transmitted to the ICS
Absence of cross-sensor or physical-plausibility validation of incoming telemetry
mitreTechniques: T1565.002 Data Manipulation: Transmitted Data Manipulation
controls: Cryptographic integrity protection on telemetry in transit
Cross-sensor and physical-plausibility validation within the ICS
ITID-64632.detection: Moderate; physical-process anomaly detection and cross-sensor validation can surface implausible telemetry.
ITID-64632.response: Fail safe on detection of implausible telemetry and isolate the affected field device pending investigation.
metrics: Count of spoofed telemetry incidents detected
Time to fail-safe response following telemetry anomaly
ITID-64632.notes: Differentiated from ITID-64631 (stored intelligence data) and ITID-64633 (runtime DNS/time-sync data) by focusing on telemetry manipulated in transit (T1565.002).

playbook.name: Spoofed Sensor/Telemetry Data Trusted by Industrial Control System
playbook.description: An attacker injects spoofed sensor or telemetry data into an industrial control system, exploiting the system's blind trust in a single sensor source to trigger incorrect automated control actions.

steps.title: Confirm spoofed sensor/telemetry data and its control impact
steps.desc: Validate that anomalous or physically implausible sensor readings were injected and confirm what automated control actions the ICS took based on them.
steps.guidance: Engage full incident response given safety implications; involve OT engineering staff immediately.
steps.outcome: Spoofing confirmed and resulting control actions identified.

steps.title: Identify the injection point and method
steps.desc: Determine how the spoofed data was introduced (compromised sensor/PLC, network injection, compromised historian) and the affected sensor(s).

steps.title: Assess safety and operational impact
steps.desc: Assess whether the incorrect control actions created any safety hazard or operational damage, in coordination with plant/OT safety personnel.

steps.title: Switch to manual control or safe-mode operation
steps.desc: If safety-critical, transition the affected process to manual control or a verified safe-mode until sensor trust is restored.
steps.guidance: This step is led by OT/plant operations, with security providing supporting analysis.
steps.outcome: Process placed under safe, verified control.

steps.title: Isolate the compromised sensor/telemetry source
steps.desc: Isolate or disconnect the compromised sensor, PLC, or network segment responsible for the spoofed data.

steps.title: Remediate or replace compromised sensor/telemetry hardware
steps.desc: Remediate the compromised device (firmware reflash, credential reset) or replace it with verified-trusted hardware.
steps.outcome: Sensor/telemetry source restored to a trusted state.

steps.title: Implement cross-validation across independent sensors
steps.desc: Implement or strengthen cross-validation logic requiring agreement across multiple independent sensors before automated control action, rather than trusting a single sensor source.
steps.guidance: This is the core technical control for this ITID category — the root vulnerability is blind trust in one data source.
steps.outcome: Cross-validation implemented for critical control decisions.

steps.title: Validate restored sensor integrity and resume automated control
steps.desc: Validate sensor readings are trustworthy and cross-corroborated, then resume normal automated control operation.
steps.guidance: OT engineering sign-off required before resuming automated control.

steps.title: Conduct joint IT/OT post-incident review
steps.desc: Conduct a joint IT/OT post-incident review and update ICS security architecture and sensor-trust standards.

ITID-64633.def: An adversary manipulates a DNS resolution result or a network time-synchronization source (e.g., NTP) that downstream systems trust and consume at runtime, causing those systems to resolve to malicious infrastructure or operate with an incorrect trusted timestamp, exploiting the trust placed in these foundational, continuously-consumed services.
ITID-64633.purpose: Captures cases where a manipulated DNS or time-synchronization source is trusted and acted upon by downstream systems in real time.
scopeIncludes: DNS cache poisoning or record manipulation causing downstream systems to resolve trusted hostnames to attacker infrastructure
NTP manipulation causing certificate validation, log timestamps, or time-dependent authorization logic to operate incorrectly
scopeExcludes: Manipulation of stored threat intelligence data (ITID-64631)
Manipulation of transmitted ICS sensor telemetry (ITID-64632)
ITID-64633.severity: Critical, given that DNS and time synchronization underpin the correct operation of nearly all downstream trust and security decisions.
ITID-64633.priority: P1 immediately upon confirmed manipulation of a DNS or time-synchronization source in active use.
ITID-64633.escalation: Escalate to network infrastructure teams to isolate the manipulated source and to any downstream systems relying on it for security decisions (e.g., certificate validation).
indicators: DNS responses inconsistent with authoritative records
Time drift on critical systems inconsistent with the expected NTP source
Downstream authentication or certificate failures traceable to a time discrepancy
vectors: DNS cache poisoning or unauthorized zone modification
Rogue or compromised NTP server providing falsified time to dependent systems
rootCauses: Lack of DNSSEC or equivalent integrity validation on DNS resolution
Reliance on a single, unauthenticated time-synchronization source
mitreTechniques: T1565.003 Data Manipulation: Runtime Data Manipulation
controls: DNSSEC or equivalent DNS integrity validation
Authenticated, redundant time-synchronization sources
ITID-64633.detection: Moderate; DNS integrity monitoring and time-drift alerting can surface manipulation, but many environments lack both today.
ITID-64633.response: Isolate and correct the manipulated source immediately and reassess any security decisions (certificate validation, log correlation) made using the falsified data.
metrics: Count of DNS/time-sync manipulation incidents detected
Percentage of critical systems using authenticated, redundant time sources
sops: DNS and Time-Sync Manipulation Response SOP
ITID-64633.notes: Differentiated from ITID-64631/64632 by focusing on foundational, continuously runtime-consumed services (DNS/time) rather than stored intelligence data or transmitted sensor telemetry; mapped to T1565.003 (Runtime Data Manipulation) accordingly.

playbook.name: Manipulated DNS/Time Sync Source Trusted by Downstream Systems
playbook.description: An attacker manipulates a trusted DNS or time-synchronization (NTP) source, causing downstream systems that blindly trust that single source to resolve to malicious destinations or operate on incorrect time, undermining certificate validation and logging integrity.

steps.title: Confirm manipulation of the trusted DNS/NTP source
steps.desc: Validate evidence that a trusted internal DNS server or NTP source is returning manipulated results (incorrect resolutions or incorrect time).
steps.guidance: Compare against independent, known-good DNS resolvers and NTP sources.
steps.outcome: Manipulation confirmed and affected source identified.

steps.title: Determine downstream impact of the manipulated data
steps.desc: Assess what downstream systems relied on the manipulated DNS resolutions or timestamps, and what incorrect actions resulted (e.g. certificate validation failures/bypasses, log timestamp corruption, traffic misdirection).

steps.title: Identify the compromise vector for the DNS/NTP source
steps.desc: Determine how the DNS server or NTP source was compromised or manipulated (credential compromise, cache poisoning, rogue upstream source).

steps.title: Fail over to a known-good DNS/NTP source
steps.desc: Immediately redirect downstream systems to a verified, trusted DNS resolver or NTP source pending remediation.
steps.outcome: Downstream systems operating on trustworthy data.

steps.title: Isolate the compromised DNS/NTP infrastructure
steps.desc: Isolate the compromised server(s) from the network to prevent continued manipulation.

steps.title: Rebuild and secure DNS/NTP infrastructure
steps.desc: Rebuild the compromised DNS/NTP service from a known-good state with hardened access controls and integrity monitoring.

steps.title: Implement cross-validation against multiple independent sources
steps.desc: Configure critical systems to cross-validate DNS resolutions and time sync against multiple independent, geographically diverse sources rather than trusting a single internal source.
steps.guidance: This is the core technical control for this ITID category.
steps.outcome: Cross-validation implemented for DNS and time synchronization.

steps.title: Validate downstream systems and correct any corrupted state
steps.desc: Validate downstream systems are resolving/timestamping correctly, and correct any state corrupted by the manipulation (e.g. reissue certificates affected by validation bypass, correct log timestamps where feasible).
steps.outcome: Downstream systems confirmed restored to correct, trustworthy state.

steps.title: Review DNS/NTP architecture and trust dependencies organization-wide
steps.desc: Review the broader architecture for other single-source trust dependencies on DNS/NTP infrastructure and remediate proactively.

ITID-64634.def: A generalized case of a trusted data source being manipulated to undermine downstream decisions in critical infrastructure, where the specific data source does not yet map to a more specific leaf.
ITID-64634.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for manipulation of trusted data sources that does not fit the threat-intel, ICS-telemetry, or DNS/time-sync leaves.
scopeIncludes: Reports of suspected trusted-data-source manipulation pending determination of the specific source
Novel trusted-data-source manipulation not yet enumerated as its own leaf
scopeExcludes: Confirmed threat intelligence feed poisoning (ITID-64631)
Confirmed ICS telemetry spoofing (ITID-64632)
Confirmed DNS/time-sync manipulation (ITID-64633)
ITID-64634.severity: Critical pending classification of the specific data source affected.
ITID-64634.priority: P1 at report; reclassify once the data source is confirmed.
ITID-64634.escalation: Escalate to the relevant data source owner and critical infrastructure operations immediately regardless of classification status.
indicators: Any downstream decision anomaly traceable to an unverified or untrusted data source not yet classified
vectors: Unclassified trusted-data-source manipulation vector pending investigation
rootCauses: Insufficient initial detail available to attribute root cause
mitreTechniques: T1565.001 Data Manipulation: Stored Data Manipulation
T1565.002 Data Manipulation: Transmitted Data Manipulation
T1565.003 Data Manipulation: Runtime Data Manipulation
controls: Data source integrity review process
Cross-validation against independent sources before automated action
ITID-64634.detection: Variable; depends on the data source once classified.
ITID-64634.response: Classify the affected data source promptly and route to the applicable specific leaf.
metrics: Count of general trusted-data-source manipulation reports pending classification
sops: Trusted Data Source Manipulation Triage SOP
ITID-64634.notes: Catch-all intake leaf for the Manipulation of Trusted Data Sources group.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Manipulation of Trusted Data Source
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident in which a data source trusted by automated systems (feed, sensor, or infrastructure service) is manipulated, causing incorrect automated action.

steps.title: Confirm trusted data source manipulation and classify type
steps.desc: Validate the report of manipulated trusted data and classify the source type (threat intel feed, ICS sensor, DNS/time sync, or other).
steps.outcome: Manipulation confirmed and source type classified.

steps.title: Assess downstream automated impact
steps.desc: Determine what automated actions or decisions were incorrectly driven by the manipulated data.

steps.title: Cross-validate against independent sources
steps.desc: Cross-check the suspect data against independent sources to confirm which specific data points were manipulated.

steps.title: Disconnect or quarantine the compromised data source
steps.desc: Disconnect the manipulated source from automated consumption or quarantine it from driving automated action.

steps.title: Reverse incorrect automated actions
steps.desc: Reverse any incorrect automated actions taken based on the manipulated data.

steps.title: Remediate the compromised data source
steps.desc: Remediate the root cause of the source's compromise (credential reset, infrastructure rebuild, provider coordination).
steps.outcome: Data source restored to a trustworthy state.

steps.title: Implement multi-source cross-validation before automated action
steps.desc: Implement a requirement for cross-validation across independent sources before automated systems act on the data, closing the single-source-trust root cause.

steps.title: Validate restored data integrity and resume normal automated operation
steps.desc: Confirm the data source and downstream automated systems are operating correctly on validated, trustworthy data.
steps.outcome: Normal automated operation validated as restored.

steps.title: Review trust model for all similar automated data dependencies
steps.desc: Review the broader trust model for automated systems' data dependencies and apply cross-validation hardening proactively.

ITID-64711.def: An adversary exploits the trust embedded in an established email-based business relationship to defraud the organization or a counterparty, scoped here to the trust-relationship-abuse framing rather than the technical delivery mechanism, which is fully documented in the taxonomy's dedicated BEC domain.
ITID-64711.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for Business Email Compromise cases viewed specifically through the trust-exploitation angle relevant to supply chain classification.
scopeIncludes: BEC incidents specifically flagged for their trust-relationship-abuse characteristics as part of supply chain risk analysis
Cross-organizational trend reporting linking BEC activity to supply chain trust exposure

ITID-64711.priority: P1, consistent with the primary BEC domain's priority guidance.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General BEC Exploiting Trust
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified Business Email Compromise incident in which an attacker exploits an established trust relationship (executive, colleague, or vendor identity) to induce a fraudulent financial transaction.

steps.title: Intake report of suspected BEC
steps.desc: Collect the suspicious email/communication and the trust relationship it exploited (executive, colleague, vendor) along with the requested financial action.

steps.title: Verify request legitimacy via out-of-band channel
steps.desc: Contact the purported sender through a verified, independent channel to confirm or deny the request.
steps.guidance: Never use contact details from the suspicious message itself.
steps.abort: If confirmed legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine if a mailbox was actually compromised
steps.desc: Investigate whether the purported sender's mailbox was compromised (login anomalies, forwarding rules) versus pure spoofing.

steps.title: Halt or reverse the financial transaction
steps.desc: Immediately contact the receiving bank/institution to halt or reverse the wire transfer or payment.
steps.guidance: Speed is critical — engage the bank's fraud recovery process within hours if possible.

steps.title: Remediate compromised mailbox if applicable
steps.desc: If a mailbox was compromised, reset credentials, revoke sessions, and remove malicious forwarding/rules.
steps.abort: Not applicable if only spoofing occurred.

steps.title: Reinforce out-of-band verification for financial requests
steps.desc: Implement or reinforce mandatory callback verification for any financial request received via email, regardless of apparent sender trust.

steps.title: Engage law enforcement and financial recovery channels
steps.desc: File a report with law enforcement (e.g. IC3) and pursue available financial recovery mechanisms.
steps.outcome: Law enforcement engaged; recovery process underway.

steps.title: Confirm financial recovery status
steps.desc: Confirm final status of fund recovery and close out financial reconciliation.
steps.outcome: Financial impact resolved to the extent possible.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review and update training
steps.desc: Review the incident with finance and security-awareness stakeholders and update training/controls accordingly.

ITID-64721.def: An adversary exploits the trust embedded in an established business relationship to induce a fraudulent wire transfer, scoped here to the trust-relationship-abuse framing rather than the technical payment-fraud mechanism, which is fully documented in the taxonomy's dedicated Financial Fraud domain.
ITID-64721.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for wire fraud cases viewed specifically through the trust-exploitation angle relevant to supply chain classification.
scopeIncludes: Wire fraud incidents specifically flagged for their trust-relationship-abuse characteristics as part of supply chain risk analysis
Cross-organizational trend reporting linking wire fraud activity to supply chain trust exposure
scopeExcludes: The full pattern-specific wire fraud treatment (compromised vendor banking details, real estate/escrow interception), which is tracked under ITID-53211 through ITID-53213
ITID-64721.severity: High, consistent with the severity guidance in the primary wire fraud domain.
ITID-64721.priority: P1, consistent with the primary wire fraud domain's priority guidance.
ITID-64721.escalation: Route to the primary wire fraud response process (ITID-53211-ITID-53213); use this leaf only for supply-chain-specific trend and risk reporting.
indicators: See the primary wire fraud domain (ITID-53211-ITID-53213) for detailed technical indicators
vectors: See the primary wire fraud domain for detailed attack vectors
rootCauses: See the primary wire fraud domain for detailed root causes
controls: See the primary wire fraud domain for detailed controls
ITID-64721.detection: See the primary wire fraud domain for detection coverage detail; this leaf adds no independent technical detection surface.
ITID-64721.response: Handled operationally under the primary wire fraud domain's response process; this leaf exists for supply-chain trust-exploitation classification and rollup purposes only.
metrics: Count of wire fraud incidents cross-tagged with supply chain trust exposure
sops: Wire Transfer Fraud Response SOP (primary, ITID-53211-ITID-53213)
detections: See the primary wire fraud domain for detection tooling
ITID-64721.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. Deliberately kept thin to avoid duplicating the fuller wire fraud treatment already documented at ITID-53211-ITID-53213; use this leaf only for the supply-chain-specific established-business-trust angle.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Wire Fraud via Established Business Trust
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident in which an attacker commits wire fraud by exploiting the established trust of an ongoing business relationship (e.g. redirected payment instructions late in a transaction).

steps.title: Intake report of suspected wire fraud
steps.desc: Collect details of the suspicious payment-instruction change or wire request tied to an established business relationship.

steps.title: Verify payment instructions via known channel
steps.desc: Contact the legitimate business partner through previously established, verified contact information to confirm the payment instructions.
steps.guidance: Do not use contact details from the suspicious communication.
steps.outcome: Legitimacy of payment instructions confirmed or denied.
steps.abort: If confirmed legitimate, close as false positive.

steps.title: Determine compromise point in the transaction chain
steps.desc: Investigate whether either party's email/systems were compromised, enabling interception and alteration of the payment instructions.

steps.title: Halt or reverse the wire transfer
steps.desc: Immediately contact the sending/receiving bank to halt or reverse the fraudulent wire transfer.
steps.guidance: Time-critical — engage bank fraud recovery immediately.

steps.title: Remediate any compromised systems in the transaction chain
steps.desc: Remediate any compromised email account or system identified as the interception point, coordinating with the counterparty if it is on their side.
steps.abort: Not applicable if no compromise found (pure spoofing).

steps.title: Implement verified callback procedure for payment-instruction changes
steps.desc: Implement or reinforce mandatory callback verification for any change to payment instructions on active transactions.

steps.title: Engage law enforcement and legal counsel
steps.desc: File reports with law enforcement and engage legal counsel to pursue recovery options.

steps.title: Confirm financial recovery status and resume transaction
steps.desc: Confirm recovery status and, where the underlying business transaction is still valid, complete it using verified instructions.
steps.outcome: Financial impact resolved and legitimate transaction completed.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review and update finance controls
steps.desc: Review the incident with finance/treasury stakeholders and update controls and training on payment-instruction verification.

ITID-64731.def: An adversary manipulates a trusted third-party payment platform (payment processor, digital wallet, invoicing platform) or the trust an organization places in its integration with that platform, causing funds to be redirected, misappropriated, or fraudulently released, exploiting the trust placed in the platform as a reliable financial intermediary.
ITID-64731.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for cases where a trusted third-party payment platform is manipulated to redirect or misappropriate funds.
scopeIncludes: Manipulation of payment platform account settings (e.g., linked bank account) to redirect legitimate payments
Exploitation of a payment platform's trusted integration/API to trigger unauthorized fund movement
scopeExcludes: BEC-driven wire fraud tracked in the primary BEC/wire-fraud domains (ITID-64711, ITID-64721)
General API/webhook manipulation with no financial payment component (ITID-64441-ITID-64443)
ITID-64731.severity: High, given the direct financial loss potential.
ITID-64731.priority: P1 upon confirmed manipulation of a payment platform resulting in or threatening fund redirection.
ITID-64731.escalation: Escalate to finance and the payment platform provider immediately to freeze or reverse affected transactions.
indicators: Unauthorized change to linked payment account/bank details on a payment platform
Anomalous fund movement inconsistent with expected transaction patterns
vectors: Account takeover of the organization's payment platform account
Exploitation of a weak change-verification process on the platform for linked payment details
rootCauses: Insufficient MFA and change-verification controls on payment platform accounts
Lack of monitoring for anomalous fund-movement patterns
controls: MFA and out-of-band verification for payment platform account changes
Anomalous fund-movement monitoring
ITID-64731.detection: Moderate; dependent on the payment platform's own security telemetry and the organization's integration monitoring.
ITID-64731.response: Freeze affected transactions and accounts immediately, coordinate with the payment platform provider on reversal, and audit for the scope of unauthorized changes.
metrics: Count of payment platform manipulation incidents
Value of fraudulent fund movement prevented or recovered
ITID-64731.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. Scoped to the trust placed in the payment platform as a financial intermediary, distinct from BEC-driven fraud (ITID-64711/64721) and from generic API/webhook manipulation with no financial component.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Manipulation of Trusted Payment Platform
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident in which an attacker manipulates a trusted payment platform (e.g. account takeover, manipulated payment routing, fraudulent merchant onboarding) to divert or steal funds.

steps.title: Confirm manipulation of the payment platform
steps.desc: Validate the report of manipulated activity on the trusted payment platform (account takeover, altered routing/payout details, fraudulent transactions).

steps.title: Determine the manipulation vector
steps.desc: Investigate how the platform/account was manipulated (compromised credentials, API abuse, platform vulnerability, insider action).

steps.title: Quantify financial impact and affected transactions
steps.desc: Identify all transactions affected by the manipulation and quantify total financial impact.

steps.title: Suspend affected payment platform account/access
steps.desc: Suspend the affected account, API keys, or access credentials on the payment platform immediately.

steps.title: Halt or reverse fraudulent transactions/payouts
steps.desc: Contact the payment platform provider to halt pending transactions/payouts and reverse completed ones where possible.

steps.title: Reset credentials and re-secure platform access
steps.desc: Reset all credentials/API keys associated with the platform account and review access-control configuration.

steps.title: Implement enhanced payment platform monitoring and controls
steps.desc: Implement transaction anomaly monitoring, MFA, and dual-approval controls for the payment platform going forward.

steps.title: Restore verified platform access and confirm normal operations
steps.desc: Restore platform access under the strengthened controls and confirm normal payment operations resume correctly.

steps.title: Conduct post-incident review with finance and platform provider
steps.desc: Conduct a post-incident review with finance stakeholders and the platform provider to capture findings and update controls.

ITID-64741.def: An insider exploits their trusted financial role (approver, accountant, treasury staff) to commit financial misconduct against the organization, encompassing both cases with a genuine technical access-abuse component and cases that are purely financial-crime in nature with no technical element.
ITID-64741.purpose: Serves as the intake bucket for insider financial misconduct viewed through the trust-exploitation angle relevant to supply chain classification.
scopeIncludes: An insider with financial system access diverting funds using legitimate credentials (technical access-abuse component present)
An insider committing financial misconduct through purely procedural means, such as falsifying paper records, with no system access abuse involved
scopeExcludes: Segregation-of-duties collusion among multiple approvers, tracked separately under ITID-64531
External BEC/wire fraud with no insider involvement (ITID-64711, ITID-64721)
ITID-64741.severity: High, given the direct financial and reputational impact of confirmed insider financial misconduct.
ITID-64741.priority: P1 upon confirmation of insider financial misconduct.
ITID-64741.escalation: Escalate to finance, internal audit, legal, and HR in parallel; determine whether a technical access-abuse component is present to guide the investigative approach.
indicators: Financial discrepancies traced to a specific individual's authorized role
Behavioral indicators (financial distress, lifestyle changes) correlating with a trusted financial role
vectors: Misuse of legitimate financial system access to divert funds
Falsification of financial records through procedural means with no system access abuse
rootCauses: Insufficient segregation of duties and independent reconciliation in financial processes
Insufficient behavioral or transactional anomaly monitoring on trusted financial roles
controls: Independent reconciliation and segregation of duties in financial processes
Behavioral and transactional anomaly monitoring on financial roles
ITID-64741.detection: Moderate; financial anomaly monitoring provides a technical signal where a system access-abuse component is present, but purely procedural misconduct relies on audit and reconciliation.
ITID-64741.response: Suspend the individual's access pending investigation, conduct a full financial audit, and coordinate with legal/HR on next steps.
metrics: Count of confirmed insider financial misconduct incidents
Value of financial loss identified and recovered
ITID-64741.notes: Lone-child cross-reference stub. Mapped to T1078 where a genuine technical access-abuse component is confirmed during investigation; classify as [] (governance/audit-only) if the misconduct is determined to be purely procedural/financial-crime with no system access-abuse element, consistent with the distinction applied elsewhere in the Insider Trust Exploitation category.

playbook.name: Unclassified / General Insider Financial Misconduct (Trust Exploitation Context)
playbook.description: A general or not-yet-classified incident in which an employee exploits their trusted financial role or access to commit embezzlement, fraud, or other financial misconduct.

steps.title: Intake and validate report of insider financial misconduct
steps.desc: Collect the initial report/detection (e.g. audit finding, anomaly, whistleblower report) of suspected financial misconduct by an employee exploiting their trusted role.
steps.guidance: Engage HR, Legal, and Internal Audit immediately given the employment and evidentiary implications, consistent with prior insider-fraud conventions.

steps.title: Engage HR, Legal, and Internal Audit for coordinated investigation
steps.desc: Establish a coordinated investigation plan with HR, Legal, and Internal Audit consistent with employment law and evidentiary/forensic-accounting requirements.

steps.title: Preserve financial and access records under legal hold
steps.desc: Preserve financial system records, transaction logs, and access history under legal hold, without alerting the subject prematurely.

steps.title: Quantify the scope of financial misconduct
steps.desc: Conduct a forensic-accounting review to quantify the full scope and duration of the misconduct.
steps.guidance: May require engaging external forensic accountants for complex or long-running schemes.

steps.title: Suspend access coordinated with HR/Legal action
steps.desc: Suspend the employee's financial-system and account access at the moment HR/Legal executes any employment action.
steps.guidance: Timing must be tightly coordinated to prevent evidence destruction or further misconduct.
steps.outcome: Access suspended without prematurely alerting the subject.

steps.title: Halt or reverse in-progress fraudulent transactions
steps.desc: Halt any pending transactions and pursue reversal of completed fraudulent transactions where feasible.
steps.outcome: Further financial loss prevented; recovery initiated where possible.

steps.title: Engage law enforcement and pursue recovery
steps.desc: Engage law enforcement and legal counsel to pursue criminal referral, civil recovery, and insurance claims as appropriate.
steps.outcome: Law enforcement/legal engaged; recovery process underway.

steps.title: Strengthen segregation of duties and financial controls
steps.desc: Review and strengthen segregation-of-duties and financial-control gaps that allowed the misconduct to occur or go undetected.

steps.title: Restore normal financial operations under strengthened controls
steps.desc: Restore normal financial operations, reassigning duties as needed, under the strengthened control environment.

steps.title: Conduct joint post-incident review with Internal Audit, HR, and Legal
steps.desc: Conduct a joint post-incident review to capture findings and update financial-control and insider-threat governance.
